## SPEC-LENS CORRECTIONS (pre-draft design lens; ADOPTED by the lead)

The house law ran the design lens over the five piece specs BEFORE
drafting; it returned 3 corrections + 2 notes, all adopted. The
drafters received them verbatim; they are recorded here as the
operative errata to the specs (the lens catching the lead's own
aggregate/per-round conflation AGAIN - third instance of the class -
is itself a process datum).

### LENS-1 [EXPONENT-ERROR] — PE.2(b) [SPEC PE2b] — the stated OUTPUT exponent

The OUTPUT 'E_Palm[outside-B_out time per cycle] <= T exp(-beta(c_H - err))' assigns the theta-to-theta AGGREGATE exponent to a PER-S-RETURN-CYCLE object. The design fixes the per-S-return-cycle occupation at exp(-beta(S_k + c_H - m_k)) (lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:100-102), with the aggregate exp(-beta c_H) = per-cycle x E[N], E[N] ~ exp(beta(S_k - m_k)) (design :106-107; ADJ-2 :724-726, 733-734). The spec's OWN route confirms per-cycle = S_k+c_H-m_k, not c_H: E_Palm[occ per cycle] = rho_beta(B_out) x E_Palm[cycle length], with rho_beta(B_out)=exp(-beta(S_k+c_H-m_k)) (PE.2(a)) and a beta-free cycle length (the spec's own basin-local branch), the product is exp(-beta(S_k+c_H-m_k)). c_H is a valid but loose upper bound; stating it as 'c_H FULL ... the design margin' for the per-cycle object mislabels the object (the honest per-cycle margin is the much fatter S_k+c_H-m_k ~ 1.02, cf. design :108) and conceptually re-imports the E[N] factor — exactly the aggregate/per-round conflation named as defect-caution 4 and by ADJ-2. Fix: state the per-cycle OUTPUT exponent as S_k+c_H-m_k, or explicitly flag c_H as a deliberately loosened bound whose true per-cycle margin is S_k+c_H-m_k. Downstream: PE.3-prime's 'consume PE.2(b) full-c_H margin, half is your budget' narrative inherits the mislabel (the non-trap round bound in fact clears c_H/2 by ~1.0, not by c_H/2).

### LENS-2 [OBJECT-ERROR] — PE.2(b) [SPEC PE2b] — the escaping-cycle split

'escaping cycles (reaching the doorway/global well): their probability per cycle is <= exp(-beta(S_k + c_H - m_k - err)) (gate cost from the ground)' conflates three distinct levels: the doorway S_k+c_H, the theta-saddle / global well S_k, and the Delta_phi gate m_k+2lambda. The cycles that can inflate E_Palm[cycle length] are the theta-saddle crossers that leave to another well for ~exp(beta(S_k-m_k)) before returning; their per-cycle probability is the crossing floor exp(-beta(S_k-m_k)) (R5a (P), lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3073), NOT exp(-beta(S_k+c_H-m_k)) (that exponent is the rarer doorway-reaching event, higher than the saddle by c_H). With the correct exponent the escaping cycles contribute p_esc x L_esc ~ exp(-beta(S_k-m_k)) x exp(beta(S_k-m_k)) = O(1) to E_Palm[cycle length] — bounded and beta-free (so the row's beta-free-cycle-length target still holds), but they are NOT 'negligible' as the spec asserts; the 'negligible' claim only follows from the wrong (larger) exponent S_k+c_H-m_k. Rename the driving event to the theta-saddle crossing, use exp(-beta(S_k-m_k)), and show E_Palm[cycle length] stays beta-free via the p_esc x L_esc = O(1) cancellation rather than via a spurious o(1).

### LENS-3 [INTERFACE-ERROR] — PE.3-prime [SPEC PE3p] — scope of the delivered row

The target equates 'E[occupation of B_out during round i | F_{sigma_{i-1}}] <= T_row exp(-beta(c_H/2-err))' with 'EXACTLY the GAP-PE-COND / PROD-EXCURSION-COND typed strength'. But GAP-PE-COND is occupation OUTSIDE R_0 (lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3164, 3077-3079), and outside R_0 = {E_eps > S_k+c_H} UNION {w_phi != 0} = B_out UNION the trap sectors ({w_theta != k} cannot occur mid-round: a theta-change is the terminus L_i, R5a §4). PE.3-prime as specified consumes only PE.2(b) (B_out); the trap sectors (PE.5(b), whose floor m_1 < S_k+c_H-m_k at large N and thus is the binding branch of the c_H/2 rate) are never carried through the conditional/pointwise upgrade. As written no piece delivers the trap-sector CONDITIONAL-on-F, uniform-over-S bound that GAP-PE-COND requires: PE.5(b)(b-iii) states a per-round trap expectation but not the conditional-uniform form, and PE.3-prime's L1' minorization is pointed only at B_out. Fix: PE.3-prime must consume the SUM (PE.2(b) B_out per-cycle + PE.5(b) trap per-cycle) and upgrade the total, OR PE.5(b) must carry its own PE.3-prime-style conditional upgrade; and the assembly B_out + traps -> outside-R_0 must be assigned. As stated PE.3-prime over-claims (B_out only) to be the whole GAP-PE-COND.

### LENS-4 [NOTE] — PE.5(b) [SPEC PE5b] (b-iii) — the upper-bound tool direction

The 'entry probability x conditional dwell' decomposition, taken literally for an UPPER bound on trap occupation, requires an UPPER bound on the trap dwell / exit time. The only named FW input in the corpus, SR-T2 (lane-c-exit-time-lower-bound-v1.md:51-96, 70: liminf beta^{-1} log E_q[tau_exit] >= H - J(q)), is a LOWER bound on exit time — the direction ADJ-2 correctly used to build the LOWER bound (PR). It cannot supply the dwell UPPER bound the row needs. The valid upper-bound route is the reversibility occupation identity (PE.5 corrected kernel, lane-prodexc-design:112-121, entry pre-payment and exit barrier CANCEL to the Gibbs weight of the floor = exp(-beta m_1); equivalently SR-PE1), which never needs a separate dwell upper bound. The spec already hedges ('if the dwell-side needs the quasi-stationary device, interface it to PE.2(b)'), but as literally written 'entry x dwell' points at an exit-time bound that exists in the corpus only in the wrong direction. Recommend making the occupation-identity route primary and dropping the entry x dwell framing (or importing a named FW UPPER exit-time bound with its own hypothesis rows).

### LENS-5 [NOTE] — PE.2(a) [SPEC PE2a] — the Laplace prefactor power

The headline formula writes the normalizer prefactor as 'c(N) beta^{-N}', but the transverse dimension off the flat 2-torus G_k is 2N-2, so the transverse Gaussian volume is beta^{-(2N-2)/2} = beta^{-(N-1)} and the two flat directions along G_k contribute an O(1) beta-free torus volume: the correct power is beta^{-(N-1)}, not beta^{-N}. The spec itself instructs 'get the power right and SAY which power it is', so this is the intended fill-in — recorded here as the exact value (N-1). Prefactor only; it is subexponential and absorbed into C(N), so it does not affect the exponent S_k+c_H-m_k. (Consistency note: L1' free-density powers cited elsewhere, lane-sh2local:276 'beta^{n/2}', agree once n is set to the actual transverse dimension.)

# PIECE SR-PE1 — the cycle-occupation identity as a NAMED CLASSICAL IMPORT (PE.1)

(grade: draft PROVED-WITH-TYPED-GAPS — the classical identity is imported
and its three hypothesis rows are MATCHED against our object; the object gap
between the Palm S-return cycle and R5a's arbitrary-start delayed-return
round is TYPED as two named interface rows for PE.3' to close, NOT papered
over. Non-goals honored: no proof reproduction, no strengthening, no
application to ROW PROD-EXCURSION.)

SCOPE. This piece discharges PE.1 of the discharge design:
"PE.1 (CYCLE-OCCUPATION IDENTITY - the recorded 'reversibility round-trip'
heuristic made rigorous). For the PLAIN reversible diffusion, S-return
cycles from the cycle-stationary (Palm) entrance law satisfy the classical
identity `E[occupation of B per cycle] = rho_beta(B) x E[cycle length]`
(renewal-reward / continuous Kac). Named classical input SR-PE1 with
hypothesis rows (positive Harris recurrence on compact M - automatic; the
Palm construction; the identity). SR discipline: named, hypothesis-checked,
non-reproduced." [lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:66-74]. It produces ONLY the
named import plus its matched hypothesis rows and the typed object gap; it
does NOT supply the Gibbs numerator (PE.2(a)), the quasi-stationary cycle
length (PE.2(b)), the restart accounting (PE.4), the level condition
(PE.5), or the pointwise/conditional upgrade (PE.3').

Standing setting inherited verbatim: "dX_t = -grad E_eps(X_t) dt +
sqrt(2/beta) dW_t on M = T^{2N}, flagship k=1, N>=10, M2-PIN (lambda>kappa),
eps in [0, eps_2) fixed" [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3001]; base ball
"S := B_{delta/4}(g*)" and collar "S^+ := B_{delta/2}(g*)"
[lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3008-3009].

============================================================
1. THE CLASSICAL INPUT (SR-PE1), STATED WITH HYPOTHESIS ROWS
============================================================
SR-PE1 (corpus-named; the renewal-reward / continuous-time Kac occupation
identity for a positive Harris recurrent process, in the cycle-stationary /
Palm form). Classical; consumed as a NAMED IMPORT and NOT reproduced (SR
discipline), on the same footing R5a consumes SR-KD and L1' consumes the
Aronson/Levi family. The statement used:

  Let {X_t}_{t>=0} be a positive Harris recurrent, cadlag, time-homogeneous
  strong Markov process on a Polish state space E, with unique invariant
  PROBABILITY measure rho. Let A subset E be a Borel set with rho(A) > 0,
  and let the successive A-cycles be delimited by a regeneration epoch
  sequence 0 <= T_0 < T_1 < T_2 < ... adapted to A (the Palm/cycle
  construction: for a Harris process the entrances to A after an intervening
  exit generate a regenerative — one-dependent, wide-sense stationary —
  structure via the Nummelin split of a small set inside A, or directly via
  the Palm calculus of the point process {T_n}). Write the cycle length
  C := T_1 - T_0 and let rho_A^Palm := the law of X_{T_0} that makes the
  cycle sequence stationary (the PALM / cycle-stationary entrance law on A).
  If

        0 < E_{Palm}[ C ] < infinity,                                  (INT)

  then for EVERY bounded Borel f : E -> R the wide-sense renewal-reward
  (ratio) identity holds:

        rho(f) = E_{Palm}[ integral_{T_0}^{T_1} f(X_s) ds ] / E_{Palm}[C].
                                                                       (RR)

  Specializing f = 1_B for a Borel set B gives the cycle-occupation /
  continuous Kac form used by PE.1:

        E_{Palm}[ occupation of B in one A-cycle ]
              = rho(B) . E_{Palm}[ C ].                                 (KAC)

  In particular, with B = A, (KAC) reduces to Kac's return-time formula
  E_{Palm}[ C ] = 1/rho(A) when cycles are the plain A-returns.

Named-theorem provenance (non-reproduced):
  - Regenerative-process ratio/time-average identity (RR): S. Asmussen,
    Applied Probability and Queues, 2nd ed., Springer 2003, Ch. VI
    (Regenerative Processes), Theorem 1.2 and Section VI.3 (the delayed /
    wide-sense-regenerative case); equivalently the Smith key renewal /
    renewal-reward theorem specialized to reward = occupation time.
  - Continuous / occupation-time Kac formula (KAC): M. Kac, "On the notion
    of recurrence in discrete stochastic processes," Bull. AMS 53 (1947)
    1002-1010, in its occupation-time generalization; see also
    Meyn & Tweedie, Markov Chains and Stochastic Stability, 2nd ed. 2009,
    Ch. 10 (positive Harris recurrence) and Ch. 17 (ratio limit theorems),
    and the Palm-calculus derivation in H. Thorisson, Coupling, Stationarity,
    and Regeneration, Springer 2000, Ch. 8-10 (Palm theory / cycle-
    stationarity), or Baccelli & Bremaud, Elements of Queueing Theory, 2nd
    ed. 2003, Ch. 1 (Palm probabilities). The Nummelin split underlying the
    A-cycle regeneration on a general space: E. Nummelin, General Irreducible
    Markov Chains and Non-negative Operators, CUP 1984, Ch. 4.

Hypothesis rows (each MATCHED against our object, one by one):

  ROW SR-PE1.1  (POSITIVE HARRIS RECURRENCE ON COMPACT M — automatic).
    The elliptic diffusion X on M = T^{2N} generated by
        L = (1/beta) Delta - grad E_eps . grad
    (Delta the flat torus Laplacian; diffusion coefficient 2/beta constant;
    E_eps smooth) is positive Harris recurrent with a unique invariant
    probability. REASON (each ingredient standard, cited, non-reproduced):
    (a) IRREDUCIBILITY / positive density. L is uniformly elliptic with
    smooth coefficients, so by the parabolic Hormander / Aronson two-sided
    heat-kernel bounds the transition density p_t(x,y) is strictly positive
    for every t>0 and all x,y in M — the diffusion is (Leb-)irreducible.
    This is exactly the property PE.2(a) already invokes: "the diffusion on
    compact M with elliptic noise is irreducible" [lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:80-82].
    (b) FELLER / strong Feller: smooth bounded coefficients on a compact
    manifold give a strong Feller, conservative semigroup.
    (c) COMPACTNESS: M = T^{2N} is compact, so the process cannot escape to
    infinity; irreducibility + compactness + Feller => positive Harris
    recurrence with a unique invariant PROBABILITY (finite state-space
    volume). Standard sources for the diffusion case: R. Z. Has'minskii
    (Khasminskii), Stochastic Stability of Differential Equations, 2nd ed.,
    Springer 2012, Ch. III-IV (recurrence and existence/uniqueness of the
    invariant measure for non-degenerate diffusions); R. N. Bhattacharya,
    "Criteria for recurrence and existence of invariant measures for
    multidimensional diffusions," Ann. Probab. 6 (1978) 541-553. MET —
    the manifold is compact and the noise is elliptic, so NO Lyapunov /
    drift-to-a-petite-set argument is even needed (the whole compact M is
    petite). This is the "positive Harris recurrence on compact M -
    automatic" of PE.1 [lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:71-73].

  ROW SR-PE1.2  (EXISTENCE / UNIQUENESS OF rho = rho_beta = GIBBS —
    reversibility, explicit detailed-balance check). Claim:
        rho_beta(dx) = Z_beta^{-1} exp(-beta E_eps(x)) dx,
        Z_beta := integral_M exp(-beta E_eps(x)) dx  in (0, infinity),
    is the unique invariant probability of L, and L is rho_beta-reversible.
    CHECK (elementary, stated not as new mathematics but to MATCH the row).
    (i) Z_beta finite and positive: E_eps is smooth on the compact M, hence
    bounded, so 0 < integral_M e^{-beta E_eps} dx < infinity. Density
    strictly positive everywhere.
    (ii) Stationary Fokker-Planck L^* rho_beta = 0. The formal adjoint of L
    w.r.t. Lebesgue is L^* u = (1/beta) Delta u + div(u grad E_eps). Plug
    u = e^{-beta E_eps}: grad u = -beta e^{-beta E_eps} grad E_eps, so
    (1/beta) Delta u = (1/beta) div(grad u) = div(-e^{-beta E_eps} grad E_eps),
    and div(u grad E_eps) = div(e^{-beta E_eps} grad E_eps); the two terms
    cancel exactly, L^* e^{-beta E_eps} = 0. Hence rho_beta is invariant.
    (iii) Detailed balance (reversibility): for f,g smooth,
    integral_M (Lf) g rho_beta dx = -(1/beta) integral_M grad f . grad g
    rho_beta dx (integration by parts on the closed manifold, using
    grad rho_beta = -beta rho_beta grad E_eps so the drift term folds into
    the density gradient); the right side is symmetric in f,g, so
    integral (Lf) g rho_beta = integral f (Lg) rho_beta, i.e. L is
    self-adjoint (reversible) on L^2(rho_beta). The associated Dirichlet
    form is E(f,g) = (1/beta) integral grad f . grad g rho_beta dx.
    (iv) UNIQUENESS: by ROW SR-PE1.1 the diffusion is irreducible on the
    connected compact M, so the invariant probability is unique; rho_beta
    is it. MET. (This is the rho_beta of PE.2(a); the k-basin-mass lower
    bound "Z_beta >= c exp(-beta m_k)" [lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:76-79]
    is PE.2(a)'s numerator work, NOT consumed here.)

  ROW SR-PE1.3  (S-RETURN-TIME INTEGRABILITY (INT) — the mean cycle length
    is finite). The identity (RR)/(KAC) requires 0 < E_{Palm}[C] < infinity
    for the PLAIN A-cycle with A = S. By Kac's return-time formula (the
    B = A specialization of (KAC), valid once the cycle regeneration is in
    place) the mean plain-return cycle length under the Palm entrance law is
        E_{Palm}[C] = 1/rho_beta(S),
    and rho_beta(S) > 0 because S = B_{delta/4}(g*) is a nonempty open ball
    and rho_beta has a strictly positive smooth density (ROW SR-PE1.2). Also
    E_{Palm}[C] > 0 because S^+ ) S and the process needs positive time to
    exit and re-enter (in the DELAYED variant this is forced; in the plain
    variant it is a.s. positive by continuity of paths). Hence
    0 < E_{Palm}[C] = 1/rho_beta(S) < infinity: (INT) MET for the PLAIN
    S-return cycle. QUANTITATIVE CAVEAT (flagged, not resolved here):
    1/rho_beta(S) is beta-dependent, and its beta-asymptotics is exactly the
    "beta-free CONDITIONED cycle length" that PE.2(b)'s quasi-stationary
    lemma must supply [lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:82-86]; SR-PE1 asserts only
    finiteness (INT), NOT a beta-free bound. Finiteness is all (RR)/(KAC)
    need to hold as an identity.

RESULT OF PART 1. SR-PE1 imports, with all three hypothesis rows MATCHED for
the PLAIN S-return cycle of our reversible elliptic diffusion under its Palm
entrance law:
    E_{Palm}[ occupation of B in one plain S-return cycle ]
          = rho_beta(B) . E_{Palm}[C],   E_{Palm}[C] = 1/rho_beta(S).   (KAC-S)
This is PE.1's "reversibility round-trip made rigorous" as an EXACT identity
on the Palm cycle — nothing more. No exponent, no o(1), no beta-asymptotics
is asserted; those are PE.2's burden.

============================================================
2. THE PRECISE OBJECT GAP (TYPED — two named interface rows for PE.3')
============================================================
DEFECT-CLASS CAUTION (1) — OBJECT SLIPS — governs here: the Palm S-return
cycle of SR-PE1 and the R5a round are DIFFERENT objects, and (KAC-S) rides
the former, NOT the latter. State exactly which object each expectation
refers to. SR-PE1 as imported lives on:

  OBJECT-PE1: the PLAIN S-return cycle {T_0, T_1} of the AUTONOMOUS diffusion
  with NO absorbing theta-label event, started from the cycle-stationary
  (Palm) entrance law rho_S^Palm on S. Its expectation operator is E_{Palm}.

The consumer object is:

  OBJECT-R5a: one R5a round on the continuous FLOORS round object. Round i
  starts at sigma_{i-1} with "X_{sigma_{i-1}} is an arbitrary
  (F_{sigma_{i-1}}-measurable) point of S" — "There is no fixed regeneration
  law nu here" [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3037]; the return is the DELAYED
  return "D(t) := inf{ s >= theta^+(t) : X_s in S }", theta^+(t) the first
  collar-exit [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3015-3016]; and the round terminus is
  "T_i := min( D(sigma_{i-1}) , L_i )" with L_i the first theta-label change
  [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3048]. Its expectation operator is E_x( . |
  F_{sigma_{i-1}}) at the arbitrary start x = X_{sigma_{i-1}} in S.

Passing from OBJECT-PE1 to OBJECT-R5a is NOT done in this piece. It requires
closing exactly two deltas, which I TYPE as named interface rows to be
discharged by PE.3' (the pointwise / conditional upgrade,
[lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:88-96]) and, for the absorption delta, PE.4:

  DELTA-PE1-ENTRANCE (entrance-law delta — the Palm-to-pointwise gap).
    (KAC-S) is an identity AVERAGED over the Palm entrance law rho_S^Palm.
    OBJECT-R5a needs the occupation bound CONDITIONAL on F_{sigma_{i-1}},
    uniform over the ARBITRARY start point X_{sigma_{i-1}} in S
    [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3037]. The averaged identity does NOT by
    itself give a pointwise-over-S statement; a start x in S concentrated at
    a trap-facing point can weight a cycle differently from rho_S^Palm.
    This is the exact "averaged cycle identity ... does NOT deliver it"
    obstruction [lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:22-26], and its closure is PE.3'
    verbatim: "PE.3' (THE POINTWISE UPGRADE ...): from the averaged cycle
    identity to an a.s. bound conditional on F_{sigma_{i-1}}, uniform over
    ARBITRARY starts X_{sigma_{i-1}} in S - candidate route: the L1'
    pointwise minorization gives every start's one-step law a density floor
    against Leb|_S, transferring the averaged bound to a pointwise one at an
    exp(beta O(h^2)) cost; the transfer must be proved on R5a's terminus,
    not asserted" [lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:88-96]. TYPED, NOT closed here.
    Interface strength required from PE.3': rho_S^Palm-averaged (KAC-S) =>
    conditional-on-F_{sigma_{i-1}} bound uniform over x in S, at a cost

### PE1 — checker findings (round 1, verbatim; repairs = round 2)

- [MAJOR] The identity E_Palm[C] = 1/rho_beta(S), presented as the 'B=A specialization of (KAC), i.e. Kac's return-time formula,' is mathematically INCORRECT for the continuous-time entrance/plain-return-delimited S-cycle.
  EVIDENCE: The draft's own occupation identity (KAC) is correct: E_Palm[occupation of B per cycle] = rho_beta(B)·E_Palm[C]. Setting B=A=S it yields E_Palm[occupation of S per cycle] = rho_beta(S)·E_Palm[C], i.e. E_Palm[C] = E_Palm[sigma_S]/rho_beta(S), where sigma_S is the mean per-cycle sojourn time INSIDE S (the initial-visit sojourn; the cycle from one S-entrance T_0 to the next entrance-after-exit T_1 contains exactly one S-sojourn, of positive random length). This equals 1/rho_beta(S) only if E_Palm[sigma_S]=1, which is false for a diffusion. The correct continuous-time Kac gives E_Palm[C]=1/lambda_S with lambda_S the entrance-point-process intensity, generally != rho_beta(S). The draft imported the DISCRETE Kac formula (E[return]=1/pi(A), valid only when cycles are single-step visits so occupation-per-cycle=1) onto an entrance-delimited continuous cycle where occupation-per-cycle is a full positive sojourn — a defect-class-(3) classical-import MISSTATEMENT. The false value is featured prominently in (KAC-S) ('E_{Palm}[C] = 1/rho_beta(S)'), in the QUANTITATIVE CAVEAT, and in the TYPED GAP QUANTITATIVE-CYCLE-LENGTH, where 'the beta-asymptotics of 1/rho_beta(S)' is handed to PE.2(b) — so the wrong object is passed across the interface. CURE (surgical, non-blocking): the row's only load-bearing need is (INT) 0 < E_Palm[C] < infinity, which holds independently (positive Harris recurrence on compact M with everywhere-positive density => finite mean return time to open S; path continuity => C>0). Delete the '=1/rho_beta(S)' identity, keep (INT) on the Harris-recurrence footing, and relabel the PE.2(b) hand-off object as E_Palm[C] itself (not 1/rho_beta(S)). Conclusion (INT met) and the delivered (KAC) identity both survive, so REPAIRABLE not BLOCKED.
- [MINOR] Even after fixing the 1/rho(S) error, the draft silently identifies the UNCONDITIONED plain-return Palm cycle length E_Palm[C] with PE.2(b)'s CONDITIONED (quasi-stationary) cycle length.
  EVIDENCE: SR-PE1.3/(KAC-S) produce the unconditioned Palm mean cycle length; the QUANTITATIVE CAVEAT and TYPED GAP assert its beta-asymptotics is 'exactly the beta-free CONDITIONED cycle length that PE.2(b)'s quasi-stationary lemma must supply' [lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:82-86]. Unconditioned mean cycle length and quasi-stationary (basin-conditioned) cycle length are different objects; equating their beta-asymptotics is glossed. It is partly excused because the item is explicitly TYPED as PE.2(b)'s burden ('flagged, not resolved here'), so it is an honestly-deferred interface rather than a smuggled claim — hence MINOR — but the deferral should name the object as 'the plain unconditioned E_Palm[C], whose relation to PE.2(b)'s conditioned length is itself PE.2(b)'s to establish,' not assert them equal.

No citation defects. Math recomputed: the detailed-balance check (ROW SR-PE1.2) is CORRECT — adjoint L*u=(1/beta)Delta u + div(u grad E_eps), plug u=e^{-beta E}: (1/beta)Delta u = -div(e^{-beta E}grad E) cancels div(u grad E)=div(e^{-beta E}grad E), so L*e^{-beta E}=0; self-adjointness with Dirichlet form (1/beta)int grad f·grad g rho verified. ROW SR-PE1.1 (positive Harris via Aronson positivity + compactness + Feller) is a legitimate named import. The (RR)/(KAC) Palm cycle formula is correctly stated and does NOT smuggle independence (wide-sense/one-dependent stationarity suffices — Thorisson/Baccelli-Bremaud). Object discipline is a genuine strength: OBJECT-PE1 (plain S-return, Palm law) vs OBJECT-R5a (delayed return D(.), arbitrary F_{sigma_{i-1}}-measurable start) are kept distinct; DELTA-PE1-ENTRANCE and DELTA-PE1-DELAYED are honestly typed for PE.3'; no aggregate/per-round conflation (E[N] correctly left at the outer Wald sum 3109-3117); no physics vocabulary. # PE.2(a) — the Gibbs numerator one-liner

(round-1 grade: draft PROVED; checker SOUND)

========================================================================
PIECE PE.2(a) — THE GIBBS NUMERATOR ONE-LINER (lens-corrected device)
Discharge of lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:75-86 clause (a).
Grade: PROVED (a complete Laplace ratio; the two probabilistic burdens
PE.2(b)/PE.3'/PE.5(b) are OUT OF SCOPE and remain typed elsewhere).
========================================================================

------------------------------------------------------------------------
0. STATEMENT
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Standing (verbatim, lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:1345): "dX = -grad E_eps(X)
dt + sqrt(2/beta) dW on the compact flat torus M = T^{2N} = T^N_theta x
T^N_phi (dim M = 2N) ... generator L_beta^eps = (1/beta) Delta -
grad E_eps . grad. E_eps is smooth and Lambda-periodic". Flagship k = 1,
N >= 10, M2-PIN (lambda > kappa), eps in [0, eps_2) fixed. The reversible
invariant (Gibbs) measure of this overdamped-Langevin generator is

      rho_beta(dx) = Z_beta^{-1} e^{-beta E_eps(x)} dx,
      Z_beta := integral_M e^{-beta E_eps(x)} dx,                    (GIBBS)

the object PE.1/SR-PE1 feed into the renewal-reward identity
E[occupation of B per cycle] = rho_beta(B) x E[cycle length]
(lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:70). Define the ABOVE-CAP region

      B_out := { x in T^{2N} : E_eps(x) >= S_k + c_H }.

CLAIM (PE.2(a)). There is a beta-free constant C(N) < infinity and a
threshold beta_0(delta, eps) < infinity such that for all beta >= beta_0,

  rho_beta(B_out) <= C(N) exp( -beta ( S_k + c_H - m_k - err ) ),   (PE2a)

with the EXACT error term

  err(delta, beta, eps) = eps w_k + (N-1) (ln beta)/beta,           (ERR)
       w_k = W*(G_k) = N(1 - cos(2 pi k/N)) = g(N) at k = 1,
       beta_0(delta, eps) = 1/(L_eps delta^2),
       L_eps := sup_U ||Hess E_eps||_op <= L + 8 eps (fixed-eps, finite).

Both err summands are non-negative and the net exponent stays STRICTLY
POSITIVE on the whole flagship range (see step 4). Equivalently, absorbing
the two err summands, rho_beta(B_out) <= C(N) exp(-beta(S_k + c_H - m_k -
eps w_k - (N-1)(ln beta)/beta)); the (N-1)(ln beta)/beta term is the
Laplace prefactor beta^{N-1} written inside the exponent, and it -> 0 as
beta -> infinity (the declared order of limits: beta first).

SCOPE (BINDING). This piece bounds ONLY the TOTAL Gibbs mass of the
above-cap level region B_out. It does NOT sub-stratify B_out into the
w_phi != 0 pinning-trap sectors G_{k,j} = C_k x C_j^phi, and it makes NO
reachability, basin, or occupation-time claim: those are PE.5(b) territory
(lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:132-137, 472-475), NOT mine. NO recurrent-class
restriction is invoked anywhere — none exists: the elliptic diffusion on
compact M is irreducible, and (GIBBS) is its unique reversible measure; the
v1 "recurrent class" parenthetical was FALSE (design page :79-82).

------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. THE NUMERATOR (one line, level bound)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
On B_out, E_eps(x) >= S_k + c_H pointwise, hence e^{-beta E_eps(x)} <=
e^{-beta(S_k + c_H)}. Therefore

  integral_{B_out} e^{-beta E_eps} dx <= Leb(B_out) e^{-beta(S_k + c_H)}
                                      <= V_M e^{-beta(S_k + c_H)},      (NUM)
  V_M := Leb(T^{2N}) = vol(M)  (beta-free; = (2 pi)^{2N} for the standard
                                lattice, kept symbolic).

No Laplace expansion is needed upstairs: the cap floor S_k + c_H is a
uniform pointwise lower bound on E_eps over B_out by the DEFINITION of
B_out. This is the whole numerator.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. THE DENOMINATOR (honest Laplace LOWER bound at the k-basin ground)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Restrict the Z_beta integral to the delta-tube of the product ground
G_k = C_k^theta x C_0^phi (E_eps-critical for every eps; the SETTING's
G_k). Write U := T_{r0}(G_k) = {dist(., G_k) <= r0}, r0 <= inj(M)/4
(lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:1375), and take delta <= r0.

(2a) THE QUADRATIC UPPER BOUND on E_eps over the tube (the corpus fact
the honest Laplace lower bound requires). Two consumed facts:

  M2P.1 (ground criticality + level): "grad E_eps = 0 on G_k for EVERY
  eps" and "E_eps(G_k) = m_k + eps w_k" (lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:1381,
  1377-1379: "e_0 := M_k(eps) = m_k + eps w_k, m_k := kappa N(1 - cos
  (2 pi k/N)), w_k := W*(G_k) = N(1 - cos(2 pi k/N))").

  M5-DRIFT (Lipschitz gradient): "|grad E_eps(x)| <= L_eps dist(x, G_k),
  L_eps <= L + 8 eps, grad E_eps L_eps-Lipschitz on U"
  (lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:1419), L := sup_U ||Hess E_0||_op finite by
  smoothness + compactness (:1406).

  Derivation of the upper bound. Fix x in U, let p := pi(x) in G_k be the
  nearest point (single-valued on U, the tube-degraded Morse-Bott
  projection, :1401), d := dist(x, G_k) = |x - p|, the fiber segment
  [p, x] subset U. By the fundamental theorem of calculus along [p, x]
  and grad E_eps(p) = 0 (M2P.1),

    E_eps(x) - E_eps(p)
      = integral_0^1 <grad E_eps(p + s(x-p)) - grad E_eps(p), x - p> ds
      <= integral_0^1 |grad E_eps(p+s(x-p)) - grad E_eps(p)| |x-p| ds
      <= integral_0^1 L_eps (s d)(d) ds  =  (L_eps/2) d^2,

  where the second inequality is Cauchy-Schwarz and the third is the
  L_eps-Lipschitz bound (M5-DRIFT) applied on the segment inside U. Since
  E_eps(p) = m_k + eps w_k (M2P.1 ground level, p in G_k),

    E_eps(x) <= m_k + eps w_k + (L_eps/2) dist(x, G_k)^2   on U.  (UP-QUAD)

  (This is the exact upper companion of the corpus COERCIVITY lower bound
  E_eps(x) - (m_k + eps w_k) >= (c_perp/2) dist^2, M5-COERCE,
  lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:1395; here only the L_eps-Lipschitz UPPER side
  is used, which needs no positive-definiteness of the Hessian.)

(2b) THE GAUSSIAN-VOLUME COMPARISON (the beta^{-(N-1)} prefactor; power
stated explicitly per the lens correction). Fermi (normal-tube)
coordinates on U write x = exp_p(v), p in G_k (a FLAT 2-torus), v normal,
|v| = dist(x, G_k); the transverse fibre has dimension 2N - 2 (dim M -
dim G_k = 2N - 2), and the two flat directions ALONG G_k contribute an
O(1) beta-free torus area vol_2(G_k). The volume element is
dx = J(p, v) dp dv with Jacobian J of the normal exponential map; on the
tube radius r0 <= inj/4 the map is a diffeomorphism and J is bounded below
by a beta-free geometric constant c_J > 0 (for the totally-geodesic flat
product ground G_k inside flat T^{2N}, in fact J == 1, so one may take
c_J = 1; c_J > 0 is kept for safety). Then, using (UP-QUAD),

  Z_beta >= integral_{dist(.,G_k) <= delta} e^{-beta E_eps} dx
        >= e^{-beta(m_k + eps w_k)} c_J vol_2(G_k)
             integral_{|v| <= delta, v in R^{2N-2}}
               e^{-beta (L_eps/2) |v|^2} dv.

Rescale u = sqrt(beta L_eps) v (dv = (beta L_eps)^{-(2N-2)/2} du =
(beta L_eps)^{-(N-1)} du):

  integral_{|v|<=delta} e^{-beta(L_eps/2)|v|^2} dv
    = (beta L_eps)^{-(N-1)} integral_{|u| <= delta sqrt(beta L_eps)}
        e^{-|u|^2/2} du.

For beta >= beta_0 := 1/(L_eps delta^2) the truncation radius
delta sqrt(beta L_eps) >= 1, so the inner integral is bounded below by the
BETA-FREE constant I_{N-1} := integral_{|u| <= 1, u in R^{2N-2}}
e^{-|u|^2/2} du > 0. Hence, for all beta >= beta_0,

  Z_beta >= c(N) beta^{-(N-1)} e^{-beta(m_k + eps w_k)},          (DEN)
  c(N) := c_J vol_2(G_k) I_{N-1} L_eps^{-(N-1)}  > 0, beta-free.

THE POWER IS beta^{-(N-1)}, NOT beta^{-N}: the transverse dimension is
2N - 2, so the transverse Gaussian volume scales as beta^{-(2N-2)/2} =
beta^{-(N-1)}, and the two along-G_k directions give the beta-free area
vol_2(G_k) (lens correction, honored). This is CONSISTENT with the L1'
free-density normalizer beta^{n/2} (lane-sh2local-proofs-v1.md:276,
"p_1(x,.) >= c_0' beta^{n/2} exp(-beta C_2(delta^2+h^2)) Leb|_{B_rho(y)}")
once n is set to the actual transverse dimension. No recurrent-class
restriction enters (DEN): it is a bare Laplace lower bound on the FULL
partition function, normalizing by the k-basin's own ground mass.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. THE RATIO (assembling (PE2a))
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Divide (NUM) by (DEN); valid for every beta >= beta_0 = 1/(L_eps delta^2):

  rho_beta(B_out) = [integral_{B_out} e^{-beta E_eps}] / Z_beta
     <= [ V_M e^{-beta(S_k + c_H)} ]
        / [ c(N) beta^{-(N-1)} e^{-beta(m_k + eps w_k)} ]
     = (V_M / c(N)) beta^{N-1}
         exp( -beta ( S_k + c_H - m_k - eps w_k ) ).

Set C(N) := V_M / c(N) (beta-free, positive, finite) and rewrite the
polynomial prefactor inside the exponent, beta^{N-1} = exp((N-1) ln beta)
= exp( beta . (N-1)(ln beta)/beta ):

  rho_beta(B_out) <= C(N)
     exp( -beta ( S_k + c_H - m_k - eps w_k - (N-1)(ln beta)/beta ) ),

which is EXACTLY (PE2a) with err(delta, beta, eps) = eps w_k +
(N-1)(ln beta)/beta as declared in (ERR). QED.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. err IS HONEST AND THE EXPONENT IS STRICTLY POSITIVE
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Handling of the two err summands, honestly:

 * eps w_k (the ground shift). The denominator floor is the TRUE ground
   level m_k + eps w_k (M2P.1), not the kappa-scale m_k; the numerator cap
   S_k + c_H is the corpus kappa-scale doorway. The gap is therefore
   S_k + c_H - m_k - eps w_k. Since 0 <= eps < eps_2 and w_k = g(N) is a
   fixed beta-free number, eps w_k <= eps_2 g(N) is a small beta-free
   shift, absorbed into err. It is eps-uniform and vanishes at eps = 0.

 * (N-1)(ln beta)/beta (the Laplace prefactor). This is the beta^{N-1}
   from the beta^{-(N-1)} normalizer of (DEN); it is a decreasing
   subexponential correction -> 0 as beta -> infinity, so it is absorbed
   into err under the declared "beta first" order of limits. delta enters
   ONLY through the validity threshold beta_0 = 1/(L_eps delta^2); it does
   NOT appear in the exponent of the sharp form.

Net exponent positivity. With c_H = (m_k + 2 kappa - S_k)/4 (the FIRST
ledger entry, active on all N >= 10 since g(N) < 2 there — ADJ-1 step 2,
lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:293-303),

  S_k + c_H - m_k = (3(S_k - m_k) + 2 kappa)/4 > 0,

strictly positive by PROD-SHELL "S_k - m_k < 2 kappa" with S_k > m_k
(lane-lp-product-saddle-v1.md:152-155; lane-lt-label-tower-v1.md:108); at
the flagship N = 10 it equals (3(0.70) + 2)/4 kappa = 1.025 kappa ~ 1.02
(lane-lt-label-tower-v1.md:116; matching PE.4's "S_k + c_H - m_k ~ 1.02 at
the flagship", lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:108-109). Because eps w_k <=
eps_2 g(N) cannot reach c_H/2 anywhere in the eps_2-capped pinning range
(lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:109-111) and (N-1)(ln beta)/beta -> 0, the net
exponent S_k + c_H - m_k - err stays strictly positive for beta large.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. ALTERNATIVE (crude uniform-tube denominator; beta-free C, delta^2 err)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Bounding E_eps <= m_k + eps w_k + (L_eps/2) delta^2 UNIFORMLY on the delta-
tube (from (UP-QUAD)) and using the beta-free tube volume
v(N, delta) := c_J vol_2(G_k) omega_{2N-2} delta^{2N-2} gives
Z_beta >= v(N, delta) e^{-beta(m_k + eps w_k + (L_eps/2)delta^2)} and hence
rho_beta(B_out) <= (V_M / v(N,delta)) exp(-beta(S_k + c_H - m_k - eps w_k -
(L_eps/2) delta^2)), i.e. a genuinely beta-free prefactor at the cost of
the delta^2 err term err = eps w_k + (L_eps/2) delta^2. Either form
discharges the clause; the sharp Gaussian form (step 2b) is presented as
primary because the lens correction asks for the correct prefactor POWER
(N-1) to be stated.

(4) NO aggregate/per-round conflation — the piece touches neither. (5) No physics/agency vocabulary. # PE.2(b) — the basin-conditional cycle length (the hard kernel)

(round-1 grade: draft PROVED-WITH-TYPED-GAPS; checker REPAIRABLE)

========================================================================
PIECE PE.2(b) — THE BASIN-CONDITIONAL CYCLE-LENGTH LEMMA
(the hard kernel; discharge of lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:82-86, 460-464)
Grade: PROVED-WITH-TYPED-GAPS. The Palm/stationary-cycle occupation
bound for the LEVEL region B_out is proved OUTRIGHT by an EXACT
renewal-reward identity in RATIO form (Z_beta cancels), consuming
SR-PE1 (wave 1) and PE.2(a) (wave 1) at exactly their stated strengths.
The Palm->R5a-round transfer is TYPED as PE.3' (the two SR-PE1 deltas),
NOT closed here; the FW-upper escape-probability companion is TYPED and
recorded NON-load-bearing; the w_phi!=0 trap sub-stratification is
PE.5(b), out of scope.
========================================================================

------------------------------------------------------------------------
0. OBJECTS, SCOPE, STANDING (state WHICH object every expectation rides)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Standing (verbatim): "dX_t = -grad E_eps(X_t) dt + sqrt(2/beta) dW_t on
M = T^{2N}, flagship k=1, N>=10, M2-PIN (lambda>kappa), eps in [0, eps_2)
fixed" [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3001]; base ball "S := B_{delta/4}(g*)"
and collar "S^+ := B_{delta/2}(g*)" [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3008-3009];
g* in G_k, the flat product-ground 2-torus, "E_eps(G_k) = m_k + eps w_k"
[lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:1377-1379]. Reversible law
rho_beta(dx) = Z_beta^{-1} e^{-beta E_eps(x)} dx, Z_beta = int_M e^{-beta
E_eps} dx [PE.2(a) (GIBBS)]. Order of limits (verbatim): "beta ->
infinity FIRST at fixed (eps, delta, h = delta/2) ... THEN delta -> 0
(h -> 0) ... THEN the eps-window is read" [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:
3121-3125].

OBJECT (defect-caution 1 — OBJECT SLIPS — governs; name it once and
hold it). Every expectation E_Palm below rides OBJECT-PE1 of SR-PE1:
"the PLAIN S-return cycle {T_0, T_1} of the AUTONOMOUS diffusion with
NO absorbing theta-label event, started from the cycle-stationary (Palm)
entrance law rho_S^Palm on S. Its expectation operator is E_{Palm}"
[wave-1 SR-PE1, section 2, OBJECT-PE1]. C := T_1 - T_0 is the plain
S-return cycle length under rho_S^Palm. This is NOT OBJECT-R5a (the
absorbed FLOORS round started POINTWISE at an arbitrary
F_{sigma_{i-1}}-measurable x in S, terminus min(D(sigma_{i-1}), L_i),
lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3037,3048); the passage OBJECT-PE1 -> OBJECT-R5a
is PE.3', NOT this piece (see typed gaps, inherited verbatim from SR-PE1).

SCOPE (BINDING). B_out := { x in T^{2N} : E_eps(x) >= S_k + c_H } — the
above-doorway LEVEL region [PE.2(a), "Define the ABOVE-CAP region
B_out := { x in T^{2N} : E_eps(x) >= S_k + c_H }"]. This piece bounds the
per-cycle occupation of the LEVEL region B_out ONLY. It does NOT
sub-stratify the row's full "outside R_0" set into the w_phi != 0
pinning-trap sectors G_{k,j}: "those are PE.5(b) territory ..., NOT mine"
[PE.2(a) SCOPE, echoing lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:132-137].

------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. STATEMENT (target first)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
CLAIM (PE.2(b)). There is a beta-free T(N, delta) < infinity and a
threshold beta_0(delta, eps) < infinity such that, for the plain
S-return Palm cycle (OBJECT-PE1) and every beta >= beta_0,

  E_Palm[ occupation of B_out in one S-return cycle ]
        <= T(N, delta) exp( -beta ( S_k + c_H - m_k - err(delta,eps) ) ),
                                                                  (PE2b)
  err(delta, eps) := eps w_k + (L_eps/2)(delta/4)^2,
  T(N, delta) := V_M / ( c_{2N} (delta/4)^{2N} ),
  beta_0(delta, eps) := 1/( L_eps (delta/4)^2 ),

with V_M = Leb(M), c_{2N} = Leb(unit 2N-ball) = pi^N/N!, L_eps =
sup_U ||Hess E_eps||_op <= L + 8 eps (finite, fixed-eps), all beta-free;
w_k = W*(G_k) = N(1 - cos(2 pi k/N)) = g(N) at k=1. Both err summands are
>= 0 and -> 0 in the declared order of limits (beta first; then delta
kills (L_eps/2)(delta/4)^2; then the eps-window kills eps w_k).

SHARP-vs-LOOSE EXPONENT (lens correction 1, honored explicitly). The
exponent in (PE2b) is S_k + c_H - m_k — the TRUE per-cycle margin (~1.02
at the flagship, cf. lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:108), NOT c_H. Because
S_k - m_k > 0 always ("PROD-SHELL gives S_k - m_k < 2 kappa" and the
ladder gives S_k - m_k > 0, lane-lp-product-saddle-v1.md:152-155), one
has S_k + c_H - m_k >= c_H, so (PE2b) LOOSENS to the design's requested
output shape

  E_Palm[ occupation of B_out per cycle ] <= T(N,delta) exp(-beta(c_H
        - err(delta,eps))),                                       (PE2b-loose)

where c_H is a DELIBERATELY loosened, valid upper bound whose true
per-cycle margin is S_k + c_H - m_k. Stating the object's exponent as
c_H WITHOUT this flag would mislabel the per-cycle object and
conceptually re-import the E[N] factor — exactly the aggregate/per-round
conflation named as defect-caution 4 and by ADJ-2. The AGGREGATE
(theta-to-theta) occupation is the SEPARATE display per-cycle x E[N] =
exp(-beta(S_k+c_H-m_k)) x exp(beta(S_k-m_k)) = exp(-beta c_H) [design
line 106-107; ADJ-2 lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:724-726, 733-734], and
E[N] is applied by M4 at the OUTER Wald sum, never folded here (PE.4).

------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. PROOF — THE RATIO IDENTITY (Z_beta cancels; global-well-independent)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Step 2.1 (consume SR-PE1 at exactly its stated strength). SR-PE1's
matched result is the EXACT cycle-occupation identity on OBJECT-PE1:
"E_{Palm}[ occupation of B in one plain S-return cycle ] = rho_beta(B) .
E_{Palm}[C], E_{Palm}[C] = 1/rho_beta(S). (KAC-S)" [wave-1 SR-PE1,
RESULT OF PART 1], whose hypothesis rows SR-PE1.1 (positive Harris
recurrence on compact elliptic M — automatic), SR-PE1.2 (rho_beta =
Gibbs, detailed balance), SR-PE1.3 (0 < E_Palm[C] = 1/rho_beta(S) <
infinity — (INT)) are MATCHED there. Specialize B = B_out and substitute
E_Palm[C] = 1/rho_beta(S):

  E_Palm[ occupation of B_out per cycle ] = rho_beta(B_out) . (1/rho_beta(S))
      = rho_beta(B_out) / rho_beta(S)
      = ( int_{B_out} e^{-beta E_eps} dx ) / ( int_S e^{-beta E_eps} dx ).   (RATIO)

The normalizer Z_beta CANCELS between numerator and denominator: (RATIO)
is a purely LOCAL Gibbs ratio. This is the load-bearing step. It is why
no "beta-free cycle length" is needed and why the metastable global well
is irrelevant to the occupation (see Step 2.4): the identity is exact and
Z_beta-free.

Step 2.2 (numerator — consume PE.2(a) NUM). PE.2(a)'s numerator line,
consumed verbatim: "integral_{B_out} e^{-beta E_eps} dx <= Leb(B_out)
e^{-beta(S_k + c_H)} <= V_M e^{-beta(S_k + c_H)}, (NUM)" [wave-1 PE.2(a),
section 1], since E_eps >= S_k + c_H pointwise on B_out by definition.
V_M := Leb(M), beta-free. Thus

  int_{B_out} e^{-beta E_eps} dx <= V_M e^{-beta(S_k + c_H)}.        (NUM)

Step 2.3 (denominator — an honest Laplace LOWER bound at the base ball,
crude Leb form, no prefactor). I need a lower bound on int_S e^{-beta
E_eps} over S = B_{delta/4}(g*). Consume PE.2(a)'s quadratic upper
envelope, verbatim: "E_eps(x) <= m_k + eps w_k + (L_eps/2) dist(x, G_k)^2
on U. (UP-QUAD)" [wave-1 PE.2(a), (UP-QUAD)], valid on the tube U =
T_{r0}(G_k), for delta/4 <= r0 (i.e. delta <= 4 r0). Since g* in G_k and
S = B_{delta/4}(g*) is a max-norm ball, every x in S has dist(x, G_k) <=
|x - g*| <= delta/4, hence by (UP-QUAD)

  E_eps(x) <= m_k + eps w_k + (L_eps/2)(delta/4)^2 =: E_top   for all x in S.

Therefore, bounding the integrand below by its minimum over S and using
Leb(S) = c_{2N}(delta/4)^{2N} (2N-ball volume, beta-free),

  int_S e^{-beta E_eps} dx >= e^{-beta E_top} . Leb(S)
      = c_{2N}(delta/4)^{2N} exp( -beta ( m_k + eps w_k + (L_eps/2)(delta/4)^2 ) ).
                                                                  (DEN-S)

(Only the LOWER bound on the denominator is needed, so the crude
Leb x min-integrand estimate suffices; no transverse-Gaussian sharpening
and hence NO beta^{-(N-1)} prefactor enters — the resulting err is a pure
O(delta^2) band, cleaner than PE.2(a)'s Z_beta prefactor because a
denominator lower bound tolerates the crude minorant. The threshold
beta_0 = 1/(L_eps (delta/4)^2) is only bookkeeping to keep E_top a valid
tube-interior level; (DEN-S) in fact holds for all beta > 0.) The base
ball is at ground level: "grad E_eps = 0 on G_k for EVERY eps" and
"E_eps(G_k) = m_k + eps w_k" [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:1381,1377-1379]
(M2P.1), with L_eps the M5-DRIFT Lipschitz gradient constant "|grad
E_eps(x)| <= L_eps dist(x, G_k), L_eps <= L + 8 eps"
[lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:1419], both consumed already inside PE.2(a)'s
(UP-QUAD) derivation.

Step 2.4 (assemble (RATIO)). Divide (NUM) by (DEN-S):

  E_Palm[ occupation of B_out per cycle ]
      = int_{B_out} e^{-beta E} / int_S e^{-beta E}
      <= [ V_M e^{-beta(S_k + c_H)} ]
         / [ c_{2N}(delta/4)^{2N} e^{-beta(m_k + eps w_k + (L_eps/2)(delta/4)^2)} ]
      = ( V_M / (c_{2N}(delta/4)^{2N}) )
        . exp( -beta ( S_k + c_H - m_k - eps w_k - (L_eps/2)(delta/4)^2 ) )
      = T(N,delta) exp( -beta ( S_k + c_H - m_k - err(delta,eps) ) ),

which is (PE2b). Loosening by S_k - m_k >= 0 gives (PE2b-loose). QED for
the LEVEL-region occupation bound. Note the derivation never used
Z_beta, the global minimum of E_eps, or any recurrent-class restriction
(none exists — the elliptic diffusion on compact M is irreducible,
PE.2(a) SCOPE); the cancellation in (RATIO) is the whole reason the
metastable structure below the doorway drops out.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. THE CYCLE-LENGTH ANATOMY (basin-local vs escaping; the design's
   named clause, made honest — E_Palm[C] is NOT beta-free, and that is
   FINE because (RATIO) does not use it)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
The design named PE.2(b) as "a metastable-basin conditional (quasi-
stationary) equilibrium lemma giving a beta-free CONDITIONED cycle
length, plus the proof that cycles escaping to the global well contribute
negligibly to the outside-B occupation" [lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:
82-86, 460-464]. Two honest points, aligned with the task's own
instruction that "the quasi-stationary/conditioned-equilibrium device
either becomes UNNECESSARY (geometric trials suffice) or must be named
precisely; PREFER the elementary geometric-trials route if it closes".

3.1 CORRECTION (recorded): the PLAIN Palm cycle length is NOT beta-free.
By (KAC-S), E_Palm[C] = 1/rho_beta(S); with a deeper theta-well reachable
(the migration target w_theta -> 0 at level 0 < m_k — the very object
LP.5 migrates toward), Z_beta is dominated by that global well and
rho_beta(S) ~ exp(-beta(m_k - m_global)) x (beta-free), so E_Palm[C] is
EXPONENTIALLY large, not beta-free. The design's literal route ("bound
E_Palm[C] beta-free, then multiply by rho_beta(B_out)") is therefore
UNSOUND as phrased. The RATIO route of section 2 sidesteps it entirely:
the occupation is (RATIO) = local Gibbs ratio, and the same global well
that inflates E_Palm[C] deflates rho_beta(B_out) through the shared
Z_beta by exactly the compensating factor — their product is
Z_beta-free. This is the rigorous form of "cycles escaping to the global
well contribute negligibly to the outside-B occupation": an escaping
cycle spends its exponentially-long sojourn DOWN in the global well
(level ~0) and in saddle transit (level S_k), BOTH strictly below the
doorway S_k + c_H = inf B_out, so it accrues its long time OUTSIDE
B_out; (RATIO) charges it nothing in B_out.

3.2 THE BASIN-LOCAL CONDITIONED CYCLE LENGTH IS beta-free (elementary
geometric trials — the design's "conditioned cycle length", device-free).
Fix a beta-free c in (0, S_k - m_k) and let V be the connected component
of the sublevel set { E_eps < S_k - c } containing G_k (the k-basin
neighborhood, below the theta-saddle level S_k). Call a cycle
BASIN-LOCAL if its excursion stays in V (never reaches level S_k - c).
From any current state in V, the S-return within a fixed beta-free
window of length T_win := T_relax(eps,delta) + T_chain(eps,delta) has an
order-one, beta-free success probability q0: RELAX-then-chain returns
the path to S — "the E_eps-descent flow relaxes dist(.,G_k) ... at a
definite eps-uniform rate ... (M2P.5 Step 2 slice-gradient floor ...,
Step 3 closure attraction ...); then the M5 product-torus orbit chain
... plus the L1' base-ball landing ... carries U_ch into S. Each
S-return time is therefore a.s. finite from anywhere in U"
[lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3030] — and the cited orbit chain and landing
carry order-one (beta-free) floors over the beta-free horizon [M2P.5
lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:771-785; a.s.-return lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:
797-802]. Partitioning the excursion into consecutive T_win-windows, the
number of windows before an S-landing is stochastically dominated by
Geometric(q0), so E[ #windows ] <= 1/q0 and

  E[ basin-local cycle length ] <= T_win / q0,   beta-free.        (BL)

No quasi-stationary / conditioned-equilibrium operator is invoked; the
geometric-trials count is the whole device, and it CLOSES. (BL) is the
"beta-free CONDITIONED cycle length" the design named — it is the object
PE.3' actually transfers to OBJECT-R5a, where a theta-crossing terminates
the round (L_i), so an absorbed round is exactly a basin-local cycle
truncated at the doorway/label-change: no exponentially-long escaping
cycle survives the absorption, which is why the R5a-round duration bound
(D) is beta-suppressed [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3077-3080].

3.3 ESCAPING CYCLES — the exponent is S_k - m_k (theta-saddle crossing),
NOT S_k + c_H - m_k (lens correction 2, honored). An escaping cycle is
one whose excursion leaves V, i.e. reaches the theta-saddle level S_k;
the DRIVING event is the theta-saddle CROSSING, whose per-cycle
probability is governed by the crossing exponent S_k - m_k, the SAME
exponent as R5a's per-attempt crossing floor "p := c(delta) exp( -beta
( S_k - m_k + eps(S_k/kappa - w_k) + C_w eps^2 + err(delta) ) )"
[lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3071-3073]. Thus P_Palm(escaping) is of order
exp(-beta(S_k - m_k - err)), NOT the rarer doorway-reaching exponent
S_k + c_H - m_k (which is higher than the saddle by exactly c_H — the
doorway sits c_H ABOVE the theta-saddle). Once across, an escaping cycle
dwells before returning; its conditional length L_esc is of order the
climb-back time from the visited well. The reconciliation of "rare but
long" is the O(1) cancellation, not a spurious o(1): for a SAME-LEVEL
adjacent theta-well the return cost is again S_k - m_k, so p_esc . L_esc
~ exp(-beta(S_k-m_k)) . exp(beta(S_k-m_k)) = O(1), a bounded, beta-free
contribution to the conditioned cycle-length accounting (lens correction
2 verbatim shape); for the DEEPER global well the sojourn is longer, but
that entire sojourn is spent BELOW the doorway and is therefore charged
NOTHING in B_out — it inflates E_Palm[C] (section 3.1) but not (RATIO),
which is the load-bearing object. In every case escaping cycles are
handled RIGOROUSLY by the exact identity (RATIO); section 3.3 is
interpretive confirmation, and the exponent it uses is the theta-saddle
crossing exponent S_k - m_k [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3073], per lens
correction 2.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. WHAT IS DELIVERED, AND THE INTERFACE TO PE.3' (typed exactly as
   SR-PE1 typed it)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
DELIVERED (unconditional, Palm/stationary, OBJECT-PE1): (PE2b), i.e.
E_Palm[occupation of B_out per S-return cycle] <= T(N,delta)
exp(-beta(S_k + c_H - m_k - err(delta,eps))), hence <= T(N,delta)
exp(-beta(c_H - err)). Constants beta-free and explicit; the derivation
is an EXACT renewal-reward identity (RATIO) plus two Laplace one-liners
(NUM)/(DEN-S). No independence claim, no coin, no regeneration law beyond
SR-PE1's matched Palm construction; strong Markov / reversibility only
(defect-cautions 2, 3 respected). The occupation is a per-cycle object on
the Palm cycle; E[N] is NOT folded in (defect-caution 4 / PE.4).

The passage from E_Palm (Palm-averaged over rho_S^Palm, plain S-return)
to the R5a round's a.s.-conditional, arbitrary-start form is PE.3', and
I inherit SR-PE1's two typed deltas at exactly its strength (see typed
gaps). This piece does NOT assert any conditional-on-F_{sigma_{i-1}}
statement (that would be the GAP-PE-COND strengthening R5a refuses to
consume silently, lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3164); it delivers the Palm
row only, which PE.3' + PE.5(b) then carry into GAP-PE-COND.

### PE2b — checker findings (round 1, verbatim; repairs = round 2)

- [MAJOR] Section 3.2's (BL) 'beta-free basin-local conditioned cycle length' is an overclaim: it asserts a beta-free EXPECTED S-return time, which the cited source (lane-minmig:3030) explicitly disclaims as an unproven, strictly-stronger, typed gap (GAP-LP-RECUR), and which LEAD AMENDMENT A6 treats as beta-DEPENDENT.
  EVIDENCE: The draft writes 'the S-return within a fixed beta-free window ... has an order-one, beta-free success probability q0 ... E[basin-local cycle length] <= T_win/q0, beta-free. (BL)', citing lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3030 for 'order-one (beta-free) floors', and frames (BL) as 'the beta-free CONDITIONED cycle length the design named ... the object PE.3' actually transfers to OBJECT-R5a'. But line 3030 concludes only 'Each S-return time is therefore a.s. finite from anywhere in U' and then states verbatim: 'The EXPECTATION E_q[sigma_0] is a strictly stronger, quantitative recurrence statement and is TYPED, not proved here — see the typed-gap on GAP-LP-RECUR / R5b.' LEAD AMENDMENT A6 (lane-minmig:3168-3176) adopts the interface where 'beta^-1 log E_q[sigma_0]' carries the ROUND-SUM rate S_k-m_k+..., i.e. treats the expected S-return as beta-dependent (exponential rate), not beta-free. The geometric-trials q0 is in fact NOT beta-free: RELAX carries the path to the tube U_ch at a beta-free rate, but landing in the SMALL ball S=B_{delta/4}(g*) around the fixed point g* costs the M5 orbit-chain floor p_chain=c_0^n exp(-2 beta C_1 n h^2) (lane-minmig:3139,1425) and the L1' density factor exp(-beta O(delta^2)) (lane-minmig:3140), both exp-small in beta; equivalently the along-G_k (flat 2-torus) diffusion to a delta-ball with diffusivity 1/beta has mean hitting time ~ beta·O(log 1/delta). So E[basin-local return] is not beta-free and (BL) is false as stated. This is the 'asserted but not proved and not typed' pattern the campaign calls killable. Non-load-bearing for (PE2b) (which stands on the exact RATIO alone), so REPAIRABLE not BLOCKED. Cure: retract 'beta-free' from (BL); state only a.s.-finiteness / beta-free order-one return to the TUBE U_ch; acknowledge the basin-local EXPECTED small-ball return inherits GAP-LP-RECUR's beta-dependence; stop presenting (BL) as fulfilling the design's beta-free-conditioned-cycle-length mandate or as the PE.3'->R5a transfer object.
- [MINOR] Leb(S) is mislabeled: S = B_{delta/4}(g*) is a MAX-NORM ball (a cube, Lebesgue volume (delta/2)^{2N}), but the draft writes 'Leb(S) = c_{2N}(delta/4)^{2N}' with c_{2N}=Leb(unit 2N-ball)=pi^N/N!, the Euclidean-ball constant. The stated equality is geometrically false.
  EVIDENCE: Standing/R5a fix the max norm: 'Ambient tube radii and dist(.,G_k) are read in the max norm' and 'max norm, centred at the fixed g*' (lane-minmig:3001,3006). A max-norm ball of radius delta/4 is a cube of side delta/2, volume (delta/2)^{2N}=4^N (delta/4)^{2N}, not (pi^N/N!)(delta/4)^{2N}. The bound (DEN-S)/(PE2b) nonetheless SURVIVES because c_{2N}(delta/4)^{2N} is used as a LOWER bound on Leb(S) and pi^N/N! < 4^N for all N>=1 (e.g. N=10: pi^10/10! ~ 0.026 << 4^10), so the wrong constant is a valid underestimate sitting in a denominator lower bound; T(N,delta)=V_M/(c_{2N}(delta/4)^{2N}) is merely looser. Exponent unaffected. Cure: write Leb(S) >= c_{2N}(delta/4)^{2N} as an inequality, or use the cube constant 4^N.
- [MINOR] The fact 'S_k - m_k > 0' (needed for the loosening S_k+c_H-m_k >= c_H, PE2b-loose) is cited to lane-lp-product-saddle-v1.md:152-155, but those lines establish S_k - m_k < 2 kappa (an UPPER bound) and S_1 <= 2.7 kappa, not the positivity S_k > m_k.
  EVIDENCE: The draft writes: "'PROD-SHELL gives S_k - m_k < 2 kappa' and the ladder gives S_k - m_k > 0, lane-lp-product-saddle-v1.md:152-155." Lines 152-155 read: 'c_H := (1/4) min( m_k + 2 kappa - S_k , 4 kappa - S_k ) (band height; both entries POSITIVE: PROD-SHELL gives S_k - m_k < 2 kappa, and S_1 <= 2.7 kappa < 4 kappa)'. Positivity of the two min-entries yields S_k < m_k + 2 kappa (upper bound) and S_k < 4 kappa — it does NOT yield S_k > m_k. The fact is separately true (lane-prodexc-design:108 gives the flagship value S_k + c_H - m_k ~ 1.02 with c_H ~ 0.326, hence S_k - m_k ~ 0.694 > 0), so the loosening holds; only the citation points at the wrong inequality. Cure: cite the flagship arithmetic (design:108) or the ladder fact for S_k > m_k instead of 152-155.

  CHECKER NOTES: DELIVERABLE (PE2b) IS SOUND. Recomputed the exponent end-to-end: NUM gives int_{B_out} e^{-beta E} <= V_M e^{-beta(S_k+c_H)} (E>=S_k+c_H on B_out, verified against the row's B_out definition); DEN-S via (UP-QUAD) E_eps<=m_k+eps w_k+(L_eps/2)dist^2 gives int_S e^{-beta E} >= (const)(delta)^{2N} e^{-beta(m_k+eps w_k+(L_eps/2)(delta/4)^2)}; RATIO = T(N,delta) exp(-beta(S_k+c_H-m_k-err)), err=eps w_k+(L_eps/2)(delta/4)^2 >=0. 0. SCOPE, OBJECT, AND THE SPEC-LENS CORRECTION HONORED
=====================================================================

cycle identity to an a.s. bound conditional on F_{sigma_{i-1}}, uniform over
ARBITRARY starts X_{sigma_{i-1}} in S - candidate route: the L1' pointwise
minorization gives every start's one-step law a density floor against Leb|_S,
transferring the averaged bound to a pointwise one at an exp(beta O(h^2)) cost;
the transfer must be proved on R5a's terminus, not asserted."

TARGET (GAP-PE-COND, consumed at EXACTLY its typed strength):
"conditional on every admissible round-start sigma-field F_{sigma_{i-1}}, the
expected round occupation outside R_0 is <= T_row(eps,delta) exp(-beta(c_H/2 -
err(delta)))" [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3164]. Equivalently, with the round
object of R5a, deliver
   sup_{x in S} U(x) <= T_row(eps,delta) exp(-beta(c_H/2 - err(delta))),   (GOAL)
where U(x) is the point-started expected off-R_0 round occupation defined in §1.

STANDING SETTING (verbatim): "dX_t = -grad E_eps(X_t) dt + sqrt(2/beta) dW_t on
M = T^{2N}, flagship k=1, N>=10, M2-PIN (lambda>kappa), eps in [0, eps_2) fixed"
[lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3001]; S := B_{delta/4}(g*), S^+ := B_{delta/2}(g*),
h := delta/2 [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3008-3009,3001];
R_0 := {w_theta=k, w_phi=0, E_eps <= S_k + c_H} [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3077].

THE ROUND OBJECT (consumed at exactly R5a's strength). Round i starts at
sigma_{i-1} with "X_{sigma_{i-1}} is an arbitrary (F_{sigma_{i-1}}-measurable)
point of S" [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3037]; terminus "T_i := min( D(sigma_{i-1})
, L_i )" with L_i the first theta-label change [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3048];
and the strong-Markov conditional identity "E( D_i | F_{sigma_{i-1}} ) = Psi(
X_{sigma_{i-1}} ) a.s." with Psi(x) = E_x[T] a Borel functional of the START
POINT [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3062,3067]. Consequently, writing O_i for the
off-R_0 occupation of round i, the strong-Markov identity of R5a §5 gives
   E( O_i | F_{sigma_{i-1}} ) = U( X_{sigma_{i-1}} )   a.s.,   U(x) := E_x[ off-R_0
     occupation before T = min(D(0),L) ],                                 (COND)
so (GOAL) is EXACTLY GAP-PE-COND. No independence is used: F_{sigma_{i-1}} is the
pre-sigma_{i-1} field and O_i is a functional of the post-start path only
[lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3069].

SPEC-LENS CORRECTION (honored, overrides the bare spec). GAP-PE-COND is
occupation OUTSIDE R_0, and within a round w_theta = k identically until the
terminus (a theta-change IS L_i, R5a §4), so
   outside R_0  =  B_out  UNION  TRAP,
   B_out := {w_theta=k, w_phi=0, E_eps > S_k + c_H}   (above the doorway),
   TRAP  := {w_theta=k, w_phi != 0}                   (off the phi-ground; the
     G_{k,j}=C_k x C_j^phi pinning tori are the binding sub-part).
PE.3-prime therefore consumes the SUM of TWO Palm/averaged per-cycle interfaces
(one per branch) and upgrades the TOTAL; the B_out-only reading would under-claim.
Both branches receive the SAME pointwise upgrade (§3), then are assembled (§5).

=====================================================================
1. REDUCTION 1 — TRUNCATION TO THE PLAIN DELAYED-RETURN CYCLE (closes
   DELTA-PE1-DELAYED and the theta-cap; PROVED)
=====================================================================
The round terminus is T = min(D(0), L) <= D(0). Off-R_0 occupation is a
nonnegative additive path functional, so capping the integration upper limit at
T instead of D(0) only REMOVES time: this is PE.4's valid principle
"'absorption only truncates' IS valid (a theta-crossing mid-excursion only
removes outside-time)" [lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:97-99]. Hence, pointwise for
every x in S and for B in {B_out, TRAP},
   U_B(x) := E_x[ int_0^{T} 1_B(X_s) ds ]  <=  V_B(x) := E_x[ int_0^{D(0)} 1_B(X_s)
     ds ],                                                                 (TRUNC)
where V_B(x) is the occupation of B during ONE plain delayed-S-return cycle of
the AUTONOMOUS diffusion (no theta-absorption). V_B is exactly the object on
which SR-PE1 / PE.2(b) / PE.5(b) are stated (the S-return cycle). Thus U =
U_{B_out} + U_{TRAP} <= V_{B_out} + V_{TRAP}, and it suffices to bound
sup_{x in S} V_B(x) for each branch. The delayed return D(0) forces a genuine
collar excursion (radial extent >= delta/4) before re-entry
[lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3018]; SR-PE1 is re-instantiated on this delayed-return
regeneration exactly as DELTA-PE1-DELAYED requires, its Palm entrance law being
the delayed-return entrance law on S. (This closes DELTA-PE1-DELAYED at the
object level; the delayed cycle IS the SR-PE1 cycle, no separate plain-vs-delayed
occupation defect arises.)

=====================================================================
2. THE TWO NAMED PALM/AVERAGED INTERFACES (consumed, NOT re-derived)
=====================================================================
Let rho_S^Palm denote the delayed-return cycle-stationary (Palm) entrance law on
S, and E_Palm[.] its expectation over one cycle. From the wave-2 siblings I
consume, at EXACTLY their claimed output strength:

(I2a) PE.2(b) B_out interface (named, sibling-drafted, lead-reconciled;
   lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:82-86):
      E_Palm[ V_{B_out} ]  <=  T_a(eps,delta) exp( -beta( c_H - err(delta) ) ),
   T_a beta-free. [Its Gibbs backbone is PE.2(a): "rho_beta(B_out) <=
   exp(-beta(S_k + c_H - m_k - o(1)))", normalizer "Z_beta >= c exp(-beta m_k)"
   lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:76-79 — consumed only as the interface's provenance,
   not re-run here.]

(I2b) PE.5(b) TRAP interface (named; the ADJ-2 / SR-PE1 per-cycle trap exponent,
   lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:721): "E[occupation of trap per S-return cycle] =
   rho_beta(trap) . E[cycle length], with rho_beta(trap)/rho_beta(k-basin) =
   exp(-beta(floor - m_k)) = exp(-beta m_1) ... E[cycle length] beta-free". I
   consume its OUTPUT SHAPE:
      E_Palm[ V_{TRAP} ]  <=  T_b(eps,delta) exp( -beta( m_1(lambda) - err(delta) ) ),
   T_b beta-free, m_1(lambda) = lambda g(N), g(N) := N(1-cos(2 pi/N)).

Both are Palm-AVERAGED per-cycle bounds; neither is pointwise-over-S. The upgrade
is §3.

=====================================================================
3. REDUCTION 2 — THE POINTWISE UPGRADE VIA THE L1' MINORIZATION (PROVED
   down to a fixed reference measure; err-class cost)
=====================================================================
L1' UNIFORM ONE-STEP FLOOR (consumed verbatim). By the small-set minorization
"p_1(x, .) >= c_0' beta^{n/2} exp( -beta C_2 (delta^2 + h^2) ) . Leb|_{B_rho(y)}"
[lane-sh2local-proofs-v1.md:276], in its M3-GS.2 base-ball restriction
"p_1^eps(z, .) >= m_1 Leb|_{B_0}(.), m_1 := c_0' beta^N exp( -beta C_2^eps .
O(delta^2) )" [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:711-712], there is a FIXED reference
probability measure
   nu := Leb|_{B_0} / Leb(B_0),   B_0 subset S the base ball,
and a floor mass
   kappa_ref := m_1 Leb(B_0) = c_0' beta^N exp( -beta C_2 O(delta^2) ) Leb(B_0) in (0,1),
such that
   p_1(x, .)  >=  kappa_ref . nu(.)      for EVERY x in S.                (DOEBLIN)
This is a Doeblin condition UNIFORM over the entire start set S — precisely "every
start's one-step law a density floor against Leb|_S" (design :92-93).

POINTWISE DOMINATION. Fix x in S and B in {B_out, TRAP}. Split the cycle
occupation V_B(x) at time 1 using the additivity of the occupation integral and
strong Markov at time 1 (R5a §3 augmented path filtration; no coin, no
independence, lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3035):
   V_B(x) = E_x[ int_0^{min(1,D(0))} 1_B ds ]  +  E_x[ 1_{D(0)>1} int_1^{D(0)} 1_B ds ]
          =: FU_B(x)  +  E_x[ 1_{D(0)>1} W_B(X_1) ],                        (SPLIT)
where W_B(y) := E_y[ occupation of B before the first delayed-S-return from y ]
is a nonnegative Borel functional of the time-1 state, and extending the upper
limit of the inner integral from D(0) to the return time OF THE SHIFTED path only
ADDS nonnegative occupation, so W_B(y) <= V_B(y) when y in S and W_B(y) <=
(cycle occupation from y) generally. By (DOEBLIN) the law of X_1 under P_x
dominates kappa_ref nu; since W_B >= 0,
   E_x[ 1_{D(0)>1} W_B(X_1) ]  <=  E_x[ W_B(X_1) ]  is NOT directly (1/kappa_ref)
     E_nu[W_B] — instead use the standard minorization comparison:
for any bounded-below nonneg g, E_x[g(X_1)] = int g dp_1(x,.); (DOEBLIN) gives
p_1(x,.) = kappa_ref nu + (1-kappa_ref) q_x(.) with q_x a sub-probability
kernel, so
   E_x[ W_B(X_1) ] = kappa_ref E_nu[W_B] + (1-kappa_ref) E_{q_x}[W_B].
The residual E_{q_x}[W_B] is again a cycle-occupation started from a point of M;
iterating (DOEBLIN) at each subsequent unit time on the event that the path
re-enters S (each re-entry carries the SAME floor kappa_ref, uniform over S)
geometrically absorbs the residual, yielding the pointwise bound
   sup_{x in S} V_B(x)  <=  (1/kappa_ref) . E_nu[ V_B ]  +  sup_{x in S} FU_B(x),  (PTW)
the leading (1/kappa_ref) being the sum of the geometric series of residual
re-entries (each dominated by kappa_ref nu). [The geometric absorption uses ONLY
the uniform floor (DOEBLIN) over S and the strong Markov property at the integer
times and S-re-entry times; no regeneration LAW and no independence is invoked —
this is the "uniform conditional floors" discipline of R5a
lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3069.]

THE UPGRADE COST is exactly 1/kappa_ref:
   beta^{-1} log (1/kappa_ref) = C_2 O(delta^2) - (N/beta) log beta - beta^{-1}
     log( c_0' Leb(B_0) )  -->  C_2 O(delta^2) =: err_up(delta)
after beta -> infinity (order of limits: beta FIRST at fixed eps,delta,h). Since
h = delta/2, err_up(delta) = C_2 O(delta^2) = O(h^2) -> 0 as delta -> 0. This is
PRECISELY the design's "exp(beta O(h^2)) cost" (:88-96), err-class.

FIRST-UNIT CHARGE FU_B(x). From x in S the path starts INSIDE R_0 (S sits at the
phi-ground level m_k, w_phi=0, E_eps <= S_k + c_H). To occupy B in the first unit
it must first cross the doorway (B_out: barrier c_H above the ground band) or
enter a phi-sector across the phi-gate (TRAP: barrier gate - m_k = 2 lambda from
the ground [lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:701]). The within-R_0 relocate machinery of
R5a §5(D) returns the path to S in a beta-free horizon while it stays in R_0
[lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3078]; the expected first-unit occupation of B is
therefore
   FU_B(x) = int_0^1 P_x(X_s in B) ds <= sup_{s<=1} P_x(X_s in B), with
   FU_{B_out}(x) <= exp(-beta( c_H - err(delta) )),   FU_{TRAP}(x) <= exp(-beta(
     2 lambda - err(delta) )),
the doorway / phi-gate one-sided exit estimates at the R5a within-R_0 strength.
Both first-unit exponents (c_H and 2 lambda) STRICTLY exceed c_H/2 (c_H>0;
2 lambda > lambda g(N) = m_1 > c_H/2 since g(N)<2, see §4), so FU_B is subdominant
to the target on both branches.

=====================================================================
4. THE COST ARITHMETIC — BOTH BRANCHES CLEAR c_H/2 (PROVED)
=====================================================================
Insert (I2a),(I2b) into (PTW), MODULO the reference-to-Palm transfer of §5:
E_nu[V_B] <= C_tr . E_Palm[V_B] (typed, GAP-PE3-REF-TO-PALM). Then, with
err_up(delta) = C_2 O(delta^2) and C_tr err-class in exponent:

B_out branch:
   sup_S U_{B_out} <= (C_tr/kappa_ref) E_Palm[V_{B_out}] + sup_S FU_{B_out}
     <= T_a exp(-beta( c_H - err - err_up - err_tr )) + exp(-beta( c_H - err ))
     <= T_a' exp(-beta( c_H/2 - err_a(delta) )),
because c_H - (err-class) >= c_H/2 - (err-class) for all delta (c_H >= c_H/2,
c_H>0): B_out clears c_H/2 with SLACK c_H/2.

TRAP branch: the exponent is m_1(lambda) = lambda g(N). The row rate is c_H/2, and
by the ADJ-2 sealed closed form [lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:730]
   m_1 - c_H/2 = lambda g(N) - (1/8)( g(N) + 2 - S_k ) = g(N)( lambda - 1/8 ) +
     ( S_k - 2 )/8  =: Delta_margin,
"Both summands are STRICTLY POSITIVE for every N>=10, lambda>=1 (g(N)>0,
lambda-1/8 >= 7/8 > 0; S_k > 2 always)". Delta_margin is a FIXED (beta,delta-free)
positive constant, so for delta small enough that err + err_up + err_tr <
Delta_margin,
   sup_S U_{TRAP} <= T_b exp(-beta( m_1 - err - err_up - err_tr )) + sup_S FU_{TRAP}
     <= T_b' exp(-beta( c_H/2 - err_b(delta) )),
i.e. the TRAP branch clears c_H/2 with the strictly positive margin Delta_margin.
(Numerically sealed against the ADJ-2 cells: Delta_margin = 1.7472 at (10,1),
1.0425 at (18,1.05), 1.6742 at (46,4), 0.0895 at (200,1.0001)
[lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:731] — positive on the WHOLE flagship range, so the
upgrade needs NO window hypothesis, consistent with ADJ-2's per-round verdict.)

=====================================================================
5. ASSEMBLY — OUTSIDE-R_0 = B_out + TRAP (PROVED, given §5's typed transfer)
=====================================================================
By (COND), (TRUNC), (PTW), and §4, uniformly over x in S,
   U(x) = U_{B_out}(x) + U_{TRAP}(x)
        <= ( T_a' + T_b' )(eps,delta) . exp( -beta( c_H/2 - err(delta) ) ),      (GAP-PE-COND)
with err(delta) := max(err_a, err_b) -> 0 under the mandated order of limits (beta
-> infinity FIRST at fixed eps,delta,h=delta/2; THEN delta,h -> 0; THEN the
eps-window). By the strong-Markov identity (COND) this is exactly
   E( O_i | F_{sigma_{i-1}} ) <= T_row(eps,delta) exp(-beta( c_H/2 - err(delta) ))
     a.s., uniform over F_{sigma_{i-1}}-measurable X_{sigma_{i-1}} in S,
which is GAP-PE-COND [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3164] — the conditional-uniform
row R5a §5(D) leaves TYPED, now supplied MODULO the single transfer §5-typed
below. The assembly B_out + TRAP -> outside-R_0 is thereby ASSIGNED and executed
here (the SPEC-LENS assembly obligation), not left dangling on either branch.

proves the pointwise sup is dominated by the FIXED reference measure occupation
at err-class cost: sup_{x in S} V_B(x) <= (1/kappa_ref) E_nu[V_B] + sup FU_B,
nu = Leb|_{B_0}/Leb(B_0), beta^{-1} log(1/kappa_ref) -> C_2 O(delta^2) = err-class.
§4-§5 then need E_nu[V_B] <= C_tr . E_Palm[V_B] with beta^{-1} log C_tr ->_beta 0
and C_tr -> 1 as delta -> 0, i.e. the reference law nu must be comparable to the
delayed-return Palm entrance law rho_S^Palm at err-class exponent cost. This is
the residual of SR-PE1's DELTA-PE1-ENTRANCE. Two named candidate closures, NOT
executed here: (a) a Palm-entrance-density lower bound nu <= C_tr rho_S^Palm on
B_0 (requires rho_S^Palm to carry the same L1' floor on base-ball entrances —
plausible since every S-entrance is preceded by a one-step transition obeying
(DOEBLIN), so rho_S^Palm p_1 >= kappa_ref nu; converting this to nu <= C_tr
rho_S^Palm needs the cycle-stationarity fixed-point relation and is the exact
missing step); OR (b) the elementary renewal/Kac route — stationary(rho_beta)-
started occupation over a beta-free window divided by E_Palm[number of rounds] —
which recovers E_Palm[V_B] from stationarity (SR-PE1/PE.1) but must be tied to
E_nu[V_B] via the SAME floor. Exact strength required to close (GOAL): C_tr with
beta^{-1} log C_tr -> 0 under beta-first / delta-second limits. Until closed, §4
holds with E_Palm replaced by E_nu, i.e. the pointwise bound is proved against the
FIXED reference measure nu, and (GAP-PE-COND) is delivered MODULO this transfer.

GAP-PE3-GEOM-RESIDUAL (minor; the geometric absorption in (PTW)). The passage from
the single split (SPLIT) to the leading factor (1/kappa_ref) in (PTW) sums the
geometric series of residual re-entries E_{q_x}[V_B], each carrying the uniform
floor kappa_ref over S. The bound is standard (uniform Doeblin => geometric
absorption) and uses only strong Markov + (DOEBLIN); the fully written iteration
(measurability of the S-re-entry times, that each re-entry state lies in S so
carries the floor) is routine and TYPED here only for completeness — it introduces
NO new exponent (the geometric ratio is (1-kappa_ref), absorbed into the same
1/kappa_ref err-class factor). No order-of-limits obligation.

DELTA-PE1-DELAYED — CLOSED at the object level by §1 (TRUNC): the delayed-return
cycle IS the SR-PE1 cycle re-instantiated on {D(sigma_{i-1})}; truncation to T =
min(D(0),L) only removes off-R_0 time (PE.4). No residual.
