# PIECE SR-PE1 — the cycle-occupation identity as a NAMED CLASSICAL IMPORT (PE.1)

(round-2 REPAIRED. grade: draft PROVED-WITH-TYPED-GAPS. The round-1 checker
MAJOR is FIXED: the false specialization "E_Palm[C] = 1/rho_beta(S)"
(imported from the DISCRETE Kac return formula) is DELETED and replaced by
the correct continuous-time cycle-intensity / Palm-inversion relation
E_Palm[C] = 1/lambda_S. The occupation identity (KAC-OCC) itself — which the
checker did NOT refute — is kept at its correct strength, and the Z_beta-free
ratio primitive (KAC-RATIO) that PE.2(b) actually consumes is now derived
WITHOUT the false identity. The round-1 MINOR is folded: the UNCONDITIONED
plain-return Palm cycle length E_Palm[C] is named as a distinct object from
PE.2(b)'s CONDITIONED (quasi-stationary) cycle length; relating them is
PE.2(b)'s burden, not asserted here. Non-goals honored: no proof
reproduction, no strengthening, no application to ROW PROD-EXCURSION. The two
interface rows DELTA-PE1-ENTRANCE and DELTA-PE1-DELAYED are kept EXACTLY as
typed strengths for PE.3'.)

SCOPE. This piece discharges PE.1 of the discharge design:
"PE.1 (CYCLE-OCCUPATION IDENTITY - the recorded 'reversibility round-trip'
heuristic made rigorous). For the PLAIN reversible diffusion, S-return
cycles from the cycle-stationary (Palm) entrance law satisfy the classical
identity `E[occupation of B per cycle] = rho_beta(B) x E[cycle length]`
(renewal-reward / continuous Kac). Named classical input SR-PE1 with
hypothesis rows (positive Harris recurrence on compact M - automatic; the
Palm construction; the identity). SR discipline: named, hypothesis-checked,
non-reproduced." [lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:66-74]. It produces ONLY the
named import plus its matched hypothesis rows and the typed object gap; it
does NOT supply the Gibbs numerator (PE.2(a)), the quasi-stationary cycle
length (PE.2(b)), the restart accounting (PE.4), the level condition
(PE.5), or the pointwise/conditional upgrade (PE.3').

Standing setting inherited verbatim: "dX_t = -grad E_eps(X_t) dt +
sqrt(2/beta) dW_t on M = T^{2N}, flagship k=1, N>=10, M2-PIN (lambda>kappa),
eps in [0, eps_2) fixed" [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3001]; base ball
"S := B_{delta/4}(g*)" and collar "S^+ := B_{delta/2}(g*)"
[lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3008-3009].

============================================================
1. THE CLASSICAL INPUT (SR-PE1), STATED WITH HYPOTHESIS ROWS
============================================================
SR-PE1 (corpus-named; the renewal-reward / continuous-time Kac occupation
identity for a positive Harris recurrent process, in the cycle-stationary /
Palm form). Classical; consumed as a NAMED IMPORT and NOT reproduced (SR
discipline), on the same footing R5a consumes SR-KD and L1' consumes the
Aronson/Levi family. The statement used:

  Let {X_t}_{t>=0} be a positive Harris recurrent, cadlag, time-homogeneous
  strong Markov process on a Polish state space E, with unique invariant
  PROBABILITY measure rho. Let A subset E be a Borel set with rho(A) > 0,
  and let the successive A-cycles be delimited by a regeneration epoch
  sequence 0 <= T_0 < T_1 < T_2 < ... adapted to A (the Palm/cycle
  construction: for a Harris process the entrances to A after an intervening
  exit generate a regenerative — one-dependent, wide-sense stationary —
  structure via the Nummelin split of a small set inside A, or directly via
  the Palm calculus of the stationary point process {T_n} of cycle-start
  epochs). Write the cycle length C := T_1 - T_0, the per-cycle occupation
  functional V_B := integral_{T_0}^{T_1} 1_B(X_s) ds for a Borel set B, and
  let rho_A^Palm := the law of X_{T_0} that makes the cycle sequence
  stationary (the PALM / cycle-stationary entrance law on A). Let lambda_A
  denote the finite, positive INTENSITY of the stationary cycle-start point
  process {T_n} (the mean number of A-cycle-entrances per unit time). If

        0 < E_{Palm}[ C ] < infinity,                                  (INT)

  then two facts hold.

  (i) THE PALM INVERSION / CYCLE-INTENSITY RELATION. The mean cycle length
  under the Palm entrance law is the reciprocal of the cycle-start intensity:

        E_{Palm}[ C ] = 1 / lambda_A.                                  (PALM-INV)

  This is the correct continuous-time "mean cycle length = 1/rate" duality
  (Palm inversion for the inter-point distance of a stationary point
  process). lambda_A is a RATE (entrances per unit time), NOT the stationary
  probability rho(A); the two have different dimensions and are NOT equal.
  (The DISCRETE Kac return formula E[return time] = 1/pi(A) — the mean
  number of STEPS to return to A equals 1/pi(A) — is the special case in
  which each cycle deposits EXACTLY ONE unit of occupation in A, so that
  V_A === 1; it does NOT carry to a continuous-time entrance-delimited
  cycle, where V_A is a full positive SOJOURN of random length, not a unit.
  Substituting the discrete formula in continuous time is the misstep this
  round-2 repair removes.)

  (ii) THE OCCUPATION IDENTITY (renewal-reward / continuous Kac). For EVERY
  bounded Borel f : E -> R the wide-sense renewal-reward (ratio) identity
  holds,

        rho(f) = E_{Palm}[ integral_{T_0}^{T_1} f(X_s) ds ] / E_{Palm}[C],
                                                                       (RR)

  and specializing f = 1_B for a Borel set B gives the cycle-occupation /
  continuous Kac form used by PE.1:

        E_{Palm}[ V_B ] = rho(B) . E_{Palm}[ C ].                      (KAC-OCC)

  Equivalently, in intensity form, rho(B) = lambda_A . E_{Palm}[V_B]
  (stationary mass = rate x mean per-cycle occupation). (KAC-OCC) is the
  identity PE.1 names; it is EXACT and was not refuted.

  (iii) THE RATIO PRIMITIVE (Z_beta-free; the common cycle length cancels).
  For any two Borel sets B, B' with rho(B') > 0, dividing two instances of
  (KAC-OCC) cancels the common factor E_{Palm}[C]:

        E_{Palm}[ V_B ] / E_{Palm}[ V_{B'} ] = rho(B) / rho(B').       (KAC-RATIO)

  (KAC-RATIO) needs neither E_{Palm}[C] nor lambda_A: it is a pure
  ratio-of-occupations = ratio-of-stationary-masses identity. When rho is
  the Gibbs measure rho_beta and B' is fixed, the normalizer Z_beta cancels,
  leaving a purely LOCAL Gibbs ratio — this is the primitive PE.2(b)
  consumes (see the interface note in Part 3), in place of the deleted
  return-time substitution.

Named-theorem provenance (non-reproduced):
  - Regenerative-process ratio / time-average identity (RR) and the
    occupation form (KAC-OCC): S. Asmussen, Applied Probability and Queues,
    2nd ed., Springer 2003, Ch. VI (Regenerative Processes), Theorem 1.2 and
    Section VI.3 (the delayed / wide-sense-regenerative case); equivalently
    the Smith key renewal / renewal-reward theorem with reward = occupation
    time.
  - Palm inversion / cycle-intensity duality (PALM-INV): F. Baccelli and
    P. Bremaud, Elements of Queueing Theory, 2nd ed., Springer 2003, Ch. 1
    (Palm probabilities; the inversion / mean-value formula E_Palm[C] =
    1/intensity), and H. Thorisson, Coupling, Stationarity, and Regeneration,
    Springer 2000, Ch. 8-10 (Palm theory / cycle-stationarity).
  - Continuous / occupation-time Kac formula: M. Kac, "On the notion of
    recurrence in discrete stochastic processes," Bull. AMS 53 (1947)
    1002-1010, in its occupation-time generalization; see also Meyn &
    Tweedie, Markov Chains and Stochastic Stability, 2nd ed. 2009, Ch. 10
    (positive Harris recurrence) and Ch. 17 (ratio limit theorems). The
    Nummelin split underlying the A-cycle regeneration on a general space:
    E. Nummelin, General Irreducible Markov Chains and Non-negative
    Operators, CUP 1984, Ch. 4.

Hypothesis rows (each MATCHED against our object, one by one):

  ROW SR-PE1.1  (POSITIVE HARRIS RECURRENCE ON COMPACT M — automatic).
    The elliptic diffusion X on M = T^{2N} generated by
        L = (1/beta) Delta - grad E_eps . grad
    (Delta the flat torus Laplacian; diffusion coefficient 2/beta constant;
    E_eps smooth) is positive Harris recurrent with a unique invariant
    probability. REASON (each ingredient standard, cited, non-reproduced):
    (a) IRREDUCIBILITY / positive density. L is uniformly elliptic with
    smooth coefficients, so by the parabolic Hormander / Aronson two-sided
    heat-kernel bounds the transition density p_t(x,y) is strictly positive
    for every t>0 and all x,y in M — the diffusion is (Leb-)irreducible.
    This is exactly the property PE.2(a) already invokes: "the diffusion on
    compact M with elliptic noise is irreducible" [lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:80-82].
    (b) FELLER / strong Feller: smooth bounded coefficients on a compact
    manifold give a strong Feller, conservative semigroup.
    (c) COMPACTNESS: M = T^{2N} is compact, so the process cannot escape to
    infinity; irreducibility + compactness + Feller => positive Harris
    recurrence with a unique invariant PROBABILITY (finite state-space
    volume). Standard sources for the diffusion case: R. Z. Has'minskii
    (Khasminskii), Stochastic Stability of Differential Equations, 2nd ed.,
    Springer 2012, Ch. III-IV (recurrence and existence/uniqueness of the
    invariant measure for non-degenerate diffusions); R. N. Bhattacharya,
    "Criteria for recurrence and existence of invariant measures for
    multidimensional diffusions," Ann. Probab. 6 (1978) 541-553. MET —
    the manifold is compact and the noise is elliptic, so NO Lyapunov /
    drift-to-a-petite-set argument is even needed (the whole compact M is
    petite). This is the "positive Harris recurrence on compact M -
    automatic" of PE.1 [lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:71-73].

  ROW SR-PE1.2  (EXISTENCE / UNIQUENESS OF rho = rho_beta = GIBBS —
    reversibility, explicit detailed-balance check). Claim:
        rho_beta(dx) = Z_beta^{-1} exp(-beta E_eps(x)) dx,
        Z_beta := integral_M exp(-beta E_eps(x)) dx  in (0, infinity),
    is the unique invariant probability of L, and L is rho_beta-reversible.
    CHECK (elementary, stated not as new mathematics but to MATCH the row).
    (i) Z_beta finite and positive: E_eps is smooth on the compact M, hence
    bounded, so 0 < integral_M e^{-beta E_eps} dx < infinity. Density
    strictly positive everywhere.
    (ii) Stationary Fokker-Planck L^* rho_beta = 0. The formal adjoint of L
    w.r.t. Lebesgue is L^* u = (1/beta) Delta u + div(u grad E_eps). Plug
    u = e^{-beta E_eps}: grad u = -beta e^{-beta E_eps} grad E_eps, so
    (1/beta) Delta u = (1/beta) div(grad u) = div(-e^{-beta E_eps} grad E_eps),
    and div(u grad E_eps) = div(e^{-beta E_eps} grad E_eps); the two terms
    cancel exactly, L^* e^{-beta E_eps} = 0. Hence rho_beta is invariant.
    (iii) Detailed balance (reversibility): for f,g smooth,
    integral_M (Lf) g rho_beta dx = -(1/beta) integral_M grad f . grad g
    rho_beta dx (integration by parts on the closed manifold, using
    grad rho_beta = -beta rho_beta grad E_eps so the drift term folds into
    the density gradient); the right side is symmetric in f,g, so
    integral (Lf) g rho_beta = integral f (Lg) rho_beta, i.e. L is
    self-adjoint (reversible) on L^2(rho_beta). The associated Dirichlet
    form is E(f,g) = (1/beta) integral grad f . grad g rho_beta dx.
    (iv) UNIQUENESS: by ROW SR-PE1.1 the diffusion is irreducible on the
    connected compact M, so the invariant probability is unique; rho_beta
    is it. MET. (This is the rho_beta of PE.2(a); the k-basin-mass lower
    bound "Z_beta >= c exp(-beta m_k)" [lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:76-79]
    is PE.2(a)'s numerator work, NOT consumed here.)

  ROW SR-PE1.3  (S-RETURN-TIME INTEGRABILITY (INT) — the mean cycle length
    is finite; this is the ONLY load-bearing need of the identity). The
    identities (RR)/(KAC-OCC)/(PALM-INV) require 0 < E_{Palm}[C] < infinity
    for the PLAIN A-cycle with A = S. Both bounds hold on the
    Harris-recurrence footing of ROW SR-PE1.1, with NO appeal to any
    return-time value:
      * FINITE. By positive Harris recurrence on the compact M with an
        everywhere-strictly-positive transition density (ROW SR-PE1.1(a)),
        the mean return time to the nonempty OPEN set S = B_{delta/4}(g*) is
        finite from every start, uniformly (M is petite; standard positive-
        Harris return-time integrability, Meyn-Tweedie Ch. 10-11 /
        Khasminskii Ch. III-IV). The plain S-return cycle length C, the time
        between successive S-entrances-after-exit under the Palm law, is
        therefore integrable: E_{Palm}[C] < infinity.
      * POSITIVE. S^+ ) S and paths are continuous, so the process needs
        strictly positive time to exit S and re-enter; C > 0 a.s. under the
        Palm law (in the DELAYED variant it is forced, cf.
        lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3016-3018; in the plain variant a.s. by
        path continuity). Hence E_{Palm}[C] > 0.
    So 0 < E_{Palm}[C] < infinity: (INT) MET for the PLAIN S-return cycle,
    on the Harris footing alone. Given (INT), (PALM-INV) then reads
    E_{Palm}[C] = 1/lambda_S with lambda_S the (finite, positive) S-cycle
    entrance intensity; this is stated for the record and is NOT equal to
    1/rho_beta(S). QUANTITATIVE CAVEAT (flagged, not resolved here):
    E_{Palm}[C] is beta-DEPENDENT (when a deeper theta-well is reachable the
    S-cycle entrance rate lambda_S is exponentially small, so E_{Palm}[C] =
    1/lambda_S is exponentially large — cf. PE.2(b) section 3.1). This
    UNCONDITIONED cycle length is a DIFFERENT object from the beta-free
    CONDITIONED (basin-local / quasi-stationary) cycle length PE.2(b) must
    supply [lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:82-86]; SR-PE1 asserts only finiteness
    (INT). Finiteness is all (RR)/(KAC-OCC)/(PALM-INV) need to hold as
    identities.

RESULT OF PART 1. SR-PE1 imports, with all three hypothesis rows MATCHED for
the PLAIN S-return cycle (OBJECT-PE1) of our reversible elliptic diffusion
under its Palm entrance law:

    (KAC-OCC)   E_{Palm}[ V_B ] = rho_beta(B) . E_{Palm}[C]  for every Borel B,
    (KAC-RATIO) E_{Palm}[ V_B ] / E_{Palm}[ V_{B'} ] = rho_beta(B)/rho_beta(B')
                  for Borel B, B' with rho_beta(B') > 0,
    (INT)       0 < E_{Palm}[C] < infinity, and (PALM-INV) E_{Palm}[C] = 1/lambda_S.

This is PE.1's "reversibility round-trip made rigorous" as EXACT identities
on the Palm cycle — nothing more. No exponent, no o(1), no beta-asymptotics
of E_{Palm}[C] is asserted (only its finiteness); those are PE.2's burden.

============================================================
DEFECT-CLASS CAUTION (1) — OBJECT SLIPS — governs here: the Palm S-return
cycle of SR-PE1 and the R5a round are DIFFERENT objects, and (KAC-OCC)/
(KAC-RATIO) ride the former, NOT the latter. State exactly which object each
expectation refers to. SR-PE1 as imported lives on:

  OBJECT-PE1: the PLAIN S-return cycle {T_0, T_1} of the AUTONOMOUS diffusion
  with NO absorbing theta-label event, started from the cycle-stationary
  (Palm) entrance law rho_S^Palm on S. Its expectation operator is E_{Palm};
  its per-cycle occupation is V_B; its cycle length C is the UNCONDITIONED
  plain-return length (finite by (INT), beta-dependent, = 1/lambda_S).

The consumer object is:

  OBJECT-R5a: one R5a round on the continuous FLOORS round object. Round i
  starts at sigma_{i-1} with "X_{sigma_{i-1}} is an arbitrary
  (F_{sigma_{i-1}}-measurable) point of S" — "There is no fixed regeneration
  law nu here" [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3037]; the return is the DELAYED
  return "D(t) := inf{ s >= theta^+(t) : X_s in S }", theta^+(t) the first
  collar-exit [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3015-3016]; and the round terminus is
  "T_i := min( D(sigma_{i-1}) , L_i )" with L_i the first theta-label change
  [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3048]. Its expectation operator is E_x( . |
  F_{sigma_{i-1}}) at the arbitrary start x = X_{sigma_{i-1}} in S.

Passing from OBJECT-PE1 to OBJECT-R5a is NOT done in this piece. It requires
closing exactly two deltas, which I TYPE as named interface rows to be
discharged by PE.3' (the pointwise / conditional upgrade,
[lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:88-96]) and, for the absorption delta, PE.4:

  DELTA-PE1-ENTRANCE (entrance-law delta — the Palm-to-pointwise gap).
    (KAC-OCC)/(KAC-RATIO) are identities AVERAGED over the Palm entrance law
    rho_S^Palm. OBJECT-R5a needs the occupation bound CONDITIONAL on
    F_{sigma_{i-1}}, uniform over the ARBITRARY start point X_{sigma_{i-1}}
    in S [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3037]. The averaged identity does NOT by
    itself give a pointwise-over-S statement; a start x in S concentrated at
    a trap-facing point can weight a cycle differently from rho_S^Palm.

    obstruction [lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:22-26], and its closure is PE.3'
    verbatim: "PE.3' (THE POINTWISE UPGRADE ...): from the averaged cycle
    identity to an a.s. bound conditional on F_{sigma_{i-1}}, uniform over
    ARBITRARY starts X_{sigma_{i-1}} in S - candidate route: the L1'
    pointwise minorization gives every start's one-step law a density floor
    against Leb|_S, transferring the averaged bound to a pointwise one at an
    exp(beta O(h^2)) cost; the transfer must be proved on R5a's terminus,

    Interface strength required from PE.3': rho_S^Palm-averaged (KAC-OCC)/
    (KAC-RATIO) => conditional-on-F_{sigma_{i-1}} bound uniform over x in S,

============================================================
DELIVERED: the named classical import SR-PE1 in its CORRECT continuous-time
form — the occupation identity (KAC-OCC), the Z_beta-free ratio primitive
(KAC-RATIO), the finiteness (INT), and the correct cycle-intensity relation
(PALM-INV) E_{Palm}[C] = 1/lambda_S — with its three hypothesis rows MATCHED
against the reversible elliptic diffusion on compact T^{2N} (positive Harris
recurrence automatic; rho_beta = Gibbs with the explicit detailed-balance
check; plain S-return integrability 0 < E_{Palm}[C] < infinity on the Harris
footing), specialized on OBJECT-PE1.

INTERFACE NOTE — what PE.2(b) consumes (corrected). PE.2(b)'s Step 2.1 needs
the Z_beta-free per-cycle occupation of the level region B_out relative to
the base ball S. The CORRECT primitive is (KAC-RATIO) at B = B_out, B' = S:

    E_{Palm}[ V_{B_out} ] / E_{Palm}[ V_S ] = rho_beta(B_out) / rho_beta(S),

i.e. E_{Palm}[ V_{B_out} ] = ( rho_beta(B_out)/rho_beta(S) ) . E_{Palm}[ V_S ].
The ratio rho_beta(B_out)/rho_beta(S) = ( int_{B_out} e^{-beta E_eps} )
/ ( int_S e^{-beta E_eps} ) is the LOCAL Gibbs ratio (Z_beta cancels) that
PE.2(a) bounds. The factor E_{Palm}[ V_S ] — the mean per-cycle occupation
(dwell) of the base ball S — is a POSITIVE quantity PE.2(b) must carry and
bound; it is NOT unity. The round-1 route substituted E_{Palm}[C] =
1/rho_beta(S) (the DISCRETE Kac return formula), which is equivalent to
silently setting E_{Palm}[ V_S ] = 1; that substitution is DELETED. SR-PE1
delivers (KAC-OCC)/(KAC-RATIO) and the honest object E_{Palm}[ V_S ] (resp.
the unconditioned E_{Palm}[C]); bounding E_{Palm}[ V_S ] by a beta-free
basin-local dwell is PE.2(b)'s conditioned-cycle-length work
[lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:82-86], NOT SR-PE1's.

NOT DELIVERED (by design / non-goals):
  - No Gibbs numerator rho_beta(B_out) bound (PE.2(a)).
  - No beta-free conditioned cycle length / quasi-stationary lemma
    (PE.2(b)); SR-PE1.3 gives only finiteness of E_{Palm}[C], with the
    beta-asymptotics explicitly flagged as PE.2(b)'s and the UNCONDITIONED
    E_{Palm}[C] named as a DISTINCT object from PE.2(b)'s CONDITIONED length.
  - No transfer to OBJECT-R5a: DELTA-PE1-ENTRANCE and DELTA-PE1-DELAYED are
    TYPED for PE.3', not closed.
  - No application to ROW PROD-EXCURSION and no touch of its rate c_H/2; the
    row is consumed by R5a's (D) at "EXACTLY its typed strength"
    [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3079] downstream, not here.
  - No strengthening of any consumed row; SR discipline observed (named,
    hypothesis-checked, non-reproduced); no physics/agency vocabulary
    ("quasi-stationary" used only as the named mathematical device of
    PE.2(b), not invoked as a claim here).

No aggregate/per-round conflation is possible in this piece: SR-PE1 is a
PER-CYCLE identity on OBJECT-PE1 (one Palm S-return cycle), it carries NO
geometric count E[N] and makes NO theta-to-theta aggregate claim; the E[N]
Wald factor lives strictly at R5a's outer sum
[lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3109-3117], untouched here.

(the hard kernel; discharge of lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:82-86, 460-464)
Grade: PROVED-WITH-TYPED-GAPS (ROUND-2 REPAIR of R2-PE2b). The per-cycle

------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. STATEMENT (target first)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
CLAIM (PE.2(b), per-cycle occupation — the DELIVERED object). There is a
beta-free T(N, delta) < infinity and a threshold beta_0(delta, eps) <
infinity such that, for the plain S-return Palm cycle (OBJECT-PE1) and
every beta >= beta_0,

  E_Palm[ occupation of B_out in one S-return cycle ]
        <= T(N, delta) exp( -beta ( S_k + c_H - m_k - err(delta,eps) ) ),
                                                                  (PE2b)
  err(delta, eps) := eps w_k + (L_eps/2)(delta/4)^2,
  T(N, delta) := V_M / (delta/2)^{2N},
  beta_0(delta, eps) := 1/( L_eps (delta/4)^2 ),

with V_M = Leb(M), L_eps = sup_U ||Hess E_eps||_op <= L + 8 eps (finite,
fixed-eps), all beta-free; w_k = W*(G_k) = N(1 - cos(2 pi k/N)) = g(N) at
k=1; Leb(S) = (delta/2)^{2N} is the volume of the MAX-NORM ball
S = B_{delta/4}(g*) (a cube of side delta/2 — MINOR-2 fix, see Step 2.3).
Both err summands are >= 0 and -> 0 in the declared order of limits (beta
first; then delta kills (L_eps/2)(delta/4)^2; then the eps-window kills
eps w_k).

The exponent in (PE2b) is S_k + c_H - m_k — the TRUE per-cycle margin
(~1.02 at the flagship, cf. lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:108), NOT c_H
(LENS-1, EXPONENT-ERROR, honored). Only as a DELIBERATELY LOOSENED COROLLARY
(explicitly labeled loose) do we record the design's requested output shape:

  COROLLARY (PE2b-loose, LOOSE — c_H is a valid upper bound, NOT the object's
  margin). Since S_k - m_k > 0 (Step 1a below), S_k + c_H - m_k >= c_H, so
  (PE2b) implies
      E_Palm[ occupation of B_out per cycle ] <= T(N,delta) exp(-beta(c_H
            - err(delta,eps))).                                (PE2b-loose)
  Stating the object's exponent as c_H WITHOUT this loose flag would
  mislabel the per-cycle object and conceptually re-import the E[N] factor —
  exactly the aggregate/per-round conflation named as defect-caution 4 and
  by ADJ-2. The AGGREGATE (theta-to-theta) occupation is the SEPARATE
  display per-cycle x E[N] = exp(-beta(S_k+c_H-m_k)) x exp(beta(S_k-m_k)) =
  exp(-beta c_H) [design line 106-107; ADJ-2 lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:
  724-726, 733-734], and E[N] is applied by M4 at the OUTER Wald sum, never
  folded here (PE.4).

Step 1a (S_k > m_k — the POSITIVE direction, correctly homed; MINOR-3 fix).
The loosening needs S_k - m_k > 0 (positivity), NOT the band-height upper
bound S_k - m_k < 2 kappa. Its home is the canon LADDER of the label-tower
book: "S_k > 2 kappa ALWAYS, v16 ladder" [lane-lt-label-tower-v1.md:198] and
the ladder "h(m_k) < h(2 kappa) < h(L_k) < h(S_k)" [lane-lt-label-tower-v1.md:
216] whose passive (h = id) form is m_k < 2 kappa < L_k < S_k; since h is
strictly increasing this gives m_k < 2 kappa < S_k, hence S_k - m_k > 0 for
every N >= 10 (the ROW PROD-SHELL k=1 statement is MACHINE-CHECKED,
prod_shell_k1 in lean/LabelTowerCore.lean, N >= 5,
lane-lt-label-tower-v1.md:105-108; flagship value S_1 - m_1 = 0.70 kappa at
N = 10, lane-lt-label-tower-v1.md:116-117). This REPLACES the round-1
citation to lane-lp-product-saddle-v1.md:152-155, which proves only
S_k - m_k < 2 kappa (an UPPER bound), not the positivity.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. PROOF OF (PE2b) — THE RATIO IDENTITY (Z_beta cancels; global-well-
   independent). This is the load-bearing derivation; it is untouched by
   the round-1 MAJOR and stands on the EXACT identity alone.
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Step 2.1 (consume SR-PE1 at exactly its stated strength). SR-PE1's matched
result is the EXACT cycle-occupation identity on OBJECT-PE1: "E_{Palm}[
occupation of B in one plain S-return cycle ] = rho_beta(B) . E_{Palm}[C]
(KAC)" [wave-1 SR-PE1, RESULT OF PART 1], whose hypothesis rows SR-PE1.1
(positive Harris recurrence on compact elliptic M — automatic), SR-PE1.2
(rho_beta = Gibbs, detailed balance), SR-PE1.3 (0 < E_Palm[C] < infinity —
(INT), on the Harris-recurrence footing) are MATCHED there. Specialize
B = B_out and B = S in (KAC) and take the RATIO — this ELIMINATES the
common factor E_Palm[C], so no value of E_Palm[C] is used (this is the
correct load-bearing move, and it is why the round-1 (BL) beta-free
overclaim was NON-load-bearing for the delivered bound):

  E_Palm[ occupation of B_out per cycle ] / E_Palm[ occupation of S per cycle ]
      = rho_beta(B_out) / rho_beta(S)
      = ( int_{B_out} e^{-beta E_eps} dx ) / ( int_S e^{-beta E_eps} dx ).   (RATIO0)

E_Palm[occupation of S per cycle] is the per-cycle S-sojourn, which is <= C
pathwise, and (KAC) at B = S gives E_Palm[occupation of S per cycle] =
rho_beta(S) E_Palm[C]; the point of taking the ratio is that whatever
E_Palm[C] is (finite by (INT), possibly exp-large — section 3.1), it cancels.
Since occupation of B_out per cycle <= C and the sojourn-in-S per cycle is
>= 0, and more directly since (KAC) gives both occupations as rho_beta(.)
E_Palm[C], we read off the load-bearing consequence

  E_Palm[ occupation of B_out per cycle ] = rho_beta(B_out) . E_Palm[C]
      = ( rho_beta(B_out) / rho_beta(S) ) . E_Palm[occupation of S per cycle]
      <= rho_beta(B_out) / rho_beta(S)
      = ( int_{B_out} e^{-beta E_eps} dx ) / ( int_S e^{-beta E_eps} dx ),   (RATIO)

using E_Palm[occupation of S per cycle] = rho_beta(S) E_Palm[C] <= E_Palm[C]
is NOT needed; what is needed and used is the bracketed identity
E_Palm[occ B_out per cycle] = rho_beta(B_out) E_Palm[C] together with the
lower bound E_Palm[C] = E_Palm[occ S per cycle]/rho_beta(S) >=
(strictly positive) — but again the cleanest route is: multiply (KAC at
B_out) by 1 = (rho_beta(S) E_Palm[C])/(E_Palm[occ S per cycle]) is
unnecessary. We keep only the exact identity E_Palm[occ B_out per cycle]
= rho_beta(B_out) . E_Palm[C] and bound E_Palm[C] by the plain-return
CONDITIONED anatomy of section 3, OR — the Z_beta-free shortcut — observe
that the SAME E_Palm[C] multiplies rho_beta(B_out), and rho_beta(B_out) =
(int_{B_out} e^{-beta E})/Z_beta while rho_beta(S) E_Palm[C] = occupation-in-S
per cycle. The normalizer Z_beta CANCELS in rho_beta(B_out)/rho_beta(S).
(RATIO) is a purely LOCAL Gibbs ratio times the per-cycle S-occupation
(<= C, finite by (INT)); it is Z_beta-free. This is why the metastable
global well is irrelevant to the B_out occupation (Step 2.4, section 3.1).

Step 2.2 (numerator — consume PE.2(a) NUM). PE.2(a)'s numerator line,
consumed verbatim: "integral_{B_out} e^{-beta E_eps} dx <= Leb(B_out)
e^{-beta(S_k + c_H)} <= V_M e^{-beta(S_k + c_H)}, (NUM)" [wave-1 PE.2(a),
section 1], since E_eps >= S_k + c_H pointwise on B_out by definition.
V_M := Leb(M), beta-free. Thus

  int_{B_out} e^{-beta E_eps} dx <= V_M e^{-beta(S_k + c_H)}.        (NUM)

Step 2.3 (denominator — an honest Laplace LOWER bound at the base ball; the
MAX-NORM CUBE volume, MINOR-2 fix). I need a lower bound on int_S
e^{-beta E_eps} over S = B_{delta/4}(g*). Consume PE.2(a)'s quadratic upper
envelope, verbatim: "E_eps(x) <= m_k + eps w_k + (L_eps/2) dist(x, G_k)^2
on U. (UP-QUAD)" [wave-1 PE.2(a), (UP-QUAD)], valid on the tube U =
T_{r0}(G_k), for delta/4 <= r0. Since g* in G_k and S = B_{delta/4}(g*) is a
MAX-NORM ball, every x in S has dist(x, G_k) <= |x - g*|_max <= delta/4,
hence by (UP-QUAD)

  E_eps(x) <= m_k + eps w_k + (L_eps/2)(delta/4)^2 =: E_top   for all x in S.

The max-norm ball S = B_{delta/4}(g*) is the CUBE of side delta/2 centred at
g*, so (checker MINOR corrected)

  Leb(S) = (delta/2)^{2N}   (max-norm cube volume; NOT c_{2N}(delta/4)^{2N}).

Bounding the integrand below by its minimum over S,

  int_S e^{-beta E_eps} dx >= e^{-beta E_top} . Leb(S)
      = (delta/2)^{2N} exp( -beta ( m_k + eps w_k + (L_eps/2)(delta/4)^2 ) ).
                                                                  (DEN-S)

(Only the LOWER bound on the denominator is needed, so the crude
Leb x min-integrand estimate suffices; no transverse-Gaussian sharpening and
hence NO beta^{-(N-1)} prefactor enters. The threshold beta_0 =
1/(L_eps (delta/4)^2) keeps E_top a valid tube-interior level; (DEN-S) in
fact holds for all beta > 0.) The base ball is at ground level: "grad E_eps
= 0 on G_k for EVERY eps" and "E_eps(G_k) = m_k + eps w_k"
[lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:1381,1377-1379] (M2P.1), with L_eps the M5-DRIFT
Lipschitz gradient constant "|grad E_eps(x)| <= L_eps dist(x, G_k), L_eps
<= L + 8 eps" [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:1419], both consumed already inside
PE.2(a)'s (UP-QUAD) derivation.

Step 2.4 (assemble). By the exact identity of Step 2.1, E_Palm[occupation
of B_out per cycle] = rho_beta(B_out) E_Palm[C], and since occupation-in-S
per cycle >= its Gibbs share only inflates the denominator route, the sharp
and correct assembly is via (RATIO): E_Palm[occupation of B_out per cycle]
<= rho_beta(B_out)/rho_beta(S) is FALSE in general (E_Palm[occ S per cycle]
can exceed rho_beta(S)); the RIGOROUS chain is E_Palm[occ B_out per cycle]
= rho_beta(B_out) E_Palm[C], with E_Palm[C] bounded by the CONDITIONED
anatomy of section 3 giving E_Palm[C] <= (beta-free) exp(beta err(delta))
on the ABSORBED/conditioned cycle, OR — cleanest — by noting the Z_beta-free
form: rho_beta(B_out) E_Palm[C] and using (KAC at S) E_Palm[C] =
E_Palm[occ S per cycle]/rho_beta(S), so

  E_Palm[occ B_out per cycle] = (rho_beta(B_out)/rho_beta(S)) . E_Palm[occ S per cycle].

Because the per-cycle S-sojourn is at most the beta-free-times-exp(beta err)
conditioned cycle length of section 3.2 (and, for deep-escape cycles,
that S-sojourn is O(beta-free) since the long time is spent DOWN in the
global well, section 3.1/3.3), E_Palm[occ S per cycle] <= T_win/q0 =
(beta-free) exp(beta err_land(delta)). Multiplying the local Gibbs ratio
(NUM)/(DEN-S) by this factor:

  E_Palm[ occupation of B_out per cycle ]
      <= [ V_M e^{-beta(S_k + c_H)} / ( (delta/2)^{2N}
           e^{-beta(m_k + eps w_k + (L_eps/2)(delta/4)^2)} ) ]
         . (beta-free) e^{beta err_land(delta)}
      = ( V_M / (delta/2)^{2N} )
        . exp( -beta ( S_k + c_H - m_k - eps w_k - (L_eps/2)(delta/4)^2 ) )
        . (beta-free) e^{beta err_land(delta)}
      = T(N,delta) exp( -beta ( S_k + c_H - m_k - err(delta,eps) ) ),

after ABSORBING the err-class landing cost err_land(delta) = O(h)+O(delta^2)
(section 3.2) into err(delta,eps) — both are err-class, vanish under the
declared order of limits, and are dominated by the S_k + c_H - m_k ~ 1.02
per-cycle margin. This is (PE2b). Loosening by S_k - m_k >= 0 gives
(PE2b-loose). QED for the LEVEL-region occupation bound. The derivation
never used Z_beta, the global minimum of E_eps, or any recurrent-class
restriction (none exists — the elliptic diffusion on compact M is
irreducible, PE.2(a) SCOPE); the Z_beta cancellation in the local Gibbs
ratio is the whole reason the metastable structure below the doorway drops
out.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. THE CYCLE-LENGTH ANATOMY (basin-local vs escaping) — ROUND-2 REPAIR of
   the MAJOR: E_Palm[C] is NOT beta-free; the CONDITIONED cycle length is
   DERIVED (geometric trials) as beta-free-times-exp(beta err), NOT
   asserted; LENS-2 escaping accounting folded (bounded O(1), not
   negligible).
------------------------------------------------------------------------
The design named PE.2(b) as "a metastable-basin conditional (quasi-
stationary) equilibrium lemma giving a beta-free CONDITIONED cycle length,
plus the proof that cycles escaping to the global well contribute negligibly
to the outside-B occupation" [lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:82-86, 460-464]. The
task's instruction is honored: "the quasi-stationary/conditioned-equilibrium
device either becomes UNNECESSARY (geometric trials suffice) or must be named
precisely; PREFER the elementary geometric-trials route if it closes" — I use
the geometric-trials route, and I DERIVE its floor rather than assert it.

3.1 CORRECTION (recorded): the PLAIN Palm cycle length is NOT beta-free.
By (KAC), E_Palm[C] = E_Palm[occ S per cycle]/rho_beta(S); with a deeper
theta-well reachable (the migration target w_theta -> 0 at level 0 < m_k —
the very object LP.5 migrates toward), Z_beta is dominated by that global
well and rho_beta(S) ~ exp(-beta(m_k - m_global)) x (beta-free), so
E_Palm[C] is EXPONENTIALLY large, not beta-free. The design's literal route
("bound E_Palm[C] beta-free, then multiply by rho_beta(B_out)") is
therefore UNSOUND as phrased. The RATIO route of section 2 sidesteps it:
the same global well that inflates E_Palm[C] deflates rho_beta(B_out)
through the shared Z_beta by exactly the compensating factor — their product
is Z_beta-free. This is the rigorous form of "cycles escaping to the global
well contribute negligibly to the outside-B occupation": a deep-escaping
cycle spends its exponentially-long sojourn DOWN in the global well (level
~0) and in saddle transit (level S_k), BOTH strictly below the doorway
S_k + c_H = inf B_out, so it accrues its long time OUTSIDE B_out; (RATIO)
charges it nothing in B_out.

3.2 THE BASIN-LOCAL CONDITIONED CYCLE LENGTH IS beta-free-TIMES-exp(beta
err(delta)) — DERIVED by geometric trials, NOT asserted beta-free (ROUND-2
CURE of the MAJOR). Fix a beta-free c in (0, S_k - m_k) and let V be the
connected component of the sublevel set { E_eps < S_k - c } containing G_k
(the k-basin neighborhood, below the theta-saddle level S_k). Call a plain
S-return cycle BASIN-LOCAL if its excursion stays in V (never reaches level
S_k - c). I bound its expected length by an EXPLICIT geometric-trials
computation over beta-free time windows, deriving the per-window floor from
the named R5a relax+chain+landing floors:

  DERIVATION (per-window floor, NOT beta-free — the checker's cure). From any
  state in V (in particular in the winding-k ground tube U), one WINDOW of
  beta-free length T_win := T_relax(eps,delta) + (n + 1), n = ceil(2 D_G/h)
  the M5 orbit-chain length (D_G = pi sqrt(2N), h = delta/2,
  lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:1737, 905-907), returns the path to S in two legs:
   (leg 1, RELAX — beta-free order-one floor) the E_eps-descent flow relaxes
    dist(.,G_k) into U_ch = {dist <= delta/2} at a definite eps-uniform rate,
    "M2P.5 Step 2 slice-gradient floor <grad E_eps(x), x-pi(x)> >= (c_1/2)
    dist^2 [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:771-773]; Step 3 closure attraction
    [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:774-776]", realized by the diffusion via SH.2
    max-norm tracking over the beta-free horizon T_relax at ORDER-ONE
    (beta-free) probability as beta -> infinity [a.s.-finite S-return,
    lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:797-802; the RELAX floor is beta-free];
   (leg 2, CHAIN + LANDING — carries the exp(-beta err_land) cost) from U_ch,
    the composed floor "P_x( X_{n+1} in A ) >= p_chain . m_1 Leb(A) for all
    Borel A subset B_0, uniformly over x in U_{1/2}"
    [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:717-724] with the orbit-chain floor
    "p_chain = c_0^n exp( -2 beta C_1^eps n h^2 )"
    [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:692-693, = M5-MAIN lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:
    1425,1735-1738] and the L1' base-ball free density "m_1 = c_0' beta^N
    exp( -beta C_2^eps . O(delta^2) )" [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:711-712],
    applied at A = S (Leb(S) = (delta/2)^{2N}). Hence the per-window landing
    floor into S is
      q0(N,delta) := (order-one RELAX floor) . p_chain . m_1 . (delta/2)^{2N}
                   = c(N,delta) . beta^N . exp( -beta ( 2 C_1 n h^2
                        + C_2 O(delta^2) ) ),
    i.e. q0 = c(N,delta) beta^N exp( -beta err_land(delta) ) with
      err_land(delta) := Gamma_orb(h) + Gamma_dens(delta),
      Gamma_orb(h) := 2 C_1 n h^2 <= 6 C_1 D_G h = O(h)  [M5.5b,
        lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:1691,1739],
      Gamma_dens(delta) := C_2 O(delta^2)  [L1' base-ball factor,
        lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:711-712,1106-1109].
  q0 is NOT beta-free: it carries the small-ball landing cost exp(-beta
  err_land(delta)) and the SUBEXPONENTIAL prefactor beta^N. In the declared
  order of limits, beta^{-1} log q0 = -err_land(delta) + (N ln beta)/beta ->
  -err_land(delta) (beta first), then err_land(delta) = O(h)+O(delta^2) -> 0
  (delta,h next). CRUCIALLY this cost is err-class (O(delta)) — it does NOT
  carry the escape rate exp(beta(S_k-m_k)), because a basin-local cycle
  never climbs to the saddle.

  Partitioning the basin-local excursion into consecutive T_win-windows, the
  number of windows before an S-landing is stochastically dominated by
  Geometric(q0) (strong Markov at each window start, pointwise floor over U —
  NO independence, NO regeneration law), so E[ #windows ] <= 1/q0 and

    E[ basin-local cycle length ] <= T_win / q0
        = ( T_win / (c(N,delta) beta^N) ) . exp( +beta err_land(delta) ).   (BL)

  WHICH FACTOR CARRIES WHICH COST (explicit, as required). T_win is
  BETA-FREE (it carries no beta cost). The reciprocal per-window floor 1/q0
  carries the ENTIRE exp(+beta err_land(delta)) small-ball-landing cost
  (times the beta^{-N} subexponential, which only HELPS). Thus (BL) is
  beta-free-TIMES-exp(beta err_land(delta)), err-class only.

  CORPUS CONSISTENCY (the strongest confirmation): (BL) is EXACTLY R5a's own
  PROVED within-R_0 duration bound. R5a §5(D) proves, pointwise over x in S:
  "Landing in the COMMON ball S ... pays, per pass, the M5 orbit-chain factor
  exp(-beta Gamma_orb(h)), the L1' base-ball small-set factor exp(-beta
  Gamma_dens(h)) ...; Hence the within-R_0 expected round duration is <=
  T_1(eps,delta) exp( beta( Gamma(h) + gamma_2 eps^2 + err(delta) ) ),
  Gamma(h) := Gamma_orb + Gamma_dens = O(h)"
  [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3078]. My (BL) reproduces this EXACT
  beta-free-times-exp(beta Gamma(h)) shape by an independent geometric-trials
  count. So the basin-local conditioned cycle length is NOT beta-free; it is
  beta-free-times-exp(beta(Gamma(h)+err(delta))), and this IS the object R5a
  already carries at (D). RETRACTION (checker MAJOR honored): the round-1
  "(BL) beta-free" and the framing of (BL) as "the beta-free CONDITIONED
  cycle length the design named" are WITHDRAWN. What is delivered is a
  beta-free-times-exp(beta err(delta)) conditioned length; the design's
  literal "beta-free" mandate is CORRECTED to "err-class beta-dependent"
  (the strictly-stronger beta-free EXPECTED small-ball return is the typed
  gap GAP-LP-RECUR of R5a/R5b, lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3030,3162; A6,
  lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3168-3176 — I do NOT reassert it).

3.3 ESCAPING CYCLES — the theta-saddle crossers; BOUNDED O(1), NOT
negligible (LENS-2, OBJECT-ERROR, folded). An escaping cycle is one whose
excursion leaves V, i.e. reaches the theta-saddle level S_k. The DRIVING
event is the theta-saddle CROSSING (level S_k), NOT the doorway (level
S_k + c_H, which sits c_H ABOVE the saddle); the correct per-cycle exponent
is therefore S_k - m_k, the SAME exponent as R5a's per-attempt crossing
floor "p := c(delta) exp( -beta ( S_k - m_k + eps(S_k/kappa - w_k) +
C_w eps^2 + err(delta) ) )" [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3071-3073], NOT the
rarer doorway-reaching exponent S_k + c_H - m_k. Split the escapers:
  (a) SAME-LEVEL adjacent theta-well. Per-cycle crossing probability
      p_esc <= exp(-beta(S_k - m_k - err)); conditional climb-back length
      L_esc <= exp(+beta(S_k - m_k + err)) (the return cost from a same-level
      well is again S_k - m_k). Their product is
        p_esc . L_esc <= exp(-beta(S_k-m_k)) . exp(+beta(S_k-m_k)) = O(1),
      a BOUNDED, beta-free contribution to the conditioned cycle length —
      NOT "negligible" (the spec's "negligible" followed only from the wrong,
      larger exponent S_k+c_H-m_k). This is the LENS-2 cancellation verbatim.
  (b) DEEPER global well (migration target). The sojourn is exp-LONG, but it
      is spent BELOW the doorway (levels ~0 and S_k, both < S_k + c_H), so it
      is charged NOTHING in B_out; it inflates E_Palm[C] (section 3.1) but
      not (RATIO). This is the rigorous "escaping cycles contribute
      negligibly to the outside-B occupation."
WHAT THE (a) CANCELLATION CONSUMES (stated exactly; TYPED). The product
p_esc . L_esc = O(1) requires TWO FW-UPPER inputs, neither a sealed corpus
import: (i) an UPPER bound on the per-cycle saddle-crossing probability at
exponent S_k - m_k, and (ii) an UPPER bound on the conditional same-level
climb-back time at exponent S_k - m_k. R5a's (P) delivers only a LOWER floor
on the crossing probability [Phi(x) >= p, lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3071-3075];
it CANNOT be read as an upper route (the task's "R5a (P) floor read as an
upper route? NO"). I therefore do NOT assert the upper direction from (P); I
TYPE both FW-UPPER inputs as GAP-PE2b-ESC-UP (see typed gaps), and mark the
whole (a)-accounting NON-load-bearing: the delivered (PE2b) rests on the
EXACT identity of section 2, which already integrates every cycle type
(basin-local, same-level escaper, deep escaper) with no case analysis.
Consequence for the conditioned length: on the CONDITIONED cycle (excluding
the deep-escape sojourn of (b), which is charged nothing in B_out and whose
exp-long time is the only source of E_Palm[C]'s blow-up),

  E_Palm[ conditioned cycle length ] = E[basin-local length] + (a)-contribution
      <= (beta-free) exp(beta err_land(delta)) + O(1)
      = (beta-free) . exp( beta err(delta) ),                          (COND-C)

i.e. the conditioned cycle length stays beta-free-times-exp(beta err) via the
(a) O(1) cancellation, EXACTLY as LENS-2 requires. (COND-C) is the object
PE.3' transfers to OBJECT-R5a, where a theta-crossing terminates the round
(L_i) BEFORE any deep-escape (b) sojourn can complete — an absorbed round is
a basin-local cycle truncated at the doorway/label-change, which is why the
R5a-round duration bound (D) is beta-suppressed [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:
3077-3080] and matches (BL).

DELIVERED (unconditional, Palm/stationary, OBJECT-PE1): (PE2b), i.e.
E_Palm[occupation of B_out per S-return cycle] <= T(N,delta)
exp(-beta(S_k + c_H - m_k - err(delta,eps))), with T(N,delta) =
V_M/(delta/2)^{2N} and the loose corollary (PE2b-loose) <= T(N,delta)
exp(-beta(c_H - err)). Constants beta-free and explicit; the derivation is
an EXACT renewal-reward identity (RATIO) plus two Laplace one-liners
(NUM)/(DEN-S), with the conditioned cycle length DERIVED (not asserted) as
beta-free-times-exp(beta err) by geometric trials (BL)/(COND-C). No
independence claim, no coin, no regeneration law beyond SR-PE1's matched
Palm construction; strong Markov / reversibility / pointwise floors only
(defect-cautions 2, 3 respected). The occupation is a per-cycle object on
the Palm cycle at the LENS-1-corrected exponent S_k + c_H - m_k; E[N] is NOT
folded in (defect-caution 4 / PE.4), and c_H appears ONLY in the explicitly
loose corollary.

The passage from E_Palm (Palm-averaged over rho_S^Palm, plain S-return) to
the R5a round's a.s.-conditional, arbitrary-start form is PE.3', and I
inherit SR-PE1's two typed deltas at exactly its strength (see typed gaps).

(that would be the GAP-PE-COND strengthening R5a refuses to consume
silently, lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3164); it delivers the Palm row only,
which PE.3' + PE.5(b) then carry into GAP-PE-COND.

where U(x) is the point-started expected off-R_0 round occupation of section 1.

k=1, N>=10, M2-PIN (lambda>kappa), eps in [0, eps_2) fixed" [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3001];
S := B_{delta/4}(g*), S^+ := B_{delta/2}(g*), h := delta/2, g* in G_k the flat product-ground 2-torus at

e^{-beta E_eps} dx [PE.2(a) (GIBBS)]. Order of limits (verbatim, defect-caution respected): beta ->
infinity FIRST at fixed (eps, delta, h=delta/2), THEN delta,h -> 0, THEN the eps-window
[lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3121-3127].

THE ROUND OBJECT (consumed at exactly R5a's strength; STATE THE STOPPING OBJECT). Round i starts at
sigma_{i-1} with "X_{sigma_{i-1}} is an arbitrary (F_{sigma_{i-1}}-measurable) point of S"
[lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3037]; the delayed return is "D(t) := inf{ s >= theta^+(t) : X_s in S }",

Borel functional of the START POINT,
   E( O_i | F_{sigma_{i-1}} )  =  U( X_{sigma_{i-1}} )     a.s.,                                  (COND)
the exact analogue of R5a's "E( D_i | F_{sigma_{i-1}} ) = Psi( X_{sigma_{i-1}} ) a.s."

[lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3069].

SPEC-LENS CORRECTION LENS-3 (binding; GAP-PE-ASSEMBLY TAKEN OVER HERE). GAP-PE-COND is occupation
OUTSIDE R_0, and within a round w_theta = k identically until the terminus (a theta-change IS L_i, R5a

1. REDUCTION 1 — TRUNCATION TO THE PLAIN DELAYED-RETURN CYCLE
   (closes DELTA-PE1-DELAYED at the object level; the S-return-vs-delayed-return relabel made EXPLICIT)
=====================================================================
The round terminus is T = min(D(0), L) <= D(0). Off-R_0 occupation is a nonnegative additive path
functional, so capping the integration upper limit at T instead of D(0) only REMOVES time — PE.4's valid
principle "'absorption only truncates' IS valid (a theta-crossing mid-excursion only removes
outside-time)" [lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:97-99]. Hence, pointwise for every x in S and B in {B_out,
TRAP},
   U_B(x) := E_x[ int_0^{T} 1_B(X_s) ds ]  <=  V_B(x) := E_x[ int_0^{D(0)} 1_B(X_s) ds ],           (TRUNC)
where V_B(x) is the occupation of B during ONE plain DELAYED-S-return cycle of the AUTONOMOUS diffusion
(no theta-absorption). Thus U = U_{B_out} + U_{TRAP} <= V_{B_out} + V_{TRAP}, and it suffices to bound
sup_{x in S} V_B(x) for each branch.

OBJECT RELABEL, MADE EXPLICIT (round-1 MINOR fixed). SR-PE1 / PE.2(b) / PE.5(b) state their identities
on the S-RETURN renewal-reward (Kac) cycle; the R5a round rides the DELAYED return D(0), which forces a
genuine collar excursion of radial extent >= delta/4 before re-entry [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3018].
These are DIFFERENT cycle objects. I do NOT gloss the swap: SR-PE1 is re-instantiated on the
delayed-return regeneration {D(sigma_{i-1})}, whose S-entrance is the delayed-return entrance law
rho_S^Palm on S (this is DELTA-PE1-DELAYED, closed at the object level here — the delayed cycle IS the
SR-PE1 cycle re-run on the delayed regeneration). The occupation-per-cycle identity rho_beta(B) x
E[cycle length] is EXPONENT-PRESERVING across the two regeneration definitions because rho_beta is the
common reversible stationary measure and the cycle length stays beta-free in the basin-local branch
(PE.2(b) section 3.2); the collar-excursion re-weighting alters only the beta-free entrance law and cycle
length, not the exponent. Hence consuming PE.2(b)/PE.5(b) "at exactly their claimed output strength"
below is legitimate PROVIDED the entrance-law re-weighting is tracked — which it is, as the residual
GAP-PE3-REF-TO-PALM (section 4, TYPED). The relabel is thus explicit, not silent.

3. REDUCTION 2a — THE NAMED RETURN / DRIFT ROW (R5b sections 1-4), CONSUMED PROVEN
   (this DISCHARGES the round-1 checker MAJOR: the geometric absorption is NOT Doeblin-alone)
=====================================================================
ROUND-1 DEFECT NAMED. The round-1 (PTW) wrote sup_{x in S} V_B(x) <= (1/kappa_ref) E_nu[V_B] +
sup_S FU_B and justified the leading 1/kappa_ref by "iterating (DOEBLIN) at each subsequent unit time on

kappa_ref nu holds ONLY on the small set — its hypotheses are dist(x,G) <= r0/4 AND d_G(pi(x),y) <=
r0/4 [lane-sh2local-proofs-v1.md:263-264] — so minorization ALONE gives geometric absorption only
together with a Foster/Lyapunov drift condition; on a small set it does not. I re-base the absorption on
that drift, supplied as a PROVEN NAMED ROW.

NAMED ROW R5b-RET (the within-round return structure; PROVED in R5b, checker SOUND
[lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3204]). On R5a's round object, inside one round i on {N >= i}, R5b sections
1-4 construct the zero-based stopped subcycle sequence m = 0, 1, ..., M_i, each subcycle = PHASE A
(recovery to R_0, or a crossing) + PHASE B (one composed attempt over the beta-free window T_sub), with
conditioning fields "H_m := F_{alpha_m} ... G_i := F_{sigma_{i-1}} ... {M_i >= m} = intersection over
j<m of Succ_j^c lies in F_{alpha_m} = H_m" [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3247], and prove:
  (R5b-P) the UNIFORM per-subcycle return floor, verbatim: "P( Succ_m | H_m ) >= ... =: p_sub" with
     "p_sub = c(delta,h) exp( -beta ( Gamma(h) + gamma_2 eps^2 + err(delta) ) ) > 0, Gamma(h) := ... =
     O(h)", and "The floor is UNIFORM over every H_m-measurable start in R_0 — core, band, and sub-cap
     alike" [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3268-3276];
  (R5b-G) the GEOMETRIC BUDGET, verbatim: "P( M_i >= m | G_i ) <= (1 - p_sub)^m, m >= 0" and
     "E[ M_i + 1 | G_i ] = sum_{m>=0} P( M_i >= m | G_i ) <= 1 / p_sub < infinity"
     [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3287-3291].

THE DRIFT UNDERNEATH (why R5b-RET is the genuine Foster/Lyapunov ingredient, not a re-labelling). The
per-subcycle floor p_sub is the composed recovery pass "(kick-or-relax) -> descent -> relocate -> orbit
chain -> landing" [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3259], whose descent leg is the STRICT-DESCENT drift:
M2-ATTR gives "Crit(E_eps) intersect closure(D_k(eps)) = G_k ... strict descent off G_k" (no foreign
attractor captures the pass), and the M2P.5 slice-gradient floor "<grad E_eps(x), x - pi(x)> >=
(c_1/2) dist(x, G_k)^2" [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:771-773] is a Lyapunov drift on dist(.,G_k)^2 driving
the path back into U_ch, realized by the diffusion via SH.2 shadowing at order-one probability
[lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3030]. This is exactly the standard "small set (L1' landing floor) PLUS
Foster/Lyapunov drift (M2P.5/M2-ATTR descent) => geometric absorption" pattern; the drift is the
ingredient the checker demanded and it is present, named, and proved.

4. REDUCTION 2b — THE POINTWISE UPGRADE (corrected (PTW); residual = GAP-PE3-REF-TO-PALM)
=====================================================================
L1' UNIFORM ONE-STEP FLOOR ON THE SMALL SET (consumed verbatim; citation MINOR fixed). By the small-set
minorization "p_1(x, .) >= c_0' beta^{n/2} exp( -beta C_2 (delta^2 + h^2) ) . Leb|_{B_rho(y)}"
[lane-sh2local-proofs-v1.md:276, C_2 := C_1 + 9/8 + C_+/4 + L^2/4, lane-sh2local-proofs-v1.md:499], in
its M3-GS.2 base-ball restriction "p_1^eps(z, .) >= m_dens Leb|_{B_0}(.), m_dens := c_0' beta^N exp(
-beta C_2^eps . O(delta^2) )" [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:733-734 — FIXED from the round-1 pointer
711-712, which is the L2 base-display preamble, not the (M3-GS.2) formula], there is a FIXED reference
probability measure nu := Leb|_{B_0} / Leb(B_0), B_0 subset S the base ball, and a floor mass
   kappa_ref := m_dens Leb(B_0) = c_0' beta^N exp( -beta C_2 O(delta^2) ) Leb(B_0)  in (0, 1),
such that
   p_1(x, .)  >=  kappa_ref . nu(.)      for EVERY x in S.                                        (DOEBLIN)
(m_dens is the M3-GS.2 base-ball density constant; it is DISTINCT from the trap floor m_1(lambda) =
lambda g(N) of section 2 — the notation is kept apart deliberately.) The hypotheses dist(x,G) <=
delta/4 <= r0/4 and d_G(pi(x),.) <= delta/4 <= r0/4 hold for EVERY x in S because S = B_{delta/4}(g*)
sits at the ground orbit: (DOEBLIN) is uniform over the WHOLE start set S, and every x in S is at ground
level (E_eps(x) <= m_k + eps w_k + (L_eps/2)(delta/4)^2, PE.2(a) (UP-QUAD)), so the small set and the
ground coincide — the drift returns the path INTO the flooring region, closing the small-set/drift loop.

THE CORRECTED (PTW). Fix x in S, B in {B_out, TRAP}. The cycle occupation V_B(x) accrues off-R_0 time
ONLY on B, beyond the doorway (B_out) or the phi-gate (TRAP); all of S is at the ground, strictly below
both. Split V_B(x) by the R5b-RET subcycle structure of section 3: the delayed cycle from x runs the
zero-based subcycles m = 0, ..., M_i^{cyc} (M_i^{cyc} the analogue of R5b's M_i for the autonomous
delayed-return cycle, same construction on the same object), and V_B(x) = sum_{m=0}^{M_i^{cyc}}
w_B^{(m)}, w_B^{(m)} := B-occupation accrued in subcycle m's span [kappa_m, kappa_{m+1}). Each w_B^{(m)}
is a functional of the post-alpha_m path, and {M_i^{cyc} >= m} in H_m = F_{alpha_m}; by the tower
property with the strong-Markov conditional law P_{X_{alpha_m}} (no independence),
   V_B(x)  =  E_x[ sum_{m>=0} 1_{M_i^{cyc} >= m} w_B^{(m)} ]
          <=  ( sup_{y in R_0} W_B(y) ) . E_x[ M_i^{cyc} + 1 ]
          <=  ( sup_{y in R_0} W_B(y) ) . (1 / p_sub),                                            (PTW)
where W_B(y) := ess sup E( w_B^{(m)} | H_m ) on {X_{alpha_m} = y in R_0} is the per-subcycle B-occupation
from an R_0 configuration, and the last step is R5b-G (E[M_i^{cyc} + 1 | any admissible start field] <=
1/p_sub, uniform). THE GEOMETRIC ABSORPTION IS NOW R5b-G — the checker's MAJOR is discharged: (PTW)
uses R5b-RET (Doeblin-on-S PLUS the descent drift), not Doeblin alone; the factor 1/p_sub is err-class
(beta^{-1} log(1/p_sub) = Gamma(h) + gamma_2 eps^2 + err(delta) -> 0 after beta-first then delta,
lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3274), NOT a new rate.

THE PER-SUBCYCLE OCCUPATION VIA THE DOEBLIN FLOOR AND THE REFERENCE MEASURE. The per-subcycle
occupation W_B(y), y in R_0, decomposes under (DOEBLIN) at the small-set re-entries: writing the
subcycle span's occupation as its first-window charge plus the post-flooring tail, (DOEBLIN) gives every
S-visit's one-step law the floor kappa_ref nu, so the per-subcycle occupation is dominated by the
reference-measure occupation at cost 1/kappa_ref:
   sup_{y in R_0} W_B(y)  <=  (1/kappa_ref) E_nu[ w_B ]  +  sup_{x in S} FU_B(x),                 (REF)
with FU_B the first-window barrier charge (section 5) and E_nu[w_B] the reference-measure per-subcycle
occupation. THE UPGRADE COST is 1/kappa_ref: beta^{-1} log(1/kappa_ref) = C_2 O(delta^2) - (N/beta) log
beta - beta^{-1} log(c_0' Leb(B_0)) -> C_2 O(delta^2) =: err_up(delta) after beta -> infinity; since h =
delta/2, err_up(delta) = O(h^2) -> 0 as delta -> 0 — PRECISELY the design's "exp(beta O(h^2)) cost"
[lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:88-96], err-class.

REFERENCE-TO-PALM (the SINGLE residual, TYPED at exact strength). Combining (PTW)+(REF), the
per-subcycle reference occupation E_nu[w_B] and the geometric count 1/p_sub reconstitute, up to the
common err-class factors, the Palm per-DELAYED-cycle occupation E_Palm[V_B] of section 2: the Palm
identity E_Palm[V_B] = E_Palm[ sum over its subcycles w_B ] = E_Palm[M^{cyc}+1] . (Palm per-subcycle
occupation) matches the count 1/p_sub against E_Palm[M^{cyc}+1] (both the geometric mean subcycle
count on the SAME object, err-class-comparable), leaving the residual comparison of the reference law nu
to the delayed-return Palm entrance law rho_S^Palm. I do NOT close this here; I TYPE it exactly:
   E_nu[ w_B ] . (1/p_sub)  <=  C_tr . E_Palm[ V_B ],   beta^{-1} log C_tr ->_{beta->inf} 0,
     C_tr -> 1 as delta -> 0.                                                                (REF-TO-PALM)
Until closed, sections 6-7 hold with E_Palm[V_B] carrying the additional err-class factor C_tr, i.e.
the pointwise-over-S bound is PROVED against the fixed reference measure nu and the R5b-RET geometric
structure, and GAP-PE-COND is delivered MODULO (REF-TO-PALM).

=====================================================================
5. FIRST-WINDOW BARRIER CHARGE FU_B (round-1 MINOR fixed: barrier S_k+c_H-m_k, not c_H)
=====================================================================
From x in S the path starts INSIDE R_0 at the ground (w_phi=0, E_eps <= m_k + err-band). To occupy B in
the first window it must first cross the doorway (B_out) or the phi-gate (TRAP). The TRUE barrier from
the GROUND is:
   FU_{B_out}(x) <= exp( -beta( (S_k + c_H - m_k) - err(delta) ) ),   FU_{TRAP}(x) <= exp( -beta( 2
     lambda - err(delta) ) ),
where the B_out barrier is the ground-to-doorway height S_k + c_H - m_k (~1.02 at the flagship,
lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:108) — NOT c_H (~0.16); c_H was the round-1 mislabel (S sits at m_k, not at
the doorway). The TRAP barrier is the ground-to-gate height gate - m_k = 2 lambda
[lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:701]. Both barriers STRICTLY exceed c_H/2 (S_k + c_H - m_k >= c_H > c_H/2;
and 2 lambda > lambda g(N) = m_1(lambda) > c_H/2 since g(N) < 2 on N >= 10, section 6), so FU_B is
subdominant to the target on both branches. (Using c_H in place of S_k + c_H - m_k would be a valid
CONSERVATIVE weakening, but the honest barrier is S_k + c_H - m_k, now stated.)

=====================================================================
6. THE COST ARITHMETIC — BOTH BRANCHES CLEAR c_H/2 (the ADJ-2 identity)
=====================================================================
Insert (I2a),(I2b) into (PTW)+(REF)+(REF-TO-PALM). All upgrade factors are err-class in the exponent:
err_up(delta) = C_2 O(delta^2) [1/kappa_ref], beta^{-1} log(1/p_sub) -> 0 [R5b-G], beta^{-1} log C_tr
-> 0 [REF-TO-PALM]; write err_tot(delta) := err(delta) + err_up(delta) + (beta-vanishing parts), all
-> 0 after beta-first then delta.

B_out branch. min-rate ingredient S_k + c_H - m_k, loosened to c_H:
   sup_S U_{B_out} <= (C_tr/p_sub . 1/kappa_ref) E_Palm[V_{B_out}] + sup_S FU_{B_out}
     <= T_a' exp( -beta( c_H - err_tot ) ) + exp( -beta( (S_k+c_H-m_k) - err ) )
     <= T_a' exp( -beta( c_H/2 - err_a(delta) ) ),
because c_H - (err-class) >= c_H/2 - (err-class) (c_H >= c_H/2, c_H > 0): B_out clears c_H/2 with SLACK
c_H/2.

TRAP branch. min-rate ingredient m_1(lambda) = lambda g(N). By the ADJ-2 sealed closed form
[lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:730],
   m_1(lambda) - c_H/2  =  lambda g(N) - (1/8)( g(N) + 2 - S_k )  =  g(N)( lambda - 1/8 ) + ( S_k - 2 )/8
     =:  Delta_margin,
"Both summands are STRICTLY POSITIVE for every N >= 10, lambda >= 1 (g(N) > 0, lambda - 1/8 >= 7/8 > 0;
S_k > 2 always)". Delta_margin is a FIXED (beta,delta-free) positive constant, so for delta small enough
that err_tot < Delta_margin,
   sup_S U_{TRAP} <= T_b' exp( -beta( m_1(lambda) - err_tot ) ) + sup_S FU_{TRAP}
     <= T_b' exp( -beta( c_H/2 - err_b(delta) ) ),
i.e. TRAP clears c_H/2 with the strictly positive margin Delta_margin. Numerically sealed against the
ADJ-2 cells: Delta_margin = 1.7472 at (10,1), 1.0425 at (18,1.05), 1.6742 at (46,4), 0.0895 at
(200,1.0001) [lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:731] — positive on the WHOLE flagship range, so the upgrade
needs NO window hypothesis, consistent with ADJ-2's per-round verdict.

EXPONENT-BUDGET CHECK (as the task requires). The binding rate is min( S_k + c_H - m_k, m_1(lambda) )
(B_out binding at the flagship, ~1.02 < 1.91 = m_1(10,1); TRAP binding as N -> infinity, where S_k + c_H
- m_k -> 2 while m_1 -> 0). By the two displays above, EACH rate individually exceeds c_H/2 by a fixed
positive margin (c_H/2 for B_out, Delta_margin for TRAP), hence
   min( S_k + c_H - m_k, m_1(lambda) )  -  err_tot(delta)  >  c_H/2   for delta small,
so the min-rate minus the (err-class) upgrade cost clears c_H/2 on the entire flagship range. QED for
the cost arithmetic.

7. ASSEMBLY — outside-R_0 = B_out + TRAP (GAP-PE-ASSEMBLY EXECUTED, given the section-4 typed transfer)
=====================================================================
By (COND), (TRUNC), (PTW)+(REF)+(REF-TO-PALM), and section 6, uniformly over x in S,
   U(x)  =  U_{B_out}(x) + U_{TRAP}(x)
        <=  ( T_a' + T_b' )(eps,delta) . exp( -beta( c_H/2 - err(delta) ) ),                (GAP-PE-COND)
with err(delta) := max(err_a, err_b) -> 0 under the mandated order of limits (beta FIRST at fixed
eps,delta,h=delta/2; THEN delta,h -> 0; THEN the eps-window). By the strong-Markov identity (COND) this
is exactly
   E( O_i | F_{sigma_{i-1}} )  <=  T_row(eps,delta) exp(-beta( c_H/2 - err(delta) ))   a.s.,
     uniform over F_{sigma_{i-1}}-measurable X_{sigma_{i-1}} in S,
which is GAP-PE-COND [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3164] — the conditional-uniform row R5a section 5(D)
leaves TYPED, now supplied MODULO the single transfer (REF-TO-PALM). The assembly B_out + TRAP ->
outside-R_0 is thereby ASSIGNED and EXECUTED here (the SPEC-LENS LENS-3 obligation), not left dangling
on either branch.

=====================================================================
(b-i) THE BASIN FLOOR — E_eps >= trap-center level - o(1) on an explicit
      set, PROVED from energy-monotonicity of the descent flow
=====================================================================
STRUCTURAL FACT F-FLOW (energy-monotone flow). The E_eps-gradient descent
semiflow Phi_t (d/dt Phi_t x = -grad E_eps(Phi_t x)), E_eps smooth on the
compact M, satisfies
   d/dt E_eps(Phi_t x) = <grad E_eps, -grad E_eps>(Phi_t x)
                       = -|grad E_eps(Phi_t x)|^2 <= 0,      (MONO)
i.e. E_eps is non-increasing along every descent trajectory. This is an
elementary identity, not a named import.

STRUCTURAL FACT F-ATTRACT (the pinning torus is a local-min attractor at
the sealed level). For j = +-1, G_{k,j} is a normally attracting E_eps-
critical manifold at level E_eps(G_{k,j}) = m_k + m_j(lambda) + eps N(1 -
cos(2 pi(k-j)/N)) [Gkj_level, lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:119-121]. Its
transverse minimality is the COSINE SECOND-ORDER FORM the task names:
writing the phi-ring energy V_phi(phi) = lambda sum_{i=1}^N (1 - cos(phi_i -
phi_{i-1})) (indices mod N; this is the phi-factor of E_eps on T^N_phi,
value m_j(lambda) at the wound circle C_j^phi = {phi_i = phi_0 + 2 pi j i/N}),
perturb phi_i = 2 pi j i/N + u_i and set a := 2 pi j/N. The linear term
sum_i sin(a)(u_i - u_{i-1}) = sin(a) sum_i (u_i - u_{i-1}) = 0 telescopes
around the loop (criticality — consistent with "grad E_eps = 0 on G_k for
EVERY eps" [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:1381], here for the phi-ring), and the
second variation is
   delta^2 V_phi = (lambda/2) cos(2 pi j/N) sum_{i=1}^N (u_i - u_{i-1})^2 >= 0,
STRICTLY positive off the flat overall-rotation mode {u_i = const}, PROVIDED
cos(2 pi j/N) > 0. For j = +-1 and N >= 10 this holds with room: cos(2 pi/N)
>= cos(2 pi/10) = cos 36 deg = 0.809 > 0. The theta-factor is transverse-
minimal at C_k identically (the M5-COERCE ground coercivity "E_eps(x) -
(m_k + eps w_k) >= (c_perp/2) dist(x, G_k)^2 on U" [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:
1395] is the k=theta analogue). Hence G_{k,+-1} is a transverse local
minimum, degenerate only along the two flat rotation circles — a normally
hyperbolic ATTRACTOR of Phi_t whose basin BASIN_{+-1} := {x in {w_theta=k} :
Phi_t x -> G_{k,+-1} as t -> infinity} is open, nonempty and forward-invariant.

BASIN FLOOR (the deliverable). For every x in BASIN_j (j = +-1), by (MONO)
E_eps(x) = E_eps(Phi_0 x) >= lim_{t->infinity} E_eps(Phi_t x) = E_eps(G_{k,j})
        = m_k + m_j(lambda) + eps N(1 - cos(2 pi(k-j)/N))
        >= m_k + m_j(lambda),                                (FLOOR)
the last step DROPPING the eps-coupling summand, which is >= 0 and only
RAISES the floor (conservative, eps-uniform — same convention as ADJ-1/ADJ-2
[lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:270-272]). Thus E_eps >= m_k + m_j(lambda) on the
EXPLICIT set BASIN_j, i.e. the pointwise trap-center level (lane-lt Z3
honesty note, POINTWISE only [lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:132-133]) is upgraded
to a genuine BASIN FLOOR, with -o(1) accommodating only the dropped
non-negative eps term. No coercivity constant, no tube radius, and no o(1)
band is needed: energy-monotonicity of the flow to the attractor gives the
floor exactly. QED (b-i).

=====================================================================
(b-ii) ROUND-REACHABILITY — every round path from S into a trap sector
       first crosses the Delta_phi gate at m_k + 2 lambda >= S_k + 4 c_H
=====================================================================
On OBJECT-R5a the round starts POINTWISE at X_{sigma_{i-1}} in S at the
phi-ground w_phi = 0, level m_k [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3037; ADJ-2
"at ground level m_k" lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:703]. The trap sectors are
the w_phi != 0 stratum; entering w_phi = +-1 from w_phi = 0 is separated
from R_0 by the Delta_phi gate. GENERAL-lambda inequality and its source:
the gate level is
   gate := m_k + 2 lambda      [lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:122-124;
                                ADJ-2 lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:699],
and on the flagship pin lambda >= kappa,
   gate = m_k + 2 lambda >= m_k + 2 kappa = S_k + 4 c_H,      (GATE)
using c_H = (m_k + 2 kappa - S_k)/4 (the active ledger branch on N >= 10,
g(N) < 2 [ADJ-1 step 2, lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:293-303]) so that S_k +
4 c_H = m_k + 2 kappa, with EQUALITY at lambda = kappa and strict for
lambda > kappa. This is the sealed pinning fact "E_0 there >= m_k + 2 lambda
> m_k + 2 kappa >= S_k + 4 c_H >= sup_{T_{r_0'}} E_0"
[lane-lp-product-saddle-v1.md:172-174] read at the round-start collar. Hence
any round path leaving R_0 into a G_{k,+-1} sector must first attain level
>= gate = m_k + 2 lambda, a barrier of height gate - m_k = 2 lambda ABOVE
the round-start ground (the "entry (ground -> gate): gate - m_k = 2 lambda"
of ADJ-2 [lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:701]). QED (b-ii). (This reachability
barrier is what the occupation identity of (b-iii) nets against the exit
barrier gate - floor = 2 lambda - m_1: "the entry pre-payment and the exit
barrier CANCEL in the occupation identity (net exponent = doorway - floor)"
[lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:112-121], leaving floor - m_k = m_1(lambda).)

=====================================================================
(b-iii) THE PER-CYCLE TRAP-OCCUPATION BOUND — occupation-identity route,
        PRIMARY (LENS-4); Z_beta-free ratio; no exit-time UPPER bound used
=====================================================================
Every expectation below rides OBJECT-PE1 (the plain S-return Palm cycle,
operator E_{Palm}); the R5a-round conditional-uniform form is PE.3'.

Step 1 (consume SR-PE1's (KAC-S) at exactly its strength; apply to the trap
set). SR-PE1's matched identity, on OBJECT-PE1, verbatim: "E_{Palm}[
occupation of B in one plain S-return cycle ] = rho_beta(B) . E_{Palm}[C]
... (KAC-S)" [wave-1 SR-PE1, RESULT OF PART 1; lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:232],
with hypothesis rows SR-PE1.1 (positive Harris recurrence on compact elliptic
M — automatic), SR-PE1.2 (rho_beta = Gibbs, detailed balance), SR-PE1.3
(0 < E_Palm[C] < infinity — (INT)) MATCHED there. NOTE (R2-PE1 discipline):
I use ONLY the identity (KAC-S) and the finiteness (INT); I do NOT use the
round-1 value "E_Palm[C] = 1/rho_beta(S)", which the SR-PE1 checker refuted
(the load-bearing need is (INT) alone). Instantiate (KAC-S) at B = TRAP and
at B = S:
   E_Palm[occ TRAP per cycle] = rho_beta(TRAP) . E_Palm[C],
   E_Palm[occ S per cycle]    = rho_beta(S)    . E_Palm[C].
Both are exact and share the SAME set-independent cycle length E_Palm[C].

Step 2 (Z_beta-free ratio — the load-bearing move, verbatim from PE.2(b)).
Dividing eliminates E_Palm[C] (hence Z_beta, hence the metastable global
well) entirely:
   E_Palm[occ TRAP per cycle]
        = ( rho_beta(TRAP)/rho_beta(S) ) . E_Palm[occ S per cycle].   (T-RATIO)
This is exactly PE.2(b)'s established reason "no beta-free cycle length is
needed and ... the metastable global well is irrelevant to the occupation:
the identity is exact and Z_beta-free" [PE.2(b) Step 2.1] — here with the
level region B_out replaced by the trap set TRAP. The exponentially-large
plain E_Palm[C] under a deeper w_theta -> 0 well (PE.2(b) section 3.1) is
irrelevant by the SAME cancellation.

Step 3 (the mass ratio, via PE.2(a)'s Laplace at the trap floor / ground).
NUMERATOR: on TRAP, E_eps >= m_k + m_1(lambda) pointwise by (FLOOR) of (b-i)
(m_{+1} = m_{-1}), so, with Leb(TRAP) beta-free,
   int_TRAP e^{-beta E_eps} dx <= Leb(TRAP) e^{-beta( m_k + m_1(lambda) )}.  (T-NUM)
DENOMINATOR: consume PE.2(a)/(PE.2(b)) SOUND round-1 base-ball lower bound
VERBATIM — from PE.2(a)'s (UP-QUAD) "E_eps(x) <= m_k + eps w_k + (L_eps/2)
dist(x, G_k)^2 on U. (UP-QUAD)" [wave-1 PE.2(a), section 2a] and Leb(S) >=
c_{2N}(delta/4)^{2N} (a valid under-estimate; the 2N-ball constant sits in
a denominator lower bound, R2-PE2b MINOR), every x in S = B_{delta/4}(g*)
has dist(x,G_k) <= delta/4, so
   int_S e^{-beta E_eps} dx
      >= c_{2N}(delta/4)^{2N} exp( -beta( m_k + eps w_k + (L_eps/2)(delta/4)^2 ) ),  (DEN-S)
the exact (DEN-S) of PE.2(b) Step 2.3, using M2P.1 "grad E_eps = 0 on G_k
for EVERY eps"/"E_eps(G_k) = m_k + eps w_k" [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:1381,
1377-1379] and M5-DRIFT "|grad E_eps(x)| <= L_eps dist(x, G_k), L_eps <=
L + 8 eps" [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:1419]. Dividing (T-NUM) by (DEN-S)
(Z_beta already cancelled in (T-RATIO)):
   rho_beta(TRAP)/rho_beta(S) = int_TRAP e^{-beta E}/int_S e^{-beta E}
      <= ( Leb(TRAP)/(c_{2N}(delta/4)^{2N}) )
         . exp( -beta( m_1(lambda) - eps w_k - (L_eps/2)(delta/4)^2 ) )
      = T_1(N,delta) exp( -beta( m_1(lambda) - err(delta,eps) ) ),        (T-MASS)
   err(delta,eps) := eps w_k + (L_eps/2)(delta/4)^2 >= 0,  w_k = g(N) at k=1,
both err summands -> 0 in the declared order (beta first; then delta kills
(L_eps/2)(delta/4)^2; then the eps-window kills eps w_k). No transverse
Gaussian sharpening and hence NO beta^{-(N-1)} prefactor enters a
denominator LOWER bound — the crude Leb x min-integrand suffices, cleaner
than PE.2(a)'s full-Z prefactor.

Step 4 (the cycle-scale factor — NAMED interface from PE.2(b) round-2).
E_Palm[occ S per cycle] is the mean per-cycle sojourn in the base ball S
on OBJECT-PE1 (one plain cycle contains exactly one S-sojourn). I consume it
as the NAMED PE.2(b) round-2 cycle-scale interface at its target shape
(beta-free x exp(beta err)): the basin-local conditioned S-scale time,
DERIVED there by geometric trials over beta-free windows with an order-one
floor per window (R2-PE2b), NOT asserted beta-free by citation. Its interface
strength (consumed, not re-proved):
   E_Palm[occ S per cycle] <= T_cyc(N,delta) exp( beta . err_cyc(delta) ),  (T-CYC)
   T_cyc beta-free, err_cyc(delta) = O(delta^2) -> 0 (beta first, then delta).
(The sojourn in S is bounded above at cycle scale — it is NOT the full,
possibly global-well-inflated E_Palm[C]; that inflation was already
cancelled in (T-RATIO).)

Step 5 (assemble). Insert (T-MASS) and (T-CYC) into (T-RATIO):
   E_Palm[occ TRAP per cycle]
      <= T_1 T_cyc . exp( -beta( m_1(lambda) - err(delta,eps) - err_cyc(delta) ) )
      =: T_trap(N,delta) exp( -beta( m_1(lambda) - err_total(delta,eps) ) ), (T-OCC)
   err_total := err + err_cyc -> 0 in the mandated order of limits.
This is the per-cycle trap-occupation bound on OBJECT-PE1, at the binding-trap
exponent m_1(lambda).

EQUIVALENT PRODUCT READING (design :721 confirmation, consumed as a NAMED
interface). Bounding rho_beta(TRAP) directly by PE.2(a)'s full-Z denominator
"Z_beta >= c exp(-beta m_k)" [lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:76-79] gives
rho_beta(TRAP) <= C(N) beta^{N-1} exp(-beta(m_1(lambda) - err)), and with a
beta-free cycle-scale factor the product "E[occupation of trap per S-return
cycle] = rho_beta(trap) . E[cycle length], with rho_beta(trap)/rho_beta(
k-basin) = exp(-beta(floor - m_k)) = exp(-beta m_1) ... E[cycle length]
beta-free" [ADJ-2, lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:721] yields the SAME exponent
m_1(lambda). This product reading is the k-basin/quasi-stationary form; its
rigorous UPPER half is the inherited GAP-ADJ2-SUBDOM. The LOAD-BEARING bound
is the Z_beta-free (T-RATIO), which needs neither a beta-free plain E_Palm[C]
nor any exit-time UPPER bound (LENS-4 honored: SR-T2 is a liminf exit-time
LOWER bound [lane-c-exit-time-lower-bound-v1.md:51-96] and is NOT consumed
upward anywhere in this piece).

=====================================================================
EXPONENT VERIFICATION — m_1(lambda) clears c_H/2 on the WHOLE flagship range
=====================================================================
WHICH j MINIMIZES: m_j(lambda) = lambda N(1-cos(2 pi j/N)) is strictly
increasing in |j| on 1 <= |j| <= N/2 (theta |-> 1-cos theta strictly
increasing on (0,pi]), so over reachable j != 0 the trap floor m_k + m_j is
MINIMIZED at |j| = 1 — the binding trap is j = +-1 (ADJ-1 step 1
[lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:274-291]), with m_{+1} = m_{-1} = m_1(lambda) =
lambda g(N). The delivered exponent of (T-OCC) is therefore m_1(lambda).

Net exponent m_1(lambda) - err_total. By the ADJ-2 sealed closed-form
identity (kappa = 1, active ledger branch),
   m_1(lambda) - c_H/2 = lambda g(N) - (1/8)( g(N) + 2 - S_k )
                       = g(N)( lambda - 1/8 ) + ( S_k - 2 )/8      (ADJ2-ID)
[lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:730; ADJ-2 banner lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:157],
"Both summands are STRICTLY POSITIVE for every N>=10, lambda>=1 (g(N)>0,
lambda-1/8 >= 7/8 > 0; S_k > 2 always)" [lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:730-731].
Hence m_1(lambda) > c_H/2 EVERYWHERE with the FIXED (beta,delta-free)
positive margin Delta_margin := m_1(lambda) - c_H/2 (numerically sealed:
1.7472 at (10,1), 1.0425 at (18,1.05), 1.6742 at (46,4), 0.0895 at the worst
cell (200,1.0001) [lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:731]). Therefore, for delta
small and eps in the window so that err_total(delta,eps) < Delta_margin,
   (m_k + m_1(lambda) - m_k) - err_total = m_1(lambda) - err_total > c_H/2,
i.e. (T-OCC) delivers
   E_Palm[occ TRAP per cycle] <= T_trap(N,delta) exp( -beta( c_H/2 -
        err_b(delta) ) ),   err_b(delta) := c_H/2 - m_1(lambda) + err_total
                             = -Delta_margin + err_total -> -Delta_margin < 0,
so the per-cycle trap occupation clears the row's c_H/2 rate with the
strictly positive slack Delta_margin, on the WHOLE flagship range N >= 10,
lambda >= 1 — REFUTED NOWHERE, consistent with ADJ-2's per-round verdict.
NO window hypothesis is needed. The AGGREGATE (theta-to-theta) trap exponent
floor - S_k = m_1 - (S_k - m_k) = (per-round) - E[N]-exponent is the SEPARATE
display (T-OCC) . E[N]; E[N] ~ exp(beta(S_k - m_k)) is applied by M4 at the
OUTER Wald sum, NEVER folded here (PE.4 double-count prohibition
[lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:97-111]; defect-caution 4).

THE COLLAPSE. Round 2's three blockers (the PE.2(b) sojourn object,

   E_Palm[V_B] / E_Palm[V_S] = rho_beta(B) / rho_beta(S).

The unknown cycle length E_Palm[C] CANCELS. Consequences, piece by
piece:

(1) THE QUASI-STATIONARY DEVICE IS DELETED. No conditioned cycle
    length, no escaping-cycle accounting (round 2's FATAL objects)
    are needed anywhere: the route never touches E_Palm[C].
(2) THE BASIN/REACHABILITY MACHINERY IS DELETED. The {w_phi != 0}
    stratum has an ELEMENTARY GLOBAL FLOOR. [DESIGN ERRATA, LENS-R3-2
    (2026-07-25): the original wording here - "the sector infimum is
    its equidistributed point for admissible |j| < N/2" - was FALSE
    for |j| >= 2 (C1-SUB(j) fails at the flagship from j = 2; the
    lens supplied an explicit N = 10, w_phi = 2 configuration BELOW
    m_2). The CORRECT floor, per the lens's constructive repair and
    proved in R3-STRAT: |j| = 1 by the ridge-law sector minimum
    (LS.2(i), machine-sealed, in scope via C1-SUB(1)); |j| >= 2 by
    the QUADRATIC floor 1 - cos d >= (2/pi^2) d^2 + Cauchy-Schwarz,
    giving J_lambda >= 8 lambda j^2 / N >= m_1(lambda) for every
    |j| >= 2, every N, every lambda. The stratum infimum >=
    m_1(lambda) stands; the m_j-monotonicity route is DELETED.] No
    trap-basin geometry, no entry pricing, no dwell bound: the Gibbs
    numerator of the entire stratum carries exponent m_1(lambda) -
    err. PE.5(b) as designed (basins + reachability) is SUPERSEDED.
(3) WHAT IS GENUINELY NEW is small: E_Palm[V_S] - the mean S-sojourn
    per delayed cycle - must be bounded ABOVE (polynomially in beta
    suffices; it enters err). Route: V_S <= (collar-exit time from
    the round start), and the collar exit is driven by the FLAT
    orbit coordinates of G_k (free diffusion along the 2-torus - no
    drift along the orbit), so optional stopping on the martingale
    |X_flat|^2 - (rate) t gives E[theta^+ - T_0] <= C beta delta^2.
    Also needed BELOW: E_Palm[V_S] > 0 trivially from the entrance
    (the path starts IN S and spends positive expected time before
    exiting the collar - a one-line diffusive lower floor
    c(delta) <= beta^{-1}-free is NOT needed if the assembly divides
