# ROUND-3 SPEC-LENS CORRECTIONS (12; BINDING - the drafters received them verbatim; LENS-R3-1/2/3 are errata'd into the design text above)

### LENS-R3-1 [OBJECT-ERROR] — R3-ASM

FATAL as designed: at PALM level the set "outside R_0" is NOT covered by the two-term split, and the missing term has EXPONENTIALLY LARGE Gibbs ratio. R_0 = {w_theta = k, w_phi = 0, E_eps <= S_k + c_H} (lane-lp:216-217, verbatim: "let R_0 := {w_theta = k, w_phi = 0, E_eps <= S_k + c_H}"). The design displays (proofs:3808-3810) 'E_Palm[V_{outside-R_0}] = E_Palm[V_{w_phi=0, E>S_k+c_H}] + E_Palm[V_{w_phi != 0}]' as an EQUALITY. It is not one: M \ R_0 also contains {w_theta != k, w_phi = 0, E_eps <= S_k + c_H}, which is non-empty and CHEAP - the fully constant configuration (all theta equal, all phi equal) has d_i = e_i = 0, hence J_kappa = J_lambda = W* = 0 and E_eps = 0 <= S_k + c_H, with w_theta = 0 != k = 1. Its Gibbs weight relative to S (whose level is m_k + eps w_k = g(N) + eps w_k > 0) is exp(+beta m_k), so rho_beta(M \ R_0)/rho_beta(S) is exponentially LARGE and the claimed <= exp(-beta(...)) is FALSE at the Palm object. This is not a cosmetic omission: it is exactly the OBJECT SLIP SR-PE1 warns of - OBJECT-PE1 is "the PLAIN S-return cycle {T_0, T_1} of the AUTONOMOUS diffusion with NO absorbing theta-label event" (proofs:1936-1937), so the Palm cycle is free to sit in the winding-0 well for its (exponentially long, cf. proofs:1902-1905) duration.
MANDATORY REPAIR (exponents survive unchanged; only the object and one domination lemma change). Apply (KAC-RATIO) with B := B_k := {w_theta = k} INTERSECT ({E_eps >= S_k + c_H} UNION {w_phi != 0}), NOT with B = M \ R_0, and prove the domination lemma FIRST: on round i the label is constantly k, because T_i := min(D(sigma_{i-1}), L_i) (lane-minmig:3048) with L_i := inf{s > sigma_{i-1} : w_theta(X_s) != k} (lane-minmig:3044), hence w_theta = k on [sigma_{i-1}, T_i) and the round's outside-R_0 occupation EQUALS its occupation of B_k; and T_i <= D(sigma_{i-1}) = the delayed-cycle terminus, so that occupation is <= the cycle's occupation of B_k. This one-line lemma also SUPERSEDES the imported PE.4 assertion 'absorption only truncates' (design:97-99) - derive it, do not cite it as an axiom. Then: the doorway leg is unaffected ({w_theta=k, E >= S_k+c_H} SUBSET B_out, so PE.2(a)'s numerator (NUM) still applies), and the stratum leg acquires the J_kappa >= m_k floor it needs (R3-STRAT already assumes it). Any draft whose Palm-level B is the unrestricted complement of R_0 is FATAL.

### LENS-R3-2 [OBJECT-ERROR] — R3-STRAT

The 'sector infimum = equidistributed point' fact is SCOPED BY C1-SUB(j) and is FALSE outside that scope, and the design's 'sum over admissible j != 0' silently DROPS the non-admissible sectors, which are part of the stratum.
(a) AUTHORITATIVE HOME (the spec asks you to find it): it is NOT reader-packet Lemma B.3 - that lemma is about the SUBLEVEL COMPONENT, verbatim "On the component `A_k` of `{J_kappa < 2 kappa}` containing `e_k` (nonempty exactly under C1-SUB(k)), the energy attains its minimum `m_k` precisely on the rotation circle `C_k`" (la3-reader-packet-v1.md:366-369) - a statement on A_k, NOT on the sector Sigma_j. The SECTOR form is the ridge-law corollary, recorded verbatim as "[STD]   sector minimum: J >= m_k on the winding-k sector (via the ridge: min over [2 pi k/N, pi] of phi_k = m_k)" (gate-v17-la2f-brief-lt-v1.md:54-55) and consumed verbatim as "J_kappa >= m_k on the winding-k sector by the ridge minimum" (lane-lp-product-saddle-v1.md:320-321, again :359-360). Its source is LS.2(i) "`J >= phi_k(M_abs)` pointwise" (lane-ls-label-sharpness-v1.md:277-278), machine-sealed, but carrying the explicit residual-mean hypothesis: "the one remaining range condition is on the residual MEAN, `r in [0, 3/4]`, carried EXPLICITLY by the machine form and discharged at the flagship and, via C1-SUB as above, at every admissible k" (lane-ls:279-283). So the floor is available for |j| = 1 (C1-SUB(1) = g(N) < 2, true for N >= 10, lambda-free since m_1(lambda) = lambda g(N)) and for w_theta = k = 1 - and ONLY there.
(b) THE CLAIM IS FALSE FOR |j| >= 2. C1-SUB(2) fails at the flagship (N = 10: m_2/lambda = 10(1-cos 72deg) = 6.910 > 2). Explicit counterexample to 'inf_{Sigma_2} J_lambda = m_2': N = 10, eight phi-bonds at 45.03deg and two at 179.88deg sums to 720.0deg = 4 pi (winding 2, off Delta_phi) with J_lambda/lambda = 8(1-cos 45.03) + 2(1-cos 179.88) = 6.346 < m_2/lambda = 6.910. So 'm_j(lambda) increases in |j|, so the sum is dominated by |j| = 1' is built on a false premise: m_j is not the sector infimum once C1-SUB(j) fails.
(c) CONSTRUCTIVE REPAIR (unconditional, elementary, keeps the m_1 exponent). For |j| >= 2 use the quadratic floor instead of the sector minimum: 1 - cos d >= (2/pi^2) d^2 on |d| <= pi (since (1-cos d)/d^2 decreases to 2/pi^2 at d = pi), so by Cauchy-Schwarz with sum_i |e_i| >= |sum_i e_i| = 2 pi |j|, J_lambda >= lambda (2/pi^2) (sum|e_i|)^2/N >= 8 lambda j^2/N. Since m_1(lambda) = lambda N(1 - cos(2 pi/N)) <= 2 pi^2 lambda/N, the floor beats m_1 as soon as 8 j^2 >= 2 pi^2, i.e. for every |j| >= 2, for EVERY N and every lambda. Therefore inf over the whole {w_phi != 0} stratum of J_lambda >= m_1(lambda), with |j| = 1 by the ridge law and |j| >= 2 by the display above - and the >= m_j-monotonicity route is DELETED. State the Delta_phi null-set caveat too: w_phi is defined only off Delta_phi, which is Lebesgue-null (hence zero Gibbs mass) and is a.s. never occupied for positive time by the nondegenerate diffusion.

### LENS-R3-3 [OBJECT-ERROR] — R3-SOJ

The stated reason why the flat coordinate is a martingale is FALSE, and the flat coordinate is not the one the phrase suggests.
(a) 'the drift vanishes identically (G_k is a critical ORBIT - every point critical)' proves only grad E_eps = 0 ON G_k - a Lebesgue-null set that the excursion is off with probability one for a.e. time. Criticality of an orbit says nothing about the drift at distance ~delta from it, which is where the whole collar excursion lives. As written the martingale claim is unproved.
(b) THE CORRECT SOURCE IS THE EXACT CONTINUOUS SYMMETRY, not criticality: E_eps depends on the configuration ONLY through the bonds, verbatim "The pair: `X = T^N x T^N`, bonds `d_i` (theta) and `e_i` (phi), energy `E = sum_i [kappa(1 - cos d_i) + lambda(1 - cos e_i) + epsilon(1 - cos(d_i - e_i))]`" (CANON-THEOREMS.md:2545-2547); the corpus states the invariance itself as a class axiom, verbatim "smooth `W >= 0` with (A1) invariance under both global rotations" (CANON-THEOREMS.md:2882-2883), and lane-lp records the group action, verbatim "the orbit action is angle translation, which preserves bonds and conjugates the Hessian" (lane-lp-product-saddle-v1.md:98-100). Under theta -> theta + a*1 the d_i are unchanged and under phi -> phi + b*1 both e_i and d_i - e_i are unchanged; hence sum_i partial_{theta_i} E_eps == 0 and sum_i partial_{phi_i} E_eps == 0 EVERYWHERE on M, not just on G_k. This is what makes the two flat coordinates exactly drift-free.
(c) CONSEQUENTLY THE FLAT COORDINATE MUST BE NAMED AS THE GROUP COORDINATE - the mean angle a_t := (1/N) sum_i (theta_i(t) - g*_i) (resp. b_t for phi) - NOT the tangential coordinate of the Fermi/nearest-point projection pi(x) of lane-minmig:1401. The projection coordinate acquires an Ito correction from the projection map and is NOT a martingale; a draft that runs optional stopping on 'the coordinate along the orbit at pi(X_t)' is unproved. State also that a_t is well defined by lifting the collar to the universal cover (|theta_i - g*_i| <= delta/2 < pi on [T_0, theta^+]), so the martingale is only needed up to the exit time it defines.

### LENS-R3-4 [EXPONENT-ERROR] — R3-SOJ

The prescribed rate constant and the prescribed window are in DIFFERENT metrics, and as literally written they contradict the stated target C N beta delta^2 by a full factor of N.
(a) THE COLLAR IS A MAX-NORM BALL, not a Euclidean one: verbatim "Define the base ball and its exit collar (max norm, centred at the fixed g*):" then "S    := B_{delta/4}(g*)" and "S^+  := B_{delta/2}(g*)" (lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3006-3009); the standing setting keeps the two metrics apart, verbatim "Ambient tube radii and dist(.,G_k) are read in the max norm as everywhere in the corpus; the orbit chain and the base-ball landing are read in the ONE declared product-Euclidean/intrinsic metric of G_k with diameter D_G = pi sqrt(2N)" (lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3001).
(b) ARITHMETIC. With dX = -grad E_eps dt + sqrt(2/beta) dW, each coordinate has QV rate 2/beta. The Euclidean ARCLENGTH coordinate along the orbit is Z_t = (1/sqrt N) sum_i (theta_i(t) - g*_i), which does have rate 2/beta - but the diagonal direction converts max-norm to Euclidean with the factor sqrt N, so the delta/2 collar corresponds to the window |Z| <= sqrt(N) delta/2, giving E[tau] <= (N delta^2/4)(beta/2) = C N beta delta^2. The MEAN-ANGLE coordinate a_t = (1/N) sum_i (theta_i(t) - g*_i) has rate 2/(beta N) (not 2/beta) and window delta/2, giving the same C N beta delta^2. Writing 'rate 2/beta per direction' TOGETHER WITH 'the flat delta/2-window', as the spec does, yields C beta delta^2 and drops the factor N - a metric-normalization error of exactly the class the house rules name. Pick one normalization and SAY it. If the 2D form |X_flat|^2 - (2 x rate) t is used, note the compensator rate is 2 x (per-direction rate) and the disc radius must be delta/sqrt 2 (a^2 + b^2 > R^2 gives only max(|a|,|b|) > R/sqrt 2), which again lands on C N beta delta^2.
(c) THE CONTAINMENT DIRECTION IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE ONE THE SPEC IMPLIES. The corpus one-way containment is Euclidean-ball SUBSET max-norm ball ("the one-way containment (Euclidean r-ball subset max-norm r-ball) is used as stated", lane-lp-product-saddle-v1.md:104-106), so the exit time from a Euclidean delta/2-ball is <= theta^+ - i.e. it is a LOWER bound on the collar exit, useless here. The correct upper route is coordinate-FORCING, not domain-comparison: if |(1/N) sum_i (theta_i(t) - theta_i(T_0))| > 3 delta/4 then some |theta_i(t) - theta_i(T_0)| > 3 delta/4, hence |theta_i(t) - g*_i| > 3delta/4 - delta/4 = delta/2 (using X_{T_0} in S = B^max_{delta/4}) and X_t is outside S^+. So theta^+ <= the exit time of that scalar martingale from (-3delta/4, 3delta/4), and E[theta^+ - T_0] <= C N beta delta^2 follows by optional stopping on the stopped square (localize at tau ^ n, then monotone convergence). The favorable direction is this forcing inclusion PLUS the fact that transversal exits can only make theta^+ smaller - say both, precisely.

     [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3016]. The DELAYED CYCLE from an S-entrance
     T_0 is [T_0, D(T_0)); its Palm entrance law is the delayed-return
     entrance law on S (OBJECT-PE1-DELAYED). Its per-cycle S-occupation is
     V_S^{del} := int_{T_0}^{D(T_0)} 1_S(X_s) ds.
  O3 PLAIN S-RETURN CYCLE. [T_0, T_1^{pl}), T_1^{pl} := the first
     S-entrance after the first exit from S — the object SR-PE1 round 2 is
     stated on: "OBJECT-PE1: the PLAIN S-return cycle {T_0, T_1} of the
     AUTONOMOUS diffusion with NO absorbing theta-label event, started from
     the cycle-stationary (Palm) entrance law rho_S^Palm on S"
     [lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:1938-1941]. Its occupation is
     V_S^{pl} := int_{T_0}^{T_1^{pl}} 1_S(X_s) ds.
  O4 R5a ROUND. [sigma_{i-1}, T_i) with "T_i := min( D(sigma_{i-1}) , L_i )"
     [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3048] and "L_i := inf{ s > sigma_{i-1} :
     w_theta(X_s) != k }" [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3044]; round start law:
     "There is no fixed regeneration law nu here: X_{sigma_{i-1}} is an
     arbitrary (F_{sigma_{i-1}}-measurable) point of S."
     [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3037]

O2, O3, O4 are DIFFERENT objects. Section 2 proves the SAME containment for
each, separately, from each one's own definition. No statement about one is
transported to another.

Balls, verbatim: "Define the base ball and its exit collar (max norm,
centred at the fixed g*):" [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3006]; "S    :=
B_{delta/4}(g*)" [:3008]; "S^+  := B_{delta/2}(g*)     (= B_h(g*) — the exit
collar),   S subset S^+ subset U_ch" [:3009]. Nothing below depends on
whether B_{delta/2}(g*) is read open or closed (Section 6, eta-robustness).

------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. STEP 1 — THE CONTAINMENT V_S <= theta^+(T_0) - T_0 (three proofs)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
(2a) DELAYED CYCLE (O2). Let T_0 be an S-entrance, so X_{T_0} in S subset
S^+. By O1 and continuity of paths, theta^+(T_0) > T_0 strictly; the corpus
states this at the object level, verbatim: "A path with X_t in S lies inside
the collar S^+, so theta^+(t) requires the radial coordinate dist(.,g*) to
reach delta/2 before D(t) can fire: every delayed return carries a genuine
excursion of radial extent >= delta/4, and D(t) > t strictly. There are NO
trivial zero-time returns" [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3018]. Now split
[T_0, D(T_0)) = [T_0, theta^+(T_0)) union [theta^+(T_0), D(T_0)). On the
SECOND piece the path is NOT in S: by the definition O2, D(T_0) is the
INFIMUM of {s >= theta^+(T_0) : X_s in S}, so for every
s in [theta^+(T_0), D(T_0)) we have X_s not in S. Hence

   V_S^{del} = int_{T_0}^{theta^+(T_0)} 1_S(X_s) ds  <=  theta^+(T_0) - T_0.

(The path may leave and re-enter S several times inside the collar before
theta^+; that is irrelevant — the occupation of any set over an interval is
at most the interval length.)

(2b) PLAIN CYCLE (O3). Let tau_S := inf{s >= T_0 : X_s not in S}. By the
definition of T_1^{pl} as the first S-entrance after tau_S, X_s not in S for
s in [tau_S, T_1^{pl}); hence V_S^{pl} = tau_S - T_0. Since S subset S^+
[:3009], exiting S^+ requires having exited S, i.e. tau_S <= theta^+(T_0).
Hence V_S^{pl} <= theta^+(T_0) - T_0.

(2c) R5a ROUND (O4). T_i = min(D(sigma_{i-1}), L_i) <= D(sigma_{i-1})
[:3048], so [sigma_{i-1}, T_i) subset [sigma_{i-1}, D(sigma_{i-1})) and the
round's S-occupation is at most the delayed cycle's, hence at most
theta^+(sigma_{i-1}) - sigma_{i-1} by (2a). This is PE.4's "absorption only
truncates" direction realised concretely on THIS object: the crossing branch
L_i < D(sigma_{i-1}) only shortens the occupation interval. I do NOT claim
the converse, and I do NOT identify the delayed cycle with the R5a round
(the design's item (4) sentence "the delayed cycle IS R5a's round on the
non-crossing branch" is R3-ASM's to carry, not mine).

Nothing in Step 1 uses a probabilistic hypothesis: it is pure definition
chasing on continuous paths.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. SPEC-LENS CORRECTION [OBJECT-ERROR] — ADOPTED, AND THE CORRECT SOURCE
------------------------------------------------------------------------
The design writes: "the collar exit is driven by the FLAT orbit coordinates
of G_k (free diffusion along the 2-torus - no drift along the orbit)"
[lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:3798-3800], with the reason that G_k is a
critical orbit. THAT REASON IS INSUFFICIENT AND I DO NOT USE IT.
Criticality of G_k gives grad E_eps = 0 ON G_k only — a Lebesgue-null set
which the collar excursion is off at a.e. time, since the excursion lives at
distance of order delta from the orbit. A martingale claim resting on it
would be unproved. Likewise I do NOT use the tangential coordinate of the
Fermi nearest-point projection pi (the projection whose admissibility is
recorded at lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:1401, "Its single load-bearing role
here is to make the tube `U` carry a single-valued nearest-point projection
`pi` and clean Fermi coordinates"): composing with pi produces an Ito
correction from the projection map, so "the coordinate along the orbit at
pi(X_t)" is NOT a martingale.

THE CORRECT SOURCE IS THE EXACT CONTINUOUS SYMMETRY OF E_eps, valid
EVERYWHERE on M, not on G_k. The energy is bond-dependent, verbatim:
"bonds d_i = theta_{i+1} - theta_i,  e_i = phi_{i+1} - phi_i (indices mod
N)" [lane-m2-coupled-pair-declaration-v1.md:34] and "E(theta, phi) = sum_i [
kappa (1 - cos d_i) + lambda (1 - cos e_i)" / "+ epsilon (1 - cos(d_i -
e_i)) ]" [:36-37] (the same object CANON-THEOREMS.md:2545-2547 records as
"The pair: `X = T^N x T^N`, bonds `d_i` (theta) and `e_i` (phi), energy" /
"`E = sum_i [kappa(1 - cos d_i) + lambda(1 - cos e_i) +" /
"epsilon(1 - cos(d_i - e_i))]`, reversible weighted-divergence generator,").
The invariance is a SEALED LEMMA, consumed as a row, verbatim:

  Lemma M2a.2 (double rotation symmetry, every epsilon) —
  "E depends on (theta, phi) only through the bonds `(d_i, e_i)`, and both"
  "bond families are invariant under the two INDEPENDENT global rotations"
  "`theta -> theta + c 1` and `phi -> phi + c' 1`.  Hence, identically on X"
  "and for every epsilon:"   ...   "sum_i dE/dtheta_i = 0     and     sum_i
  dE/dphi_i = 0,"
  [lane-m2-coupled-pair-declaration-v1.md:61-64, 67]

and the corpus states the invariance as a CLASS axiom, so the row survives
the coupling-class substitution: "becomes ONE MEMBER of a declared class cW
- smooth `W >= 0` with" / "(A1) invariance under both global rotations;"
[CANON-THEOREMS.md:2882-2883]. lane-lp records the same group action
geometrically: "frame is rotation-parallel over the orbit: the orbit action
is" / "angle translation, which preserves bonds and conjugates the" /
"Hessian)." [lane-lp-product-saddle-v1.md:97-99].

Under theta -> theta + a·1 every d_i is unchanged; under phi -> phi + b·1
every e_i AND every d_i - e_i is unchanged. Differentiating each invariance
in its parameter gives sum_i dE_eps/dtheta_i = 0 and sum_i dE_eps/dphi_i = 0
IDENTICALLY ON M — at every point, at every distance from G_k, for every
eps. THIS, not criticality, is what makes the coordinate drift-free.

CONSEQUENTLY THE COORDINATE IS THE GROUP (MEAN-ANGLE) COORDINATE, defined in
Section 5 by lifting, not the Fermi tangential coordinate.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. THE EXACT GENERATOR DECOMPOSITION USED, AND ITS SOURCE
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Generator, verbatim: "L f = beta^-1 rho_E^-1 div(rho_E grad f)" / "= beta^-1
Laplacian f - <grad E, grad f>   on T^{2N}"
[lane-m2-coupled-pair-declaration-v1.md:45-46], with wellposedness declared:
"wellposedness + core + uniqueness = the named standard family (smooth" /
"coefficients, compact connected T^{2N}, diffusion beta^-1 I uniformly" /
"nondegenerate - the generator has no other second-order structure)"
[:47-49]. The equivalent path form is R5a's standing setting, verbatim:
"dX_t = -grad E_eps(X_t) dt + sqrt(2/beta) dW_t on M = T^{2N}, flagship k=1,
N>=10, M2-PIN (lambda>kappa), eps in [0, eps_2) fixed"
[lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3001].

I use the decomposition in exactly this form:
   L f = (1/beta) Delta f - <grad E_eps, grad f>,
   carre du champ  Gamma(f,f) := (1/2)( L(f^2) - 2 f L f ) = (1/beta)|grad f|^2,
   and for a smooth f the process f(X_t) - f(X_0) - int_0^t (Lf)(X_s) ds is
   a continuous local martingale with quadratic variation
   int_0^t 2 Gamma(f,f)(X_s) ds.
Sanity check of the normalisation on a single coordinate: f = theta_1 gives
|grad f|^2 = 1, hence QV rate 2/beta — which is exactly the sqrt(2/beta) of
the SDE. The second-order part is the FLAT torus Laplacian times 1/beta and
"the generator has no other second-order structure" [:49], so this is the
complete decomposition; no cross terms, no state-dependent diffusion matrix.

NOTE ON THE HOUSE RULE "NO INDEPENDENCE CLAIMS". Nothing above is an
independence assertion. I never claim independence of past and future, of
rounds, of cycles, or of coordinates. The only structural input is the
DECLARED generator (the diffusion matrix is (2/beta)·Id, [:46-49]) — a
definition of the process, not a probabilistic factorisation. In particular
I do not write the driving noise in components and do not invoke
independence of its components: the quadratic variation below is computed
from Gamma(a,a) alone.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. STEP 2 — THE MEAN-ANGLE COORDINATE AND ITS EXACT MARTINGALE PROPERTY
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Fix an S-entrance epoch T_0 (T_0 = the delayed-cycle start of O2, or
T_0 = sigma_{i-1} for O4, or the plain-cycle start of O3; the construction
is identical and is done once).

LIFT. For each theta-index i let r_i be the unique representative in
(-pi, pi] of theta_i(T_0) - g*_i (mod 2pi); r_i is F_{T_0}-measurable, and
since X_{T_0} in S = B^{max}_{delta/4}(g*) we have |r_i| <= delta/4. Let
tilde-theta : [T_0, infinity) -> R^N be the continuous lift of the theta-block
of the path started from the representative theta(T_0) (continuous lifts of
continuous torus paths exist and are unique given the initial
representative). Put

   Y_i(t) := r_i + ( tilde-theta_i(t) - tilde-theta_i(T_0) ),
   a_t    := (1/N) sum_i Y_i(t)      (the MEAN-ANGLE coordinate).

Y_i(t) is congruent to theta_i(t) - g*_i mod 2pi for every t, Y is
continuous, Y_i(T_0) = r_i, and a is (F_t)-adapted (a measurable functional
of the path on [T_0,t] together with the F_{T_0}-measurable r). a_{T_0}
satisfies |a_{T_0}| <= max_i |r_i| <= delta/4. The lift is needed ONLY to
make a_t well defined as a real number; the bound is used only up to the
exit time it defines, so no global lift issue arises (Section 6).

DRIFT. grad_theta E_eps is a smooth PERIODIC vector field on M, so the lift
tilde-theta solves, in R^N, the same equation with drift
-(grad_theta E_eps)(X_t). Applying the decomposition of Section 4 to the
affine functional a (affine on the lift, hence Delta a = 0):

   L a = (1/beta) Delta a - <grad E_eps, grad a>
       = 0 - (1/N) sum_i ( dE_eps/dtheta_i )(X_t)
       = 0        IDENTICALLY ON M, by Lemma M2a.2 [lane-m2:67].

QUADRATIC VARIATION. grad a = (1/N)·(1_N in the theta block, 0 in the phi
block), so |grad a|^2 = (1/N^2)·N = 1/N and

   Gamma(a,a) = (1/beta)|grad a|^2 = 1/(beta N),
   d<a>_t = 2 Gamma(a,a) dt = ( 2/(beta N) ) dt.

Hence a is, on [T_0, infinity), a continuous local martingale with
DETERMINISTIC quadratic variation <a>_t - <a>_{T_0} = (2/(beta N))(t - T_0).
The drift-freeness is EXACT and holds at every point of M, not only on G_k
— which is precisely the [OBJECT-ERROR] correction of Section 3 cashed in.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. STEP 3 — COORDINATE FORCING IN THE MAX NORM (no metric conversion)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
[EXPONENT-ERROR], ADOPTED. The collar is a MAX-NORM ball ["Define the base
ball and its exit collar (max norm, centred at the fixed g*):",
lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3006; ":= B_{delta/2}(g*)", :3009] while the corpus
keeps two metrics apart: "Ambient tube radii and dist(.,G_k) are read in the
max norm as everywhere in the corpus; the orbit chain and the base-ball
landing are read in the ONE declared product-Euclidean/intrinsic metric of
G_k with diameter D_G = pi sqrt(2N)" [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3001].
Writing "rate 2/beta per direction" TOGETHER WITH "the flat delta/2-window",
as the design display does [lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:3800-3801], mixes the
two and yields C beta delta^2 — short by a factor N. And the corpus's
one-way containment runs the WRONG WAY for a domain-comparison route:
"max-norm positions and back; the one-way containment (Euclidean" /
"r-ball subset max-norm r-ball) is used as stated"
[lane-lp-product-saddle-v1.md:100-101] — a Euclidean delta/2-ball is INSIDE
the max-norm collar, so its exit time is a LOWER bound on theta^+ and is
useless for an upper bound. I therefore use NO metric conversion at all and
NO domain comparison: the route is COORDINATE FORCING, entirely inside the
max norm. (GAP-M5-EUC is therefore not touched by this piece.)

Fix eta > 0 with delta/2 + eta < pi and set

   tau_eta := inf{ t >= T_0 : |a_t| >= delta/2 + eta }.

tau_eta is an (F_t)-stopping time (hitting time of a closed set by a
continuous adapted process on a right-continuous complete filtration,
[lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3035]).

FORCING INCLUSION. Claim: theta^+(T_0) <= tau_eta pathwise.
Proof. Let t < theta^+(T_0), so X_s in S^+ for every s in [T_0, t], i.e. the
max-norm distance of X_s from g* is <= delta/2 for every such s (this is the
weaker of the open/closed readings, so the argument covers both). Let
A := { s in [T_0,t] : max_i |Y_i(s)| < pi }. A is relatively open in [T_0,t]
and contains T_0 (max_i|Y_i(T_0)| <= delta/4). For s in A, no theta-coordinate
has wrapped, so the per-coordinate torus distance equals |Y_i(s)|, whence
max_i |Y_i(s)| = max-norm theta-block distance of X_s from g* <= max-norm
distance of X_s from g* <= delta/2. If A were a proper subset, put
s* := sup A; by continuity max_i|Y_i(s*)| = lim_{s->s*, s in A}
max_i|Y_i(s)| <= delta/2 < pi, so s* in A, and A open then contradicts
maximality. Hence A = [T_0,t] and max_i |Y_i(s)| <= delta/2 on [T_0,t].
Since a_s is the MEAN of the Y_i(s), |a_s| <= max_i |Y_i(s)| <= delta/2 <
delta/2 + eta on [T_0,t]. Therefore tau_eta > t. As t < theta^+(T_0) was
arbitrary, tau_eta >= theta^+(T_0). QED.

Contrapositive form (the forcing statement itself): if the MEAN of the
displacements exceeds delta/2 + eta then SOME coordinate displacement
exceeds delta/2 + eta, hence the max-norm distance from g* exceeds delta/2
and X has left the collar. Max >= |mean| is the whole content; no norm
equivalence, no dimensional constant, no metric conversion is used.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. STEP 4 — OPTIONAL STOPPING, AND THE ARITHMETIC WITH THE N IN IT
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Named classical imports (SR discipline: named, hypotheses matched, NOT
reproduced):

  SR-SOJ.1  ITO / MARTINGALE-PROBLEM FORM FOR A SMOOTH FUNCTIONAL OF A
    NONDEGENERATE DIFFUSION WITH SMOOTH COEFFICIENTS. Statement used: for
    f in C^2, f(X_t) - f(X_0) - int_0^t (Lf)(X_s) ds is a continuous local
    martingale with quadratic variation int_0^t 2 Gamma(f,f)(X_s) ds.
    Source: D. Revuz & M. Yor, Continuous Martingales and Brownian Motion,
    3rd ed., Springer 1999, Ch. IV §3 (Ito's formula) and Ch. VII §2
    (martingale problem / generator form); or I. Karatzas & S. Shreve,
    Brownian Motion and Stochastic Calculus, 2nd ed., Ch. 3 Thm 3.6.
    HYPOTHESIS ROWS. (h1) coefficients smooth and the second-order part
    uniformly nondegenerate on a compact connected manifold — MET verbatim:
    "smooth" / "coefficients, compact connected T^{2N}, diffusion beta^-1 I
    uniformly" / "nondegenerate - the generator has no other second-order
    structure" [lane-m2-coupled-pair-declaration-v1.md:47-49]. (h2) f in
    C^2 — MET: a is affine on the lift, and grad_theta E_eps is smooth and
    periodic so the lifted equation has the same smooth coefficients.

  SR-SOJ.2  OPTIONAL SAMPLING FOR A BOUNDED CONTINUOUS MARTINGALE AT A
    BOUNDED STOPPING TIME. Statement used: if M is a continuous martingale,
    uniformly bounded on [T_0, rho] for a bounded stopping time rho, then
    E[M_rho | F_{T_0}] = M_{T_0}. Source: Revuz & Yor, Ch. II Thm 3.2
    (optional stopping) — equivalently Karatzas & Shreve Thm 1.3.22.
    HYPOTHESIS ROWS. (h1) continuity — MET (a is continuous by Section 5).
    (h2) boundedness of the stopped process — MET: on [T_0, tau_eta] we have
    |a| <= delta/2 + eta, and the stopped compensated square is bounded on
    [T_0, (T_0+n) ^ tau_eta] for each finite n. (h3) bounded stopping time —
    MET by truncating at T_0 + n; the limit n -> infinity is taken by
    monotone convergence, NOT by an unproved uniform-integrability claim.

COMPUTATION. By SR-SOJ.1 applied to f = a (Section 5), a is a continuous
local martingale with <a>_t - <a>_{T_0} = (2/(beta N))(t - T_0); hence

   M_t := a_t^2 - ( 2/(beta N) )( t - T_0 )

is a continuous local martingale on [T_0, infinity) with M_{T_0} =
a_{T_0}^2. Stop at rho_n := tau_eta ^ (T_0 + n). On [T_0, rho_n], |a| <=
delta/2 + eta and (t - T_0) <= n, so M is bounded there and SR-SOJ.2 applies
(with the conditioning sigma-field NAMED as F_{T_0}):

   E[ a_{rho_n}^2 | F_{T_0} ] - ( 2/(beta N) ) E[ rho_n - T_0 | F_{T_0} ]
       = a_{T_0}^2       a.s.

Since a_{rho_n}^2 <= (delta/2 + eta)^2,

   E[ rho_n - T_0 | F_{T_0} ] <= ( beta N / 2 ) ( (delta/2 + eta)^2 - a_{T_0}^2 )
                              <= ( beta N / 2 ) ( delta/2 + eta )^2 .

rho_n - T_0 increases to tau_eta - T_0 as n -> infinity, so by monotone
convergence for conditional expectations,

   E[ tau_eta - T_0 | F_{T_0} ] <= ( beta N / 2 )( delta/2 + eta )^2  a.s.,

in particular tau_eta < infinity a.s. Combining with the forcing inclusion
theta^+(T_0) <= tau_eta of Section 6 and letting eta decrease to 0:

   E[ theta^+(T_0) - T_0 | F_{T_0} ]  <=  ( beta N / 2 )( delta / 2 )^2
                                       =  (1/8) N beta delta^2 .   (COLLAR)

WHERE THE N COMES FROM, SAID EXPLICITLY (the [EXPONENT-ERROR] fix). The
mean-angle coordinate a has QV rate 2/(beta N), NOT 2/beta; its window is
the max-norm radius delta/2, NOT a Euclidean radius. Rate 2/(beta N) with
window delta/2 gives (delta/2)^2 / (2/(beta N)) = N beta delta^2 / 8. The
alternative NORMALISATION — the Euclidean arclength coordinate
Z_t = (1/sqrt N) sum_i (theta_i - g*_i), which does have rate 2/beta — must
be paired with the window sqrt(N)·delta/2 (the diagonal direction converts a
max-norm radius to a Euclidean one with the factor sqrt N), giving
(N delta^2/4)·(beta/2) = N beta delta^2 / 8: the SAME answer. Either
normalisation lands on C N beta delta^2 with C = 1/8; pairing rate 2/beta
with window delta/2, as the design display does, drops the N. I use the
FIRST normalisation and say so. (If one instead ran the 2-dimensional form
|X_flat|^2 - (2 x per-direction rate) t on the pair (a,b), a = mean theta
angle, b = mean phi angle: the compensator rate is twice the per-direction
rate, and a^2 + b^2 > R^2 forces only max(|a|,|b|) > R/sqrt 2, so the disc
radius must be taken delta/(2 sqrt 2); that route gives
(delta^2/8)/(4/(beta N)) = N beta delta^2 / 32 — no better than a factor,
and it needs the phi coordinate too. I do not use it; the one-dimensional
theta route above suffices and is tighter to state.)

------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. STEP 5 — THE CONTAINMENT DIRECTION IS FAVORABLE (said precisely)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Two separate favorable directions, both upper-bounding:

(8a) THE COLLAR EXIT IS A MINIMUM OVER EXIT ROUTES. theta^+(T_0) is the
first time the path leaves the max-norm ball S^+ BY ANY COORDINATE — the N
theta-coordinates AND the N phi-coordinates. My forcing uses only the
theta-block mean. Any exit driven by a phi-coordinate, or by a single
theta-coordinate whose displacement outruns the mean, occurs no later and
only makes theta^+ SMALLER. Formally: theta^+(T_0) <= tau_eta is an
INEQUALITY in the direction I need; nothing in the argument requires the
exit to be realised BY the mean-angle coordinate. The corresponding
phi-coordinate b_t := (1/N) sum_i (phi-displacements), drift-free by the
second half of Lemma M2a.2 [lane-m2:67], would give an identical bound;
using min(tau_eta^theta, tau_eta^phi) can only lower the constant. The row
is therefore stated with the single-coordinate constant 1/8 and is
CONSERVATIVE.

(8b) THE OCCUPATION IS TRUNCATED, NOT EXTENDED, BY EVERY OTHER TERMINUS.
Section 2 shows V_S^{del}, V_S^{pl} and the R5a-round S-occupation are ALL
at most theta^+(T_0) - T_0; the theta-label event L_i can only cut the
interval shorter (2c). Again the inequality points the right way.

I explicitly do NOT claim any matching lower bound on theta^+ or on V_S, and
none is used.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. THE ROW, IN THE THREE FORMS THE ASSEMBLY MAY WANT
------------------------------------------------------------------------
(COLLAR) holds for EVERY S-entrance epoch T_0 and is a bound on a
conditional expectation given F_{T_0}, uniform over the start point. Since
the right-hand side is a constant, the same argument run from a fixed
deterministic start x gives

   (R3-SOJ.a)   sup_{x in S} E_x[ theta^+(0) ]  <=  (1/8) N beta delta^2 .

Indeed sup_{x in S^+} E_x[theta^+(0)] <= (1/8) N beta delta^2 as well (the
proof only used |a_{T_0}| <= delta/2, and the bound is monotone in the start
displacement, maximal at a_{T_0}=0).

BECAUSE (R3-SOJ.a) IS A SUPREMUM OVER STARTS, IT IS VALID UNDER ANY ENTRANCE
LAW. In particular, integrating over the Palm entrance law of whichever
cycle object the assembly instantiates:

   (R3-SOJ.b)   E_{Palm}^{del}[ V_S ]   <= (1/8) N beta delta^2   (object O2)
                E_{Palm}^{plain}[ V_S ] <= (1/8) N beta delta^2   (object O3)

and, using the strong-Markov conditional identity template of R5a §5 —
verbatim: "By the strong Markov property at sigma_{i-1} (§3), the regular
conditional law of the post-sigma_{i-1} path given F_{sigma_{i-1}} is
P_{X_{sigma_{i-1}}}, evaluated at the F_{sigma_{i-1}}-measurable random
variable X_{sigma_{i-1}}" [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3064] — together with
X_{sigma_{i-1}} in S pointwise [:3037]:

   (R3-SOJ.c)   E( int_{sigma_{i-1}}^{T_i} 1_S(X_s) ds | F_{sigma_{i-1}} )
                     <= (1/8) N beta delta^2   a.s.   (object O4)

(R3-SOJ.c) is CONDITIONAL on the named round-start sigma-field and UNIFORM
over its S-valued data, at no extra cost, because a supremum over start
points is exactly what the strong-Markov template converts into an a.s.
conditional bound. This does NOT close DELTA-PE1-ENTRANCE: that row is about
transporting the Palm-AVERAGED occupation of B_out (and of the trap
stratum) to a pointwise statement [lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:1959-1980], a
quantity for which no pointwise sup route exists here. Only the S-sojourn
factor is delivered pointwise. I state this narrowly and claim nothing more.

ERR-CLASS READING. beta^{-1} log( (1/8) N beta delta^2 ) -> 0 as beta ->
infinity at fixed (N, delta), so under the mandated order — "beta ->
infinity FIRST at fixed (eps, delta, h = delta/2) ... THEN delta -> 0 (h ->
0) ... THEN the eps-window is read" [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3113] — the
sojourn factor contributes NOTHING to any exponent. It is err-class in
exactly the sense R5a records for D_bar, verbatim: "D_bar is err-class:
beta^{-1} log D_bar = Gamma(h) + gamma_2 eps^2 + err(delta) -> 0 after beta
-> infinity then h,delta -> 0" [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3080]. N is FIXED
throughout (flagship N >= 10, [:3001]), so the linear N is inert.

PER-CYCLE / PER-ROUND DISCIPLINE. Every display above is a single-cycle or
single-round quantity. No E[N], no geometric count, no theta-to-theta
aggregate appears anywhere in this piece; the aggregate/per-round conflation
that ADJ-2 diagnoses [lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:738] cannot arise here
because no summation over rounds is performed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
10. THE HONEST LOWER-SIDE NOTE THE DESIGN DEMANDS: NOT NEEDED
------------------------------------------------------------------------
The design asks whether a lower floor on E_Palm[V_S] is required and offers
"a one-line diffusive lower floor" [lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:3803-3805].
THE ANSWER IS: NO LOWER BOUND IS NEEDED, and the design's parenthetical
should be closed by citation rather than proved.

REASON 1 (the assembly multiplies). The interface consuming this row
multiplies by E_Palm[V_S]; verbatim: "i.e. E_{Palm}[ V_{B_out} ] = (
rho_beta(B_out)/rho_beta(S) ) . E_{Palm}[ V_S ]."
[lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:2032]. E_Palm[V_S] therefore appears as a FACTOR
on the bounded side, so only the UPPER bound is load-bearing. Dividing by it
never occurs in the round-3 route.

REASON 2 (where positivity IS needed it is already automatic, and it is a
GIBBS fact, not a probabilistic one). The only place positivity enters is
the derivation of the ratio primitive from the occupation identity. The
hypothesis (KAC-RATIO) actually carries is on the GIBBS mass, verbatim:
"For any two Borel sets B, B' with rho(B') > 0, dividing two instances of"
[lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:1787], i.e. rho_beta(S) > 0 — which holds because
the Gibbs density is strictly positive and S is a nonempty open ball:
"(i) Z_beta finite and positive: E_eps is smooth on the compact M, hence" /
"bounded, so 0 < integral_M e^{-beta E_eps} dx < infinity. Density" /
"strictly positive everywhere." [lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:1856-1858].
Positivity of the SOJOURN is then a CONSEQUENCE, not a hypothesis: from
(KAC-OCC), verbatim "E_{Palm}[ V_B ] = rho(B) . E_{Palm}[ C ]."
[lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:1780], taken at B = S, together with
"(INT)       0 < E_{Palm}[C] < infinity" [lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:1919],
one gets E_Palm[V_S] = rho_beta(S) · E_Palm[C] in (0, infinity). That is
exactly what (KAC-RATIO) needs and it is already proved in SR-PE1 round 2
(checker SOUND). Nothing further is required, and I manufacture no diffusive
floor.

SCOPE OF REASON 2. As written, that derivation rides OBJECT-PE1 (the PLAIN
cycle, O3), the object SR-PE1 round 2 states its rows on. For the DELAYED
cycle (O2) the same three rows must be re-run on the delayed chain; SR-PE1
records that this is legitimate but types it, verbatim: "the delayed-return
chain is itself a positive Harris chain on S with its own Palm law and its
own entrance intensity lambda_S^{delayed}, so ROWS SR-PE1.1-1.3 re-run), but
it is a DIFFERENT Palm object" [lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:1993-1995]. That
re-instantiation is DELTA-PE1-DELAYED, owned by R3-PE3p, not by me. It does
NOT affect my upper bound, which is entrance-law-free (Section 9).

### SOJ round 3 — checker findings (verbatim; the round-4 spec)

- [MAJOR] The PLAIN-cycle instance (R3-SOJ.b, object O3) rests on a delimiter the draft supplies itself, and under that delimiter the draft's own Step (2b) collides with (KAC-OCC) at B = S. Either O3 is not the object the draft says it is (so (2b) proves nothing about it) or SR-PE1's identity fails on it. Since the assembly interface is stated on exactly this plain object, this is load-bearing.
  EVIDENCE: The draft defines O3 by 'T_1^{pl} := the first S-entrance after the first exit from S' and attributes it to lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:1938-1941. The cited bytes say only 'OBJECT-PE1: the PLAIN S-return cycle {T_0, T_1} of the AUTONOMOUS diffusion / with NO absorbing theta-label event, started from the cycle-stationary / (Palm) entrance law rho_S^Palm on S' (actual span :1936-1938) — no delimiter is given there. The corpus's only delimiter gloss is at :1982-1983, 'SR-PE1's cycle {T_0,T_1} is delimited by PLAIN S-returns (first re-entry to S)'. Under that reading the draft's (2b) gives V_S^{pl} = tau_S - T_0; but for the nondegenerate diffusion of lane-m2-coupled-pair-declaration-v1.md:45-49 the first re-entry to the open max-norm ball S after tau_S IS tau_S a.s. (the exit point lies a.s. in the relative interior of a face and the inward normal coordinate is immediately negative) — exactly the 'next entrance = start time' degeneracy the delayed convention was invented to kill, lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3018 ('There are NO trivial zero-time returns'), which the draft itself quotes in (2a). # R3-STRAT — the stratum floor + Gibbs sum (supersedes the round-2 PE.5(b) basin route)

(round-3 grade: draft PROVED-WITH-TYPED-GAPS; checker REPAIRABLE)

========================================================================
PIECE R3-STRAT — THE {w_phi != 0} STRATUM FLOOR AND ITS GIBBS RATIO
Round-3 design item (2). SUPERSEDES the round-2 PE.5(b) basin route.
Grade: PROVED-WITH-TYPED-GAPS (the FLOOR and the RATIO are proved
unconditionally on the flagship range; the gaps are interface gaps
belonging to R3-ASM / R3-PE3p, not holes in this piece).
========================================================================

------------------------------------------------------------------------
0. OBJECT, STANDING DATA, AND WHAT THIS PIECE IS *NOT*
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Standing setting, verbatim: "`dX = -grad E_eps(X) dt + sqrt(2/beta) dW`
on the compact flat torus `M = T^{2N} = T^N_theta x T^N_phi`
(`dim M = 2N`), `W` a standard `2N`-dim Brownian motion, generator
`L_beta^eps = (1/beta) Delta - grad E_eps . grad`. `E_eps` is smooth and
`Lambda`-periodic" [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:1345]. Flagship: k = 1,
N >= 10, kappa = 1, M2-PIN lambda > kappa, eps in [0, eps_2).

Write d_i for the theta-bonds, e_i for the phi-bonds; J_kappa(theta) =
kappa sum_i (1 - cos d_i), J_lambda(phi) = lambda sum_i (1 - cos e_i);
Delta_theta / Delta_phi are the antipodal sets (some bond = pi); off
them the winding labels w_theta, w_phi are integers, "well defined and
locally constant off `Delta`. The SECTORS `Sigma_k = {w = k}` are open"
[la3-reader-packet-v1.md:55-56]. Levels: m_j(mu) = N mu (1 - cos(2 pi
j/N)); "`m_k := kappa N(1 - cos(2 pi k/N))`, `w_k := W*(G_k) = N(1 -
cos(2 pi k/N))`" [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:1377-1378]; g(N) :=
N(1 - cos(2 pi/N)), so at k = 1, m_k = kappa g(N) and m_1(lambda) =
lambda g(N).

THE STRATUM. Define
      STRAT := { x in M : w_theta(x) = k }  \  { w_phi(x) = 0 }
             = the union of the slices {w_theta = k, w_phi = j}, j != 0,
               TOGETHER WITH {w_theta = k} intersect Delta_phi.
This is exactly the "w_phi != 0" half of outside-R_0, R_0 being
"`R_0 := {w_theta = k, w_phi = 0, E_eps <= S_k + c_H}`"
[lane-lp-product-saddle-v1.md:216-217].

WHAT THIS PIECE IS NOT. It is a purely STATIC computation: it produces a
pointwise level floor on STRAT and a ratio of two Gibbs masses. It
contains NO stopping time, NO conditional expectation (hence there is no
sigma-field to name — the absence is structural, not an omission), NO
independence claim of any kind, NO reachability/basin/dwell/entry claim,
and NO per-round or per-cycle occupation claim. In particular it does
NOT convert the ratio into an occupation: that conversion is SR-PE1's
(KAC-RATIO) and it rides the PLAIN Palm S-return cycle (OBJECT-PE1),
which is a DIFFERENT stopping object from R5a's delayed round; see the
typed gaps and section 6.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. THE COUPLING TERM: E_eps >= J_kappa + J_lambda POINTWISE, NO eps DEFICIT
   (this DELETES the design's "- 2 eps N" slack)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
The design's stratum display reads, verbatim: "so on the whole slice
E_eps >= m_k + m_j(lambda) - 2 eps N" [lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:3790].
The "- 2 eps N" is the sup-side slack of the coupling, i.e. "`sup W* <=
W_sup := 2N` (M2P Standing Data)" [lane-lp-product-saddle-v1.md:88]. It
is the WRONG direction and it is not needed. The corpus fact is

  "`E_0 := J_kappa + J_lambda` (the eps-free envelope); `E_eps = E_0 +
   eps W*`, `W* >= 0`" [lane-lp-product-saddle-v1.md:85-86],

with the explicit member form "`W = sum_i (1 - cos(d_i - e_i))`, 0 <= W
<= 2N" [c6-la2f-brief-gate-v11-surface-v1.md:37; identically
c7-la2f-brief-parity-artifact-v1.md:37-38, "E_eps = J_kappa(theta) +
J_lambda(phi) + eps W(theta, phi) with W = sum_i (1 - cos(d_i - e_i))"].
Every summand 1 - cos(d_i - e_i) lies in [0, 2], so W* >= 0 POINTWISE,
and since eps >= 0,

      E_eps(x) >= J_kappa(theta) + J_lambda(phi)   for every x in M
                                                   and every eps >= 0.
                                                                 (SHARP)

This is the sharp direction: no eps appears in the FLOOR. Numerically the
deleted term matters: at the flagship (N, eps) = (10, 0.05) it is
2 eps N = 1.00 in kappa units, while the whole assembly margin
min(S_k + c_H - m_k, m_1) - c_H/2 = 1.0244 - 0.1626 = 0.8617; carrying it
would make err exceed the margin and FAIL the row. It is deleted here on
the corpus's own text, not weakened.

The ONLY eps cost that survives into the final exponent is the eps w_k of
the DENOMINATOR — the true ground level of G_k is m_k + eps w_k, "`e_0 :=
M_k(eps) = m_k + eps w_k`" [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:1377] — see section 5.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. THE SECTOR-MINIMUM FACT: AUTHORITATIVE HOME, AND ITS EXACT SCOPE
------------------------------------------------------------------------
The fact needed is: on the winding-j sector, J >= m_j. Its authoritative
home is NOT reader-packet Lemma B.3, which is a statement about the
SUBLEVEL COMPONENT, verbatim:

  "LEMMA B.3 (ground levels).  On the component `A_k` of
   `{J_kappa < 2 kappa}` containing `e_k` (nonempty exactly under
   C1-SUB(k)), the energy attains its minimum `m_k` precisely on the
   rotation circle `C_k = {all bonds equal 2 pi k/N}`."
   [la3-reader-packet-v1.md:366-369]

— a statement on A_k, not on the sector Sigma_j. The SECTOR form is the
ridge-law corollary, recorded verbatim as

  "[STD]   sector minimum: J >= m_k on the winding-k sector (via the
        ridge: min over [2 pi k/N, pi] of phi_k = m_k)."
        [gate-v17-la2f-brief-lt-v1.md:54-55]

and consumed verbatim twice in the product lane as "J_kappa >= m_k on the
winding-k sector by the ridge minimum" [lane-lp-product-saddle-v1.md:
320-321, again :359-360]. Its source is LS.2(i), machine-sealed:

  "`J >= phi_k(M_abs)` pointwise: no minimizer existence, no exchange
   argument, no PER-BOND convexity-range caveat (the one remaining range
   condition is on the residual MEAN, `r in [0, 3/4]`, carried EXPLICITLY
   by the machine form and discharged at the flagship and, via C1-SUB as
   above, at every admissible k).  MACHINE SEAL: this exact argument is
   formalized sorry-free in `lean/RidgeLaw.lean`"
   [lane-ls-label-sharpness-v1.md:277-283]

SCOPE, STATED HONESTLY. The fact is carried by C1-SUB: "SUB-BARRIER
CONDITION C1-SUB(k):  m_k(mu) < 2 mu, equivalently gamma_k > 1 - 2/N.
For k = 0 always (m_0 = 0).  For k != 0 it FIRST holds at N = 10 (k = 1)"
[la3-reader-packet-v1.md:69-72]. Hence:

  (2a) THETA SIDE. C1-SUB(1) with mu = kappa reads kappa g(N) < 2 kappa,
  i.e. g(N) < 2, true for every N >= 10 (g is strictly decreasing,
  g(10) = 1.90983 < 2 — [lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:299-303]). Therefore
        J_kappa >= m_k        on the sector {w_theta = k}, k = 1, N >= 10.
                                                              (THETA-FLOOR)
  This is the theta-side care the spec demands: during a round the label
  is w_theta = k [terminus law, lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3044-3048], and
  (THETA-FLOOR) holds ON THAT SECTOR by the same ridge fact.

  (2b) PHI SIDE, |j| = 1 ONLY. C1-SUB(1) with mu = lambda reads
  lambda g(N) < 2 lambda, i.e. again g(N) < 2 — LAMBDA-FREE, because
  m_1(lambda) = lambda g(N) is homogeneous in lambda. Therefore
        J_lambda >= m_1(lambda)   on the sectors {w_phi = +1} and
                                  {w_phi = -1}  (m_{+1} = m_{-1}, cos even).
                                                                (PHI-FLOOR-1)
  The residual-mean condition r in [0, 3/4] is discharged at k = 1,
  N >= 10 by lane-ls:279-283 quoted above.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. THE CLAIM "inf_{Sigma_j} J = m_j" IS **FALSE** FOR |j| >= 2 — AND THE
   "m_j INCREASES IN |j|" ROUTE IS THEREFORE DELETED
------------------------------------------------------------------------
C1-SUB(2) FAILS at the flagship: m_2(lambda)/lambda = 10(1 - cos 72deg) =
6.90983 > 2. So neither Lemma B.3 nor the [STD] sector row is available at
|j| = 2, and the sector infimum is NOT the equidistributed point.

EXPLICIT COUNTEREXAMPLE (N = 10, winding 2, off Delta_phi). Take eight
phi-bonds equal to 45.03deg and two equal to 179.88deg. Bond sum =
8(45.03) + 2(179.88) = 360.24 + 359.76 = 720.00deg = 4 pi exactly, so
w_phi = 2; every bond has |e_i| < pi, so the point is off Delta_phi and
the label is defined. Its level is
  J_lambda/lambda = 8(1 - cos 45.03deg) + 2(1 - cos 179.88deg)
                  = 8(0.2932635) + 2(1.9999978)
                  = 2.346108 + 3.999996 = 6.346104
                  <  m_2(lambda)/lambda = 6.909830.
Hence inf_{Sigma_2} J_lambda < m_2(lambda), strictly, by 0.5637 lambda.

CONSEQUENCE. The design's route "m_j(lambda) increases in |j|, so the sum
is dominated by |j| = 1" [monotonicity proved at
lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:274-282: "the map j |-> m_j(lambda) = lambda
N(1 - cos(2 pi j/N)) is a strictly increasing function of |j| for
1 <= |j| <= N/2"] rests on a FALSE premise once C1-SUB(j) fails: m_j
stops being the sector infimum. The monotonicity itself is true and
elementary (1 - cos is strictly increasing on (0, pi] and 2 pi |j|/N
traverses (0, pi]), but it is monotonicity of the WRONG quantity. This
route is DELETED and replaced by section 4. (The same correction removes
the design's silent restriction to "admissible j": section 4 covers EVERY
realizable j, so no sector of the stratum is dropped.)

------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. THE CONSTRUCTIVE REPAIR FOR |j| >= 2: A QUADRATIC FLOOR THAT BEATS m_1
   (unconditional, elementary, every N, every lambda)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
LEMMA 4.1 (elementary chord bound). For |d| <= pi,
      1 - cos d  >=  (2/pi^2) d^2,
with equality exactly at d = 0 and |d| = pi.
Proof. Both sides are even; take d in [0, pi]. Put f(d) := 1 - cos d -
(2/pi^2) d^2. Then f(0) = 0, f(pi) = 2 - 2 = 0, f'(0) = 0, and
f''(d) = cos d - 4/pi^2, which is > 0 for d < d* := arccos(4/pi^2)
(4/pi^2 = 0.405285, d* = 1.15357) and < 0 for d in (d*, pi]. On [0, d*]
f is convex with f(0) = 0, f'(0) = 0, so f' >= 0 and f >= 0, with
f(d*) > 0 (strict since f'' > 0 on the interior). On [d*, pi] f is
concave, so f >= min(f(d*), f(pi)) = 0. Hence f >= 0 throughout. QED.

LEMMA 4.2 (stratum floor for |j| >= 2). On {w_phi = j} with j != 0,
      J_lambda  >=  8 lambda j^2 / N.
Proof. Off Delta_phi every bond satisfies |e_i| < pi, so Lemma 4.1
applies bond-by-bond:
      J_lambda = lambda sum_i (1 - cos e_i) >= lambda (2/pi^2) sum_i e_i^2.
By Cauchy-Schwarz (sum_i |e_i|)^2 <= N sum_i e_i^2, and by the definition
of the winding label sum_i e_i = 2 pi j, so sum_i |e_i| >= |sum_i e_i| =
2 pi |j|. Chaining,
      J_lambda >= lambda (2/pi^2) (2 pi |j|)^2 / N = 8 lambda j^2 / N. QED.

LEMMA 4.3 (the quadratic floor beats m_1 exactly from |j| = 2). Since
1 - cos x <= x^2/2 for all real x,
      m_1(lambda) = lambda N (1 - cos(2 pi/N)) <= lambda N (2 pi/N)^2/2
                  = 2 pi^2 lambda / N.
Therefore 8 lambda j^2/N >= m_1(lambda) as soon as 8 j^2 >= 2 pi^2 =
19.7392, i.e. as soon as j^2 >= 2.4674, i.e. for EVERY |j| >= 2 — for
EVERY N and EVERY lambda > 0, with no C1-SUB, no admissibility, no
range condition. (Sanity at the flagship N = 10: 8 j^2/N = 3.20 at
|j| = 2 versus m_1/lambda = 1.90983; the gap only widens, 7.20, 12.80,
20.00 at |j| = 3, 4, 5.) QED.

RANGE OF j. Off Delta_phi, |e_i| < pi gives |2 pi j| = |sum_i e_i| <
N pi, so |j| < N/2 — every realizable nonzero label satisfies this, and
the number of nonzero realizable labels is at most N - 1 < N. (The
equidistributed point e_j does lie in Sigma_j exactly when |j| < N/2,
[la3-reader-packet-v1.md:57-58], so nothing is realizable outside this
range and nothing is dropped.)

------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. THE STRATUM FLOOR (the deliverable of part (i))
------------------------------------------------------------------------
PROPOSITION 5.1 (FLOOR). For k = 1, N >= 10, lambda > kappa, eps in
[0, eps_2), pointwise on STRAT = {w_theta = k} \ {w_phi = 0}:
      E_eps(x)  >=  m_k + m_1(lambda).                            (FLOOR)
Proof. By (SHARP), E_eps >= J_kappa + J_lambda. By (THETA-FLOOR),
J_kappa >= m_k on {w_theta = k}. For the phi factor, three exhaustive
cases:
  (i) |w_phi| = 1: J_lambda >= m_1(lambda) by (PHI-FLOOR-1).
  (ii) |w_phi| >= 2: J_lambda >= 8 lambda j^2/N >= m_1(lambda) by
       Lemmas 4.2 and 4.3.
  (iii) x in Delta_phi: the corpus barrier row, verbatim, "On Delta_phi:
       J_lambda >= 2 lambda" [gate-v17-la2f-brief-lt-v1.md:49-50] (the
       one-line reason recorded at la3-reader-packet-v1.md:355-357,
       "LEMMA B.1 (barrier).  `J_mu >= 2 mu` on `Delta`"). And
       2 lambda > lambda g(N) = m_1(lambda) precisely because g(N) < 2
       for N >= 10. So the Delta_phi face carries a STRICTLY HIGHER
       floor and needs no null-set excuse.
In all three cases J_lambda >= m_1(lambda). QED.

NULL-SET CAVEATS (stated, as the spec requires, though (FLOOR) does not
need them). (a) w_phi is defined only off Delta_phi; Delta_phi is a finite
union of smooth codimension-1 tori, hence Lebesgue-null, hence
rho_beta-null (rho_beta has a smooth strictly positive density w.r.t.
Lebesgue). (b) The nondegenerate (uniformly elliptic, constant diffusion
matrix (2/beta) I) diffusion of the standing setting has transition
densities w.r.t. Lebesgue for every t > 0, so by Tonelli
E_x[ int_0^T 1_{Delta_phi}(X_s) ds ] = int_0^T P_x(X_s in Delta_phi) ds =
0 for every x, T: Delta_phi is a.s. never occupied for positive time.
This is used ONLY as a remark; case (iii) above already gives Delta_phi a
genuine level floor. NAMED IMPORT for (b), non-reproduced, hypotheses
checked: existence of a Lebesgue transition density for a uniformly
elliptic diffusion with smooth bounded coefficients on a compact manifold
(Friedman, Stochastic Differential Equations and Applications, Ch. 6;
hypothesis rows: M compact and smooth — HOLDS [lane-minmig:1345];
diffusion coefficient constant and nondegenerate, = (2/beta) I — HOLDS
[same line]; drift smooth, grad E_eps with E_eps smooth — HOLDS [same]).
The SAME remark, and ONLY this remark, is what covers Delta_theta: STRAT
is defined inside {w_theta = k}, which is defined off Delta_theta, and
Delta_theta is likewise Lebesgue-null and a.s. unoccupied for positive
time. I do NOT claim a level floor >= m_k + m_1(lambda) on Delta_theta
(the barrier there gives only J_kappa >= 2 kappa, which need not exceed
m_k + m_1(lambda)); see the typed gaps.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. THE GIBBS RATIO (the deliverable of part (ii))
------------------------------------------------------------------------
6.1 THE OBJECT, AND WHY PE.2(a)'s (DEN) IS THE WRONG DENOMINATOR.
The exported primitive is, verbatim,
  "(KAC-RATIO) E_{Palm}[ V_B ] / E_{Palm}[ V_{B'} ] = rho_beta(B)/rho_beta(B')
                  for Borel B, B' with rho_beta(B') > 0"
  [lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:1917-1918],
with B' := S the base ball "S := B_{delta/4}(g*)"
[lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3008]. So the object this piece must produce is
      rho_beta(STRAT) / rho_beta(S)
        = ( int_STRAT e^{-beta E_eps} dx ) / ( int_S e^{-beta E_eps} dx ),
in which Z_beta CANCELS. PE.2(a)'s round-1 denominator,
  "Z_beta >= c(N) beta^{-(N-1)} e^{-beta(m_k + eps w_k)},          (DEN)"
  [lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:637],
is a lower bound on Z_beta, i.e. on the integral over the FULL delta-tube
T_delta(G_k); since S = B^max_{delta/4}(g*) is a small piece of that tube,
(DEN) STRICTLY DOMINATES int_S. Substituting it would bound
int_STRAT / int_tube, which is SMALLER than int_STRAT / int_S — an
INVALID upper bound in the direction needed. PE.2(a)'s section-5
alternative, the "beta-free tube volume v(N, delta)"
[lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:709-712], has the identical defect. I therefore
do NOT consume (DEN); I consume only PE.2(a)'s (NUM) shape and (UP-QUAD),
and I write a NEW S-LOCALIZED denominator display below. This is an
ORIGINAL display of this piece, flagged as such for the checker.

6.2 NUMERATOR. Slice STRAT by the label: STRAT = (union over nonzero
realizable j of {w_theta = k, w_phi = j}) union ({w_theta = k} inter
Delta_phi). Each slice is Borel (w_phi is integer-valued and locally
constant off Delta_phi, [la3-reader-packet-v1.md:55-56]); there are at
most N - 1 nonzero labels (section 4) plus one null face. On the |j| = 1
slices, and on all other pieces, (FLOOR) gives E_eps >= m_k + m_1(lambda)
pointwise; on |j| >= 2 the sharper floor m_k + 8 lambda j^2/N holds. In
the pattern of PE.2(a)'s numerator line, consumed verbatim —
  "integral_{B_out} e^{-beta E_eps} dx <= Leb(B_out) e^{-beta(S_k + c_H)}
   <= V_M e^{-beta(S_k + c_H)}, (NUM)" [lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:
   sections 0-1, cited at :1224 and :1132-1134] —
a pointwise level floor times the Lebesgue measure of the region gives

  int_STRAT e^{-beta E_eps} dx
     = sum_{j != 0} int_{w_phi = j} e^{-beta E_eps} dx      (Delta_phi is null)
     <= sum_{j != 0} Leb({w_theta=k, w_phi=j}) e^{-beta(m_k + F_j)},
        F_1 := m_1(lambda),  F_j := 8 lambda j^2/N for |j| >= 2,
     <= V_M ( sum_{j != 0} e^{-beta F_j} )  e^{-beta m_k}
     <= N V_M exp( -beta ( m_k + m_1(lambda) ) ),                   (NUM-STRAT)

using F_j >= m_1(lambda) for every j != 0 (Lemmas 4.2-4.3 and
(PHI-FLOOR-1)) and #{j != 0 realizable} <= N - 1 < N. V_M := Leb(M) =
(2 pi)^{2N}, beta-free. NOTE: the count N is crude on purpose — the
|j| >= 2 terms are individually exp(-beta 8 lambda j^2/N)-small and could
be summed geometrically, but N is beta-free and honest, and no exponent
weight rides on it.

6.3 DENOMINATOR, LOCALIZED ON S (NEW DISPLAY). Consume PE.2(a)'s
quadratic upper envelope verbatim:
  "E_eps(x) <= m_k + eps w_k + (L_eps/2) dist(x, G_k)^2   on U.  (UP-QUAD)"
  [lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:601],
valid on the tube U = T_{r0}(G_k), with L_eps from M5-DRIFT, verbatim
"|grad E_eps(x)|  <=  L_eps dist(x, G_k),   L_eps <= L + 8 eps,
grad E_eps  L_eps-Lipschitz on U" [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:1419], and
the ground level from M2P.1, verbatim "`grad E_eps = 0` on `G_k` for
EVERY eps" [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:1381] and "`e_0 := M_k(eps) = m_k +
eps w_k`" [:1377]. Standing requirement (inherited, same as PE.2(b) step
2.3): delta/4 <= r0, i.e. delta <= 4 r0.

Norm bookkeeping, made explicit because it is where the delta^2
coefficient comes from: "Tube radii and dist(., Z) are MAX NORM (as
everywhere in the corpus)" [lane-lp-product-saddle-v1.md:93]. S =
B^max_{delta/4}(g*) with g* in G_k, so every x in S has
dist_max(x, G_k) <= |x - g*|_max <= delta/4, hence
dist_euc(x, G_k) <= sqrt(2N) . delta/4 and
      (L_eps/2) dist_euc(x, G_k)^2 <= (L_eps/2)(2N)(delta/4)^2
                                    = L_eps N delta^2 / 16.
Therefore E_eps <= m_k + eps w_k + L_eps N delta^2/16 =: E_top on all of
S, and bounding the integrand below by its minimum over S,

  int_S e^{-beta E_eps} dx  >=  Leb(S) e^{-beta E_top}
     = (delta/2)^{2N} exp( -beta ( m_k + eps w_k + L_eps N delta^2/16 ) ),
                                                                  (DEN-S3)

where Leb(S) = (delta/2)^{2N} is the volume of the max-norm box of
half-side delta/4 in dimension 2N (delta small enough that the box
embeds in M — implied by delta <= 4 r0 <= inj(M), [lane-minmig-proofs-
v1.md:1375]). (DEN-S3) is BETA-FREE in its prefactor and holds for every
beta > 0; no Gaussian rescaling and hence NO beta^{N-1} enters. This is
the sole place the piece departs from PE.2(a)'s round-1 text, and the
departure is forced (section 6.1).

6.4 THE RATIO. Divide (NUM-STRAT) by (DEN-S3); m_k CANCELS exactly
(numerator and denominator both sit over the same theta-ground level):

  rho_beta(STRAT) / rho_beta(S)
     = ( int_STRAT e^{-beta E_eps} ) / ( int_S e^{-beta E_eps} )
     <= [ N V_M e^{-beta(m_k + m_1(lambda))} ]
        / [ (delta/2)^{2N} e^{-beta(m_k + eps w_k + L_eps N delta^2/16)} ]
     = N V_M (2/delta)^{2N}
         exp( -beta ( m_1(lambda) - eps w_k - L_eps N delta^2/16 ) ).

OUTPUT (the deliverable, in the mandated shape):

  rho_beta(STRAT) / rho_beta(S)
        <=  C(N, delta) . poly(beta) . exp( -beta ( m_1(lambda) - err ) ),
                                                                (R3-STRAT)
  C(N, delta) := N V_M (2/delta)^{2N} = N (4 pi/delta)^{2N},  beta-FREE,
  poly(beta)  ==  1  (no beta power at all),
  err(eps, delta) := eps w_k + L_eps N delta^2/16
                   = eps g(N) + O(N L_eps delta^2)   at k = 1.

The beta-free prefactor is legitimately of row type: the row allows
"<= T_row(eps, delta) exp(-beta(c_H/2 - err(delta))), T_row beta-free"
[lane-lp-product-saddle-v1.md:223-224].

------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. err IS err-CLASS: THE MARGIN ARITHMETIC
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Two summands, both honest.

(a) L_eps N delta^2/16. Vanishes under the mandated order of limits —
"beta -> infinity FIRST at fixed (eps, delta, h = delta/2) ... THEN
delta -> 0 (h -> 0)" [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3125]. Pure O(delta^2)
band, same class as PE.2(b)'s (DEN-S) err.

(b) eps w_k = eps g(N). This is the only eps cost in the exponent, and it
is the DENOMINATOR's cost (the true ground level is m_k + eps w_k), not a
numerator deficit — the numerator's eps cost was deleted in section 1. It
is N-UNIFORMLY compatible with the margin, and here is the exact reason.
The target margin is ADJ-2's identity, verbatim:
  "m_1 - c_H/2 = lambda g(N) - (1/8)( g(N) + 2 - S_k ) = g(N)( lambda -
   1/8 ) + ( S_k - 2 )/8."  [lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:730]
  "Both summands are STRICTLY POSITIVE for every N>=10, lambda>=1"
   [:731].
So m_1(lambda) - err > c_H/2 holds as soon as
      eps g(N) + O(N L_eps delta^2) < g(N)(lambda - 1/8) + (S_k - 2)/8,
for which a SUFFICIENT condition (drop the strictly positive
(S_k - 2)/8, divide by g(N) > 0, send delta -> 0 first) is simply
      eps  <  lambda - 1/8.
Since M2-PIN gives lambda > kappa = 1, every eps <= 7/8 works — and the
condition is N-FREE precisely because the eps cost eps g(N) and the
margin's leading term g(N)(lambda - 1/8) scale with the SAME factor
g(N). This is the eps-window the design already relies on in the sister
row: "the eps-window (~0.035 at eps = 0.05) cannot reach c_H/2 anywhere
in the eps_2-capped pinning range" [lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:109-111].
I state the exact inequality eps < lambda - 1/8 rather than asserting a
numeric cap on eps_2 valid for every N; see typed gaps.

FLAGSHIP CHECK (kappa = 1, N = 10, lambda = 1, eps = 0.05, delta -> 0),
all recomputed here: g(10) = 1.909830; m_k = 1.909830; m_1(lambda) =
1.909830; S_k = 2 + 8(1 - cos(pi/8)) = 2.608964; c_H = (m_k + 2 - S_k)/4
= 0.325217, c_H/2 = 0.162608; S_k + c_H - m_k = 1.024350;
m_1 - c_H/2 = g(10)(1 - 1/8) + (S_k - 2)/8 = 1.671101 + 0.076121 =
1.747222 > 0. Assembly margin min(S_k + c_H - m_k, m_1) - c_H/2 =
1.024350 - 0.162608 = 0.861742. err = eps g(10) = 0.095492 << 0.861742.
By contrast the DELETED design slack 2 eps N = 1.000000 EXCEEDS 0.861742
— confirming that deleting it (section 1) is not cosmetic but the
difference between a passing and a failing row.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. WHAT R3-ASM MAY CONSUME FROM THIS PIECE, AT EXACTLY THIS STRENGTH
------------------------------------------------------------------------
(FLOOR)     E_eps >= m_k + m_1(lambda) pointwise on
            STRAT = {w_theta = k} \ {w_phi = 0}. Unconditional on the
            flagship range (k = 1, N >= 10, lambda > kappa, eps >= 0).
            Sharper on |j| >= 2: E_eps >= m_k + 8 lambda j^2/N.
(R3-STRAT)  rho_beta(STRAT)/rho_beta(S) <= N (4 pi/delta)^{2N}
            exp(-beta(m_1(lambda) - err)), err = eps g(N) +
            L_eps N delta^2/16, prefactor beta-free, poly(beta) == 1.
(DEN-S3)    int_S e^{-beta E_eps} >= (delta/2)^{2N}
            exp(-beta(m_k + eps w_k + L_eps N delta^2/16)) — the
            S-LOCALIZED denominator, NEW here, REQUIRED as the
            substitute for PE.2(a)'s (DEN) in the doorway leg of R3-ASM
            as well (the identical direction defect applies there).

R3-ASM converts (R3-STRAT) into an occupation ratio by SR-PE1's
(KAC-RATIO) at B := STRAT, B' := S — an identity on the PLAIN Palm
S-return cycle, OBJECT-PE1, with operator E_{Palm}. That is NOT R5a's
delayed round, and this piece performs no such conversion.

### STRAT round 3 — typed gaps

GAP-R3STRAT-DELTATHETA (scope boundary of the delivered floor; NOT a hole in the proof, but it must be carried by R3-ASM). (FLOOR) is proved on STRAT = {w_theta = k} \ {w_phi = 0}, which by construction lives OFF Delta_theta (w_theta is defined only off the theta-antipodal set, la3-reader-packet-v1.md:55-56). On {w_theta undefined} = Delta_theta the only available floor is the barrier J_kappa >= 2 kappa ("LEMMA B.1 (barrier).  `J_mu >= 2 mu` on `Delta`", la3-reader-packet-v1.md:355-356), and 2 kappa need NOT exceed m_k + m_1(lambda) (at N = 10, lambda = 1: 2 vs 3.8197). I therefore do NOT claim (FLOOR) on Delta_theta. What IS available and stated: Delta_theta is a finite union of smooth codimension-1 tori, hence Lebesgue-null, hence rho_beta-null, and by the named transition-density import it carries zero expected occupation for the nondegenerate diffusion. R3-ASM must use the null-mass route (not a level route) for Delta_theta, and must note that a Delta_theta hit "IS the renewal's target event" (lane-lp-product-saddle-v1.md:219), i.e. it terminates the round rather than contributing outside-R_0 time. NOT closed here.

GAP-R3STRAT-DENNEW (originality flag, addressed to the checker; NOT inherited). (DEN-S3) — int_S e^{-beta E_eps} >= (delta/2)^{2N} exp(-beta(m_k + eps w_k + L_eps N delta^2/16)) — is a NEW display written in this piece. It is NOT PE.2(a)'s (DEN) "Z_beta >= c(N) beta^{-(N-1)} e^{-beta(m_k + eps w_k)}" (lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:637), which is a lower bound on the FULL tube integral and therefore DOMINATES int_S; substituting it would produce int_STRAT/int_tube < int_STRAT/int_S, an INVALID upper bound. PE.2(a)'s section-5 "beta-free tube volume v(N, delta)" alternative (lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:709-712) has the identical defect. (DEN-S3) consumes only PE.2(a)'s (UP-QUAD) (:601) plus the corpus max-norm convention (lane-lp:93) and the max-to-Euclidean conversion dist_euc <= sqrt(2N) dist_max; it requires delta/4 <= r0 and delta small enough that the max-norm box of half-side delta/4 embeds. GAP-R3STRAT-EPSWINDOW (a one-line arithmetic check I state rather than assert). The exponent margin needs eps w_k < m_1(lambda) - c_H/2, for which a sufficient N-FREE condition is eps < lambda - 1/8 (divide ADJ-2's identity m_1 - c_H/2 = g(N)(lambda - 1/8) + (S_k - 2)/8, lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:730, by g(N) > 0 and drop the positive second summand). Given M2-PIN lambda > kappa = 1 this holds for every eps <= 7/8, and it is N-uniform precisely because eps w_k = eps g(N) and the margin's leading term g(N)(lambda - 1/8) carry the SAME factor g(N). I do NOT assert a numeric bound on eps_2 valid for all N: the corpus caps I located are eps_2 := min(epsilon_1(eps'_0) ...) (lane-lp-product-saddle-v1.md:182) and "eps < epsilon_0 <= (2 kappa - m_k)/w_k" (lane-lp-product-saddle-v1.md:408-409), the latter of which does not tighten uniformly as N grows. The operative design scale is eps = 0.05 (lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:109-110), far inside eps < 7/8. TYPED so the assembler can discharge it against whichever eps_2 ledger entry is active, in one line.

DELTA-PE1-DELAYED / OBJECT DISCIPLINE (inherited; owned by R3-ASM and R3-PE3p, NOT closed here). This piece delivers a STATIC Gibbs-mass ratio rho_beta(STRAT)/rho_beta(S). Converting it into an occupation ratio is SR-PE1's (KAC-RATIO) "E_{Palm}[ V_B ] / E_{Palm}[ V_{B'} ] = rho_beta(B)/rho_beta(B')" (lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:1917), an identity on OBJECT-PE1 = the PLAIN Palm S-return cycle under the Palm entrance law rho_S^Palm. R5a's round (terminus T_i = min(D(sigma_{i-1}), L_i), lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3044-3048) is a DIFFERENT stopping object, and the round-1 typed deltas DELTA-PE1-ENTRANCE and DELTA-PE1-DELAYED are exactly the two transfers required (Palm-averaged => conditional on F_{sigma_{i-1}} uniform over starts in S; plain S-return cycle => delayed round). I perform NEITHER transfer and append NO uniformity qualifier. Consequently this piece makes NO per-cycle and NO per-round occupation claim, and there is no aggregate/per-round conflation risk inside it.

NO OTHER GAPS. (FLOOR) is unconditional on the flagship range: the |j| = 1 leg rests on the machine-sealed ridge law scoped by C1-SUB(1) = g(N) < 2 (lambda-free), the |j| >= 2 leg is elementary and needs NO admissibility condition at all, the Delta_phi face carries the strictly higher barrier floor 2 lambda > m_1(lambda), and the coupling contributes with the correct sign (W* >= 0) so no eps deficit enters the numerator. The design's "sum over admissible j != 0" is REPLACED by a sum over EVERY realizable j (|j| < N/2 is forced off Delta_phi), so no sector of the stratum is silently dropped. No independence claim, no conditional expectation, no reachability/basin/dwell/entry claim, no exit-time bound in either direction, no physics vocabulary.
