5. (PE3p.3) THE DOORWAY FUNNEL, WITH THE L_i READING DECLARED
========================================================================
THE L_i READING, DECLARED (round-3 MINOR, cured). R5a offers two readings of a
theta-label change: the literal one at :3044, "L_i := inf{ s > sigma_{i-1} :
w_theta(X_s) != k }", under which a Delta_theta touch (where w_theta is
undefined, hence "!= k") FIRES L_i; and the standing-setting one at :3001, "a
theta-label change is the first hit of a different open theta-sector across
Delta_theta, i.e. tau_change^theta", under which a touch-and-return does NOT
fire L_i. I ADOPT THE :3001 READING - the conservative one for me, since it
makes the round longer and the occupation larger. I then verify the lemma BOTH
WAYS, and the Delta_theta trace is carried INSIDE the statement.

LEMMA PE3p.3 (DOORWAY FUNNEL). Let x in S, T = min(D(0), L),
   tau_lev := inf{ s >= 0 : E_eps(X_s) >= S_k + c_H }.
Then, up to a set of times of ZERO Lebesgue measure a.s. (the Delta_theta
trace), every s in [0, T) with X_s not in R_0 satisfies tau_lev <= s. Hence
   E_x[ integral_0^{T wedge t} 1_{M\R_0}(X_s) ds ]
        = E_x[ 1_{tau_lev <= t} integral_{tau_lev}^{T wedge t} 1_{M\R_0} ds ]
   for every t, and in particular the outside-R_0 occupation of the round
   vanishes on {tau_lev >= T}.

PROOF. Fix s < T with X_s not in R_0, and suppose first X_s is not on
Delta_theta. Since s < T <= L, under the :3001 reading the path has not crossed
into a different open theta-sector, and the sectors are open
[la3-reader-packet-v1.md:55-56]; hence w_theta(X_s) = k. Three exhaustive cases.
 (a) E_eps(X_s) > S_k + c_H: then tau_lev <= s directly.
 (b) w_phi(X_s) = j != 0: the start x in S has w_phi = 0 (Lemma PE3p.2(iii)(b)),
     w_phi is locally constant off Delta [la3:55-56], so by path continuity
     there is s' in (0, s] with X_{s'} in Delta_phi; case (c) applies at s'.
 (c) X_s (resp. X_{s'}) in Delta_phi: "LEMMA B.1 (barrier).  `J_mu >= 2 mu` on
     `Delta`." [la3-reader-packet-v1.md:355-356] gives J_lambda >= 2 lambda; the
     theta-label being k, "[STD]   sector minimum: J >= m_k on the winding-k
     sector" [gate-v17-la2f-brief-lt-v1.md:54-55] gives J_kappa >= m_k; and
     "`E_eps = E_0 + eps W*`, `W* >= 0`" [lane-lp:85-86] has the correct sign.
     Hence E_eps >= m_k + 2 lambda >= m_k + 2 kappa = S_k + 4 c_H > S_k + c_H,
     using M2-PIN and the ACTIVE ledger branch c_H = (m_k + 2 kappa - S_k)/4
     [lane-lp:153-156; active on all N >= 10, lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:297-300
     per AM-R4-6]. So tau_lev <= s' <= s.
THE Delta_theta TRACE. The remaining times are those with X_s in Delta_theta.
Delta_theta is a finite union of smooth codimension-1 tori, hence Lebesgue-null;
by SR-DENS the law of X_u has a density w.r.t. Lebesgue for every u > 0, so
P(X_u in Delta_theta) = 0 for every u > 0, and by Fubini
E[ integral_0^infinity 1_{Delta_theta}(X_s) ds ] = 0. This is verbatim the
mechanism AM-R4-1 installs and AM-R4-2 places INSIDE a statement rather than
beside it; I do the same here. Hence the trace contributes zero to every
occupation EXPECTATION below, which is the only use made of the lemma.
VERIFICATION UNDER THE OTHER READING. Under the literal :3044 reading a
Delta_theta touch fires L, so s < T <= L excludes X_s in Delta_theta outright
and the trace clause is vacuous; cases (a)-(c) are unchanged. So the lemma holds
under BOTH readings, with the trace clause needed only under :3001. QED.

READING. On R5a's terminus the ONLY way to accrue outside-R_0 time is to climb
the LEVEL to the doorway S_k + c_H. The theta-label exit is not an exit that
accrues time - IT IS THE TERMINUS (I4), exactly as the ROW says: "a Delta_theta
hit IS the renewal's target event" [lane-lp:219]. The Delta_phi exit is
level-blocked, again as the ROW says: "Delta_phi is level-blocked inside R_0 by
the c_H ledger" [lane-lp:218-219]. This is the object-level reason the ridge law
is NOT load-bearing here (Section 6.4).

========================================================================
6. (PE3p.4) THE FIRST-WINDOW CHARGE
========================================================================
6.1 WHY A CHARGE IS UNAVOIDABLE, AND WHY NO LD UPPER BOUND EXISTS. The integrand
is bounded by 1 per unit time, so any decomposition at a horizon t_0 pays at
most t_0 on the first window; but T_row must be beta-free against
exp(-beta(c_H/2 - err)), so an ADDITIVE beta-free t_0 destroys the row for every
t_0 > 0. The [0,t_0] outside occupation must itself be exponentially small. The
only large-deviation tools in the corpus are the FW LOWER halves SR-T2
[lane-c-exit-time-lower-bound-v1.md:51-96] and SR-T3
[lane-c-sector-persistence-readout-theorem-v1.md:30-51], which cannot bound an
escape probability from ABOVE; every other allowed source is a FLOOR (L1/L1'/L2,
M5-MAIN, M3-GS, R5b §3), a determinism (M2P.5), an identity (SR-PE1) or a static
ratio (PE.2(a), R3-STRAT). I assert NO large-deviation upper bound. This is
LENS-R3-9's diagnosis, adopted; its CONSTRUCTIVE ROUTE is executed next.

6.2 LEMMA PE3p.4 (FIRST-WINDOW CHARGE). Put M_2^eps := sup_M |Delta E_eps|,
finite, the corpus's named constant class "M_2  := sup_M |Delta E|
(< infinity)" [lane-sh2local-proofs-v1.md:244], with the EXPLICIT beta-free
bound computed from the member form "[ENER]  E_eps = J_kappa(theta) +
J_lambda(phi) + eps W(theta, phi) with W = sum_i (1 - cos(d_i - e_i))"
[c7-la2f-brief-parity-artifact-v1.md:36-38]:
   Delta J_kappa = 2 kappa sum_i cos d_i,  Delta J_lambda = 2 lambda sum_i cos e_i,
   Delta W = 4 sum_i cos(d_i - e_i),   hence
   M_2^eps <= 2N(kappa + lambda) + 4 eps N      (beta-free).
Then for every t_0 > 0 and every y in M,
   P_y( tau_lev <= t_0 )  <=  exp( M_2^eps t_0 ) exp( -beta ( S_k + c_H
                                                    - E_eps(y) ) ),      (FW)
and consequently, by Lemma PE3p.3,
   E_y[ integral_0^{T wedge t_0} 1_{M\R_0}(X_s) ds ]  <=  t_0 . (FW).
PROOF. Set f := exp(beta E_eps) in C^infinity(M), bounded on the compact M.
   grad f = beta f grad E_eps,
   Delta f = f( beta^2 |grad E_eps|^2 + beta Delta E_eps ),
   L f = (1/beta) Delta f - grad E_eps . grad f
       = f( beta |grad E_eps|^2 + Delta E_eps ) - beta f |grad E_eps|^2
       = f . Delta E_eps  <=  M_2^eps f .
The |grad E_eps|^2 terms CANCEL EXACTLY, so M_2^eps is BETA-FREE. Put
Y_t := exp(-M_2^eps t) f(X_t). By SR-ITO,
   dY_t = e^{-M_2^eps t}[ (L f - M_2^eps f)(X_t) dt + sqrt(2/beta) grad f(X_t).dW_t ];
the drift is <= 0 and grad f is bounded on the compact M, so the stochastic
integral is a true martingale on [0,t_0] and Y is a supermartingale there. By
SR-OST at the BOUNDED stopping time tau_lev wedge t_0,
E_y[ Y_{tau_lev wedge t_0} ] <= Y_0 = f(y). Y >= 0, and on {tau_lev <= t_0}
continuity of E_eps o X gives E_eps(X_{tau_lev}) = S_k + c_H, so
Y_{tau_lev} >= e^{-M_2^eps t_0} e^{beta(S_k + c_H)}. Rearranging gives (FW). QED.

6.3 THE CHARGE FROM THE COLLAR BOUNDARY. For z in S^+, (E-TOP+) gives
E_eps(z) <= m_k + eps w_k + L_eps N delta^2/4, so
   sup_{z in S^+} P_z( tau_lev <= t_0 )
     <= e^{M_2^eps t_0} exp( -beta ( S_k + c_H - m_k - eps w_k
                                     - L_eps N delta^2/4 ) ).           (FW-C)
The prefactor is BETA-FREE - the only thing the row requires of T_row
[lane-lp:223-224] - and the exponent is EXACTLY the doorway exponent
S_k + c_H - m_k less the err budget. Section 8 verifies it against c_H/2.
WHAT (FW-C) IS AND IS NOT. It is the sharp bound on the DETERMINISTIC-HORIZON
instance of GAP-PE3P-DOORREACH. It is NOT a bound on P_z(tau_lev < T), because
T is random and the discount e^{M_2^eps t} is only useful for beta-free t. That
extension is GAP-PE3P-DOORREACH (Section 9) and is the piece's principal open
item. I say this here so no reader takes Section 8 for more than it is.

6.4 THE RIDGE LAW: IN THE DAG, NOT LOAD-BEARING, AND ITS ARITHMETIC CORRECTED
(single statement; the round-3 internal contradiction resolved). LENS-R3-9
prices a theta-label exit by the ridge law "`J >= phi_k(M_abs)` pointwise"
[lane-ls-label-sharpness-v1.md:278] and warns that without it the theta-exit
forces only J_kappa >= 2 kappa, exponent (2 - 1.9098)/2 = 0.045 < c_H/2. On
R5a's terminus that charge DOES NOT ARISE: by Lemma PE3p.3 and I4 the
theta-label exit IS the terminus and accrues no outside time. The ridge law is
nevertheless ENTERED IN THE DAG (I18) as the lens requires, and its arithmetic
is recorded as a robustness leg with ONE CORRECTION: a Delta_theta hit forces
the max absolute bond to pi, not pi - a_k, so the level it forces is phi_k(pi),
NOT S_k. From "phi_k(m) := kappa [(1 - cos m) + (N - 1)(1 - cos((2 pi k -
m)/(N - 1)))]" [lane-ls:205] at k = 1, m = pi:
   phi_1(pi) = 2 + (N-1)(1 - cos(pi/(N-1)))  <  S_1 = 2 + (N-2)(1 - cos(pi/(N-2))),
since "phi(s) := (1 - cos s)/s - STRICTLY INCREASING on (0, 2]"
[lane-lt-label-tower-v1.md:113-115] and pi/(N-1) < pi/(N-2). The residual mean
at m = pi is r = pi/(N-1) <= pi/9 = 0.349, inside the ridge law's explicit range
condition "r in [0, 3/4]" [lane-ls:280-286], so the law applies. At N = 10,
kappa = 1: phi_1(pi) = 2.542767 against S_k = 2.608964, and the honest
theta-exit robustness margin is
   phi_1(pi) - m_k - c_H = 2.542767 - 1.909830 - 0.325217 = 0.307720 > 0,
against the 0.373910 the lens's S_k-based figure would give.
DIRECTION, STATED ONCE AND CONSISTENTLY (round-3 contradiction cured): the
corrected level is LOWER, so the ROBUSTNESS MARGIN OF THIS NON-LOAD-BEARING LEG
IS SMALLER than the lens states. The DELIVERED bound is UNCHANGED, because the
leg is not load-bearing. The round-3 sentence "it makes the delivered bound
STRONGER, not weaker" is WITHDRAWN as false. The margin is increasing in N
(0.307720, 0.442360, 0.558320, 1.009350, 1.602090, 1.981500 at
N = 10, 11, 12, 18, 46, 1000).

========================================================================
7. (PE3p.5) THE BLOCK-RENEWAL LEMMA AND THE TWO-FACTOR REDUCTION
   (the honest replacement for the withdrawn Doeblin lemma)
========================================================================
7.0 WHAT IS WITHDRAWN, AND WHY. Round 3's Lemma 6.5 assumed "(H3) K = S
(equivalently: the residual state is confined to S)". (H3) is FALSE on R5a's
terminus: on {T > t_0} with theta^+(0) <= t_0, "D(t) := inf{ s >= theta^+(t) :
X_s in S }" [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3016] FORCES X_{t_0} not in S, so the
(1-c) residual mass sits OFF S - possibly on "the G_{k,j} = C_k x C_j^phi
pinning tori ... REAL traps in the excursion region" [lane-lp:226-229].
Everything the round-3 body derived from that lemma is WITHDRAWN. So is the
design's candidate route "the L1' pointwise minorization gives every start's
one-step law a density floor against Leb|_S, transferring the averaged bound to
a pointwise one at an exp(beta O(h^2)) cost; the transfer must be proved on
R5a's terminus, not asserted" [lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:92-96] IN ITS DOEBLIN
FORM (LENS-R3-11's restatement): a one-step Doeblin inequality on S is not
available on this object. The clause "must be proved on R5a's terminus, not
asserted" is doing its work: the terminus is what breaks it.
A SECOND, INDEPENDENT STRUCTURAL FINDING, PRESERVED FROM ROUND 3 (it is correct
and it closes off a family of future routes): the delayed-return chain
{X_{sigma_j}} is a chain on S whose steps are FIRST S-entrances after a collar
excursion, so by path continuity X_{sigma_j} lies on the topological BOUNDARY of
S a.s.; its Palm entrance law is therefore carried by boundary-S, a Lebesgue-null
set, and NO minorization of that chain against Leb|_S can hold. Any future
Leb-to-Palm route must minorize against a measure carried by boundary-S.

7.1 THE ADMISSIBLE FLOOR (the input that replaces Doeblin). Read R5b §3 as the
POINTWISE statement it is - a bound on a start-point functional, converted to
its conditional form by the very template of R5a §5 [:3064]:
   (P-SUB)  inf_{z in R_0} P_z( the round terminates within T_sub ) >= p_sub,
   T_sub := T_relax(eps,delta) + T_reloc(eps) + T*(h), T*(h) := n + 1,
   n := ceil(4 pi sqrt(2N)/delta), all three constituents BETA-FREE
   [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3230];
   "termination" = "Succ_m := { a delayed S-return D(sigma_{i-1}) into S occurs
   during (alpha_m, alpha_m + T_sub] } union { w_theta has changed by time
   alpha_m + T_sub }" [:3241];
   p_sub = c(delta,h) exp( -beta ( Gamma(h) + gamma_2 eps^2 + err(delta) ) ) > 0,
   Gamma(h) := Gamma_orb(h) + Gamma_dens(h) = 6 C_1 D_G h + 2 C_2 h^2 = O(h)
   [:3274]; "The floor is UNIFORM over every H_m-measurable start in R_0 - core,
   band, and sub-cap alike" [:3276]; valid for beta >= beta_0(h) = O(h^{-2})
   [:3276; XF A3, lane-sh2local:33-35].
THIS IS A FLOOR, NOT A MOMENT. That is the whole point of the re-route: the
round-3 checker's demolition of the (D-in) route - "a bound on E[duration], with
no exponential moment ... Optimising K leaves O(1/beta) - POLYNOMIAL" - is a
demolition of FIRST-MOMENT compositions. A uniform per-window termination FLOOR
gives a GEOMETRIC tail directly, with no optimisation and no moment.
NON-CIRCULARITY OF THIS EDGE, RE-STATED. (P-SUB) is the display at :3268-3276
together with the composed-pass trichotomy at :3252-3259. It does NOT include
the "Recovery exhaustiveness" paragraph at :3261 (which cites R5b §7 = my target
row) nor R5b §4's induction (which routes through :3261). I re-derive the count
myself in 7.2 without either.

7.2 LEMMA PE3p.5 (BLOCK RENEWAL). Fix x in S and work on the post-collar path.
Define, with T := min(D(0), L) the round terminus,
   xi_0 := theta^+(0),   xi_{j+1} := inf{ s >= xi_j + T_sub : X_s in R_0 } wedge T
                                     (j >= 0),
   V_j  := integral_{xi_j wedge T}^{xi_{j+1}} 1_{M\R_0}(X_s) ds ,
   B_bar := sup_{z in R_0} E_z[ integral_0^{(T_sub + H_{R_0} o vartheta_{T_sub})
                                 wedge T} 1_{M\R_0}(X_s) ds ] ,
where H_{R_0} is the hitting time of R_0. Then
 (a) each xi_j is an (F_t)-stopping time and X_{xi_j} in R_0 on {xi_j < T}
     (for j = 0 by Lemma PE3p.2(iii), for j >= 1 by definition);
 (b) P( xi_{j+1} < T | F_{xi_j} ) <= (1 - p_sub) 1_{xi_j < T}  a.s., hence
     P( xi_j < T ) <= (1 - p_sub)^j for every j >= 0;
 (c) E( V_j | F_{xi_j} ) <= B_bar . 1_{xi_j < T}  a.s.;
 (d) consequently, for every x in S,
        W( X_{theta^+(0)} )-expectation obeys
        u(x)  =  E_x[ sum_{j>=0} V_j ]  <=  B_bar / p_sub .            (BLK)
PROOF. (a) Hitting times of the closed set R_0 by the continuous X after a
stopping time are stopping times [:3035]; the case j = 0 is Lemma
PE3p.2(iii)(a)-(c). (b) {xi_{j+1} < T} is contained in {T > xi_j + T_sub}, i.e.
in the complement of the R5b success event over the window [xi_j, xi_j + T_sub].
By strong Markov at xi_j and (P-SUB) applied at the R_0-valued X_{xi_j}, that
success event has conditional probability >= p_sub on {xi_j < T}. Induct. (c) is
strong Markov at xi_j plus the definition of B_bar (the block's outside time is
accrued during the window plus during the ensuing wait for R_0, and the block
ends at the first R_0-re-entry after the window or at T, whichever is first).
(d) The blocks partition [theta^+(0), T); by Lemma PE3p.2(iii) nothing accrues
before theta^+(0); {xi_j < T} in F_{xi_j}; so by the tower property
   u(x) = E_x[ sum_j V_j ] = sum_j E_x[ 1_{xi_j<T} E( V_j | F_{xi_j} ) ]
        <= B_bar sum_j P_x( xi_j < T ) <= B_bar sum_j (1-p_sub)^j = B_bar/p_sub.
All terms are non-negative, so no integrability hypothesis is needed and the
inequality is valid even if some block never terminates. QED.

NO ROUND LENGTH ANYWHERE. (BLK) contains no expectation of T, no exponential
moment of T, and no duration bound of any kind. What it contains is a count of
beta-free windows, geometric by a FLOOR. This is the verification the lead asked
for: GAP-PE3P-ROUNDLEN as typed in round 3 asked for the wrong object and is
DELETED. Nothing in this body asks for a round length.

7.3 THE TWO-FACTOR REDUCTION. Combine the funnel with (BLK). By Lemma PE3p.3
the outside occupation vanishes on {tau_lev >= T}; by strong Markov at tau_lev
(a stopping time) and Door := {E_eps = S_k + c_H, w_theta = k, w_phi = 0}
subset R_0 (R_0 is defined by E_eps <= S_k + c_H, so the doorway level belongs
to R_0),
   u(x) = E_x[ 1_{tau_lev < T} . E( residual outside occupation | F_{tau_lev} ) ]
        <= P_x( tau_lev < T ) . sup_{y in Door} E_y[ integral_0^{T}1_{M\R_0} ]
        <= P_x( tau_lev < T ) . ( B_bar / p_sub ) ,                    (RED)
the last step being (BLK) applied from y in Door subset R_0 (with xi_0 := 0
there, no collar step needed). Note X_{tau_lev} lies in Door with w_phi = 0:
at the FIRST time E_eps = S_k + c_H the path can be neither on Delta_phi nor in
a j != 0 slice, since those force E_eps >= m_k + 2 lambda >= S_k + 4 c_H.
Taking the supremum over x in S and combining with Lemma PE3p.1:
   (COND*) HOLDS AS SOON AS
     [ sup_{z in dS^+} P_z(tau_lev < T) ] . B_bar / p_sub
                     <= T_row exp(-beta(c_H/2 - err)).                  (REQ)
This is the piece's structural deliverable: the entire residual burden of ROW
PROD-EXCURSION-COND is two scalars, both on ONE object (O_R5a), with an
err-class amplification 1/p_sub that is DERIVED, not assumed.
INTERFACE HONESTY (round-3 overclaim withdrawn). I make NO claim that the R5a
factor and the Palm-cycle factor are "the same interface Door shared verbatim".
They are not: the R5a factor is a SUPREMUM over Door, while the Palm delayed-
cycle analogue is an AVERAGE against the delayed entrance law, which Section 7.0
shows is carried by boundary-S and incomparable to Lebesgue. The two objects
funnel through the same SET; that is a weaker and true statement, and it is the
one I make.

8. (PE3p.6) THE BUDGET - THE ARITHMETIC OF (REQ), DISPLAYED
========================================================================
READ THIS FIRST. Section 8 is the arithmetic of the PRODUCT in (REQ). Its two
factors are TYPED (Section 9). Section 8 therefore verifies that the exponents
CLEAR c_H/2 at the strengths those gaps are typed at; it does NOT bound
sup_S u. No reader should schedule a round on the basis of Section 8 alone.

8.1 THE EXPONENT LEDGER. At the strengths of Section 9,
   P_z(tau_lev < T)  <=  C_1(eps,delta) exp( -beta ( S_k + c_H - m_k
                                     - eps w_k - L_eps N delta^2/4 ) ),
   B_bar             <=  C_2(eps,delta) exp( +beta . err_B(eps,delta) ),
   1/p_sub           =   c(delta,h)^{-1} exp( +beta ( Gamma(h) + gamma_2 eps^2
                                     + err(delta) ) )  [I8, :3274],
so the exponent of the product is
   ( S_k + c_H - m_k ) - eps w_k - L_eps N delta^2/4
        - Gamma(h) - gamma_2 eps^2 - err(delta) - err_B ,
and (REQ) is the requirement that this EXCEED c_H/2.

8.2 THE CLOSED FORM AND THE MARGIN. With the active branch
c_H = (m_k + 2 kappa - S_k)/4,
   ( S_k + c_H - m_k ) - c_H/2  =  (7/8)( S_k - m_k ) + kappa/4 ,      (MRG)
STRICTLY POSITIVE for every N and every lambda, LAMBDA-FREE (the doorway is a
theta-side level), and INCREASING in N because "S_1 - m_1 INCREASES toward
2 kappa (0.70 kappa at N = 10; 0.882 at N = 12; 1.295 at N = 20)"
[lane-lt-label-tower-v1.md:116-118], with S_k > m_k by PROD-SHELL
[lane-lt:106-109]. Numerically (kappa = 1): 0.861742 at N = 10; 0.946990 at
N = 11; 1.021520 at N = 12; 1.319160 at N = 18; 1.723200 at N = 46; 1.987050 at
N = 1000. Worst cell on the flagship range: N = 10.
CROSS-CHECK AGAINST THE SIBLING. This is R3-ASM's Regime-B closed form
"Delta_door - c_H/2 = ( 7( S_k - m_k ) + 2 kappa )/8 ,   LAMBDA-FREE"
[lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:5621] - the same identity. Consistency with the
sibling is a check, not an input.

8.3 THE eps CONDITION. (MRG) must absorb eps w_k = eps g(N). Since g(N)
decreases in N and (MRG) exceeds kappa/4 for every N, the N-FREE sufficient
condition is eps < kappa/(4 g(10)) = 0.130906; a fortiori eps < 1/8 suffices on
all N >= 10 (eps g(10) <= 0.238729 < 0.25 <= (MRG)). The cell-wise cap is
eps < (MRG)/g(N) = 0.451214 at N = 10 - which is EXACTLY R3-ASM's binding
condition "(EPS-2-ASM)   eps < 0.4512 kappa-units, N-uniformly on the flagship
range" [lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:5680-5682], reproduced here independently
because the doorway leg is what binds in both. The operative design scale
eps = 0.05 [lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:109-111] gives eps g(10) = 0.095492
against 0.861742.

8.4 THE AMPLIFIED-TRANSFER BUDGET (LENS-R3-11, in its corrected form). The lens
asked for the transfer cost to be shown as an AMPLIFICATION, not an addition,
and for the resulting smallness condition to be displayed. In this route the
amplification is 1/p_sub, whose exponent is Gamma(h) + gamma_2 eps^2 +
err(delta) with Gamma(h) = Gamma_orb(h) + Gamma_dens(h) = 6 C_1 D_G h + 2 C_2 h^2
= O(h) [I8 :3274; I12 :1713]. Note this is the SAME err-class as the lens's
Doeblin 1/c, and for the same reason - it is built from the M5 orbit chain and
the L1' base-ball density - but it is O(h) = O(delta), not merely O(h^2),
because the ORBIT CHAIN, not L1' alone, is what makes the floor uniform over
R_0. With h = delta/2 the explicit smallness condition to display is
   Gamma(delta/2) + gamma_2 eps^2 + err(delta) + err_B + L_eps N delta^2/4
        <  (7/8)( S_k - m_k ) + kappa/4 - eps g(N) ,                   (SML)
whose right side at the flagship (10, 1, 1, 0.05) is
   0.861742 - 0.095492 = 0.766250 .
RECONCILIATION WITH THE LENS'S OWN FIGURE. LENS-R3-11 computes the available
slack as 0.187 from "(S_k-m_k)/2 = 0.350 vs c_H/2 = 0.163" and asks for
C_2(delta^2 + h^2) < 0.187. That figure prices the THETA-EXIT branch via the
ridge law. On R5a's terminus the theta-exit is the terminus (Section 5), so the
binding branch is the DOORWAY, and the correct slack is 0.766250, four times
larger. The lens's condition is therefore satisfied a fortiori; I display the
doorway-based one because it is this route's actual budget. The left side of
(SML) is O(delta) and beta-free, so (SML) is satisfiable and COMPATIBLE WITH THE
DECLARED ORDER OF LIMITS - verbatim "beta -> infinity FIRST at fixed (eps, delta,
h = delta/2) ... THEN delta -> 0 (h -> 0) ... THEN the eps-window is read"
[lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3125].

8.5 THE beta PREFACTORS, ABSORBED (AM-R4-15). Two sub-exponential factors
appear: the beta^{-N} inside 1/p_sub (from L1's m(beta,h) = c_0' beta^N
exp(-beta Gamma_dens(h)), I8/I11) which only HELPS, and, if R3-ASM's landed
output is used as a cross-check, its single factor beta from (R3-SOJ.a)/
(R3-SOJ.b-prime). Per AM-R4-15, verbatim "beta <= e^{beta eta} for every eta > 0
eventually, so the beta factor is absorbable into err; the final assembly makes
this absorption explicit when it states the row" - I make it explicit here in
the sharp form: with 2 mu := (the Section 8.1 exponent) - c_H/2 > 0,
   sup_{beta >= 0} beta e^{-beta mu} = 1/(e mu) ,   hence
   T(N,delta) . beta . e^{-beta(c_H/2 + 2 mu)} <= [T(N,delta)/(e mu)] e^{-beta c_H/2},
so T_row := T(N,delta)/(e mu) is BETA-FREE and the row's literal shape
"<= T_row(eps, delta) exp(-beta(c_H/2 - err(delta))), T_row beta-free"
[lane-lp:222-224] is met with err(delta) taken to be 0 in the exponent - the
margin is cleared outright, not spent. This is the same absorption R3-ASM
performs at its Section 9 [lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:5697-5706]; I reproduce it
because my prefactor is a different one.

8.6 THE STRATUM LEG AND THE SIBLING EXPONENT (no silent strengthening). Where
the w_phi != 0 stratum enters (through Door's complement in the assembly view),
the governing exponent is R3-STRAT's, consumed BY ITS LANDED NAME at its LANDED
strength: "(FLOOR)   E_eps  >=  m_k + m_1(lambda)" on
STRAT = {w_theta = k} \ {w_phi = 0} [lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:4905-4907],
together with (NUM-STRAT) [:4991] over (DEN-S3) [:5025]. I RECORD EXPLICITLY, as
the round-3 checker required, that this LANDED (FLOOR) already carries no
"- 2 eps N" deficit, so consuming it in this form is NOT a strengthening beyond
the sibling's delivered strength; the design's collapse-item-(2) wording with
"- 2 eps N" is superseded by AM-R4-7, which records that the deletion "is
correct mathematics and a genuine sharpening, but it is NOT the difference
between a passing and a failing row". I make no use of the deletion in any

( S_k - 2 )/8" [lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:730], = 1.747222 at (10, 1).

8.7 NO AGGREGATE / PER-ROUND CONFLATION. Everything above is PER ROUND on
O_R5a. E[N] and the Wald tower live at R5a §7 and are NOT consumed (C3). No
factor exp(beta(S_k - m_k)) appears anywhere. The carried exponent is the

        <= C_1(eps,delta) exp( -beta ( S_k + c_H - m_k - eps w_k
                                       - L_eps N delta^2/4 ) ),  C_1 beta-free,

THEM: (i) the supermartingale discount e^{M_2^eps t} is useless for

EXACT REQUIRED STRENGTH: sup_{z in boundary-S^+} P_z(tau_lev < T) <= C_1(eps,delta) exp(-beta(S_k + c_H - m_k - eps w_k - L_eps N delta^2/4)), C_1 beta-free, tau_lev the doorway-level hitting time, T = min(D(0), L). PROVED HERE: the deterministic-horizon instance (FW-C), sup_{z in S^+} P_z(tau_lev <= t_0) <= e^{M_2^eps t_0} exp(-beta(S_k + c_H - m_k - eps w_k - L_eps N delta^2/4)) for every beta-free t_0, at exactly the required exponent. MISSING: the extension from a beta-free horizon to the random terminus. THREE COMPOSITIONS EXPLICITLY RULED OUT (so nobody repeats them): (i) horizon optimisation fails because the discount e^{M_2^eps t} is useless for t >> 1 while the round runs ~ T_sub/p_sub = e^{+beta Gamma(h)} windows; (ii) a per-window union of (FW) over the block scaffold is VACUOUS because blocks j >= 1 start in R_0 but possibly AT the doorway level, where (FW) degenerates to >= 1 (the round-3 checker's objection (b), which applies to any window decomposition); (iii) no level-based superharmonic certificate exists: phi(E) needs phi''/phi' <= beta - Delta E/|grad E|^2, impossible at a local minimum of E. DISCHARGE ROUTES, RANKED, ALL COND-FREE: (R2-PRIMARY) capacity estimate for the reversible generator with the Gibbs weight — P_z(tau_Door < H_S) <= cap(B_rho(z),Door)/cap(B_rho(z),S); the UPPER capacity is elementary by the Dirichlet principle with a level-ramp test function on {E_eps in [S_k+c_H-1/beta, S_k+c_H]}, giving cap <= C beta^2 e^{-beta(S_k+c_H)}; the LOWER capacity needs a test flow (Thomson / Berman-Konsowa) and is the genuine new content; inputs are reversibility (SR-PE1.2, lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:1855-1885) plus a variational principle, no dynamical row, hence COND-free. (R3-ALT) an exponential-moment upgrade of the within-R_0 duration, which would rescue composition (i); strictly harder than (R2) and needs an R5a lead edit. (R4-ALT) the Palm route: R3-ASM's landed (ASM-PALM) bounds the averaged analogue outright, so the pointwise statement reduces to DELTA-PE1-ENTRANCE — the campaign's other open item, not a shortcut. TYPED, NOT ASSERTED.

GAP-PE3P-BLOCK (LOAD-BEARING; owned by this piece; NOT closed). AVAILABLE: the window part contributes at most the beta-free T_sub; the entire burden is the R_0-recovery part, i.e. the expected time above the doorway before re-entering R_0 or terminating the round. WHY GENUINELY OPEN: the ROW itself flags it — "the G_{k,j} = C_k x C_j^phi pinning tori ... are REAL traps in the excursion region - any bare probability-floor version of this row is FALSE at them, which is why the row carries the EXCURSION shape" (lane-lp-product-saddle-v1.md:226-230) — and no UPPER bound on a trap dwell is in the allowed list (SR-T2/SR-T3 are LOWER halves). ### AM-R5-2 (R4c MAJOR-2, the ground-collar fact - THE COLLAR GEOMETRY LEMMA)

The
delegation chain is DELETED and replaced by a self-contained
elementary lemma, consuming nothing but the max-norm definition of
the collar and the bond map:

  COLLAR GEOMETRY LEMMA. Let g* in G_k (theta-bonds all 2 pi k/N,
  phi-bonds all 0) and let x in S^+ = B_{delta/2}(g*) (max norm on
  T^{2N}). Every theta-bond satisfies |d_i(x) - 2 pi k/N| <=
  |x_{i+1} - g*_{i+1}| + |x_i - g*_i| <= delta, and every phi-bond
  |e_i(x)| <= delta. Hence if delta < pi - 2 pi k/N (at the
  flagship k = 1, N >= 10: delta < pi - 2 pi/N, and every corpus
  delta-threshold is far below this), then NO theta-bond reaches pi
  and NO phi-bond reaches pi: S^+ misses Delta_theta AND Delta_phi
  OUTRIGHT, by geometry. Consequently w_theta and w_phi are defined
  and continuous on the connected set S^+, and equal their values
  at g*: w_theta = k, w_phi = 0 on all of S^+. In particular
  S^+ subset {w_theta = k, w_phi = 0}, and with (UP-QUAD) at radius
  delta/2 (E_eps <= m_k + eps w_k + L_eps N delta^2/16 <=
  S_k + c_H for the corpus's delta, eps ranges), S^+ subset R_0.

# LEMMA PE-DOORREACH (closes GAP-PE3P-DOORREACH; checker SOUND)

(scalar-round grade: draft PROVED-WITH-TYPED-GAPS; checker SOUND)

LEMMA PE-DOORREACH (closes GAP-PE3P-DOORREACH at the exact required strength, modulo three typed hypothesis rows listed under typed_gaps).

=====================================================================
0. OBJECTS, SIGMA-FIELDS, STOPPING TIMES
=====================================================================
M := T^{2N}, n := 2N. E_eps : M -> R smooth. X = (X_t)_{t>=0} the diffusion with generator
  L u = (1/beta) Delta u - <grad E_eps, grad u>,
read off the adjoint recorded in ROW SR-PE1.2: "L^* u = (1/beta) Delta u + div(u grad E_eps)" [lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:1891]. (F_t)_{t>=0} := the usual augmentation of the natural filtration of X (right-continuous, P-complete); X has continuous paths, so hitting times of closed sets are (F_t)-stopping times.

Sets (all from the corpus, verbatim):
  S  := B_{delta/4}(g*),  S^+ := B_{delta/2}(g*)   ["S := B_{delta/4}(g*)" and collar "S^+ := B_{delta/2}(g*)", lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:130]
  Door := B_out = { x in T^{2N} : E_eps(x) >= S_k + c_H }   [lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:551]
  dS^+ := { x : dist(x,g*) = delta/2 }, g* in G_k.

Stopping times:
  tau_lev := inf{ t >= 0 : E_eps(X_t) = S_k + c_H },
  tau_Y   := inf{ t >= 0 : X_t in Y } for closed Y,
  T := min(D(0), L)  ["The round terminus is T = min(D(0), L) <= D(0)", lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:1385].

Weights and forms. mu(dx) := e^{-beta E_eps(x)} dx (unnormalized Gibbs weight; rho_beta = Z_beta^{-1} mu and L is rho_beta-reversible — ROW SR-PE1.2: "rho_beta(dx) = Z_beta^{-1} exp(-beta E_eps(x)) dx ... is the unique invariant probability of L, and L is rho_beta-reversible" [lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:1881-1885]). Put w := (1/beta) e^{-beta E_eps}, and for Lipschitz f
  D(f) := int_M w |grad f|^2 dx,   cap(Y,Y') := inf{ D(f) : f=1 on Y, f=0 on Y', f Lipschitz }.
Note div(w grad u) = mu * L u, which is the only reversibility input used; the construction is COND-free.

Constants (all beta-free): G := sup_M |grad E_eps| < inf, V_M := Leb(M), v_n and omega_{n-1} the Lebesgue volumes of the unit balls in R^n and R^{n-1}, L_eps <= L + 8 eps ["|grad E_eps(x)| <= L_eps dist(x, G_k), L_eps <= L + 8 eps, grad E_eps L_eps-Lipschitz on U", lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:612-613].

Scale choice: rho := 1/beta, ell := delta/2, A_tube := m_k + eps w_k + (25/128) L_eps delta^2,
  Xi := S_k + c_H - m_k - eps w_k - (N/4) L_eps delta^2,  s := (N/4 - 25/128) L_eps delta^2 > 0 (s > 0 for every N >= 1 since 32N/128 - 25/128 >= 7/128).
Threshold beta_* := max( 16/delta , 2/(S_k + c_H - A_tube) ), finite because S_k + c_H - m_k > 0 ["S_k + c_H - m_k = (3(S_k - m_k) + 2 kappa)/4 > 0", lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:725] and delta is small (H-SEP). All statements are for beta >= beta_*.

=====================================================================
1. REDUCTION TO A TWO-SET HARMONIC FUNCTION
=====================================================================
(1a) Regular doorway. E_eps is smooth; by SARD'S THEOREM (hypothesis row: E_eps in C^inf(M), M compact — met) almost every value is regular, so pick a regular value theta in [S_k + c_H - 1/beta, S_k + c_H] and set Door' := { E_eps >= theta } . Then Door subset Door', dDoor' is a smooth compact hypersurface, and by path continuity from a start z with E_eps(z) < theta,
  tau_lev = tau_Door <= tau_{Door'}   is FALSE in general, but the inclusion we need is the other one:
  { tau_lev < t } subset { tau_{Door'} < t } is also false. Correct direction: E_eps(z) < theta <= S_k+c_H, so by continuity the path attains the level S_k+c_H only after attaining theta if theta <= S_k+c_H; hence tau_{Door'} <= tau_lev, i.e. { tau_lev < t } subset { tau_{Door'} < t }. This is the direction used: enlarging the target set only increases the probability, and Door' ⊇ Door.

(1b) Round terminus. T <= D(0) [lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:1385], so { tau_lev < T } subset { tau_lev < D(0) }. Under (H-DELAY) (typed) D(0) is the first hitting time of S after at most one forced collar excursion. Set
  q := sup_{z in dS^+} P_z( tau_{Door'} < tau_S ).
If no further excursion is forced, sup_{z in dS^+} P_z(tau_lev < D(0)) <= q. If one is, decompose at the (F_t)-stopping times tau_S and sigma := inf{ t > tau_S : X_t in dS^+ }: on { tau_S < tau_{Door'} } the path must cross dS^+ before Door' (Door' ∩ B_delta(g*) = empty by (H-SEP)), so by the STRONG MARKOV PROPERTY (hypothesis row: X Feller, tau_S and sigma are (F_t)-stopping times — met) the post-sigma probability is <= q. Hence in both readings
  sup_{z in dS^+} P_z( tau_lev < T ) <= 2 q.                                   (RED)
So it suffices to bound q, and h(x) := P_x( tau_{Door'} < tau_S ) is the object of interest: h = 1 on Door', h = 0 on S, 0 <= h <= 1, and h is the classical solution of L h = 0 on Omega := M \ (S ∪ Door') by the PROBABILISTIC REPRESENTATION OF THE DIRICHLET PROBLEM (NAMED: Friedman, Stochastic Differential Equations and Applications I, Thm 6.5.1; equivalently Karatzas-Shreve Ch. 4.3. Hypothesis rows: (i) uniform ellipticity — met, diffusion matrix (1/beta) Id; (ii) smooth bounded coefficients on compact M — met; (iii) every boundary point regular — met, dS and dDoor' are smooth hypersurfaces so the exterior sphere condition holds; (iv) exit time a.s. finite — met by ellipticity plus compactness, cf. the positive Harris recurrence recorded at lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:1867-1879). h is smooth in Omega by interior elliptic regularity.

=====================================================================
2. THE CAPACITY RATIO (Green identity + maximum principle; no citation of a "capacity ratio lemma" is needed)
=====================================================================
Fix z in dS^+ and put A := closed B_rho(z), rho = 1/beta. For beta >= beta_*, dist(z,S) = delta/4 > 2rho, so A, S, Door' are pairwise disjoint compacts with smooth boundaries. Let h_A be the equilibrium potential of A against S ∪ Door': h_A = 1 on A, h_A = 0 on S ∪ Door', L h_A = 0 on Omega' := M \ (A ∪ S ∪ Door'), smooth up to the boundary (Schauder). Write e(dsigma) := w partial_{n_A} h_A dS on dA with n_A the normal pointing into A; e >= 0 and e(dA) = D(h_A) = cap(A, S ∪ Door').

(2a) Green's second identity on Omega' with the pair (h_A, h), using div(w grad u) = mu L u and L h_A = L h = 0 on Omega':
  0 = int_{dOmega'} w [ h_A partial_n h - h partial_n h_A ] dS.
On dS ∪ dDoor' one has h_A = 0, h = 1 on dDoor', h = 0 on dS, leaving + Fl := - int_{dDoor'} w partial_n h_A dS >= 0 (the flux of h_A absorbed at Door'). On dA one has h_A = 1, and int_{dA} w partial_{n_A} h dS = int_A div(w grad h) dx = int_A mu L h dx = 0 because h is L-harmonic inside A as well (A subset Omega). Hence
  int_{dA} h de = Fl.                                                          (FLUX-ID)

(2b) Fl <= cap(A, Door'). Let h_{A,D} be the equilibrium potential of A against Door' alone on D := M \ (A ∪ Door'). Extended by 0 across S, h_A attains a minimum on S, so L h_A >= 0 distributionally on D (a positive surface measure on dS), i.e. h_A is an L-subsolution on D. Then phi := h_{A,D} - h_A satisfies L phi <= 0 on D with phi = 0 on dA and on dDoor', so phi >= 0 by the MINIMUM PRINCIPLE for uniformly elliptic operators without zeroth-order term (NAMED: Gilbarg-Trudinger Thm 8.1; hypothesis rows: uniform ellipticity and bounded coefficients — met; c = 0 — met). Since phi = 0 on dDoor' and phi >= 0 inside, the inward normal derivative of phi at dDoor' is >= 0, so the flux absorbed at Door' obeys Fl(h_A) <= Fl(h_{A,D}) = cap(A, Door').

(2c) Monotonicity: cap(A, S ∪ Door') >= cap(A, S) (the admissible class shrinks). Combining with (FLUX-ID), with nu := e / e(dA) a PROBABILITY measure on dA,
  E_nu[h] = Fl / cap(A, S ∪ Door') <= cap(A, Door') / cap(A, S).               (RATIO)

=====================================================================
3. UPPER CAPACITY (Dirichlet principle, level ramp) — elementary
=====================================================================
Set a := theta - 1/beta and f(x) := median{0, (theta - E_eps(x)) * beta, 1}, i.e. f = 1 on { E_eps <= a }, f = 0 on Door', linear in E_eps on the ramp R := { a <= E_eps <= theta }. f is Lipschitz. On A ∪ S one has, by (UP-QUAD) below and (H-SEP), E_eps <= A_tube <= a for beta >= beta_*, so f = 1 there; f = 0 on Door'. Admissible for cap(A, Door') and for cap(S, Door'). On R, grad f = -beta grad E_eps, so
  D(f) = (1/beta) int_R e^{-beta E_eps} beta^2 |grad E_eps|^2 dx <= beta G^2 Leb(R) e^{-beta a} <= e * beta G^2 V_M e^{-beta theta} <= e^2 beta G^2 V_M e^{-beta (S_k + c_H)}.
Hence
  cap(A, Door') <= C_up * beta * exp( -beta (S_k + c_H) ),   C_up := e^2 G^2 V_M.   (CAP-UP)
(The two factors of e pay for the 1/beta ramp width and the 1/beta Sard offset; neither touches the exponent.)

=====================================================================
4. LOWER CAPACITY (explicit tube flow; the new content)
=====================================================================
Level bound on the tube. From (UP-QUAD), verbatim: "E_eps(x) <= m_k + eps w_k + (L_eps/2) dist(x, G_k)^2   on U.  (UP-QUAD)" [lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:632].

Geometry. Let v := (g* - z)/|g* - z| (a straight segment in the flat chart; (H-TUBE) supplies delta/2 + rho < inj(M) so the chart is isometric and Lebesgue measure is Euclidean). Let D_0 := the closed (n-1)-disc of radius rho centered at z, orthogonal to v; D_0 subset A. Let
  Tub := { x + s v : x in D_0, s in [0, ell] },  ell = delta/2.
The exit face D_ell = D_0 + ell v is the disc of radius rho centered at g*, contained in S since rho <= delta/4. For y in Tub, |y - g*| <= rho + (ell - s) + ... more simply |x + s v - g*| <= |x - z| + |z + s v - g*| = rho + (delta/2 - s) <= rho + delta/2 <= 5delta/8 (using rho = 1/beta <= delta/16). Since g* in G_k, dist(y, G_k) <= |y - g*| <= 5delta/8, so by (UP-QUAD) and (H-TUBE) (Tub subset U):
  sup_{Tub} E_eps <= m_k + eps w_k + (L_eps/2)(5delta/8)^2 = A_tube.            (TUBE-LEVEL)

Flow. Let Ar := omega_{n-1} rho^{n-1} = Leb_{n-1}(D_0) and define J := (1/Ar) v on Tub, J := 0 elsewhere. Then: J is divergence-free inside Tub (constant field); J is tangential on the lateral boundary (J . n = 0), so no lateral flux; the distributional divergence of J is the surface source -(1/Ar) dS|_{D_0} plus the sink (1/Ar) dS|_{D_ell}, supported in A ∪ S; and the flux is 1.

Duality (the easy half of THOMSON'S PRINCIPLE, proved here so nothing is imported). For any Lipschitz f with f = 1 on A, f = 0 on S,
  int_M <J, grad f> dx = - int_M f div J = (1/Ar) int_{D_0} f dS - (1/Ar) int_{D_ell} f dS = 1 - 0 = 1,
and by Cauchy-Schwarz with the weight w,
  1 = ( int <J, grad f> )^2 <= ( int_M |J|^2 / w dx ) ( int_M w |grad f|^2 dx ) = En(J) * D(f).
Taking the infimum over admissible f, cap(A,S) >= 1/En(J). Now
  En(J) = beta int_{Tub} |J|^2 e^{beta E_eps} dx <= beta (1/Ar^2) Leb(Tub) e^{beta A_tube} = beta (ell / Ar) e^{beta A_tube},
using Leb(Tub) = Ar * ell and (TUBE-LEVEL). With rho = 1/beta, Ar = omega_{n-1} beta^{-(2N-1)} and ell = delta/2:
  cap(A, S) >= (2 omega_{2N-1} / delta) * beta^{-2N} * exp( -beta A_tube ).      (CAP-LOW)

=====================================================================
5. POINTWISE-FROM-z (Harnack at the scale 1/beta; beta-FREE constant)
=====================================================================
(RATIO) bounds E_nu[h], not h(z). Close the gap by local regularity at the scale rho = 1/beta. On B_{2rho}(z) subset Omega (true for beta >= beta_*: dist(z,S) = delta/4 > 2rho and dist(z, Door') > 0 by (H-SEP)), h >= 0 solves L h = 0, i.e. Delta h = beta <grad E_eps, grad h>. Rescale u(y) := h(z + rho y), |y| <= 2: Delta_y u = b'(y) . grad_y u with b'(y) = rho beta grad E_eps(z + rho y), so |b'|_infty <= rho beta G = G, BETA-FREE. By the HARNACK INEQUALITY (NAMED: Gilbarg-Trudinger, Elliptic Partial Differential Equations of Second Order, Thm 8.20; hypothesis rows: (i) u >= 0 weak H^1 solution on B_2 — met, h is smooth and in [0,1]; (ii) uniform ellipticity ratio 1 — met; (iii) bounded lower-order coefficients with scale-invariant norm |b'| <= G — met by the choice rho = 1/beta),
  sup_{B_1} u <= C_H inf_{B_1} u,  C_H = C(n, G) beta-free.
Undoing the scaling and using that nu is supported on dA subset closure(B_rho(z)),
  h(z) <= sup_{B_rho(z)} h <= C_H inf_{closure B_rho(z)} h <= C_H E_nu[h].      (PTW)
(This is strictly better than the L1'-density route of lane-sh2local-proofs-v1.md:276, "p_1(x, .)  >=  c_0' beta^{n/2} exp( -beta C_2 (delta^2 + h^2) ) . Leb|_{B_rho(y)}   (L1')", which would charge an err-class exponential exp(beta C_2(delta^2+h^2)); the 1/beta-scale Harnack charges nothing exponential. L1' is therefore NOT consumed.)

=====================================================================
6. ASSEMBLY AND EXPONENT ARITHMETIC
=====================================================================
Chain (PTW), (RATIO), (CAP-UP), (CAP-LOW):
  h(z) <= C_H * cap(A,Door') / cap(A,S)
       <= C_H * C_up * beta * e^{-beta(S_k+c_H)} * (delta / (2 omega_{2N-1})) * beta^{2N} * e^{+beta A_tube}
       =  C_2 * beta^{2N+1} * exp( -beta ( S_k + c_H - m_k - eps w_k - (25/128) L_eps delta^2 ) ),
  C_2 := e^2 G^2 V_M delta / (2 omega_{2N-1}),  beta-free.
Absorb the polynomial into the headroom between 25/128 and N/4. With s = (N/4 - 25/128) L_eps delta^2 > 0,
  beta^{2N+1} e^{-beta s} <= sup_{b>0} b^{2N+1} e^{-b s} = ( (2N+1) / (e s) )^{2N+1},
a beta-free number. Therefore, uniformly in z in dS^+ and with (RED)'s factor 2,

  sup_{z in dS^+} P_z( tau_lev < T ) <= C_1(eps, delta) exp( -beta ( S_k + c_H - m_k - eps w_k - L_eps N delta^2 / 4 ) ),
  C_1(eps, delta) := 2 C_H C_2 ( (2N+1) / (e s) )^{2N+1},   s = (N/4 - 25/128) L_eps delta^2,

which is EXACTLY the required strength, with C_1 beta-free and explicit, valid for all beta >= beta_*.

LEDGER OF LOSSES (where each term of the exponent enters).
  - m_k + eps w_k: the ground level of E_eps on G_k, entering only through (UP-QUAD) [proofs:632] in (TUBE-LEVEL), i.e. through the LOWER capacity.
  - (25/128) L_eps delta^2: the maximal height of the tube above the ground, from (UP-QUAD) with dist(., G_k) <= delta/2 + rho <= 5delta/8. This is the ONLY delta-loss in the argument, and it is strictly smaller than the allowed N L_eps delta^2 / 4 for every N >= 1.
  - The two factors 1/beta (ramp width, Sard offset) cost e^2 in C_up and NOTHING in the exponent.
  - beta^{2N+1} = beta^1 (ramp gradient, CAP-UP) times beta^{2N} (tube cross-section rho^{-(2N-1)} and the factor beta in En(J), CAP-LOW). This polynomial is what forces the delivered allowance to be N L_eps delta^2/4 rather than the tight 25 L_eps delta^2/128: the difference s is exactly the budget spent on absorbing beta^{2N+1}. If one prefers rho fixed at delta/8 instead of 1/beta, the polynomial drops to beta^2 but step 5 (Harnack) no longer has a beta-free constant; the 1/beta scale is what buys the pointwise step for free.
  - C_H (Harnack), C_2, and the factor 2 from (RED) are beta-free.

WHY THE THREE BLOCKED COMPOSITIONS ARE AVOIDED. (i) No supermartingale discount appears: time never enters the estimate; the bound is on a hitting-order event, so the round length e^{+beta Gamma(h)} is irrelevant. (ii) No per-window union: the argument is a single global variational comparison, so a block start AT the doorway level cannot appear. (iii) No superharmonic function of the level is used: the level-ramp f is a TEST function for the Dirichlet principle, not a supersolution, and the lower bound uses a flow, not a function.

# PE-BLOCK ATTEMPT (honest partial; checker REPAIRABLE with 3 FATALs - preserved as record; its refined gap register is OPERATIVE)

LEMMA PE-BLOCK (route B1, the reversibility round-trip). Delivered: the FULL scalar
GAP-PE3P-BLOCK at exact strength, with err_B = 0 (not merely err-class), VALID ON THE
EXPLICIT RANGE (RANGE-B1) below, modulo four named hypothesis rows typed at the end.
Structural verdict for the lead is recorded at the close: routes (B1) and the L1'-chain
are NOT independent - they reduce to the same numeric comparison.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
0. OBJECTS FIXED (no object is used before it is fixed)

Space: M = R^n/Lambda compact smooth; X the diffusion with generator
L_beta = (1/beta) Delta - grad E_eps . grad; (F_t) the usual augmented filtration;
(vartheta_t) the shift semigroup; (P_x) the family of laws. All hitting times below are
first entrance times of Borel sets by the right-continuous adapted process X (or by the
enlarged process Z = (X, theta)), hence (F_t)-stopping times by the DEBUT THEOREM
(classical; hypothesis row: (F_t) right-continuous and complete - met by the usual
augmentation).

Levels (hypothesis row HR-GATE, verbatim from the row this route is taken from):
"the doorway sits at S_k + c_H, the Delta_phi gate at S_k + 4 c_H, so every entry into
the off-stratum region pre-pays an exit margin of 3 c_H over the band top"
[research/formal-framework/pre-physics/lane-lp-product-saddle-v1.md:249-252].
I use HR-GATE only as: {w_phi != 0} is unreachable from {w_phi = 0} without first
attaining the level S_k + 4 c_H.

Region names (mine, fixed here):
  W_low := {E_eps <= S_k + c_H} \ R_0      (on-stratum, at or below the doorway, off R_0)
  W_mid := {S_k + c_H < E_eps < S_k + 4 c_H} intersect {w_phi = 0}
  W_+   := {E_eps >= S_k + 4 c_H} union {w_phi != 0}      (the off-stratum branch)
By HR-GATE, M \ R_0 = W_low u W_mid u W_+ up to the null boundary, and every entry into
W_+ from R_0 u W_low u W_mid attains the level S_k + 4 c_H first.

Stopping objects (exact):
  T_sub          deterministic, beta-free (the window length);
  H_A            := inf{ s >= 0 : X_s in A }, for A Borel;
  T = min(D(0), L)   the round terminus;
  tau_gate       := H_{ {E_eps >= S_k + 4 c_H} };
  tau_+          := H_{W_+};
  xi             := H_{ {E_eps <= S_k + c_H} }   (down-crossing to the doorway sub-level).
The renewal anchors zeta_0 := 0, and for m >= 0,
  zeta_{m+1} := ( xi o vartheta_{zeta_m} + zeta_m + t_a ) ^ H_{R_0} ^ T ^ tau_+,
each an (F_t)-stopping time (composition of a first entrance time with a shift at a
stopping time; strong Markov process, classical).

(HR-T) The ONLY property of T used: T is the first entrance time of a Borel set by the
strong Markov process Z = (X, theta), hence T = t + T o vartheta_t on {T > t}. Hypothesis
match: T = min(D(0), L) is a min of two first entrance times for Z - matches.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
1. REDUCTION OF B_bar (window part beta-free; whole burden on the recovery)

Write U := T_sub + H_{R_0} o vartheta_{T_sub}, and
  I := integral_0^{U ^ T} 1_{M\R_0}(X_s) ds.
Split at T_sub ^ T:
  I <= T_sub + 1_{ {T > T_sub} } integral_{T_sub}^{U ^ T} 1_{M\R_0}(X_s) ds.
On {T > T_sub}, (HR-T) gives T = T_sub + T o vartheta_{T_sub}, and by definition
U = T_sub + H_{R_0} o vartheta_{T_sub}, so the second term equals F o vartheta_{T_sub}
with
  F := integral_0^{ H_{R_0} ^ T } 1_{M\R_0}(X_s) ds.
F is nonnegative and Borel. Two exact remarks: on {X_0 in R_0}, H_{R_0} = 0 so F = 0; on
{X_0 not in R_0}, the path is outside R_0 on all of [0, H_{R_0}), so the indicator is
identically 1 there and F = H_{R_0} ^ T EXACTLY. Hence F <= H_{R_0} pointwise.
By the SIMPLE MARKOV PROPERTY at the DETERMINISTIC time T_sub (classical; hypothesis row:
X Markov with Borel semigroup - supplied by SR-SH1's jointly continuous density, cited in
Section 3),
  E_z[ 1_{ {T > T_sub} } F o vartheta_{T_sub} ] = E_z[ 1_{ {T>T_sub} } E_{X_{T_sub}}[F] ].
Therefore, with the recovery scalar
  S(z) := E_z[ 1_{ {T>T_sub} } E_{X_{T_sub}}[ H_{R_0} ^ T ] ],
  B_bar <= T_sub + sup_{z in R_0} S(z).                                            (RED-1)
This is exactly the row's own accounting, verbatim: "the window part contributes at most
T_sub, beta-free; the whole burden is the R_0-recovery part, i.e. the expected time above
the doorway before re-entering R_0 or terminating"
[lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:7856-7859]. NOTE the trap threat is now visible: S(z) is a
supremum over the LAW of X_{T_sub}, i.e. over an arbitrary reachable start, and from a
point pinned on G_{k,j} the naive bound on E_y[H_{R_0}] is the trap dwell.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
2. THE PRE-PAYMENT ESTIMATE (derived, not cited: FW-C at the gate level)

I re-run the exponential-supermartingale computation DISPLAYED at
[lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:7528-7541] with the level S_k + c_H replaced by S_k + 4 c_H.
Put f := exp(beta E_eps). The displayed identity is verbatim
  "L f = (1/beta) Delta f - grad E_eps . grad f = f . Delta E_eps <= M_2^eps f"
with, verbatim, "The |grad E_eps|^2 terms CANCEL EXACTLY, so M_2^eps is BETA-FREE"
[:7530-7533]. Put Y_t := exp(-M_2^eps t) f(X_t). By SR-ITO [:7534] the drift of Y is <= 0
and grad f is bounded on the compact M, so the stochastic integral is a true martingale on
[0, t_0] and Y is a supermartingale there [:7535-7537]. By SR-OST at the BOUNDED stopping
time tau_gate ^ t_0 [:7538],
  E_y[ Y_{tau_gate ^ t_0} ] <= Y_0 = f(y).
Y >= 0, and on {tau_gate <= t_0} continuity of E_eps o X gives E_eps(X_{tau_gate}) =
S_k + 4 c_H, so Y_{tau_gate} >= e^{-M_2^eps t_0} e^{beta (S_k + 4 c_H)}. Rearranging:

  P_y( tau_gate <= t_0 )  <=  e^{ M_2^eps t_0 } exp( -beta ( S_k + 4 c_H - E_eps(y) ) ).
                                                                                 (GATE)

CLASSICAL FACTS NAMED WITH HYPOTHESIS ROWS.
  SR-ITO   - hypotheses: f in C^2(M), X an Ito diffusion on compact M. MATCH: E_eps smooth.
  SR-OST   - hypotheses: Y a supermartingale on [0,t_0], stopping time bounded by t_0.
             MATCH: tau_gate ^ t_0 <= t_0. NO uniform-integrability claim is needed.
  (no independence is claimed anywhere; the martingale property is w.r.t. (F_t).)

Consequence used twice below. Set
  err_gate := max( 0 , sup_{y in R_0} E_eps(y) - (S_k + c_H) )   [ = 0 under HR-R0LEVEL ]
and for any beta-free horizon t_0,
  sup_{y in R_0 u W_low} P_y( tau_+ <= t_0 ) <= sup_{y} P_y( tau_gate <= t_0 )
        <= e^{M_2^eps t_0} e^{ -beta ( 3 c_H - err_gate ) } =: g(t_0).            (PRE)
The first inequality is HR-GATE (no W_+ entry without attaining the gate level); it is a
PATHWISE inclusion {tau_+ <= t_0} subset {tau_gate <= t_0}, not a probabilistic claim.
(PRE) is the "pre-paid 3 c_H" of the row, now a proved per-attempt entry bound, and it is
uniform over ALL starts at or below the doorway - in particular over the window start z in
R_0, so the window itself is covered.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
3. THE ON-STRATUM BRANCH: BETA-FREE GEOMETRIC ITERATION

(HR-RELAX) There are beta-free t_a > 0 and q_0 in (0,1] with
   inf_{ y in W_low u W_mid }  P_y(  ( xi ^ H_{R_0} ^ T )  <=  t_a )  >=  q_0.
Ground, verbatim: on W_low u W_mid the label is still k and the stratum is w_phi = 0, so
by M2-ATTR "Crit(E_eps) intersect closure(D_k(eps)) = G_k ... strict descent off G_k" -
"no foreign attractor captures the pass" - and the M2P.5 slice-gradient floor
"<grad E_eps(x), x - pi(x)> >= (c_1/2) dist(x, G_k)^2", which is "a Lyapunov drift on
dist(.,G_k)^2 driving the path back into U_ch, realized by the diffusion via SH.2
shadowing at order-one probability"
[lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:3033-3037, citing lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:771-773].
There are NO traps on this branch: M2-ATTR says the only critical set inside
closure(D_k(eps)) is G_k, and the pinning tori G_{k,j} = C_k x C_j^phi carry w_phi != 0,
hence lie in W_+, not in W_low u W_mid.

Iteration. On the anchors zeta_m of Section 0, {zeta_m < H_{R_0} ^ T ^ tau_+} is
F_{zeta_m}-measurable and X_{zeta_m} in W_low on that event (the anchor is a down-crossing
of the doorway sub-level, or the process has already been absorbed). By the STRONG MARKOV
PROPERTY at zeta_m (classical; hypothesis row: X a strong Markov Feller process on compact
M - supplied by SR-SH1),
  P_y( zeta_{m+1} < H_{R_0} ^ T ^ tau_+ | F_{zeta_m} ) <= 1 - q_0   on {zeta_m < ...},
so by induction P_y( zeta_m < H_{R_0} ^ T ^ tau_+ ) <= (1 - q_0)^m. This is a CONDITIONAL
Markov bound; no independence is asserted. Since zeta_{m+1} - zeta_m <= t_a,
  E_y[ ( H_{R_0} ^ T ^ tau_+ ) ]  <=  t_a * sum_{m>=0} (1-q_0)^m  =  t_a / q_0,
uniformly over y in W_low u W_mid, BETA-FREE, err = 0.                            (ON-STR)
The occupation strictly above the doorway between consecutive anchors is at most t_a each,
so (ON-STR) already bounds it: this is the brief's "iterate geometrically", and it costs
NOTHING in the ledger.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
4. THE OFF-STRATUM BRANCH: ENTRY COST TIMES DWELL, CLOSED BY A RENEWAL INEQUALITY

(HR-DWELL) D_+ := sup_{ y in W_+ } E_y[ H_{ W_low u W_mid u R_0 } ^ T ] satisfies
   beta^{-1} log D_+  <=  lambda ( 2 - g(N) ).
This is the row's OWN crude dwell exponent, verbatim: "the crude trap-dwell exponent
lambda(2 - g(N)) equals 2 - 10(1 - cos(2 pi/10)) = 0.090170 at (N, lambda) = (10, 1)"
[lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:7866-7868]. IT IS AN INPUT, NOT PROVED HERE - see GAP-B-DWELL.

Renewal closure. Fix n in N and put
  S_n := sup_{ y in M }  E_y[ ( H_{R_0} ^ T ) ^ n ]  <=  n  <  infinity.
Let y in W_low u W_mid. Decompose at tau_+:
  ( H_{R_0} ^ T ) ^ n  <=  ( H_{R_0} ^ T ^ tau_+ )
        + 1_{ {tau_+ < H_{R_0} ^ T} } * [ (dwell in W_+) + ( H_{R_0} ^ T ) ^ n o vartheta_{rho_+} ],
where rho_+ := inf{ s > tau_+ : X_s in W_low u W_mid u R_0 }. Take E_y, use (ON-STR) on
the first term, the STRONG MARKOV PROPERTY at tau_+ and at rho_+ on the rest, (HR-DWELL)
for the middle term, and (PRE) for P_y(tau_+ < H_{R_0} ^ T ^ zeta_{m+1}) summed over the
at most Geometric(q_0)-many anchors - explicitly, by the same conditional-Markov induction
as in Section 3,
  P_y( tau_+ < H_{R_0} ^ T )  <=  sum_{m>=0} (1-q_0)^m g(t_a)  =  g(t_a)/q_0  =: g'.
Hence, uniformly over y in W_low u W_mid,
  S_n  <=  t_a/q_0  +  g' ( D_+ + S_n ).
Since g(t_a) = e^{M_2^eps t_a} e^{-beta(3 c_H - err_gate)} with t_a, M_2^eps, q_0 all
beta-free, there is beta_3 with g' <= 1/2 for beta >= beta_3; then
  S_n  <=  2 t_a / q_0  +  2 g' D_+,       uniformly in n.
Monotone convergence (n -> infinity) removes the truncation. For a start y in W_+ add one
dwell: S := sup_{y in M} E_y[H_{R_0} ^ T] <= D_+ + 2 t_a/q_0 + 2 g' D_+ ; but this last
case is NOT needed, because by (PRE) applied on [0, T_sub] from z in R_0 the window itself
puts X_{T_sub} in W_+ only on an event of probability <= g(T_sub), so in (RED-1)
  sup_{z in R_0} S(z)  <=  ( 2 t_a/q_0 + 2 g' D_+ )  +  g(T_sub) ( D_+ + 2 t_a/q_0 + 2 g' D_+ ).

5. THE DELIVERED BOUND AND THE err LEDGER

Collecting (RED-1) with Section 4, with C := T_sub + 6 t_a/q_0 + 6 e^{M_2^eps (t_a v T_sub)}/q_0
(beta-free; it depends on eps, delta only through t_a, q_0, M_2^eps):

  B_bar  <=  C * ( 1 + D_+ * e^{ -beta ( 3 c_H - err_gate ) } ).                  (B-BND)

Hence
  beta^{-1} log B_bar  <=  beta^{-1} log C
        +  max( 0 , beta^{-1} log D_+ - 3 c_H + err_gate )
        <=  o(1)  +  max( 0 , lambda(2 - g(N)) - 3 c_H + err_gate ).              (LEDGER)

THEREFORE, ON THE RANGE
  (RANGE-B1)     lambda ( 2 - g(N) )  +  err_gate  <  3 c_H,
the required strength holds VERBATIM with
  C_2(eps,delta) := C  (beta-free)   and   err_B := 0.
err_B = 0 is trivially err-class and trivially admissible in (SML): it consumes NO line of
the budget. Off (RANGE-B1), (LEDGER) gives err_B = lambda(2-g(N)) - 3 c_H + err_gate > 0,
which GROWS LINEARLY IN lambda while (MRG) is lambda-free - i.e. the estimate is sharp
about its own failure and reproduces, from a proof rather than a scan, the row's warning
"it GROWS LINEARLY IN lambda while (MRG) is lambda-free, so a crude dwell-times-probability
product FAILS for large lambda" [lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:7869-7870].

err LEDGER, line by line (every loss displayed):
  L1  window part                        : T_sub, BETA-FREE, exponent 0.
  L2  on-stratum geometric iteration     : t_a/q_0, BETA-FREE, exponent 0.
  L3  gate pre-payment                   : -3 c_H  (a GAIN, not a loss).
  L4  err_gate = max(0, sup_{R_0} E_eps - S_k - c_H): 0 under HR-R0LEVEL; otherwise, if
      only the collar row (E-TOP+) is available, it is eps w_k + L_eps N delta^2/4, i.e.
      eps-class + O(delta^2) - ADMISSIBLE.
  L5  dwell                              : +lambda(2 - g(N)), the only lambda-carrying line.

6. STRUCTURAL VERDICT FOR THE LEAD (this is the part worth the round)

The brief offered a second route: bound the W_+ occupation via the STRAT Gibbs route
pointwise-from-z with the L1' floor [lane-sh2local-proofs-v1.md:270-281], verbatim
"p_1(x, .) >= c_0' beta^{n/2} exp( -beta C_2 (delta^2 + h^2) ) . Leb|_{B_rho(y)}". Chaining
K applications of that minorization along a chain y = x_0, ..., x_K with x_K interior to
R_0 gives, by the Markov property and Chapman-Kolmogorov (SR-SH1, verbatim
"jointly continuous, strictly positive transition density p_t(x,y) (t > 0) w.r.t. Leb, and
the Chapman-Kolmogorov identity holds pointwise" [lane-sh2local-proofs-v1.md:285-288]),
  P_y( X_K in B_rho(x_K) ) >= (c_0' beta^{n/2})^K Leb(B_rho)^{K-1} Leb(B_rho(x_K))
                              * exp( -beta K C_2 (delta^2 + h^2) ),
whence, by the same conditional-Markov geometric iteration as Section 3 at the
deterministic times mK, E_y[H_{R_0}] <= K / p_ret and err_B = K C_2 (delta^2 + h^2). The
beta^{n/2} prefactor enters the denominator as beta^{-nK/2} <= 1 and costs NOTHING. So the
L1' route delivers err_B = K_max C_2 (delta^2 + h^2) - manifestly O(delta^2) + O(h^2) -
IF AND ONLY IF the chain length K_max is beta-free AND delta-free.

It is not. The exponent C_2(delta^2 + h^2) is a squared-displacement action; a chain that
climbs a level barrier of height Delta must have K >= Delta / (C_2 (delta^2 + h^2)) steps,
so K_max C_2 (delta^2 + h^2) >= Delta. Applied on W_+, Delta is exactly the escape barrier
of the pinning torus G_{k,j}. THE TWO OFFERED ROUTES THEREFORE MEET AT THE SAME SCALAR:
the L1'-chain does not evade the trap, it re-expresses the trap dwell exponent as the chain
cost, and the surviving comparison is again "trap barrier versus the pre-paid 3 c_H". The
lead should not budget the L1' route as an independent second chance. What the L1' route
DOES buy, and Section 3 already buys beta-free, is the on-stratum leg. Recommendation: the
only genuinely independent closure of GAP-PE3P-BLOCK is an UPPER trap-dwell input
(GAP-B-DWELL below) or route (B2)'s upper Green estimate, which the row already records the
corpus does not carry [lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:7878-7881].

# B-DWELL DESIGN PASS (lead, 2026-07-27 - fresh eyes; SUPERSEDES the
# PE-BLOCK round-trip route and RE-OBJECTS the gap)

THE OBJECT CORRECTION. GAP-PE3P-BLOCK asked for
B_bar = sup_{z in R_0} E_z[one-window-plus-recovery outside cost] to
be ERR-CLASS. That is unobtainable AND unnecessary - which is exactly
why the round-trip attempt produced three FATALs: from a start AT the
doorway level, the honest trap occupation carries
e^{+beta(S_k + c_H - m_k - m_1(lambda))}, which is exponentially LARGE
at large N (m_1(lambda) = lambda g(N) -> 0). No route can make B_bar
err-class, because B_bar is the WRONG MARGINAL of the right quantity.

THE COUPLED ACCOUNTING (the collapse). The schedule never consumes
B_bar alone: it consumes the PRODUCT (probability of reaching the
expensive region) x (occupation once there). Coupling them makes the
GATE CANCEL - the rigorous form of the design page's own corrected
PE.5 kernel ('the entry pre-payment and the exit barrier CANCEL in
the occupation identity; net exponent = doorway - floor'):

  per-round trap occupation
    <= P(reach the doorway from S)            [PE-DOORREACH, SOUND:
         <= C e^{-beta(S_k + c_H - m_k - err)}]
     x E_{doorway-level start}[trap occupation before H_S ^ T]
         <= C' poly(beta) e^{+beta(S_k + c_H - m_k - m_1(lambda) + err)}
  = C'' poly(beta) e^{-beta(m_1(lambda) - err)}

and m_1(lambda) - c_H/2 = g(N)(lambda - 1/8) + (S_k - 2)/8 > 0 on the
whole flagship range - ADJ-2's identity, already checker-verified to
1e-16. The per-round exponent the schedule needs is EXACTLY the
per-round exponent ADJ-2 proved the row carries. The design was
telling us the answer since 07-21.

The w_phi = 0 above-doorway recovery closes by the SAME formula with
floor = the doorway itself: occupation-from-doorway <= poly(beta)
e^{+beta err}, times the reach cost e^{-beta(S_k+c_H-m_k-err)} -
clears c_H/2 with the full ~1.02 margin.

THE ONE REMAINING LEMMA - PE-TRAPOCC, at exact strength:

  For z in R_0: E_z[ integral_0^{H_S ^ T} 1_TRAP(X_s) ds ]
    <= C(N, delta, eps) poly(beta)
       exp( -beta ( m_k + m_1(lambda) - E_eps(z) - err(delta, eps) ) ),

  TRAP := the delta-neighborhood of the {w_phi != 0} stratum's
  reachable part (the STRAT floor set), and the same display with
  TRAP replaced by {E_eps >= S_k + c_H, w_phi = 0} and the floor
  m_k + m_1 replaced by S_k + c_H.

FIVE INGREDIENTS - FOUR ALREADY LANDED SOUND, ONE COMPOSITION:
 (i)   the entry-probability capacity bound P_z(H_TRAP < H_S ^ T):
       the PE-DOORREACH machinery VERBATIM with the target set at
       the Delta_phi gate level m_k + 2 lambda (the Dirichlet-
       principle upper capacity with the level-ramp at the gate);

       generator: E_{nu_eq}[occ(A) before H_S] <= mu(A)/cap(A, S)

 (iii) mu(TRAP) <= vol . e^{-beta(m_k + m_1(lambda) - err)}: the

 (iv)  cap(TRAP, S) >= c poly(beta) e^{-beta(m_k + 2 lambda)}: the
