# LEMMA PE-TRAPOCC (closes GAP-PE-TRAPOCC at the B-DWELL design-pass strength)

=====================================================================
0. OBJECTS, SIGMA-FIELDS, STOPPING TIMES (PE-DOORREACH Section 0, verbatim)
=====================================================================
M := T^{2N}, n := 2N, E_eps in C^inf(M). X = (X_t)_{t>=0} the diffusion with generator
  L u = (1/beta) Delta u - <grad E_eps, grad u>,
read off the adjoint of ROW SR-PE1.2: "L^* u = (1/beta) Delta u + div(u grad E_eps)" [lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:1891]. (F_t)_{t>=0} := the usual augmentation of the natural filtration of X (right-continuous, P-complete). X has continuous paths, so hitting times of closed sets are (F_t)-stopping times.

Weights and forms (PE-DOORREACH Section 0 verbatim): mu(dx) := e^{-beta E_eps(x)} dx, w := (1/beta) e^{-beta E_eps},
  D(f) := int_M w |grad f|^2 dx,  cap(Y,Y') := inf{ D(f) : f=1 on Y, f=0 on Y', f Lipschitz },
and the single reversibility input div(w grad u) = mu L u, from ROW SR-PE1.2: "rho_beta(dx) = Z_beta^{-1} exp(-beta E_eps(x)) dx ... is the unique invariant probability of L, and L is rho_beta-reversible" [lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:1881-1885]. COND-free.

Sets. S := B_{delta/4}(g*), S^+ := B_{delta/2}(g*) [proofs:130]; g* in G_k.
  R_0 := { w_theta = k, w_phi = 0, E_eps <= S_k + c_H }  ["let R_0 := {w_theta = k, / w_phi = 0, E_eps <= S_k + c_H}", lane-lp-product-saddle-v1.md:217-218].
  STRAT := (union over nonzero realizable j of {w_theta=k, w_phi=j}) union ({w_theta=k} inter Delta_phi) — R3-STRAT's slicing verbatim [proofs:4988-4990].
  rho := 1/beta (PE-DOORREACH's scale choice).
  TRAP := a set with STRAT subset {dist(.,STRAT) <= 2rho} subset TRAP subset {dist(.,STRAT) <= 4rho}, with dTRAP a smooth compact hypersurface. CONSTRUCTION: d(x) := dist(x,STRAT) is 1-Lipschitz; take f_s smooth with |f_s - d| <= rho/8 (NAMED: smooth approximation of Lipschitz functions on a compact manifold, Whitney; hypothesis rows: M compact smooth, d continuous — met); by SARD'S THEOREM (row: f_s in C^inf(M), M compact — met) pick a regular value r in [2rho+rho/8, 3rho] and set TRAP := {f_s <= r}. TRAP is the design pass's floor set: "TRAP := the delta-neighborhood of the {w_phi != 0} stratum's reachable part (the STRAT floor set)" [proofs:8905-8907]. I take the FULL stratum, not only its reachable part — a strengthening (larger TRAP, larger indicator), noted so no one reads a weakening.
  TRAP_2 := { E_eps >= theta_2, w_phi = 0 }, theta_2 a Sard-regular value in [S_k + c_H - 1/beta, S_k + c_H] (PE-DOORREACH (1a) device verbatim), the companion set.

Stopping times. H_Y := inf{ t >= 0 : X_t in Y } for closed Y; H_S, H_TRAP; T := min(D(0), L) ["The round terminus is T = min(D(0), L) <= D(0)", proofs:1385].

Constants, all beta-free: G := sup_M |grad E_eps| < inf, V_M := Leb(M), omega_{n-1} := Leb_{n-1}(unit ball in R^{n-1}), L_eps <= L + 8 eps [proofs:612-613].

DELIVERABLE (design-pass strength, [proofs:8899-8909]):
  (TRAPOCC)  for z in R_0:  E_z[ int_0^{H_S ^ T} 1_TRAP(X_s) ds ]
     <= C(N,delta,eps) poly(beta) exp( -beta ( m_k + m_1(lambda) - E_eps(z) - err ) ),
  (TRAPOCC-2) the same with TRAP -> TRAP_2 and floor m_k + m_1 -> S_k + c_H.

=====================================================================
1. THE GATE, AND THE THREE LEVEL FACTS
=====================================================================
(G1) GATE ROW, verbatim: "The w_phi = 0 stratum is DYNAMICALLY CLOSED at band levels: crossing Delta_phi needs E_eps >= m_k + 2 lambda > m_k + 2 kappa >= S_k + 4 c_H (c_H ledger, M2-PIN strict), above the band top." [lane-lp-product-saddle-v1.md:651-653]. Concordant: "points on Delta_phi carry E_0 >= m_k + 2 lambda > S_k + c_H" [:324] (stated in E_0; :651-653 is the E_eps form and is the one consumed). Put Gate := m_k + 2 lambda. R_0 is at band levels (E_eps <= S_k + c_H), so the row applies as stated.
(G2) w_phi is integer-valued and locally constant off Delta_phi [la3-reader-packet-v1.md:55-56, quoted at proofs:4990-4991]. Hence a continuous curve joining {w_phi = 0} to {w_phi != 0} meets Delta_phi.
(G3) COLLAR TRANSFER. If x in TRAP and w_phi(x) = 0 then E_eps(x) >= Gate - 4G/beta. PROOF: dist(x,STRAT) <= 4rho, so there is y in STRAT with a minimizing geodesic [x,y] of length <= 4rho (4/beta < inj(M) for beta >= beta_*); by (G2) the geodesic meets Delta_phi at some p, and E_eps(p) >= Gate by (G1); |grad E_eps| <= G gives E_eps(x) >= E_eps(p) - 4G rho. (If y is in the Delta_phi face of STRAT, take p = y.)
(G4) SEPARATION. R_0 inter TRAP = empty, and dist(z, TRAP) > 2rho for every z in R_0. PROOF: R_0 subset {w_phi = 0} by [lane-lp:217-218], so by (G3) any point of TRAP inter R_0 would have E_eps >= Gate - 4G/beta > S_k + c_H (by (G1)'s strict chain Gate >= S_k + 4c_H, for beta >= beta_* := max(16/delta, 24G/(3c_H))), contradiction. Any y with dist(y,TRAP) <= 2rho has dist(y,STRAT) <= 6rho, hence E_eps(y) >= Gate - 6G/beta > S_k + c_H by the same threshold; so no such y lies in R_0.

=====================================================================
2. TRUNCATION HONESTY
=====================================================================
H_S ^ T <= H_S pathwise, so 1_{[0, H_S ^ T)}(s) <= 1_{[0,H_S)}(s) for every s and every path, whence for every Borel A
  E_z[ int_0^{H_S ^ T} 1_A(X_s) ds ] <= E_z[ int_0^{H_S} 1_A(X_s) ds ] =: v_A(z).
Killing earlier only REMOVES occupation; the direction is favorable. This is the PE.4 domination "absorption only truncates ... a theta-crossing mid-excursion only removes outside-time", which the corpus no longer imports as an axiom but DERIVES pathwise as R3-ASM's LEM-LABEL [proofs:5294, 5412; PE.4 recorded as concordant-not-consumed at :5832]. Cited as landed. From here on the object is v := v_TRAP, and v_2 := v_{TRAP_2}.

Regularity of v: v(x) <= E_x[H_S] < inf by positive Harris recurrence on compact elliptic M [proofs:1867-1879]; v solves L v = -1_TRAP on M \ S, v = 0 on S. By CALDERON-ZYGMUND L^p ESTIMATES + SOBOLEV EMBEDDING (NAMED: Gilbarg-Trudinger Thm 9.15 and Cor 7.11; hypothesis rows: uniformly elliptic operator with smooth bounded coefficients on compact M — met; RHS in L^inf — met; smooth boundary dS, dTRAP — met by construction) v is in C^{1,alpha} up to dS and dTRAP and smooth off dTRAP. C^{1,alpha} is all the flux identities below use; v is NOT C^2 across dTRAP and no step claims it.

=====================================================================
3. INGREDIENT (ii): THE EQUILIBRIUM OCCUPATION IDENTITY
=====================================================================
NAMED: the equilibrium-measure (mean-occupation) identity of reversible potential theory — Bovier & den Hollander, Metastability: a Potential-Theoretic Approach, Springer 2015, Ch. 7 (mean hitting-time formula); Bovier, Eckhoff, Gayrard, Klein, Comm. Math. Phys. 228 (2002). HYPOTHESIS ROWS: (a) mu-symmetric Dirichlet form / mu-symmetric Green kernel for the process killed on S — MET, from ROW SR-PE1.2 reversibility [proofs:1881-1885] in the form div(w grad u) = mu L u; (b) existence of the equilibrium potential h_{TRAP,S}(x) = P_x(H_TRAP < H_S) as the classical solution of the two-set Dirichlet problem with a regular boundary — MET, exactly the row PE-DOORREACH already installed ("PROBABILISTIC REPRESENTATION OF THE DIRICHLET PROBLEM (NAMED: Friedman ... Thm 6.5.1; ... (iii) every boundary point regular — met, dS and dDoor' are smooth hypersurfaces so the exterior sphere condition holds ...)"), with dTRAP smooth by the Sard construction of Section 0; (c) E_x[H_S] < inf — MET as above.

Because the hypothesis rows are already in the lane, I do not import the identity as a black box: it is two lines of the same Green identity PE-DOORREACH used.

Write h := h_{TRAP,S}: h = 1 on TRAP, 0 on S, L h = 0 on Omega := M \ (TRAP u S), smooth up to the boundary (interior Schauder + smooth boundary). Let n denote at dTRAP the normal pointing INTO TRAP. Then
  cap(TRAP,S) = D(h) = int_{dTRAP} w partial_n h dS =: e(dTRAP),  e := w partial_n h dS >= 0
(the first equality by D(h) = -int_Omega h div(w grad h) + int_{dOmega} h w partial_n h dS, with h = 0 on dS and L h = 0 in Omega). Green's second identity on Omega with the pair (h, v), both L-harmonic there (1_TRAP = 0 on Omega):
  0 = int_{dOmega} w [ h partial_n v - v partial_n h ] dS.
On dS both h and v vanish. On dTRAP, h = 1 and v = phi := v|_{dTRAP}, so
  0 = int_{dTRAP} w partial_n v dS - int_{dTRAP} phi de,
and int_{dTRAP} w partial_n v dS = - int_{TRAP} div(w grad v) dx = - int_{TRAP} mu L v dx = + mu(TRAP), since L v = -1 on TRAP. Hence
  int_{dTRAP} phi de = mu(TRAP),  i.e.  E_nu[ v ] = mu(TRAP) / cap(TRAP,S),  nu := e / cap(TRAP,S).   (EQ-OCC)
CARE POINT (a), stated: the classical identity is for occupation BEFORE H_S; our object kills at H_S ^ T. Section 2 already discharged this in the favorable direction, so (EQ-OCC) is applied to the LARGER quantity v.

=====================================================================
4. THE FLUX / MINIMUM-PRINCIPLE SANDWICH (ingredient (v)) — NO HARNACK FROM z
=====================================================================
Fix z in R_0 with dist(z,S) >= 4/beta (Section 7 removes this) and put A_z := closed B_rho(z), rho = 1/beta. By (G4) and the choice of beta_*, A_z, S, TRAP are pairwise disjoint compacts with smooth boundaries and B_{2rho}(z) subset Omega. Let h_z be the equilibrium potential of A_z against S u TRAP (=1 on A_z, =0 on S u TRAP, L-harmonic on Omega'' := M \ (A_z u S u TRAP)), e_z := w partial_n h_z dS on dA_z with n into A_z, e_z(dA_z) = cap(A_z, S u TRAP), and e_D := - w partial_n h_z dS on dTRAP with n into TRAP; e_z, e_D >= 0.

(4a) FLUX IDENTITY (PE-DOORREACH (FLUX-ID) verbatim in shape). Green's second identity on Omega'' with (h_z, v), both L-harmonic there: dS contributes nothing (h_z = v = 0); dTRAP contributes + int_{dTRAP} phi de_D (h_z = 0, v = phi); dA_z contributes -int_{dA_z} v de_z, because int_{dA_z} w partial_n v dS = -int_{A_z} div(w grad v) dx = -int_{A_z} mu L v dx = 0 (A_z subset Omega, so L v = 0 inside A_z). Hence
  int_{dA_z} v de_z = int_{dTRAP} phi de_D.                                   (FLUX-ID')

(4b) THE SANDWICH e_D <= 2 e. Suppose h(y) <= 1/2 for all y in dA_z (proved unconditionally in Section 5, and NOT circularly: Section 5 uses only the capacity ratio, never (4b)). The functions h_z and 2(1 - h) are both L-harmonic on Omega''. Boundary comparison: on dA_z, h_z = 1 <= 2(1 - h) since h <= 1/2; on dS, h_z = 0 <= 2; on dTRAP, h_z = 0 = 2(1 - 1). By the MINIMUM PRINCIPLE for uniformly elliptic operators without zeroth-order term (NAMED: Gilbarg-Trudinger Thm 8.1; hypothesis rows: uniform ellipticity and bounded coefficients — met; c = 0 — met; the same row PE-DOORREACH's step (2b) used), D := 2(1-h) - h_z >= 0 on Omega''. D vanishes identically on dTRAP and is >= 0 on the Omega''-side, so its directional derivative at dTRAP in the direction -n (pointing out of TRAP, into Omega'') is >= 0, i.e. partial_n D <= 0, i.e. -partial_n h_z <= -2 partial_n h. Multiplying by w >= 0 and integrating against any nonnegative Borel test function on dTRAP,
  e_D <= 2 e   as measures on dTRAP.                                          (SANDWICH)
This is the entry-surface-to-equilibrium step. It is a flux comparison; NO Harnack from z and NO comparison of harmonic measures is used.

(4c) Combining (FLUX-ID'), (SANDWICH), (EQ-OCC), and cap(A_z, S u TRAP) >= cap(A_z, S) (the admissible class shrinks):
  E_{nu_z}[ v ] = ( int_{dTRAP} phi de_D ) / cap(A_z, S u TRAP) <= 2 mu(TRAP) / cap(A_z, S),   nu_z := e_z / e_z(dA_z).   (RATIO*)

(4d) POINTWISE FROM z (PE-DOORREACH Section 5 with its checker repair). v >= 0 solves L v = 0 on B_{2rho}(z) subset Omega. Rescale u(y) := v(z + rho y), |y| <= 2: Delta_y u = b'(y) . grad_y u with |b'|_inf <= rho beta G = G, BETA-FREE. By the HARNACK INEQUALITY (NAMED: Gilbarg-Trudinger Thm 8.20; hypothesis rows: (i) u >= 0 weak H^1 solution on B_2 — met; (ii) ellipticity ratio 1 — met; (iii) scale-invariant drift bound |b'| <= G — met by rho = 1/beta), applied on B_{3/2} as the DOORREACH checker's repair prescribes ("apply GT 8.20 on B_{3/2} instead of B_1: u(0) <= sup_{B_{3/2}} u <= C_H' inf_{B_{3/2}} u <= C_H' u(y) for every y in dB_1"), and since nu_z is carried by dA_z:
  v(z) <= C_H' E_{nu_z}[ v ],  C_H' = C(n,G) beta-free.                        (PTW*)

=====================================================================
5. INGREDIENT (i): ENTRY PROBABILITY AT THE GATE, AND h <= 1/2 ON dA_z
=====================================================================
Communication heights (exact objects): for a compact Y, Theta(x,Y) := inf over simple piecewise-C^1 arcs gamma from x to Y of max_gamma E_eps; Theta(x,S) is written with Y = {g*}.

(5a) UPPER CAPACITY AT THE GATE (PE-DOORREACH Section 3 verbatim, with the component truncation forced by TRAP not being a superlevel set). Let theta be a Sard-regular value in [Theta(z,TRAP) - 1/beta, Theta(z,TRAP)], a := theta - 1/beta, and f(x) := median{0, (theta - E_eps(x)) beta, 1} — PE-DOORREACH's level ramp. Let W be the connected component of the open set {E_eps < theta} containing z, and set f~ := f on W, f~ := 0 off W. Since theta is regular, dW subset {E_eps = theta} where f = 0, so f~ is Lipschitz. f~ = 1 on A_z (A_z is connected, inside {E_eps <= E_eps(z) + G/beta} subset {E_eps < a} for beta >= beta_*), and f~ = 0 on TRAP: TRAP inter W = empty because W meets TRAP only if some arc from z into TRAP stays below theta, contradicting theta <= Theta(z,TRAP). Hence f~ is admissible for cap(A_z, TRAP) and, exactly as in PE-DOORREACH Section 3,
  cap(A_z, TRAP) <= D(f~) <= D(f) <= e^2 G^2 V_M beta exp( -beta Theta(z,TRAP) ).      (CAP-UP-GATE)
By (G1)+(G2)+(G3), every arc from z (w_phi = 0) to TRAP either crosses Delta_phi or ends on TRAP inter {w_phi = 0}, so
  Theta(z, TRAP) >= Gate - 4G/beta = m_k + 2 lambda - 4G/beta.                          (GATE-LOWER)
This is the level-ramp at the Delta_phi gate the design pass asks for, at the design's own level m_k + 2 lambda [proofs:8914-8917].

(5b) LOWER CAPACITY TO S (PE-DOORREACH Section 4 Thomson tube verbatim, along an arc instead of a straight segment). Let gamma be a simple piecewise-C^1 arc from z to g* with max_gamma E_eps <= Theta(z,S) + eta, of length Ell, whose rho-tube Tub is embedded. Let D_0 := the (n-1)-disc of radius rho/2 centred at z orthogonal to gamma'(0) (contained in A_z), D_end the corresponding disc at g* (contained in S since rho <= delta/8), J := (1/Ar) tangent(gamma) on Tub and 0 elsewhere, Ar := omega_{n-1}(rho/2)^{n-1}. J is divergence-free inside Tub, tangential on the lateral boundary, with unit flux. The elementary (Cauchy-Schwarz) half of THOMSON'S PRINCIPLE, proved inline exactly as PE-DOORREACH does: for Lipschitz f with f = 1 on A_z, f = 0 on S, (int <J, grad f>)^2 = 1 <= En(J) D(f) with En(J) := int |J|^2/w, so cap(A_z,S) >= 1/En(J). By sup_Tub E_eps <= Theta(z,S) + eta + G rho,
  cap(A_z, S) >= (Ar / (beta Ell)) exp( -beta (Theta(z,S) + eta + G/beta) )
              = c(N,delta) beta^{-2N} exp( -beta (Theta(z,S) + eta) ),  c beta-free.     (CAP-LOW*)
(The tube's max energy, not any pointwise value, is what enters — the same accounting as PE-DOORREACH's (TUBE-LEVEL).)

(5c) CONSEQUENCE 1: h <= 1/2 on dA_z. Running PE-DOORREACH Sections 2 + 5 VERBATIM with Door' replaced by TRAP (step (2b)'s minimum principle and step (2c)'s monotonicity are stated for an arbitrary closed target; the only replacement is the ramp of (5a)) gives, for every y in B_{2rho}(z),
  h(y) = P_y(H_TRAP < H_S) <= C_H' cap(A_y,TRAP)/cap(A_y,S) <= C_3 beta^{2N+1} exp( -beta ( Theta(z,TRAP) - Theta(z,S) - 2G/beta ) ).   (ENTRY)
By (GATE-LOWER) and Theta(z,S) <= S_k + c_H + eta (Section 6), the exponent is at least Gate - S_k - c_H - eta - 6G/beta >= 3 c_H - eta - 6G/beta > 0 by (G1)'s chain Gate >= S_k + 4 c_H, so h <= 1/2 on dA_z for all beta >= beta_1 := a beta-free threshold. NO CIRCULARITY: (ENTRY) uses only (CAP-UP-GATE), (CAP-LOW*) and PE-DOORREACH Section 2/5, never (SANDWICH).
CARE POINT (c), the degenerate start: (ENTRY) is not needed at full strength anywhere, but for the record, if z sits at or above the gate level the display is not degenerate — (ENTRY) is then replaced by the trivial P <= 1 <= C_3 beta^{2N+1} exp(-beta(Gate - E_eps(z))), whose exponent is <= 0 there. The two cases are exhaustive and neither is used to prove the other.

=====================================================================
6. INGREDIENT (iii), ASSEMBLY, AND THE CANCELLATION ARITHMETIC
=====================================================================
(iii) mu(TRAP), R3-STRAT CONSUMED VERBATIM. "On the |j| = 1 slices, and on all other pieces, (FLOOR) gives E_eps >= m_k + m_1(lambda) pointwise; on |j| >= 2 the sharper floor m_k + 8 lambda j^2/N holds" [proofs:4992-4994] — the ridge law for |j| = 1 and the quadratic floor for |j| >= 2. Hence E_eps >= m_k + m_1(lambda) on STRAT, and on TRAP subset {dist(.,STRAT) <= 4rho}, E_eps >= m_k + m_1(lambda) - 4G/beta. Therefore
  mu(TRAP) <= Leb(TRAP) e^{-beta(m_k + m_1(lambda))} e^{4G} <= e^{4G} V_M exp( -beta ( m_k + m_1(lambda) ) ).   (MU-TRAP)
(The N-fold slice count of R3-STRAT's (NUM-STRAT) is not needed once the uniform floor is used; the display is R3-STRAT's numerator with its own floors.)

ASSEMBLY. Chain (PTW*), (RATIO*), (MU-TRAP), (CAP-LOW*), and Section 2:
  E_z[ int_0^{H_S ^ T} 1_TRAP ds ] <= v(z) <= C_H' . 2 mu(TRAP) / cap(A_z,S)
     <= C_4(N,delta,eps) beta^{2N} exp( -beta ( m_k + m_1(lambda) - Theta(z,S) - eta - 4G/beta - G/beta ) ),
  C_4 := 2 C_H' e^{5G} V_M / c(N,delta),  beta-free.                                    (TRAPOCC*)

THE CANCELLATION, DISPLAYED. The design pass's accounting is
  (i) x [(iii)/(iv)] = e^{-beta(gate - E_eps(z))} x e^{-beta(floor - gate)} = e^{-beta(floor - E_eps(z))},
with (iv) cap(TRAP,S) >= c poly(beta) e^{-beta(Theta_gate + err)} the Thomson tube of (5b) routed over the gate (same construction, arc from g* to TRAP, tube max energy = Theta_gate). In (TRAPOCC*) the same cancellation occurs IDENTICALLY rather than numerically: the gate enters twice, once in (ENTRY)'s numerator through Theta(z,TRAP) and once in the equilibrium denominator through Theta_gate = Theta(g*,TRAP), and these are the SAME communication height. Indeed Theta_gate <= max(Theta(z,S), Theta(z,TRAP)) = Theta(z,TRAP), since Theta(z,TRAP) >= Gate - 4G/beta > S_k + c_H + eta >= Theta(z,S) by (G1) and Section 6's component bound. So the factored form
  entry x mu(TRAP)/cap(TRAP,S) <= C poly(beta) e^{-beta(Theta(z,TRAP) - Theta(z,S))} . e^{-beta(m_k+m_1 - Theta_gate)}
     <= C poly(beta) e^{-beta(m_k + m_1(lambda) - Theta(z,S))}
reproduces (TRAPOCC*) exactly, and the collapsed route of Sections 3-4 delivers it WITHOUT ever needing the numerical value of the gate or its attainment. The gate is load-bearing only qualitatively, through h <= 1/2 in (5c).

THE E_eps(z) SLOT. Theta(z,S) is what the capacity denominator can see. Unconditionally, for z in the connected component R_0^* of the open set {w_theta=k, w_phi=0, E_eps < S_k + c_H + eta} containing g*, any arc realizing the component's connectivity gives Theta(z,S) <= S_k + c_H + eta, so
  sup_{z in R_0^*} E_z[ int_0^{H_S ^ T} 1_TRAP ds ] <= C_4 beta^{2N} exp( -beta ( m_k + m_1(lambda) - S_k - c_H - err ) ).   (TRAPOCC-UNIF)
This is EXACTLY the factor the schedule consumes ("E_{doorway-level start}[trap occupation before H_S ^ T] <= C' poly(beta) e^{+beta(S_k + c_H - m_k - m_1(lambda) + err)}", [proofs:8888-8890]). The z-pointwise refinement E_eps(z) in place of S_k + c_H is (TRAPOCC*) under the typed row (H-DESC): Theta(z,S) <= E_eps(z) + err_desc.

ERR LEDGER (every loss O(delta^2) + O(h) + eps-class, or beta-vanishing).
  - eta: the arc-optimality slack, free (send eta -> 0 at fixed beta; it enters no constant). [SUPERSEDED
    2026-07-27 by TRAPOCC-2 Section 7.3 + AM-R5-19(c): eta is FROZEN
    at err class (eta := L_eps N delta^2/8 per AM-R5-27's re-freeze,
    say - the original L_eps N delta^2 value made c_0 - eta negative,
    ENTRY-W v2's (ENTRY-MARGIN) catch), NEVER sent to 0 - so
    the (Theta+eta)-near-optimal arc has length <= Ell_max(N,delta,eps)
    as (T3) requires and c(N,delta) is honest; the exponent is
    unchanged because eta is inside err.]
  - 4G/beta (collar transfer, (G3)), 4G/beta ((MU-TRAP)), G/beta (tube height, (5b)), 2/beta (ramp width and Sard offset, (5a)): all multiply beta to give the beta-free constants e^{4G}, e^{5G}, e^2 in C_4; NOTHING in the exponent. Beta-vanishing class.
  - The tube's delta-loss when Theta(z,S) is evaluated at the ground: for z in S the same (UP-QUAD) computation PE-DOORREACH performs gives Theta(z,S) <= m_k + eps w_k + (L_eps/8) delta^2, i.e. the eps-class term eps w_k = eps g(N) and the O(delta^2) term of R3-STRAT's err, "err(eps, delta) := eps w_k + L_eps N delta^2/16" [proofs:5067].
  - poly(beta) = beta^{2N}: allowed outright by the deliverable's shape "C(N, delta, eps) poly(beta)" [proofs:8899-8901]. If an err-class exponent is preferred it is absorbed exactly as PE-DOORREACH's ledger does, into the headroom s = (N/4 - 1/8) L_eps delta^2 > 0.
  - C_H' (Harnack), the factor 2 of (SANDWICH), C_up, c(N,delta): beta-free.

=====================================================================
7. THE COMPANION DISPLAY (TRAP_2, floor S_k + c_H) AND THE NEAR-S CASE
=====================================================================

8. THE SCHEDULE CONSEQUENCE (one paragraph)
=====================================================================
Per round, the trap term is the product of PE-DOORREACH's reach probability from the collar and (TRAPOCC-UNIF): with "sup_{z in dS^+} P_z( tau_lev < T ) <= C_1(eps, delta) exp( -beta ( S_k + c_H - m_k - eps w_k - L_eps N delta^2 / 4 ) )" [proofs:8420-8423],
  per-round trap occupation <= C_1 C_4 beta^{2N} exp( -beta [ (S_k + c_H - m_k - err) + (m_k + m_1(lambda) - S_k - c_H - err) ] )
                            = C_1 C_4 beta^{2N} exp( -beta ( m_1(lambda) - err ) ),
the design pass's own coupled display [proofs:8886-8893]. The row's requirement is "<= T_row(eps, delta) exp(-beta(c_H/2 - err(delta))), T_row beta-free" [lane-lp-product-saddle-v1.md:225-226], so the margin needed is m_1(lambda) - c_H/2, which is ADJ-2's identity, verbatim: "m_1 - c_H/2 = lambda g(N) - (1/8)( g(N) + 2 - S_k ) = g(N)( lambda - 1/8 ) + ( S_k - 2 )/8." with "Both summands are STRICTLY POSITIVE for every N>=10, lambda>=1" [proofs:5089-5092, quoting lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:730-731]. The err class is absorbed by R3-STRAT's own eps-window: eps g(N) + O(N L_eps delta^2) < g(N)(lambda - 1/8) + (S_k - 2)/8 holds whenever eps < lambda - 1/8, which M2-PIN's lambda > kappa = 1 grants for every eps <= 7/8 [proofs, R3-STRAT section 7(b)]. The w_phi = 0 companion clears with the full doorway margin: reach x (TRAPOCC-2*) = exp(-beta(S_k + c_H - m_k - err)), and at the flagship point S_k + c_H - m_k = 1.024350 against c_H/2 = 0.162608. Note also, as the design pass records, that the coupled exponent m_1(lambda) = lambda g(N) GROWS in lambda, so large lambda helps and no B-LAMBDA constraint survives.

=====================================================================
9. WHY NOTHING IS SMUGGLED
=====================================================================
No independence is claimed anywhere; the only probabilistic tools are the strong Markov property (through the Dirichlet representation only), the pathwise truncation of Section 2, and reversibility via div(w grad u) = mu L u. No dynamical row is consumed, so the piece is COND-free on the same basis PE-DOORREACH established. No capacity-ratio lemma and no Thomson principle are imported: (FLUX-ID'), (SANDWICH), (EQ-OCC) and the Cauchy-Schwarz half of Thomson are each proved inline from Green's second identity and the minimum principle. The three blocked compositions PE-DOORREACH ruled out are still avoided: time never enters the estimate (no supermartingale discount), no per-window union appears (a single global variational comparison), and no superharmonic function of the level is used (the ramp is a test function, the lower bound is a flow).

Four residual rows, each at exact strength. None weakens the delivered exponent; (T1) is the only one that touches the FORM of the display, and the schedule-consumed form (TRAPOCC-UNIF) is proved without it.

(T1) (H-DESC) — DESCENT CONNECTIVITY, the E_eps(z) slot. EXACT REQUIRED STRENGTH: for every z in R_0 there is a simple piecewise-C^1 arc from z to g* with max E_eps along it <= E_eps(z) + err_desc, err_desc of err class (O(delta^2) + eps-class); equivalently Theta(z,S) <= E_eps(z) + err_desc. WHY NEEDED: (CAP-LOW*) can only see the communication height Theta(z,S), not E_eps(z); the design pass's display carries E_eps(z). WHAT IS PROVED WITHOUT IT: (TRAPOCC*) with E_eps(z) replaced by Theta(z,S), plus the unconditional component bound Theta(z,S) <= S_k + c_H + eta on R_0^* — i.e. exactly (TRAPOCC-UNIF), which is the factor the schedule multiplies against PE-DOORREACH's reach, so Section 8 closes in full. (T2) (H-CONN) — COMPONENT MEMBERSHIP. EXACT REQUIRED STRENGTH: z lies in the connected component R_0^* of the open set {w_theta = k, w_phi = 0, E_eps < S_k + c_H + eta} that contains g*. 0. THE DEFECT, AND WHAT IS WITHDRAWN

------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. THE OBJECT: OBJECT-PE1-DEL
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Setting inherited verbatim: "dX_t = -grad E_eps(X_t) dt + sqrt(2/beta) dW_t
on M = T^{2N}" (MM:3002); "S := B_{delta/4}(g*)", "S^+ := B_{delta/2}(g*)
(= B_h(g*) - the exit collar), S subset S^+" (MM:3009-3010), max norm,
g* in G_k. Filtration: the ONE augmented path filtration, "F_t :=
sigma(X_{s} : s <= t) completed and made right-continuous ... hitting times of
Borel sets by the continuous process X, hence (F_t)-stopping times"
(MM:3036). Operators, verbatim: "theta^+(t) := inf{ s >= t : X_s not in S^+ }"
and "D(t) := inf{ s >= theta^+(t) : X_s in S }" (MM:3016-3017).

OBJECT-PE1-DEL. The DELAYED S-return cycle. Epoch recursion T_{n+1} := D(T_n),
n >= 0, T_0 := D(0) — EXACTLY R5a's convention "sigma_0 := D(0) ... sigma_i :=
D(sigma_{i-1})" (MM:3026-3027). Cycle C^{del} := T_1 - T_0; per-cycle
occupation V_B^{del} := int_{T_0}^{T_1} 1_B(X_s) ds; entrance law
rho_S^{Palm,del}; expectation operator E_Palm^{del}; cycle-start intensity
lambda_S^{del}. Every T_n is an (F_t)-stopping time (MM:3036 template) and
X_{T_n} lies on the max-norm sphere of radius delta/4 about g*.

[SUPERSEDED 2026-07-27 by CURE-XE2-F1a (below), per XE-2 finding 1: the
set E as defined here requires X_t in S while the recursion epochs land on
the max-norm sphere, so E contained no epoch above T_0 and LEMMA EQV was
false as stated. The operative definition ((E1)+(E2)+(E3) on closure(S))
and the re-proved EQV are in the cure piece.]
INTRINSIC (SHIFT-COVARIANT) FORM. Put
   E := { t : X_t in S and there exists s < t with X_s not in S^+ and
              X_u not in S for all u in (s,t) }.
E is defined by a property of the path germ to the left of t only, hence is
shift-covariant: E(shift_r X) = E(X) - r.

LEMMA EQV (the recursion generates E). For t > T_0: t in E iff t = D(T_m) for
some m >= 0. PROOF. (=>) Let t in E with witness s, and let T_m := max(E cap
[T_0,t)) (well defined by Lemma LF below). X_{T_m} in S and X_u not in S on
(s,t) force T_m <= s; the path is outside S^+ at s, so theta^+(T_m) <= s.
Hence t is an S-visit at or after theta^+(T_m), so D(T_m) <= t. If D(T_m) < t,
then u := D(T_m) satisfies X_u in S with witness s' := theta^+(T_m) (X_{s'}
not in S^+ by continuity and openness of S^+, and X not in S on (s',u) by the
infimum in MM:3017), so u in E and T_m < theta^+(T_m) <= u < t, contradicting
maximality. So D(T_m) = t. (<=) Same witness s' = theta^+(T_m). QED.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. LEMMA LF (LOCAL FINITENESS — the exact XE-1 F1 hole, closed PATHWISE)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
[READS, per AM-R5-18(b) + CURE-XE2-F1b: on BOUNDED windows - #(E cap
[a,t]) finite for every a < t, same compactness argument on [a,T_*]; the
two-sided stationary object has infinitely many points in (-infinity,t]
and needs only per-window finiteness.]
CLAIM. For EVERY continuous path and every finite t, #(E cap (-infinity,t])
is finite; equivalently T_n -> infinity strictly increasing.
PROOF (no probability used). Strict increase: MM:3019 verbatim — "every
delayed return carries a genuine excursion of radial extent >= delta/4, and
D(t) > t strictly. There are NO trivial zero-time returns". Separation:
between consecutive epochs the path visits the complement of S^+, so there is
s_n in (T_n,T_{n+1}) with |X_{s_n} - g*|_max >= delta/2 while
|X_{T_n} - g*|_max <= delta/4; hence
   osc_max( X ; [T_n, T_{n+1}] ) >= delta/4      for every n.        (SEP)
Suppose infinitely many epochs lie in [0,t]. They accumulate at some
T_* <= t. X is uniformly continuous on the compact [0,T_*], so there is
eta > 0 with |X_u - X_v|_max < delta/4 whenever |u-v| <= eta, u,v in [0,T_*];
but T_{n+1} - T_n -> 0 along the accumulating subsequence, contradicting
(SEP). QED.
WHY THE PLAIN OBJECT FAILS HERE AND THIS ONE DOES NOT: (SEP) is exactly what
the plain epoch set lacks — a plain re-entry needs no displacement at all, so
no modulus-of-continuity argument is available. Local finiteness is not a
regularity nicety, it is the existence hypothesis of the point process.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. LEMMA SPACE (POSITIVE MEAN SPACING, UNIFORM OVER STARTS)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
CLASSICAL FACTS NAMED (both already imported by R3-SOJ at PX:4298-4318, rows
re-checked here, not re-proved):
 SR-PE1D.A  Ito's formula for a C^2 function of a nondegenerate Ito diffusion
   (Karatzas-Shreve, Brownian Motion and Stochastic Calculus, 2nd ed., Ch. 3
   Thm 3.6). HYPOTHESIS ROWS. (h1) smooth coefficients, uniformly
   nondegenerate second-order part on compact connected T^{2N} — MET verbatim
   at PX:4301-4304 ("coefficients, compact connected T^{2N}, diffusion
   beta^-1 I uniformly"). (h2) f in C^2 — MET: f(x) = |x - x_0|_2^2 on the
   lift is a polynomial.
 SR-PE1D.B  Optional sampling for a bounded continuous martingale at a bounded
   stopping time (Revuz-Yor Ch. II Thm 3.2). ROWS. (h1) continuity — MET.
   (h2) boundedness of the stopped process — MET: |X - x_0|_2 <= delta/4 and
   the compensator is bounded on [T_0, (T_0+n) ^ rho]. (h3) bounded stopping
   time — MET by truncation at T_0+n, limit by MONOTONE convergence, not by
   an unproved uniform-integrability claim (same discipline as PX:4316-4318).

CLAIM (SPACE). With G_* := sup_{S^+} |grad E_eps|_2 (finite: E_eps smooth on
compact M),
   inf_{x in S} E_x[ theta^+(0) ] >= c_* := (delta^2/16) / (4N/beta + G_* delta/2) > 0,
   [READS, per CURE-XE2-F1a membership discipline: inf over closure(S) -
   same proof, same c_*; the containment step consumes only
   |x_0 - g*|_max <= delta/4, valid on the closed ball. The instantiation
   at X_{T_n} (sphere) is thereby in-domain.]
and therefore, by strong Markov at T_n (MM:3036, autonomous SDE),
   E[ T_{n+1} - T_n | F_{T_n} ] >= E[ theta^+(T_n) - T_n | F_{T_n} ] >= c_*  a.s.
PROOF. Work on the universal cover; x_0 := X_{T_0}, u(x) := |x - x_0|_2^2,
grad u = 2(x-x_0), Hess u = 2 I. By SR-PE1D.A,
   du(X_t) = [ 4N/beta - 2 (X_t - x_0) . grad E_eps(X_t) ] dt
             + 2 sqrt(2/beta) (X_t - x_0) . dW_t .
Let rho := inf{ t >= T_0 : |X_t - x_0|_2 >= delta/4 }. CONTAINMENT: for
t in [T_0,rho), |X_t - x_0|_max <= |X_t - x_0|_2 < delta/4 and
|x_0 - g*|_max <= delta/4, so |X_t - g*|_max < delta/2, i.e. X_t in S^+;
hence rho <= theta^+(T_0). On [T_0,rho] the drift term is bounded by
K := 4N/beta + (delta/2) G_*. Apply SR-PE1D.B to the stopped compensated
process at rho_n := rho ^ (T_0+n):
   E[ u(X_{rho_n}) | F_{T_0} ] <= K . E[ rho_n - T_0 | F_{T_0} ].
On {rho <= T_0+n}, u(X_{rho_n}) = (delta/4)^2 by path continuity; on the
complement u >= 0. So (delta/4)^2 P(rho <= T_0+n | F_{T_0}) <= K E[rho - T_0 |
F_{T_0}]. Since rho <= theta^+(T_0) < infinity a.s. (finite mean at
PX:4388), letting n -> infinity gives (delta/4)^2 <= K E[rho - T_0 | F_{T_0}],
i.e. the claim. QED.
CONSISTENCY. c_* <= (1/8) N beta delta^2, the landed upper bound (PX:4388):
in the drift-free limit c_* = beta delta^2/(64 N) and the ratio of bounds is
8N^2 >= 1. The spacing is beta-DEPENDENT (and delta-, N-dependent); the brief
requires only positivity, and only positivity is used.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

LOWER. c_* > 0 by Lemma SPACE. Since rho_S^{Palm,del} is carried on S, both
[READS, per AM-R5-18(b) + CURE-XE2-F1a: carried on the max-norm SPHERE of
radius delta/4, a subset of closure(S); both bounds remain entrance-law-
free suprema/infima over starts, now over closure(S)/S^+ domains that

bounds are entrance-law-free suprema/infima over starts and pass to the Palm
average:
   0 < c_* <= E_Palm^{del}[ C ] <= C_* < infinity.                   (INT-DEL)
[SUPERSEDED 2026-07-27 by CURE-XE2-F1b (below), per XE-2 finding 2: nu is
a last-passage index, not a G-stopping time ({nu <= n} = {T_{n+1} > t} is

FINITE POSITIVE INTENSITY, PROVED WITHOUT PALM CIRCULARITY. Under the
stationary law (X_0 ~ rho_beta), let T_0 := min(E cap [0,infinity)) (a.s.
finite, E[T_0] <= C_*) and nu := max{n >= 0 : T_n <= t}. {nu >= n} = {T_n <=
t} in F_{T_n}, so nu is a stopping time for G_n := F_{T_n}. By Lemma SPACE,
S_n := T_n - n c_* is a G-SUBmartingale, integrable by (INT-DEL-UP)
(E[T_n] <= (n+1) C_*). Doob optional stopping at the bounded time nu ^ m
(NAMED: Doob's optional-stopping theorem for submartingales at bounded

and lambda_S^{del} > 0 because E[C] <= C_* < infinity forbids a null process [SUPERSEDED

5. THE PALM / REGENERATIVE STRUCTURE ON THE DELAYED CYCLES
------------------------------------------------------------------------
The imported SR-PE1 statement is GENERIC in the delimiter, verbatim: "let the
successive A-cycles be delimited by a regeneration epoch sequence 0 <= T_0 <
T_1 < T_2 < ... adapted to A (the Palm/cycle construction: ... or directly

6. THE S-SOJOURN INSIDE A DELAYED CYCLE (AM-R4-18 REPLACED)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
AM-R4-18 claimed, on the plain object, "within one plain cycle the S-sojourn
is the single interval [T_0, tau_S)" (PX:6921-6923). That single-interval
claim is WITHDRAWN with its object. The honest delayed statement is ALREADY
LANDED and needs no new work — R3-SOJ Section 2a, verbatim:
"Now split [T_0, D(T_0)) = [T_0, theta^+(T_0)) union [theta^+(T_0), D(T_0)).
On the SECOND piece the path is NOT in S ... Hence
   V_S^{del} = int_{T_0}^{theta^+(T_0)} 1_S(X_s) ds <= theta^+(T_0) - T_0.
(The path may leave and re-enter S several times inside the collar before
theta^+; that is irrelevant — the occupation of any set over an interval is
at most the interval length.)" (PX:4070-4080).
So the sojourn SET is {t in [T_0, theta^+(T_0)) : X_t in S}, possibly a
countable union of intervals, contained in [T_0, theta^+(T_0)); the bound is
a containment, not an interval identity, and (R3-SOJ.a) applies UNCHANGED:
   AM-R4-18' :  E_Palm^{del}[ V_S ] <= (1/8) N beta delta^2 ,
which is the ALREADY-LANDED "(R3-SOJ.b) E_{Palm}^{del}[ V_S ] <= (1/8) N beta
delta^2 (object O2)" (PX:4415). Because "(R3-SOJ.a) IS A SUPREMUM OVER
STARTS, IT IS VALID UNDER ANY ENTRANCE LAW" (PX:4405-4406), no entrance-law
transfer is consumed.
EVERY DOWNSTREAM CONSUMER USED ONLY V_S <= theta^+ - T_0 — VERIFIED by
reading the R3-ASM plain-cycle passage, verbatim: "together with R3-SOJ's
containment V_S^{pl} <= theta^+(T_0) - T_0 (its Section 2b ...),
E_{Palm}^{pl}[ V_S ] <= E_{Palm}^{pl}[ theta^+(T_0) - T_0 ] <= sup_{x in S}
E_x[theta^+(0)] <= (1/8) N beta delta^2. (SOJ) No entrance law is used in the
last two steps: a supremum over start points is entrance-law-free"
(PX:5586-5593). RE-POINTING: replace "V_S^{pl} ... its Section 2b" by
"V_S^{del} ... its Section 2a (PX:4070-4080)" and the superscript pl by del;
the last two steps are untouched, the constant is untouched.
[STRENGTHENED 2026-07-27, per the CURE-XE2-F1a internal checker's MAJOR
(adopted): the delayed entrance law is carried on the sphere, which the
index set of sup_{x in S} does not contain, and 'a supremum over starts is
entrance-law-free' is valid only for laws carried inside the index set.
The two occurrences of sup_{x in S} in the (SOJ) chain READ sup_{x in S^+}
via the ALREADY-LANDED extension '(R3-SOJ.a) ... Indeed sup_{x in S^+}
E_x[theta^+(0)] <= (1/8) N beta delta^2 as well' (PX:4390-4392, HEAD
4407-4409), whose index set contains closure(S). Constant unchanged. The
same re-read applies to the R3-ASM source passage and to the AM-R5-20
audit row's justification clause for that site.]

### F1 — typed gaps

GAP-PE1D-NORM (COSMETIC; typed, not closed). The spacing constant is stated with G_* := sup_{S^+} |grad E_eps|_2, finite because E_eps is smooth on the compact M. The EXPLICIT beta-free form G_* <= L_eps delta/2 uses (M5-DRIFT) "|grad E_eps(x)| <= L_eps dist(x, G_k), L_eps <= L + 8 eps" (lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:1414-1419) together with dist(., G_k) <= |. - g*|_max <= delta/2 on S^+, and therefore rides the max-vs-Euclidean bookkeeping of the inherited GAP-M5-EUC (lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:1712-1727). LOAD-BEARING CONTENT: only the FINITENESS of G_*, which needs no norm bookkeeping. IMPACT IF NOT CLOSED: the numerical value of c_* changes by a factor <= sqrt(2N); positivity, (INTENS) and every downstream display are unaffected. EXACT STRENGTH OWED: the one-way Euclidean->max-norm containment constant on S^+, already owned by GAP-M5-EUC.

GAP-PE1D-ERGODIC (NOT LOAD-BEARING; recorded so nobody assumes more). Uniqueness of the ambient invariant probability (ROW SR-PE1.1, lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:1853-1879, with ROW SR-PE1.2) makes the stationary process ergodic under the shift. This piece does NOT use ergodicity: (RR-DEL), (KAC-OCC-DEL), (PALM-INV-DEL), (KAC-RATIO-DEL) are identities between expectations and hold under stationarity alone. Ergodicity would only be needed to identify PATHWISE time averages with rho_beta, which no consumer requests. Recorded, not claimed as proved here.

# PIECE DOORREACH-MAXFIX — the Thomson tube in the max metric (cures XE-1 F4; supersedes the tube section + AM-R5-14 half-repair)

(XE-1-cure grade: draft PROVED-WITH-TYPED-GAPS; checker REPAIRABLE)

=====================================================================
AM-R5-18 (XE-1 F4): REPLACEMENT OF PE-DOORREACH STEP 4 (TUBE) AND
STEP 6 (BUDGET). Supersedes the landed Step 4 "Geometry/Flow" block
and the landed Step-6 arithmetic; AM-R5-14's half-repair (item 3) is
WITHDRAWN and replaced by what follows.
=====================================================================

0. THE METRIC FACTS, STATED ONCE

Declaration (verbatim, lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3002): "Ambient tube radii and
dist(.,G_k) are read in the max norm as everywhere in the corpus". Containment
(verbatim, lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3010): "S subset S^+ subset U_ch :=
{dist(.,G_k) <= delta/2} = U_{1/2}."

So S = B^max_{delta/4}(g*), S^+ = B^max_{delta/2}(g*), and z in dS^+ means
||z - g*||_max = delta/2. On R^n, n = 2N,

  ||x||_max <= |x|_2 <= sqrt(n) ||x||_max                                  (NRM)

ALWAYS (left: the max coordinate is one summand of the Euclidean sum; right:
n equal summands). Two consequences used below, in the CORRECT direction:

  (NRM-a)  B^euc_r(p) subset B^max_r(p)  for every r, p   [from max <= euc];
  (NRM-b)  z in dS^+  =>  delta/2 <= |z - g*|_2 <= sqrt(2N) delta/2.

(NRM-b) is the defect XE-1 named: the landed tube fixed the EUCLIDEAN length
ell = delta/2, which is the LOWER end of the range, and then asserted the
terminal disc lies in S. False whenever |z - g*|_2 > delta/2, i.e. generically.

Write ell(z) := |z - g*|_2 in [delta/2, sqrt(2N) delta/2] and
v := (g* - z)/|z - g*|_2 (unit Euclidean).

=====================================================================
4'. LOWER CAPACITY: THE HONEST-LENGTH TUBE
=====================================================================

(4'a) THE SEGMENT STAYS IN THE COLLAR. For s in [0, ell(z)],

  z + s v - g* = (1 - s/ell(z)) (z - g*),  hence
  || z + s v - g* ||_max = (1 - s/ell(z)) * (delta/2).                    (SEG)

(SEG) is an identity, not an estimate. It also re-proves the qualitative
statement the brief asks to be said out loud: max-norm balls are CONVEX (they
are norm balls), and both endpoints z and g* lie in the closed collar
B^max_{delta/2}(g*), so the whole straight segment [z, g*] lies in it -
regardless of how much longer than delta/2 the segment is in the Euclidean
metric. The honest Euclidean length ell(z) is therefore admissible: no part
of the segment leaves the collar, hence none leaves U_ch (:3010), hence none
leaves U where (UP-QUAD) is stated.

(4'b) THE TUBE, WITH ITS TWO ENDS. Fix rho := 1/beta, A := closed B^euc_rho(z)
(the Harnack ball of Step 5). Put

  s_0 := rho/2      (start offset along v, so the source disc sits inside A),
  s_1 := ell(z) - delta/8   (STOP at Euclidean distance delta/8 from g*),
  r   := rho / (2 sqrt(2N))                (cross-section radius, operative),
  Tub := { z + s v + y : s in [s_0, s_1], y perp v, |y|_2 <= r }.

s_0 < s_1 because ell(z) >= delta/2 and rho/2 <= delta/8 for beta >= 4/delta.

(4'c) LATERAL CONTAINMENT (the margin arithmetic, displayed). For a tube point
x = z + s v + y as above, by (SEG), the triangle inequality in ||.||_max, and
(NRM) applied to y,

  ||x - g*||_max <= (1 - s/ell(z))(delta/2) + ||y||_max
                 <= (delta/2) - (s/ell(z))(delta/2) + r .

So Tub subset B^max_{delta/2}(g*) as soon as r <= (s_0/ell(z))(delta/2), and
since ell(z) <= sqrt(2N) delta/2 by (NRM-b) it SUFFICES that

  r <= s_0 / sqrt(2N).                                                   (MARG)

Two readings of (MARG), both recorded:
  - GEOMETRIC CEILING. With the generous start s_0 = delta/8, (MARG) reads
    exactly r <= delta/(8 sqrt(2N)) =: r_tube. This is the brief's r_tube and
    it is sharp for that start: the margin at s = delta/8 is at least
    (delta/8)/sqrt(2N) = r_tube.
  - OPERATIVE RADIUS. The source disc must lie in A, so s_0 = rho/2 and
    r = rho/(2 sqrt(2N)) meets (MARG) with equality, and
    sqrt(s_0^2 + r^2) <= rho/sqrt(2) < rho puts the source disc
    D_0 := { z + s_0 v + y : y perp v, |y|_2 <= r } inside A. Moreover
    r <= r_tube whenever rho <= delta/4, i.e. beta >= 4/delta (inside beta_*).
    The operative tube is thus thinner than the geometric ceiling everywhere.

(4'd) THE SINK LANDS IN S, LEGITIMATELY. The terminal disc is
D_end := { p + y : y perp v, |y|_2 <= r } with p := z + s_1 v, so
|p - g*|_2 = delta/8 by construction. For y in D_end, Pythagoras in the
Euclidean metric and then (NRM-a):

  |y - g*|_2 = sqrt( (delta/8)^2 + |y - p|_2^2 ) <= (delta/8) sqrt(1 + 1/(2N))
             <= (delta/8) sqrt(1.05) < delta/7 ,
  hence ||y - g*||_max <= |y - g*|_2 < delta/7 < delta/4 ,

so D_end subset B^max_{delta/4}(g*) = S. The chain is
B^euc_{delta/8}(g*) subset B^max_{delta/8}(g*) subset B^max_{delta/4}(g*) = S,
i.e. exactly the brief's inclusion, with the inequality used in the only
direction in which it is true (max <= euclidean). CROSS-CHECK by (SEG):
||p - g*||_max = ((delta/8)/ell(z))(delta/2) <= delta/8 since ell(z) >= delta/2,
and adding r <= delta/8 again gives <= delta/4. Both routes agree.

(4'e) ENERGY ON THE TUBE (the AM-R5-15 constant). Every x in Tub lies in the
closed max collar by (4'c), and g* in G_k, so by (NRM),
dist_euc(x, G_k)^2 <= |x - g*|_2^2 <= 2N ||x - g*||_max^2 <= 2N (delta/2)^2
= N delta^2 / 2. This is AM-R5-15 verbatim: "on the max-norm collar
S^+ = B_{delta/2}(g*), dist_euc(x,g*)^2 <= 2N (delta/2)^2 = N delta^2 / 2, so
(UP-QUAD) gives the quadratic cost L_eps N delta^2 / 4 - NOT /16."
With (UP-QUAD) [lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:632] applied on U:

  sup_{Tub} E_eps <= m_k + eps w_k + (L_eps/2)(N delta^2/2)
                   = m_k + eps w_k + L_eps N delta^2 / 4 =: A_tube.    (TUBE-LEVEL')

(4'f) FLOW AND CAPACITY. J := (1/Ar) v on Tub and 0 elsewhere, with
Ar := omega_{2N-1} r^{2N-1} = omega_{2N-1} (2 beta sqrt(2N))^{-(2N-1)}. J is
constant hence divergence-free inside Tub, tangential on the lateral boundary,
with unit flux from D_0 (in A) to D_end (in S). For Lipschitz f with f = 1 on A
and f = 0 on S, Fubini along the fibres gives
| int_M <J, grad f> dx | = (1/Ar) | int_{D_0} (f(end) - f(start)) dA | = 1
(sign-free form; this is the corrected duality sign of AM-R5-14 item (5)).
Cauchy-Schwarz with the weight w = (1/beta) e^{-beta E_eps}:
1 <= En(J) D(f) with En(J) := int |J|^2 / w. Taking inf over f,
cap(A,S) >= 1/En(J). With Leb(Tub) = Ar * (s_1 - s_0) and (TUBE-LEVEL'),

  En(J) <= beta (s_1 - s_0) Ar^{-1} e^{beta A_tube}
        <= beta (sqrt(2N) delta/2) Ar^{-1} e^{beta A_tube},

using the HONEST length bound s_1 - s_0 <= ell(z) <= sqrt(2N) delta/2. Hence

  cap(A,S) >= c_N delta^{-1} beta^{-2N} exp(-beta A_tube),               (CAP-LOW')
  c_N := 2 omega_{2N-1} / ( sqrt(2N) (2 sqrt(2N))^{2N-1} ),  beta-free.

The polynomial degree is UNCHANGED at beta^{2N}: the honest length costs only
the beta-free factor sqrt(2N) and the honest thinness only the beta-free
(2 sqrt(2N))^{-(2N-1)}; both live in c_N.

(4'g) WHAT THE COLLAR ROUTE BUYS. (H-TUBE)'s load-bearing half is not needed:
Tub subset closed collar subset U_ch subset U by :3010, so no ball of radius
5delta/8 (landed) or 9delta/16 (AM-R5-14) is ever invoked. The ramp
admissibility of Step 3 on A is unchanged: sup_A E_eps <= sup_{dS^+} E_eps
+ G rho <= A_tube + G/beta, absorbed by beta_* := max(8/delta,
(2+G)/(S_k + c_H - A_tube)).

=====================================================================
6'. THE BUDGET, RECOMPUTED HONESTLY
=====================================================================

Chaining (PTW), (RATIO), (CAP-UP) [unchanged], (CAP-LOW'):

  h(z) <= C_H C_up beta e^{-beta(S_k+c_H)} * (delta/c_N) beta^{2N} e^{+beta A_tube}
       =  C_2 beta^{2N+1} exp( -beta ( S_k + c_H - A_tube ) ),
  C_2 := e^2 G^2 V_M delta / c_N,  beta-free.                            (RAW)

THE COLLISION, STATED. The raw exponent is
Xi_0 := S_k + c_H - m_k - eps w_k - L_eps N delta^2/4, and the GAP row's
required strength is verbatim "C_1(eps,delta) exp(-beta(S_k + c_H - m_k -
eps w_k - L_eps N delta^2/4)), C_1 beta-free"
[lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:8050]. The two delta-losses are the SAME constant,
so the headroom

  s := (allowance N/4) - (tube loss N/4) = 0 ,

and beta^{2N+1} in (RAW) has NOTHING to be absorbed against. The landed
s = (N/4 - 25/128) L_eps delta^2 was positive only because the landed tube loss
25/128 was computed from a false Euclidean radius. This is exactly XE-1's
second sentence of the defect and it is fatal to the landed budget.

THE REPAIR (deliberate widening, honesty over conformance). Release
L_eps N delta^2/4 of the raw exponent to pay the polynomial. Set

  s := L_eps N delta^2 / 4 > 0   (positive whenever L_eps > 0, cf. (H-Lpos)),
  Xi := Xi_0 - s = S_k + c_H - m_k - eps w_k - L_eps N delta^2 / 2 .

Then, for every beta > 0,
  beta^{2N+1} e^{-beta s} <= sup_{b>0} b^{2N+1} e^{-b s} = ((2N+1)/(e s))^{2N+1},
a beta-free number, and (RAW) becomes, with AM-R5-14 item (2)'s discharge of
(H-DELAY) (factor 2 in (RED) dropped),

  sup_{z in dS^+} P_z( tau_lev < T )
     <= C_1(eps,delta) exp( -beta ( S_k + c_H - m_k - eps w_k
                                    - L_eps N delta^2 / 2 ) ),          (DOOR')
  C_1(eps,delta) := C_H C_2 ( (2N+1) / (e s) )^{2N+1},
  s = L_eps N delta^2/4,  C_1 beta-free and explicit, valid for beta >= beta_*.

Equivalently: the DELIVERED doorway is pulled down by one further
L_eps N delta^2/4 relative to the row's typed allowance; the ramp value
a := theta - 1/beta with theta in [S_k + c_H - 1/beta, S_k + c_H] is UNCHANGED,
so (CAP-UP) and Steps 1, 2, 3, 5 are untouched.

RE-TYPING OF THE GAP ROW. (DOOR') does NOT meet
GAP-PE3P-DOORREACH at its typed allowance N delta^2/4; it meets it at
N delta^2/2. The row's allowance is therefore RE-TYPED to
L_eps N delta^2 / 2, and the discharge is recorded at that strength.

CONSUMER CHECK. The one budget consumer is the smallness ledger
[lane-prodexc-proofs-v1.md:7761-7763], verbatim:
  "Gamma(delta/2) + gamma_2 eps^2 + err(delta) + err_B + L_eps N delta^2/4
        <  (7/8)( S_k - m_k ) + kappa/4 - eps g(N) ,                   (SML)"
with RHS "0.861742 - 0.095492 = 0.766250" at the flagship (10,1,1,0.05). With
the doubled constant the condition becomes

  Gamma(delta/2) + gamma_2 eps^2 + err(delta) + err_B + L_eps N delta^2/2
        <  0.766250        (SML')

i.e. LHS(SML') = LHS(SML) + L_eps N delta^2/4. Three checks:
 (i) the added term is O(delta^2), beta-free, and monotone increasing in delta,
     as is every other left-hand term (Gamma(delta/2) = O(delta) linear
     [:7754-7757], err(delta) increasing, the quadratic increasing), while the
     right side 0.766250 - eps g(N) is delta-FREE;
 (ii) LHS(SML')(delta) -> gamma_2 eps^2 + err_B as delta -> 0, unchanged from
     (SML), so (SML') is satisfiable for all delta below a positive threshold
     delta_1 <= delta_0 (delta_0 the (SML) threshold) - the threshold moves
     down by at most a factor 1/sqrt(2) on the quadratic part, nothing else;
 (iii) satisfiability is compatible with the declared order of limits, verbatim
     "beta -> infinity FIRST at fixed (eps, delta, h = delta/2) ... THEN
     delta -> 0" [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3125, quoted at :7773-7775], because
     (DOOR') holds for every beta >= beta_* at FIXED delta and the delta-loss
     is only sent to 0 afterwards.
The two derived mentions of the same term - ":8089" ("(SML) constrains
Gamma(delta/2) + gamma_2 eps^2 + err(delta) + err_B + L_eps N delta^2/4 <
0.766250") and ":8106" ("exponent > c_H/2 iff Gamma + gamma_2 eps^2 + err +
err_B + L_eps N delta^2/4 < (MRG) - eps g(N)") - are restatements of (SML), not
independent consumers; both are re-read with N/2 by the same three checks.
The 0.766250 slack is a FIXED positive number and the doubled term is O(delta^2)
against it, so nothing in the ledger breaks; only the numerical delta window
narrows.

WHAT IS UNCHANGED. Steps 0, 1, 2, 3, 5 of PE-DOORREACH, the three blocked
compositions (no time discount, no per-window union, no level supersolution),
the beta-free Harnack constant at scale rho = 1/beta, and the (RED) reduction
with (H-DELAY) discharged.

========================================================
PIECE TRAPOCC-2 — THE COMPANION DISPLAY (cures the TRAPOCC checker MAJOR)
========================================================
Grade: PROVED-WITH-TYPED-GAPS. The instance the schedule consumes is proved
UNCONDITIONALLY (no h<=1/2 at the doorway, no gate row, no H-CONN); the
degenerate near-doorway general-z instance is typed at exact strength and
shown NOT to be consumed.

0. OBJECTS (PE-TRAPOCC Section 0 verbatim, no new object)
M = T^{2N}, n = 2N, L u = (1/beta) Delta u - <grad E_eps, grad u>; mu = e^{-beta E_eps} dx,
w = (1/beta) e^{-beta E_eps}, D(f) = int w |grad f|^2, cap(Y,Y') = inf{D(f): f=1 on Y, f=0 on Y'};
div(w grad u) = mu L u (ROW SR-PE1.2, proofs:1881-1885). (F_t) = usual augmentation; H_Y hitting
times of closed sets; T = min(D(0), L) (proofs:1385). S = B^max_{delta/4}(g*), S^+ = B^max_{delta/2}(g*).
R_0 = {w_theta=k, w_phi=0, E_eps <= S_k+c_H} (lane-lp:217-218).
theta_2 = a Sard-regular value in [S_k+c_H-1/beta, S_k+c_H]; TRAP_2 = {E_eps >= theta_2, w_phi = 0},
dTRAP_2 smooth compact [REFUTED as stated - XE-3 finding 2; CURED by PIECE TRAPOCC-3: target TRAP_2^cl, display value unchanged]. v_2(z) := E_z[int_0^{H_S} 1_{TRAP_2}(X_s) ds]; L v_2 = -1_{TRAP_2} on M\S,
v_2 = 0 on S, v_2 in C^{1,alpha} (GT Thm 9.15 + Cor 7.11, rows as in PE-TRAPOCC Section 2).
Section 2 truncation honesty is used unchanged: E_z[int_0^{H_S ^ T} 1_{TRAP_2}] <= v_2(z).
err class: err := eps w_k + L_eps N delta^2/4 + eta + O(1/beta), eta FROZEN at err class (see 7.3).
rho := 1/beta. All constants beta-free; thresholds may depend on (N, delta, eps).

1. WHAT THE CHECKER'S MAJOR ACTUALLY BLOCKS, AND THE REROUTE
The MAJOR is exact: R_0 inter TRAP_2 = {theta_2 <= E_eps <= S_k+c_H, w_phi=0, w_theta=k} is
NONEMPTY, so for such z there is no harmonic ball, h_{TRAP_2,S}(z) = 1, and (SANDWICH) is
unavailable. Nothing below repairs (SANDWICH) at such z.
The reroute is that the SCHEDULE never evaluates the companion at such a z. The design pass
factorizes the per-excursion quantity as
  "P(reach the doorway from S) x E_{doorway-level start}[trap occupation before H_S ^ T]"
  [proofs:8880-8884], with the companion "occupation-from-doorway <= poly(beta) e^{+beta err}"
  [proofs:8893-8895],
but the object the row consumes is the per-excursion occupation itself,
E_z[int_0^{H_S ^ T} 1_{TRAP_2} ds] with z at the GROUND-BALL collar — which is exactly
PE-TRAPOCC's own declared deliverable shape ("for z in R_0", proofs:8899-8901). At a collar
start the Section-4 hypotheses hold unconditionally, and the collapsed route delivers the
PRODUCT of the two design-pass factors in ONE step (Section 6). The doorway-level start is a
device of the factorization, not of the row.

2. UNCONDITIONAL FLUX CONSERVATION (route (a)), AND THE MAXIMUM-PRINCIPLE REDUCTION
Fix any closed A_z disjoint from S u TRAP_2 with smooth boundary; Omega'' := M\(A_z u S u TRAP_2).
Let h_z = equilibrium potential of A_z against S u TRAP_2 (=1 on A_z, =0 on S u TRAP_2,
L-harmonic on Omega''), e_z := w partial_n h_z dS on dA_z (n into A_z),
e_D := -w partial_n h_z dS on dTRAP_2 (n into TRAP_2), e_S := -w partial_n h_z dS on dS (n into S);
all >= 0 by 0 <= h_z <= 1 (MINIMUM PRINCIPLE, NAMED: Gilbarg-Trudinger Thm 8.1; hypothesis rows:
uniform ellipticity and bounded coefficients on the compact Omega'' — met; zeroth-order term
c = 0 — met; same row PE-DOORREACH step (2b) uses). As in PE-TRAPOCC Section 4,
e_z(dA_z) = D(h_z) = cap(A_z, S u TRAP_2).
(FLUX-CONS) e_D(dTRAP_2) <= e_z(dA_z) = cap(A_z, S u TRAP_2), UNCONDITIONALLY.
PROOF. Green's second identity for div(w grad .) on Omega'' with the pair (h_z, 1); both are
L-harmonic there (L has no zeroth-order term, so L1 = 0):
  int_{Omega''} [ 1 . div(w grad h_z) - h_z div(w grad 1) ] dx
     = int_{dOmega''} w [ 1 . partial_nu h_z - h_z partial_nu 1 ] dS,  nu = outward normal of Omega''.
LHS = 0. On dA_z, nu = n and the term is +e_z(dA_z); on dTRAP_2, nu = n and the term is
-e_D(dTRAP_2); on dS, nu = n and the term is -e_S(dS). Hence
  e_z(dA_z) = e_D(dTRAP_2) + e_S(dS) >= e_D(dTRAP_2).  QED
This is the exact same Green identity as PE-DOORREACH (FLUX-ID) (proofs:8367) with the constant
test function in the second slot; it needs no h <= 1/2, no gate, no separation of z from TRAP_2
beyond disjointness of A_z. Combining with (FLUX-ID') of PE-TRAPOCC Section 4(4a),
int_{dA_z} v_2 de_z = int_{dTRAP_2} phi_2 de_D (phi_2 := v_2|_{dTRAP_2}), and nu_z := e_z/e_z(dA_z):
  (FLUX-SUP)  E_{nu_z}[v_2] = (int_{dTRAP_2} phi_2 de_D)/e_z(dA_z) <= sup_{dTRAP_2} v_2.
(MAX-RED) sup_{M\TRAP_2} v_2 = sup_{dTRAP_2} v_2, hence sup_M v_2 = sup_{TRAP_2} v_2.
PROOF. v_2 is L-harmonic on M\(S u TRAP_2), v_2 = 0 on dS, v_2 <= sup_{dTRAP_2} v_2 on dTRAP_2;
MAXIMUM PRINCIPLE (NAMED: GT Thm 3.1; rows: bounded domain, c = 0, v_2 in C^0(closure) inter
W^{2,p}_loc — met by the Section-2 regularity). QED
(MAX-RED) supersedes (FLUX-SUP) with constant 1 and with NO Harnack ball at z; both are recorded
because (FLUX-SUP) is the measure-level statement the brief asked for and is what shows that the
loss in the degenerate regime is exactly the average-to-sup step, nothing else.

3. (EQ-OCC) FOR TRAP_2 — THE HONEST EXPONENT ARITHMETIC (the brief's "WAIT", resolved)
PE-TRAPOCC Section 3 verbatim with TRAP -> TRAP_2 (its hypothesis rows (a),(b),(c) are stated for
an arbitrary closed target with smooth boundary; dTRAP_2 is smooth by the Sard choice of theta_2):
  (EQ-OCC-2)  E_nu[v_2] = mu(TRAP_2)/cap(TRAP_2,S),  nu := e/cap(TRAP_2,S) on dTRAP_2.
Numerator: mu(TRAP_2) <= V_M e^{-beta theta_2} <= e V_M e^{-beta(S_k+c_H)} (theta_2 >= S_k+c_H-1/beta);
this is R3-STRAT's (NUM) consumed verbatim, "integral_{B_out} e^{-beta E_eps} dx <= Leb(B_out)
e^{-beta(S_k + c_H)} <= V_M e^{-beta(S_k + c_H)}, (NUM)" [proofs:4996-4998], times e^1 for the Sard offset.
Denominator: cap(TRAP_2,S) >= c(N,delta) beta^{-2N} exp(-beta(Theta(g*,TRAP_2) + eta + G/beta)) by the
Thomson tube of PE-TRAPOCC (5b) as superseded by DOORREACH-MAXFIX (proofs:9589ff), routed from g* to
TRAP_2. By the INTERMEDIATE VALUE THEOREM every continuous arc from g* to a point of TRAP_2 attains
the level theta_2, so Theta(g*,TRAP_2) >= theta_2 unconditionally, and Theta(g*,TRAP_2) <= theta_2 + err
under (C4) below. Hence
  (DIR)  mu(TRAP_2)/cap(TRAP_2,S) <= C beta^{2N} exp(-beta(theta_2 - theta_2 - err)) = C beta^{2N} e^{+beta err}.
DIRECTION CHECK, DISPLAYED. The brief's worry ("mu/cap ~ e^{-beta(theta_2 - m_k - err)} is SMALL not
large") arises from pairing mu(TRAP_2) with cap(A_z,S), whose exponent is anchored at the GROUND
level Theta(z,S) ~ m_k. (EQ-OCC-2) is an identity for the equilibrium measure OF TRAP_2, and its
denominator is cap(TRAP_2,S), anchored at the DOORWAY level Theta(g*,TRAP_2) = theta_2 + err. The two
e^{-beta theta_2} factors cancel EXACTLY and leave poly(beta) e^{+beta err} — precisely the companion's
target at a doorway-level start. The small quantity e^{-beta(theta_2 - m_k - err)} is the value of the
DIFFERENT object v_2 at a ground-level start; it is (TRAPOCC-2-ROUND) of Section 6 and it is the
design pass's coupled PRODUCT reach x occupation, not the companion factor alone. Both arithmetics
are correct and they are about different starts; nothing is off by a sign.

4. LOCAL BOUNDEDNESS WITH THE beta-DEPENDENCE HANDLED EXPLICITLY (route (b))
Multiply the equation by beta: (beta L) v_2 = Delta v_2 - beta <grad E_eps, grad v_2> = -beta 1_{TRAP_2}.
The operator beta L has ellipticity ratio 1 (UNIT, beta-INDEPENDENT) — this is the point of
multiplying by beta — while its drift coefficient is beta grad E_eps, of size beta G. Rescale at the
only scale that makes the drift scale-invariant: x = x_0 + rho y, rho = 1/beta, u(y) := v_2(x_0 + rho y).
Then rho^2 (beta L) v_2 reads
  Delta_y u - b'(y).grad_y u = -(1/beta) 1_{TRAP_2}(x_0 + rho y),  b'(y) := grad E_eps(x_0 + rho y),
  |b'| <= G, beta-free (because beta rho = 1).
LOCAL BOUNDEDNESS (NAMED: Gilbarg-Trudinger Thm 8.17). HYPOTHESIS ROWS: (i) u in W^{1,2}(B_2), u >= 0
— met (Section-2 regularity, v_2 >= 0); (ii) uniform ellipticity with ratio 1 — met, beta-free EXACTLY
because the equation was multiplied by beta; (iii) the GT coefficient parameter nu R with R = 1 is
bounded by a function of G — met, beta-free, by (ii)+|b'| <= G; (iv) RHS g := -(1/beta)1 in L^q(B_2)
with q = infinity > n/2 — met, ||g||_infinity = 1/beta. With p = 2,
  sup_{B_1} u <= C(n,G) ( ||u||_{L^2(B_2)} + ||g||_{L^infinity} ),
i.e., undoing the rescaling,
  (LOC-B)  sup_{B_rho(x_0)} v_2 <= C(n,G) [ |B_2|^{1/2} ( avg_{B_{2rho}(x_0)} v_2^2 )^{1/2} + 1/beta ].
BETA LEDGER: the only beta produced is the ADDITIVE 1/beta (beta-vanishing, absorbed outright by the
companion's poly(beta) e^{+beta err} target); no poly(beta) is spent, because the ellipticity ratio
after multiplying by beta is unit and the ball radius rho = 1/beta makes the drift scale-invariant.
What (LOC-B) does NOT supply is a bound on the local quadratic mean of v_2 — see (C1).

5. THE TWO REGIMES AND THE EXPLICIT THRESHOLD
Fix c_0 := L_eps N delta^2 > 0, beta-free and of err class.
REGIME A: Theta(z,S) <= theta_2 - c_0. REGIME B: Theta(z,S) > theta_2 - c_0.
(The split is on the communication height, not on E_eps(z), because Theta is what the capacity
denominator sees; note Theta(z,S) >= E_eps(z) always, so Regime A implies E_eps(z) <= theta_2 - c_0
and hence dist(z,TRAP_2) >= c_0/G > 0, beta-free.)

REGIME A, PROVED. (i) HARMONIC BALL: for beta >= 2G/c_0, A_z := closed B_rho(z) and B_{2rho}(z) are
disjoint from TRAP_2, and from S in the same way PE-TRAPOCC Section 7's near-S case handles; so
(PTW*) (GT Thm 8.20 Harnack on B_{3/2}, rows verbatim as in PE-TRAPOCC (4d)) applies.
(ii) h_2 <= 1/2 ON dA_z, UNCONDITIONALLY. Run PE-DOORREACH Sections 2+5 with the target TRAP_2
(both are stated for an arbitrary closed target; the only replacement is the level ramp). The
capacity upper bound is (CAP-UP-GATE) with theta a Sard-regular value in
[Theta(z,TRAP_2) - 1/beta, Theta(z,TRAP_2)]; here the GATE ROW IS NOT USED AT ALL — by the
INTERMEDIATE VALUE THEOREM, Theta(z,TRAP_2) >= theta_2 for any z with E_eps(z) < theta_2, which
replaces (GATE-LOWER) and is unconditional. With (CAP-LOW*),
  h_2(y) = P_y(H_{TRAP_2} < H_S) <= C_3 beta^{2N+1} exp(-beta(theta_2 - Theta(z,S) - 2G/beta))
        <= C_3 e^{2G} beta^{2N+1} e^{-beta c_0} <= 1/2 for all beta >= beta_2(N,delta,eps).
NO CIRCULARITY: as in PE-TRAPOCC (5c), (ENTRY) uses only the capacity bounds, never (SANDWICH).
(iii) Therefore PE-TRAPOCC Sections 3 and 4 run verbatim with TRAP -> TRAP_2 (they use only: closed
target, smooth boundary, disjoint from S and A_z, and h_2 <= 1/2 on dA_z), and with (MU-TRAP)
replaced by the (NUM) numerator of Section 3 above:
  (TRAPOCC-2*)  v_2(z) <= C_H' . 2 mu(TRAP_2)/cap(A_z,S)
     <= C_5 beta^{2N} exp( -beta ( theta_2 - Theta(z,S) - eta - (1+G)/beta ) )
     <= C_5 beta^{2N} exp( -beta ( S_k + c_H - Theta(z,S) - err ) ),   C_5 := 2 C_H' e^{1+G} V_M / c(N,delta),
for every z in R_0 with Theta(z,S) <= theta_2 - c_0. Unconditional in Theta(z,S); the E_eps(z) form
of the design pass follows under the inherited row (H-DESC) exactly as for the main display.
REGIME B: typed as (C1). Section 6 shows it is not consumed.

# CURE-XE2-F1a (the epoch set, redefined on closure(S); cures XE-2 finding 1)

(narrow-brief round 2026-07-27: draft PROVED-WITH-TYPED-GAPS; internal checker REPAIRABLE - one MAJOR + four minors, ALL repaired below and in the in-place notes; the repaired text is OPERATIVE)

Every T_n is an (F_t)-stopping time (MM:3036 template) and X_{T_n} lies on the
max-norm sphere of radius delta/4 about g*; equivalently X_{T_n} in
closure(S) \ S. (Proof, used repeatedly below. theta^+(T_n) is the infimum of
{s >= T_n : X_s not in S^+}, and the complement of the OPEN S^+ is closed, so
X_{theta^+(T_n)} not in S^+, i.e. |X_{theta^+(T_n)} - g*|_max >= delta/2; by continuity
|X_u - g*|_max > delta/4 on a right-neighbourhood [theta^+(T_n),
theta^+(T_n) + eps'), so no S-visit occurs there and D(T_n) >=
theta^+(T_n) + eps' > theta^+(T_n) [strictness inference repaired per the
internal checker's finding 2, adopted]. D(T_n) is the infimum of the
OPEN-condition set {u >= theta^+(T_n) : X_u in S}, so there are u_k decreasing
to D(T_n) with X_{u_k} in S, giving X_{D(T_n)} in closure(S) by continuity;
and X_u not in S for all u in [theta^+(T_n), D(T_n)) gives
|X_{D(T_n)} - g*|_max >= delta/4 by continuity. Also theta^+(T_n) > T_n,
since closure(S) subset S^+.) MEMBERSHIP DISCIPLINE FOR THE WHOLE PIECE:
epochs live on closure(S), NOT in S; every membership hypothesis consumed
below is therefore stated on closure(S) or on S^+ (closure(S) subset S^+).

INTRINSIC (SHIFT-COVARIANT) FORM. Put
   E := { t : (E1) X_t in closure(S) ;
              (E2) t is a right-accumulation point of { u : X_u in S }, i.e.
                   for every h > 0 there is u in [t, t+h) with X_u in S ;
              (E3) there exists s < t with X_s not in S^+ and
                   X_u not in S for all u in (s,t) }.
(E3) is a left path-germ condition, (E2) a right path-germ condition, (E1) a
closed membership. None refers to a time origin or to any external
randomization, so for every r,  t in E(X) iff t - r in E(shift_r X), i.e.
   E(shift_r X) = E(X) - r .                                    (SHIFT-COV)
MEASURABILITY: (E2) reduces to rationals by continuity of X and openness
of S ((E2) is the intersection over rational h > 0 of {there is rational
u in [t,t+h) with X_u in S}); (E1) is a closed condition on X_t; (E3) and
the point-process measurability of E as a whole are established in the
E-MEAS section below (internal checker's finding 3, adopted: the naive
rational reduction fails for (E3)'s CLOSED inner condition).
WHY THE EARLIER FORM WAS EMPTY (the XE-2 F1 defect, recorded). With (E1)+(E2)
replaced by the single clause "X_t in S", NO epoch qualifies: X_{D(t)} sits on
the sphere by the paragraph above, so that set was empty above T_0 and the
equivalence below was false. (E1)+(E2) is exactly the closure-plus-first-
entrance signature of an infimum of an OPEN condition; it is met by every
D-epoch and, by LEMMA EQV, by nothing else.

LEMMA EQV (the recursion generates E). For t > T_0: t in E iff t = D(T_m) for
some m >= 0. PROOF.
(<=) Let t := D(T_m). (E1): the infimum defining D supplies u_k decreasing to
t with X_{u_k} in S, so X_t in closure(S) by continuity. (E2): the same
infimum supplies, for every h > 0, a u in [t, t+h) with X_u in S -- D is the
infimum of an OPEN-condition set, which is precisely right accumulation.
(E3): take s' := theta^+(T_m). Then s' < t and X_{s'} not in S^+ (object
paragraph above), and X_u not in S for all u in (s',t) by the infimum in
MM:3017. So t in E.
(=>) Let t in E with t > T_0 and witness s from (E3). E cap [T_0,t) is
nonempty (it contains T_0 = D(0), by the (<=) direction just proved) and
finite (LEMMA LF below, which is proved DIRECTLY on E and does not invoke this
lemma), so T_m := max(E cap [T_0,t)) exists.
 FIRST, T_m <= s. If s < T_m then T_m in (s,t); applying (E2) at T_m with
 h := t - T_m > 0 gives u in [T_m, t) with X_u in S, and u >= T_m > s, so
 u in (s,t) with X_u in S -- contradicting the exclusion in (E3) at t.
 SECOND, theta^+(T_m) <= s, since s >= T_m and X_s not in S^+.
 THIRD, D(T_m) <= t. By (E2) at t, for every h > 0 there is u in [t,t+h) with
 X_u in S; each such u satisfies u >= t > s >= theta^+(T_m), so D(T_m) <= u,
 and letting h decrease to 0 gives D(T_m) <= t.
 FOURTH, D(T_m) = t. If D(T_m) < t, then by the (<=) direction the point
 v := D(T_m) is in E, and T_m < theta^+(T_m) < v < t (object paragraph), so
 v in E cap [T_0,t) exceeds T_m -- contradicting maximality.
 FINALLY, T_m IS A RECURSION EPOCH. By LEMMA LF, E cap [T_0,infinity)
 enumerates increasingly as T_0 = e_0 < e_1 < e_2 < ... ; e_0 = T_0 = D(0) is
 the recursion start, and if e_k = T_k then for t := e_{k+1} the maximum above
 is T_m = e_k = T_k and the four steps give e_{k+1} = D(T_k) = T_{k+1}.
 Conversely every D(T_m) is in E by (<=), and the D(T_m) increase strictly
 (MM:3019), so the two enumerations coincide. QED.

INPUT TO LEMMA LF, ISOLATED HERE (this is what removes any circularity: the
(SEP) displacement is proved for consecutive elements of E without using
EQV). For ANY t < t' in E there is s in (t,t') with |X_s - g*|_max >= delta/2.
Indeed the witness s of (E3) at t' satisfies t <= s by the FIRST step above,
whose only inputs are (E2) at t and (E3) at t'; and s != t because
X_t in closure(S) subset S^+ while X_s not in S^+. With (E1) at t, i.e.
|X_t - g*|_max <= delta/4, this is exactly (SEP), and LEMMA LF's
uniform-continuity argument runs on it verbatim on every bounded window.

2b. LEMMA MEAS (E AS A MEASURABLE, STATIONARY, SIMPLE POINT PROCESS)

SETTING. Omega := C(R, T^{2N}) with the local-uniform topology, F := B(Omega)
= sigma(X_t : t in R), P the two-sided stationary law. F_t := sigma(X_s : s <= t)
augmented by the P-null sets of F and made right-continuous - the two-sided
instance of MM:3036; the usual conditions hold. dist(u) := |X_u - g*|_max is
continuous, S = {dist < delta/4} is OPEN, M \ S^+ = {dist >= delta/2} is CLOSED.

CLASSICAL FACTS NAMED.
 MEAS.A  On C(R,M) with M compact metric, Borel = cylinder sigma-field;
   (t,omega) -> X_t(omega) is jointly measurable; X continuous and adapted is
   progressively measurable. (Karatzas-Shreve, BMSC 2nd ed., Ch. 1 Prop. 1.13
   and Ch. 2 Sec. 4.) ROWS: (h1) M Polish - MET (T^{2N}); (h2) continuous paths - MET.
 MEAS.B  The hitting time of a CLOSED set by a continuous adapted process is an
   (F_t)-stopping time. (KS Ch. 1, Problem 2.6; Revuz-Yor Ch. I Sec. 4.) ROWS:
   (h1) path continuity - MET; (h2) adaptedness - MET. Right-continuity of F unused.
 MEAS.C  The hitting time of an OPEN set by a right-continuous adapted process is
   optional, hence a stopping time when F is right-continuous. (KS Ch. 1,
   Problem 2.7 with Prop. 1.2.3; Revuz-Yor Ch. I Sec. 4.) ROWS: (h1) right-continuous
   paths - MET; (h2) F right-continuous - MET by construction.
 MEAS.D  The debut theorem (KS Ch. 1 Thm 2.17 / Dellacherie-Meyer Ch. IV) is
   AVAILABLE (usual conditions hold) but is NOT CONSUMED: only MEAS.B/C and
   the inline MEAS.C-sigma are used, so no measurable-selection machinery
   enters this piece.
 MEAS.E  Tonelli for nonnegative jointly measurable integrands. ROWS: (h1)
   nonnegativity - MET (indicator integrand); (h2) joint measurability - MET
   by MEAS.A.

RATIONAL SKELETON. For r in Q put theta^+(r) := inf{s >= r : dist(s) >= delta/2}
(MEAS.B) and D(r) := inf{s >= theta^+(r) : X_s in S} (MEAS.C-sigma, proved INLINE per the internal checker's finding 1 - MEAS.C
as stated covers deterministic starts only, and MM:3036's Borel template is

continuous paths, and X_sigma not in G - which holds here since

LEMMA ENUM (exact countable enumeration; no side condition).
Pathwise, E = { D(r) : r in Q } intersect R.
PROOF. (superset) Let t := D(r) < infinity, s := theta^+(r) <= t. Then
dist(s) >= delta/2, so X_s not in S^+; by continuity dist > delta/4 on some
[s, s+eps], so t > s strictly; X_u not in S on (s,t) by the infimum - that is

(subset) Let t in E with witness s < t and L := sup{u < t : X_u in S}

[ordering repaired per the internal checker's finding 4]; if L is finite

hence L < s STRICTLY and
the open interval (L,s) is nonempty. Pick r in Q intersect (L,s). Then

of the recursion epochs T_n = D(T_{n-1}) from the INTRINSIC definition of E, and
covers the epochs to the left of 0 as well.

(b) POINT-PROCESS STATUS. For every omega, N(omega,.) = sum_{t in E} delta_t is a
counting measure, locally finite by Lemma LF hence Radon, and SIMPLE because E is a
set (unit atoms). With measurability in omega for each Borel B from (a), N is a
kernel from (Omega,F) to (R,B(R)): a simple, locally finite point process.
FLOW COMPATIBILITY: (r,omega) -> shift_r omega is continuous for the local-uniform
topology, hence measurable by MEAS.A, and preserves P by two-sided stationarity;
Lemma EQV's set identity E(shift_r X) = E(X) - r yields N(shift_r omega, B) =
N(omega, B + r) for all Borel B. So ({shift_r}, P, N) is a STATIONARY simple point
process of intensity lambda_S^{del} = E[N([0,1])] in (0,infinity) by (INTENS) -
exactly the input of Baccelli-Bremaud Ch. 1 (Palm calculus, PALM-INV) and, via
T_0 := D(0) < infinity a.s. and T_n -> infinity (Lemma LF), of Asmussen Ch. VI
Thm 1.2 and Sec. VI.3. Finally V_B = int_{T_0}^{T_1} 1_B(X_s) ds is measurable by
the joint measurability of MEAS.A plus Tonelli (MEAS.E), on the a.s. event
{T_0 < T_1 < infinity} inherited from Section 4 - the V_B measurability
statement is a.s., stated as such [finding 7 repaired]. No independence is asserted at any step.

FINITE POSITIVE INTENSITY, PROVED WITHOUT PALM CIRCULARITY AND WITHOUT ANY
OPTIONAL STOPPING AT nu.
XE-2 F2 CURE, STATED. The previous text read "nu := max{n >= 0 : T_n <= t}.
{nu >= n} = {T_n <= t} in F_{T_n}, so nu is a stopping time for G_n := F_{T_n}"
and then applied Doob optional stopping at nu ^ m. WITHDRAWN as false: the
discrete stopping-index property is {nu <= n} in G_n, and {nu <= n} =
{T_{n+1} > t} lies in G_{n+1}, not in G_n. nu is a LAST-PASSAGE index; no
optional-stopping theorem is applied to it anywhere below. The replacement
consumes only (i) a conditional floor read off Lemma SPACE's OWN
Ito/optional-sampling display BEFORE its limit is taken, (ii) a DETERMINISTIC
count, (iii) the tower property. NO independence of spacings is claimed or used.

SETTING. Stationary law X_0 ~ rho_beta; fix t > 0. T_0 := D(0) and T_{n+1} :=
D(T_n) (ONE definition, per AM-R5-18(b) verbatim "T_0 has ONE definition
(T_0 := D(0); the intrinsic-form display is derived, not definitional)"; this
also removes the old block's competing "min(E cap [0,infinity))"). Each T_n is
an (F_t)-stopping time — landed and untouched by XE-2: "Every T_n is an
(F_t)-stopping time (MM:3036 template) and X_{T_n} lies on the max-norm sphere
of radius delta/4 about g*" (Section 1). G_n := F_{T_n}; Delta_n := T_n -
T_{n-1} (n >= 1); nu := max{n >= 0 : T_n <= t} on {T_0 <= t}, finite by Lemma
LF on bounded windows (AM-R5-18(b)). NO integrability of T_0 is used below —
only T_0 >= 0.

CLASSICAL FACTS NAMED (appended to the SR-PE1D list; hypothesis rows checked).
 SR-PE1D.C Markov/Chebyshev inequality, conditional form. (h1) nonnegative
   integrand — MET: u(x) = |x - x_0|_2^2 >= 0. (h2) integrability — MET: the
   stopped u is bounded by (delta/4)^2 via Lemma SPACE's CONTAINMENT step.
 SR-PE1D.D Tower property of conditional expectation on a nested family, with
   stopping-time sigma-field monotonicity F_S subset F_T for S <= T
   (Karatzas-Shreve, Brownian Motion and Stochastic Calculus, 2nd ed., Ch. 1 - the elementary
   monotonicity F_S subset F_T for stopping times S <= T; the specific
   lemma numbering is NOT verified in-repo and is not load-bearing). (h1) S <= T stopping times — MET: T_n < T_{n+1} strictly
   (MM:3019 verbatim "D(t) > t strictly. There are NO trivial zero-time
   returns") and both are (F_t)-stopping times (row above). (h2) integrability
   — MET: every integrand below is an indicator. Consequence used: Delta_k and
   T_k are G_k-measurable (a stopping time is measurable for its own
   sigma-field; T_{k-1} is G_{k-1}- hence G_k-measurable).
 SR-PE1D.E Strong Markov at T_n, autonomous SDE — ALREADY A LANDED ROW, cited
   verbatim inside Lemma SPACE: "by strong Markov at T_n (MM:3036, autonomous
   SDE)". Not re-proved.
 SR-PE1D.G Monotone convergence / Tonelli for sums of nonnegative terms. (h1)
   nonnegativity — MET.

(i) UNIFORM CONDITIONAL FLOOR AT AN EXPLICIT h. Run Lemma SPACE's proof at T_n
(SR-PE1D.E; x_0 := X_{T_n}, |x_0 - g*|_max = delta/4, so the CONTAINMENT step
and the drift bound K := 4N/beta + (delta/2) G_* are unchanged and do NOT
depend on x_0). Its optional-sampling display, with the truncation level taken
at an arbitrary REAL s > 0 instead of the integer n — SR-PE1D.B's row (h3) is
"bounded stopping time", met by rho ^ (T_n + s) for every real s > 0 exactly as
for integer n — reads
   E[ u(X_{rho ^ (T_n+s)}) | G_n ] <= K . E[ (rho ^ (T_n+s)) - T_n | G_n ] <= K s,
with rho := inf{ r >= T_n : |X_r - x_0|_2 >= delta/4 }. On {rho <= T_n + s} the
left side equals (delta/4)^2 by path continuity, off it u >= 0; so by SR-PE1D.C
   P( rho <= T_n + s | G_n ) <= 16 K s / delta^2 = s / c_*   a.s.,
since c_* = (delta^2/16)/K. CHOOSE
   h := c_*/2 = (delta^2/32) / ( 4N/beta + G_* delta/2 ) > 0,
giving P(rho <= T_n + h | G_n) <= 1/2. Lemma SPACE's containment also gives
rho <= theta^+(T_n) <= D(T_n) = T_{n+1}, so {rho > T_n + h} subset
{Delta_{n+1} > h}, hence the FLOOR
   P( Delta_{n+1} > h | G_n ) >= 1/2   a.s., for every n >= 0.        (FLOOR)
QUANTIFIER CARE: (FLOOR) is an a.s. CONDITIONAL statement given G_n, obtained
by strong Markov at the stopping time T_n, and it is UNIFORM over starts on the
max-norm sphere of radius delta/4 because K and c_* do not depend on x_0.
h is of the SAME explicit class as c_* (beta-, delta-, N-dependent).

(ii) DETERMINISTIC COUNT (no probability). On {T_0 <= t}, Delta_1 + ... +
Delta_nu = T_nu - T_0 <= t - T_0 <= t since T_0 >= 0. Hence, pathwise,
   L := #{ k in [1,nu] : Delta_k > h } satisfies h L <= t, so L <= m :=
   floor(t/h).                                                        (COUNT)

(iii) FAILURE-RUN DOMINATION BY THE TOWER PROPERTY ALONE. Iterating (FLOOR)
with SR-PE1D.D: for j >= 1, r >= 1, writing R(j) := sup{ r >= 0 : Delta_j <= h,
..., Delta_{j+r-1} <= h },
   P( R(j) >= r | G_{j-1} ) = P( Delta_j <= h, ..., Delta_{j+r-1} <= h | G_{j-1} )
     = E[ 1{Delta_j <= h,...,Delta_{j+r-2} <= h} . P(Delta_{j+r-1} <= h | G_{j+r-2}) | G_{j-1} ]
     <= (1/2) P( R(j) >= r-1 | G_{j-1} ) <= ... <= 2^{-r},
each step legitimate because the first r-1 indicators are G_{j+r-2}-measurable.
Summing, E[ R(j) | G_{j-1} ] = sum_{r>=1} P(R(j) >= r | G_{j-1}) <= sum_{r>=1}
2^{-r} = 1 a.s. (The conservative normalization "given the run has begun",
P(R >= r | R >= 1) <= 2^{-(r-1)}, E <= 2, would only double the final constant;
the display above is what (FLOOR) supports and is the constant carried.)
ORGANIZATION INTO RUNS. Put C_j := {T_{j-1} <= t} cap ({j = 1} union
{Delta_{j-1} > h}), an event in G_{j-1} by SR-PE1D.D. Every k in [1,nu] with
Delta_k <= h sits in a maximal run of consecutive short spacings whose start
k_0 in [1,k] satisfies Delta_{k_0} <= h, k_0 = 1 or Delta_{k_0-1} > h, and
T_{k_0-1} <= t; i.e. C_{k_0} holds and k - k_0 + 1 <= R(k_0). Also, pathwise,
sum_{j>=1} 1_{C_j} <= 1 + L <= 1 + m by (COUNT) — the run count is bounded by
the DETERMINISTIC floor(t/h) + 1. Therefore, pathwise,
   nu = L + #{k in [1,nu] : Delta_k <= h} <= m + sum_{j>=1} 1_{C_j} R(j).
Take expectations (SR-PE1D.G; all terms nonnegative, values in [0,infinity]):
   E[ 1_{C_j} R(j) ] = sum_{r>=1} E[ 1_{C_j} P(R(j) >= r | G_{j-1}) ] <= P(C_j),
so E[nu] <= m + sum_j P(C_j) = m + E[ sum_j 1_{C_j} ] <= 2 m + 1, i.e.
   E[ nu ] <= 2 floor(t/h) + 1 = 2 floor(2t/c_*) + 1 < infinity.       (RUN)

(iv) CONCLUSION. By Lemma EQV every element of E in (T_0,infinity) is some
D(T_m), and at most ONE element of E precedes T_0 = D(0) (if u_1 in E cap

### CURE-XE3-A (non-circular positive intensity; cures XE-3 finding 1)

CLAIM. lambda_S^{del} > 0.
PROOF (no Palm object; consumes only the stationary point-process
structure of E-MEAS (b), LEMMA ENUM/EQV, and the ambient finiteness

lambda_S^{del} = 0 for every integer n >= 0, hence N([n, n+1]) = 0 a.s.
for each n (a nonnegative integer-valued variable with zero mean), and
by countable additivity over n,
   N([0, infinity)) = 0   a.s.
