# PIECE TRAPOCC-3 (cures XE-3 finding 2: the companion target is retyped CLOSED, and the consumed machinery is re-verified step by step)

(narrow-brief round 2026-07-27; grade PROVED-WITH-TYPED-GAPS; supersedes the two
"dTRAP_2 smooth compact" declarations already flagged [REFUTED as stated] at
proofs:10014 and proofs:9109)

========================================================
0. WHAT IS CURED, AND WHAT IS NOT TOUCHED
========================================================
XE-3 finding 2 is CONCEDED as stated: with w_phi defined only off Delta_phi
("w_phi is defined only off Delta_phi; Delta_phi is a finite union of smooth
codimension-1 tori", proofs:4940-4942), the set TRAP_2 := {E_eps >= theta_2,
w_phi = 0} is NOT closed. The exhibited sequence is correct: at N = 10, phi-bonds
(pi - eta, -pi + eta, 0, ..., 0) carry w_phi = 0 and J_lambda -> 4 lambda > theta_2
(theta_2 <= S_1 + c_H = 2.93418...), while the limit bond vector (pi, -pi, 0, ..., 0)
lies on Delta_phi where w_phi carries no value. So "dTRAP_2 smooth compact" was
never established and every step that consumed "closed target with smooth boundary"
was, as displayed, unlicensed. Nothing below disputes this.
NOT IMPLICATED: PE-TRAPOCC's MAIN target TRAP (the 4rho-collar of STRAT, closed by
construction) and its displays (TRAPOCC), (TRAPOCC-UNIF). This piece touches only
the companion.

========================================================
1. THE NEW TARGET
========================================================
DEFINITION. TRAP_2^cl := {E_eps >= theta_2} inter closure({w_phi = 0}), with
theta_2 as in Section 0 of TRAPOCC-2 (Sard-regular in [S_k + c_H - 1/beta, S_k + c_H])
strengthened as in (T3.3) below. All other objects are PE-TRAPOCC Section 0 verbatim.

(T3.1) CLOSED AND COMPACT. {E_eps >= theta_2} is closed (E_eps continuous);
closure({w_phi = 0}) is closed by definition; the intersection of two closed sets is
closed, and a closed subset of the compact M = T^{2N} is compact. No regularity of
any kind is asserted. QED

(T3.2) CONSERVATIVE COVER: TRAP_2 subset TRAP_2^cl, and
closure({w_phi = 0}) \ {w_phi = 0} subset Delta_phi.
PROOF. The inclusion is immediate ({w_phi = 0} subset its closure). For the second
claim: by (G2) verbatim, "w_phi is integer-valued and locally constant off Delta_phi"
[proofs:9002, quoting la3-reader-packet-v1.md:55-56]. Hence {w_phi = 0} is OPEN in M:
if w_phi(x) = 0 then x lies off Delta_phi, and local constancy gives a neighbourhood
U of x, U inter Delta_phi = empty, on which w_phi = 0. Now let
y in closure({w_phi = 0}) with y not in Delta_phi. Local constancy at y gives a
neighbourhood V of y off Delta_phi on which w_phi is constant; V meets {w_phi = 0}
(y is in the closure), so that constant is 0, so w_phi(y) = 0. QED
CONSEQUENCE (COVER DIRECTION). 1_{TRAP_2} <= 1_{TRAP_2^cl} pointwise off Delta_phi,
so every UPPER bound proved for the ^cl occupation is an upper bound for the TRAP_2
occupation, and wherever the schedule uses the companion set as a COVER of the trap
event the inclusion keeps the direction. The cure is conservative by construction; the
identity of Section 2 then shows nothing is even lost.

========================================================
2. DISPLAY-VALUE IDENTITY: NO EXPONENT MOVES
========================================================
(T3-ID) For every z in M, E_z[ int_0^{H_S} 1_{TRAP_2^cl}(X_s) ds ]
= E_z[ int_0^{H_S} 1_{TRAP_2}(X_s) ds ] = v_2(z), and a fortiori
E_z[ int_0^{H_S ^ T} 1_{TRAP_2^cl} ds ] = E_z[ int_0^{H_S ^ T} 1_{TRAP_2} ds ].
PROOF. By (T3.2) the symmetric difference satisfies
TRAP_2^cl \ TRAP_2 subset Delta_phi inter {E_eps >= theta_2} subset Delta_phi.
The landed NULL-TRACE row applies verbatim: "the nondegenerate (uniformly elliptic,
constant diffusion matrix (2/beta) I) diffusion of the standing setting has transition
densities w.r.t. Lebesgue for every t > 0, so by Tonelli
E_x[ int_0^T 1_{Delta_phi}(X_s) ds ] = int_0^T P_x(X_s in Delta_phi) ds = 0 for every
x, T" [proofs:4944-4948], with its NAMED IMPORT and three hypothesis rows checked in
place (Friedman Ch. 6; M compact smooth, diffusion coefficient constant nondegenerate,
drift = grad E_eps smooth - all HOLDS [lane-minmig:1345]). Since E_z[H_S] < infinity
by positive Harris recurrence [proofs:1867-1879], Tonelli on [0, infinity) gives
E_z[ int_0^{H_S} 1_{Delta_phi} ds ] = int_0^infinity P_z(X_s in Delta_phi, s < H_S) ds = 0.
The stopped version follows from H_S ^ T <= H_S pathwise (Section 2 truncation honesty,
proofs:8998-9000). QED
STATUS CHANGE, RECORDED: the null-trace remark, landed as "used ONLY as a remark"
[proofs:4949-4950], is now LOAD-BEARING and CONSUMED by this piece.
CONSEQUENCE. v_2 is literally the SAME function under either target, and
L v_2 = -1_{TRAP_2^cl} = -1_{TRAP_2} is the same element of L^p (indicators of sets
differing by a Lebesgue-null set). Therefore (TRAPOCC-2-ROUND) keeps its exact
statement and its exact exponent
  sup_{z in S^+} E_z[ int_0^{H_S ^ T} 1_{TRAP_2^cl} ds ]
     <= C_5 beta^{2N} exp(-beta(S_k + c_H - m_k - eps w_k - L_eps N delta^2/4 - err)),
and the row check "1.024350 - 0.162608 = 0.861742 > 0" is untouched. NO EXPONENT MOVES.

========================================================
3. BOUNDARY STRUCTURE LEMMA (stated at exactly the strength proved)
========================================================
(T3.3) SARD DEVICE, STRENGTHENED. Choose theta_2 in [S_k + c_H - 1/beta, S_k + c_H]
to be simultaneously a regular value of E_eps on M and of the restriction
E_eps|_{B_i}, where B_i := {d_i = pi} is the i-th bond torus, i = 1..N (d_i the i-th
phi-bond). Each B_i is a compact embedded real-analytic hypersurface and each
restriction is smooth, so SARD's THEOREM (NAMED; hypothesis rows: domain a compact
smooth manifold - HOLDS; map smooth real-valued - HOLDS) applied N + 1 times excludes
a finite union of Lebesgue-null subsets of the interval; the choice is available.
This is a strict strengthening of the landed PE-DOORREACH (1a) device and costs nothing.

(T3.4) DECOMPOSITION. boundary(TRAP_2^cl) is contained in
  (i) LEVEL FACE  {E_eps = theta_2} inter closure({w_phi = 0}),  union
  (ii) LABEL FACE  Delta_phi inter {E_eps >= theta_2}  =  union_{i=1..N} (B_i inter {E_eps >= theta_2}).
PROOF. Let x in boundary(TRAP_2^cl). If E_eps(x) > theta_2 and w_phi(x) = 0 then, both
{E_eps > theta_2} and {w_phi = 0} being open (the latter by (T3.2)), a whole
neighbourhood of x lies in TRAP_2 subset TRAP_2^cl, contradicting x in the boundary.
So E_eps(x) = theta_2 (face (i)) or x not in {w_phi = 0}, whence by (T3.2) x in
Delta_phi (face (ii)). QED

(T3.5) WHAT IS PROVED ABOUT THE FACES. (a) The relative interior of face (i),
{E_eps = theta_2} inter {w_phi = 0}, is a smooth embedded hypersurface (theta_2 regular
for E_eps on M; the sector is open). (b) The relative interior of face (ii), points
with EXACTLY ONE bond at pi and E_eps > theta_2, is a smooth (indeed real-analytic)
embedded hypersurface piece, and locally TRAP_2^cl is one closed side of B_i, because
crossing B_i changes w_phi by exactly 1 so the zero-winding sector occupies exactly one
local side. (c) The differentials dd_1, ..., dd_N satisfy exactly one linear relation
(sum_i d_i = 0 mod 2 pi), so any k <= N - 1 distinct bond tori meet transversally in
codimension k, and every multi-bond point has codimension >= 2 in M. (d) By (T3.3), face
(i) meets each B_i transversally, so {E_eps = theta_2} inter B_i is a smooth codimension-2
submanifold and near its points TRAP_2^cl is, in suitable local coordinates, the
intersection of two transverse closed half-spaces: a Lipschitz wedge.
CONCLUSION AT PROVED STRENGTH: TRAP_2^cl is a COMPACT set whose boundary is PIECEWISE
SMOOTH - finitely many smooth faces meeting along sets of Hausdorff dimension <= n - 2 -
and which is locally Lipschitz at every one-bond and every level-face point. A GLOBAL
Lipschitz certificate (uniform interior cone at every boundary point, including
multi-bond corners) is NOT claimed; see (G3-CORNER). This is why Section 4 executes the
WEAK route, which needs none of (T3.4)-(T3.5).

========================================================
4. ROUTE (b), EXECUTED: THE WEAK FLUX FRAMEWORK
========================================================
ROUTE CHOICE, STATED ONCE: route (a) (Gauss-Green on Lipschitz domains) is NOT taken,
because (T3.5) does not deliver a global Lipschitz certificate. Route (b) is executed
for exactly the identities the CONSUMED Regime-A chain needs. Throughout,
T_g(f) := D(g,f) = int_M w <grad g, grad f> dx, the distribution -div(w grad g).
Y := TRAP_2^cl; A_z, S as in TRAPOCC-2 Section 2; Omega'' := M \ (A_z u S u Y).

(WFF-1) DIRICHLET PRINCIPLE FOR COMPACTS. For disjoint compacts Y, Y' the class
K(Y,Y') := {f in H^1(M): f = 1 q.e. on Y, f = 0 q.e. on Y'} is nonempty, convex and
closed in H^1(M); D is coercive on it; the unique minimizer h_{Y,Y'} satisfies
0 <= h <= 1 (truncation lowers D) and cap(Y,Y') = D(h_{Y,Y'}) - which is the corpus's
OWN definition "cap(Y,Y') = inf{D(f): f=1 on Y, f=0 on Y'}" [proofs:10008], so no
object is redefined. Moreover h_{Y,Y'}(x) = P_x(H_Y < H_{Y'}) q.e.
NAMED: Fukushima-Oshima-Takeda, Dirichlet Forms and Symmetric Markov Processes, Ch. 2
(equilibrium potential and capacity of compact sets) and Ch. 4 (identification with
hitting probabilities). HYPOTHESIS ROWS: (D, H^1(M)) is a regular Dirichlet form on
L^2(M, mu) - HOLDS (M compact smooth; w = (1/beta) e^{-beta E_eps} smooth, bounded above
and below away from 0; mu = e^{-beta E_eps} dx smooth strictly positive); the associated
Hunt process is the standing diffusion - HOLDS by ROW SR-PE1.2 reversibility
div(w grad u) = mu L u [proofs:1881-1885]; Y, Y' compact and disjoint - HOLDS by (T3.1)
and Regime-A separation. NO boundary regularity of Y enters. This UPGRADES the landed
row "existence of the equilibrium potential ... as the classical solution of the two-set
Dirichlet problem with a regular boundary ... (Friedman Thm 6.5.1; every boundary point
regular - met, dS and dDoor' are smooth hypersurfaces)" [proofs:9022-9024], whose
regularity clause is exactly what TRAP_2 could not supply.

(WFF-2) RIESZ REPRESENTATION OF THE FLUX MEASURES. Let h = h_{Y,Y'}. First variation on
the affine class gives T_h(f) = 0 for every f in C_c^inf(M \ (Y u Y')), so T_h is a
distribution carried by Y u Y'; it is a signed Radon measure T_h = e_Y - e_{Y'} with
e_Y carried by Y, e_{Y'} carried by Y'. BOTH ARE NONNEGATIVE. PROOF of e_Y >= 0: by
(WFF-1) h(x) = P_x(H_Y < H_{Y'}); by the STRONG MARKOV PROPERTY for the Feller diffusion
(corpus row, already named), for the semigroup P_t^{Y'} of the process killed on Y',
P_t^{Y'} h (x) = P_x(t < H_{Y'}, the shifted path hits Y before Y') <= h(x), i.e. h is
excessive for the killed semigroup. The form-semigroup relation
D(h, f) = lim_{t -> 0} t^{-1} <h - P_t^{Y'} h, f>_mu (NAMED: FOT Ch. 1, the standard
identity for u in the form domain; rows: h in H^1 - met by (WFF-1); f in the form domain
of the killed form, i.e. f = 0 q.e. on Y' - imposed) gives D(h,f) >= 0 for every such
f >= 0, which is precisely e_Y >= 0. Applying the same to 1 - h = h_{Y',Y} gives
e_{Y'} >= 0. Both measures have finite energy and charge no set of zero capacity, so
they integrate quasi-continuous functions unambiguously (NAMED: FOT Ch. 2, measures of
finite energy integral). NO SURFACE INTEGRAL, NO NORMAL DERIVATIVE, NO SMOOTH dY.
NOTATION MATCH: with Y' = S, e := e_Y is the corpus's equilibrium measure on the target
and cap(Y,S) = D(h) = T_h(h) = e(Y) (test f = h: h = 1 q.e. on Y, 0 q.e. on S), which is
the landed "cap(TRAP,S) = D(h) = e(dTRAP)" [proofs:9028] with dTRAP replaced by Y.
For h_z := h_{A_z, S u Y}: T_{h_z} = e_z - e_D - e_S with e_z >= 0 on A_z, e_D >= 0 on Y,
e_S >= 0 on S, and e_z(A_z) = cap(A_z, S u Y).

(WFF-3) THE WEAK EQUATION FOR v_2. v_2 in H^1(M) is the unique element with v_2 = 0
q.e. on S and D(v_2, f) = int_M f 1_Y dmu for every f in H^1(M) with f = 0 q.e. on S.
(This is the weak form of "L v_2 = -1_{TRAP_2^cl} on M\S, v_2 = 0 on S" via
div(w grad v_2) = mu L v_2; existence/uniqueness by the same Dirichlet principle,
boundedness by v_2 <= E_.[H_S] < infinity.)

RE-PROVED IDENTITIES (each exactly the landed display, with dY-integrals read as
Y-integrals against the measures of (WFF-2)):
(EQ-OCC-2w) int_Y v_2 de = mu(Y), i.e. E_nu[v_2] = mu(Y)/cap(Y,S), nu := e/cap(Y,S).
PROOF. Take f = h in (WFF-3): D(v_2, h) = int h 1_Y dmu = mu(Y) (h = 1 q.e. on Y; h = 0
q.e. on S so f = h is admissible). Take f = v_2 in (WFF-2) for h: D(h, v_2) = int v_2 de
- int v_2 de_S = int v_2 de (v_2 = 0 q.e. on S). D is symmetric. QED
(FLUX-ID'w) int_{A_z} v_2 de_z = int_Y v_2 de_D.
PROOF. f = h_z in (WFF-3) is admissible (h_z = 0 q.e. on S) and gives
D(v_2, h_z) = int h_z 1_Y dmu = 0 (h_z = 0 q.e. on Y). f = v_2 in (WFF-2) for h_z gives
D(h_z, v_2) = int v_2 de_z - int v_2 de_D - 0. Symmetry. QED
(FLUX-CONSw) e_z(A_z) = e_D(Y) + e_S(S) >= e_D(Y), unconditionally.
PROOF. f = 1 in (WFF-2) for h_z: D(h_z, 1) = 0. QED  [This is the landed (FLUX-CONS)
with the constant test function, now with no Green surface identity; (FLUX-SUP) follows
by dividing (FLUX-ID'w) by e_z(A_z) as before.]
(SANDWICHw) e_D <= 2 e as measures on Y, under the landed hypothesis h <= 1/2 on
B_{2rho}(z) (supplied unconditionally in Regime A by (ENTRY)).
PROOF. Put V := M \ (A_z u S), an open set containing Y, and u := 2(1 - h) - h_z.
(1) u is L-harmonic on V \ Y = Omega'' (both h and h_z are, and T_1 = 0).
(2) u >= 0 q.e. on M \ Omega'': on Y, h = 1 and h_z = 0 so u = 0; on S, h = 0, h_z = 0,
u = 2; on A_z, h_z = 1 and h <= 1/2 by (ENTRY) on B_{2rho}(z) superset A_z, so
u = 1 - 2h >= 0. Hence u^- lies in H^1_0(Omega''), and 0 = D(u, u^-) = -D(u^-, u^-)
forces u^- = 0: u >= 0 on V. (Elementary weak minimum principle; it replaces the
C^0(closure) framing of GT Thm 8.1 at this one step and imports nothing.)
(3) Let H be the L-harmonic function on V with H = u q.e. on dV = dA_z u dS (variational
solution; dA_z, dS are smooth spheres, so this is the landed regular case), and
p := H - u. Then p in H^1_0(V), p is L-harmonic on V \ Y, p = H q.e. on Y, and p >= 0.
By the strong Markov property and harmonicity of H,
p(x) = E_x[ H(X_{H_Y}) ; H_Y < tau_V ], which is excessive for the process killed on dV
(same one-line computation as in (WFF-2)). Hence T_p >= 0 on V by the form-semigroup
relation. Since T_H = 0 on V, T_u|_V = -T_p <= 0. Restricting to Y and using
T_u|_Y = -2 e + e_D gives e_D <= 2 e. QED
This is the landed (SANDWICH) with its normal-derivative comparison at dTRAP replaced by
an excessivity argument; it consumes NO boundary regularity of Y.

WITH (EQ-OCC-2w), (FLUX-ID'w), (SANDWICHw) and cap(A_z, S u Y) >= cap(A_z, S) (the
admissible class shrinks), (RATIO*) is recovered verbatim:
  E_{nu_z}[v_2] = (int_Y v_2 de_D)/cap(A_z, S u Y) <= 2 mu(Y)/cap(A_z, S),
and Regime A of TRAPOCC-2 Section 5 closes as landed.

7. WHY NOTHING IS SMUGGLED
========================================================
The probabilistic content is the Dirichlet principle, reversibility div(w grad u) = mu L u,

of conditional laws. This is the CLOSED half of DELTA-PE1-ENTRANCE, landed.

v1 DAG notes: VERDICT: clean = false. The final chain's CONCLUSION is not refuted — no withdrawn object is consumed as live, no Palm-averaged display enters, and every exponent/margin I checked reproduces the landed arithmetic — but four defects survive the walk, two of them structural.

WITHDRAWN-OBJECT SWEEP (all clear): OBJECT-PE1, plain S-return cycle, AM-R4-18, (R3-SOJ.b-prime), the unrestricted (TRAPOCC-2*), and the 'reach x (TRAPOCC-2*)' composition are all correctly declined and are named in the piece's NOT-CONSUMED list. The exact-N/4 BETA-FREE reach display (PX:8435-8436, C_1 beta-free via s = (N/4 - 25/128) L_eps delta^2) is NOT consumed: the piece consumes AM-R5-22's s-parametric retype and carries the extra '- s' inside its TRAP-leg exponent, with s displayed as a LOSS in (A3)(i). B_bar is superseded, not consumed as a bound — but see defect 1.

DEFECT 1 (structural, Lemma PE3p.5 edge). (A2) STEP 5's "only the per-block bound changes: B_bar is replaced by the bracket of STEP 4" is not licensed. (BLK)(c) quantifies over block starts X_{xi_j} in ALL of R_0; the bracket's TRAP_2 term is a sup over S^+ only, and doorway-level R_0 starts are TRAPOCC-2 Regime B = (C1) DOOR-SUP (PX:10197-10199), which the piece declines. The displayed (RED') is nevertheless TRUE, because STEPS 1-4 already bound the whole round: from z in dS^+ one has H_S ^ T = T, so W(z) IS the full post-collar outside occupation, and multiplying a valid bound by 1/p_sub >= 1 only loses. So the correct statement is that the block count is REDUNDANT here (PE-TRAPOCC Section 8 already delivers a per-round bound with no 1/p_sub), not that it is "unchanged". Consequences: (P-SUB) and its AM-R5-16 admission are not actually load-bearing for the row, which would STRENGTHEN the register; the piece keeps them as costs instead.

# PIECE TRAPOCC-4 (cures XE-4 finding 1: the rough-target (ENTRY) capacity ratio, re-proved via the smooth envelope)
============================================================================

(narrow-brief round 2026-07-27; grade PROVED; supersedes the machinery-table row 7

========================================================
0. WHAT IS CURED, AND WHAT IS NOT TOUCHED
========================================================
XE-4 finding 1 is CONCEDED as stated. TRAPOCC-2 Section 5 (ii) obtains the row

[proofs:8392]. Both consume a smooth target boundary. TRAPOCC-3 re-proved
(EQ-OCC-2w), (FLUX-ID'w), (FLUX-CONSw) and (SANDWICHw) in weak form for the
nonsmooth target TRAP_2^cl, but it did NOT re-prove this ratio; row 7 of its

NOT IMPLICATED: PE-TRAPOCC's MAIN target TRAP (the 4rho-collar of STRAT, closed
by construction) and its own (ENTRY) at proofs:9073-9074; XE-4 findings 2, 3
and 4; the killing plate S, which this piece does not touch in any way.

STANDING OBJECTS AND THE FILTRATION. (F_t)_{t>=0} is the augmented natural
filtration of the standing diffusion X used throughout PE-TRAPOCC Section 0, the
same filtration under which row MEAS.B is stated [proofs:10807]; right-continuity
is not needed (MEAS.B note, proofs:10937), exactly as recorded in TRAPOCC-3
machinery row 1. The stopping objects are the hitting times
  H_Y      := inf{ t >= 0 : X_t in Y },        Y := TRAP_2^cl,
  H_{D_2}  := inf{ t >= 0 : X_t in D_2 },      D_2 as in (T4.1),
  H_S      := inf{ t >= 0 : X_t in S },        S the landed base ball, read under
                                               the landed plate convention.
NO INDEPENDENCE IS CLAIMED ANYWHERE IN THIS PIECE. The one new probabilistic step
is PATHWISE set monotonicity (T4.3), not a distributional statement.

========================================================
1. THE ENVELOPE, AND WHY IT IS A LANDED OBJECT AND NOT A NEW ONE
========================================================
(T4.1) DEFINITION. D_2 := { E_eps >= theta_2 }, with theta_2 the value already
fixed in Section 0 of TRAPOCC-2, drawn from [S_k + c_H - 1/beta, S_k + c_H] and
Sard-regular for E_eps on M by (T3.3) [proofs:11513-11519].

KEY OBSERVATION (this is the whole cure). PE-DOORREACH (1a) constructs its own
target by exactly this recipe: "pick a regular value theta in
[S_k + c_H - 1/beta, S_k + c_H] and set Door' := { E_eps >= theta }"
[proofs:8372]. Since (T3.3) delivers theta_2 in that same interval, regular for
E_eps on M, the choice theta := theta_2 gives
  D_2 = Door'|_{theta = theta_2}
LITERALLY. PE-DOORREACH Sections 2 and 5 are therefore INSTANTIATED at D_2, not
re-proved by analogy: every hypothesis row of those sections was checked in place
for an arbitrary admissible theta, and theta_2 is admissible. This is why the
repair costs no exponent and no constant.

(T4.2) SMOOTH COMPACT BOUNDARY. D_2 is compact and boundary(D_2) =
{ E_eps = theta_2 } is a smooth compact embedded hypersurface of M.
PROOF. D_2 is closed (E_eps continuous) and M = T^{2N} is compact, so D_2 is
compact. By the REGULAR VALUE THEOREM / PREIMAGE THEOREM (NAMED: Guillemin-Pollack,
Differential Topology, Ch. 1 Sec. 4; equivalently Milnor, Topology from the
Differentiable Viewpoint, Sec. 1. Hypothesis rows: (i) E_eps : M -> R smooth —
HOLDS, "E_eps is smooth" [proofs:8372] and E_eps in C^inf(M); (ii) M a compact
smooth manifold without boundary — HOLDS, M = T^{2N}; (iii) theta_2 a regular
value of E_eps — HOLDS by (T3.3)), the level set { E_eps = theta_2 } is a compact
embedded smooth hypersurface. Boundary identification, two inclusions:
(a) boundary(D_2) subset { E_eps = theta_2 }, since { E_eps > theta_2 } is open
    and contained in D_2, hence in int(D_2);
(b) { E_eps = theta_2 } subset boundary(D_2), since grad E_eps(x) =/= 0 at every
    such x (regularity), so every neighbourhood of x contains points with
    E_eps > theta_2 and points with E_eps < theta_2.
Nonemptiness is not needed but holds: D_2 contains TRAP_2^cl (T4.3) which is
nonempty, and D_2 =/= M since E_eps(z) < theta_2 at any Regime-A start z, so the
level set separates and is nonempty. QED

CONSEQUENCE (the row that TRAP_2^cl failed and D_2 meets). Every boundary point
of D_2 satisfies the exterior sphere condition, so every boundary point is
regular for the Dirichlet problem; Green's second identity applies on
M \ (A_z u S u D_2) with a genuine surface measure on boundary(D_2); and the
inward normal derivative at boundary(D_2) used by PE-DOORREACH (2b) exists. These
are precisely the three consumptions that TRAPOCC-3 could not license at
TRAP_2^cl, and they are licensed here by (T4.2) alone.

========================================================
2. CONTAINMENT AND PATHWISE MONOTONICITY (the only new content)
========================================================
(T4.3) ENVELOPE MONOTONICITY. Y := TRAP_2^cl subset D_2, and for every start y
and every path,
  H_{D_2} <= H_Y      pathwise,                                        (ENV-PATH)
hence { H_Y < H_S } subset { H_{D_2} < H_S } and
  P_y( H_Y < H_S ) <= P_y( H_{D_2} < H_S )      for every y.           (ENV-MON)

PROOF. CONTAINMENT: by the definition of the target,
"TRAP_2^cl := {E_eps >= theta_2} inter closure({w_phi = 0})" [proofs:11456], so
Y subset {E_eps >= theta_2} = D_2. This is the target's LEVEL CLAUSE and nothing
else; no property of the label factor closure({w_phi = 0}) is used, and no
regularity of Y is asserted or needed.

(ENV-PATH): for each fixed path, { t >= 0 : X_t in Y } subset
{ t >= 0 : X_t in D_2 }, and the infimum over a superset is not larger, so
inf{ t : X_t in D_2 } <= inf{ t : X_t in Y }. This is set-theoretic, holds for
every path with no exception set, and uses no continuity, no Markov property and
no independence.

MEASURABILITY OF BOTH SIDES: H_Y is an (F_t)-stopping time by row MEAS.B
[proofs:10807], whose hypothesis row reads "hitting time of a CLOSED set by a
continuous adapted process" and is met for Y by (T3.1) (TRAPOCC-3 machinery
row 1). The SAME row is met for D_2, which is closed by continuity of E_eps
(T4.2), and for S under the landed plate convention. Hence both events
{ H_Y < H_S } and { H_{D_2} < H_S } lie in the relevant sigma-field and
(ENV-MON) follows from (ENV-PATH) by monotonicity of P_y. QED

DIRECTION CHECK. (ENV-MON) points the conservative way: the quantity actually
required to be <= 1/2 is bounded ABOVE by the envelope quantity. Enlarging the
target can only raise the probability, so proving the bound for the LARGER,
SMOOTH target proves it for the smaller, rough one. This is the same conservative
direction already recorded in TRAPOCC-3 machinery row 7's closing sentence and in
(T3.2)'s COVER DIRECTION [proofs:11475-11479].

========================================================
3. HYPOTHESIS ROWS OF PE-DOORREACH SECTIONS 2 + 5, RE-CHECKED AT D_2
========================================================
Regime A is the standing hypothesis: Theta(z,S) <= theta_2 - c_0, with c_0 the
beta-free err-class margin fixed at proofs:10118. Set
  beta_env := max( 4G / c_0 , 2 / c_0 ),   G := sup_M |grad E_eps| < infinity
                                           [proofs:8363],
a beta-free number. All rows below are checked for beta >= beta_env.

ROW (i) — TARGET CLOSED WITH SMOOTH COMPACT BOUNDARY. MET by (T4.2). (This is the
row that fails at TRAP_2^cl and is the entire reason the envelope exists.)

ROW (ii) — A_z, S, D_2 PAIRWISE DISJOINT, EACH WITH SMOOTH BOUNDARY.
  - A_z := closed B_rho(z), rho = 1/beta: boundary is a smooth sphere (landed).
  - dist(z, D_2) >= c_0 / G. PROOF, verbatim in structure with TRAPOCC-3
    machinery row 15 and proofs:10121-10122: Theta(z,S) >= E_eps(z) always, so
    Regime A gives E_eps(z) <= theta_2 - c_0; on D_2 one has E_eps >= theta_2 by
    definition; |grad E_eps| <= G on M, so any path from z to D_2 raises E_eps by
    at least c_0 and therefore has length at least c_0/G. Note this is STRICTLY
    more direct than the landed instance: at D_2 the clause "E_eps >= theta_2 on
    the target" is the DEFINITION of the target, not a derived property.
  - Hence for beta >= beta_env: 2rho = 2/beta <= c_0/(2G) < c_0/G, so the closed
    ball B_{2rho}(z) is disjoint from D_2 with a strict margin. The landed
    threshold for the same statement at TRAP_2 was "for beta >= 2G/c_0"
    [proofs:10124]; beta_env >= 2G/c_0 dominates it and buys strictness.
  - Disjointness from S: UNCHANGED and INHERITED. TRAPOCC-2 handles it "in the
    same way PE-TRAPOCC Section 7's near-S case handles" [proofs:10125], and
    independently E_eps <= A_tube on the collar by (UP-QUAD) with
    A_tube < theta_2 - 1/beta for beta >= beta_*, which is the landed admissibility
    line "On A u S one has, by (UP-QUAD) and (H-SEP), E_eps <= A_tube <= a for
    beta >= beta_*" [proofs:8400]. Since D_2 = {E_eps >= theta_2} and
    A_tube < theta_2, S inter D_2 = empty. NOTHING ABOUT THE PLATE CHANGES.

ROW (iii) — (CAP-UP-GATE) LEVEL RAMP, INSTANTIATED AT THE LEVEL SET D_2 ITSELF.
Put a := theta_2 - 1/beta and f := median{ 0, (theta_2 - E_eps) * beta, 1 }, i.e.
f = 1 on { E_eps <= a }, f = 0 on D_2 exactly, linear in E_eps on the ramp
R := { a <= E_eps <= theta_2 }. This is the landed ramp of PE-DOORREACH Section 3
[proofs:8400] with theta := theta_2 — the MOST NATURAL instance, since the ramp's
zero set is by construction the target itself rather than a Sard-perturbed
superset. Admissibility for cap(A_z, D_2) needs f = 1 on A_z: for y in A_z,
E_eps(y) <= E_eps(z) + G rho <= theta_2 - c_0 + c_0/4 = theta_2 - (3/4) c_0 <= a,
the last step because (3/4) c_0 >= 1/beta for beta >= 2/c_0. Both inequalities
hold for beta >= beta_env. The landed computation then gives
  D(f) = (1/beta) int_R e^{-beta E_eps} beta^2 |grad E_eps|^2 dx
       <= beta G^2 Leb(R) e^{-beta a} <= e * beta G^2 V_M e^{-beta theta_2},
so
  cap(A_z, D_2) <= C_up' * beta * exp( -beta theta_2 ),  C_up' := e G^2 V_M.
CONSTANT LEDGER: the landed C_up := e^2 G^2 V_M [proofs:8403] carries TWO factors
of e, "for the 1/beta ramp width and the 1/beta Sard offset" [proofs:8404]. Here
only the ramp-width factor is spent, because theta_2 IS the regular value; the
second e reappears on the other side via theta_2 >= S_k + c_H - 1/beta. Net: the
envelope constant is no larger than the landed one, so no constant increases.

ROW (iv) — IVT FLOOR AT D_2. For any y with E_eps(y) < theta_2,
  Theta(y, D_2) >= theta_2.
PROOF. Every continuous arc from y to a point of D_2 terminates at a point where
E_eps >= theta_2, so its maximum of E_eps is at least theta_2; taking the infimum
over arcs gives the claim. (The INTERMEDIATE VALUE THEOREM route of
proofs:10130-10132 also applies verbatim; at D_2 the endpoint value alone
suffices, so the floor is if anything cheaper here.) As landed, this REPLACES
(GATE-LOWER) and is UNCONDITIONAL — the gate row is not used at all.

ROW (v) — (CAP-LOW*) / DOORREACH-MAXFIX. UNCHANGED, verbatim TRAPOCC-3 machinery
row 6: "The tube joins z to g* and never touches the target; the target appears
only as the grounding set of a capacity that is bounded BELOW." The Thomson tube
lies in the collar where E_eps <= A_tube < theta_2, hence is disjoint from D_2 as
well. No property of the target enters.

ROW (vi) — PE-DOORREACH SECTION 2 CLASSICAL REPRESENTATION AND MINIMUM PRINCIPLE.
h_{D_2}(x) := P_x( H_{D_2} < H_S ) is the classical solution of the two-set
Dirichlet problem by the PROBABILISTIC REPRESENTATION OF THE DIRICHLET PROBLEM
(NAMED, as landed: Friedman, Stochastic Differential Equations and Applications I,
Thm 6.5.1; equivalently Karatzas-Shreve Ch. 4.3. Hypothesis rows re-checked:
(i) uniform ellipticity — MET, diffusion matrix (1/beta) Id; (ii) smooth bounded
coefficients on compact M — MET; (iii) every boundary point regular — MET, dS is
a smooth sphere and boundary(D_2) is a smooth hypersurface by (T4.2), so the
exterior sphere condition holds; (iv) exit time a.s. finite — MET by ellipticity
plus compactness, cf. positive Harris recurrence at proofs:1867-1879). Step (2b)'s
MINIMUM PRINCIPLE (NAMED: Gilbarg-Trudinger Thm 8.1; rows: uniform ellipticity and
bounded coefficients — MET; c = 0 — MET) is unchanged. Step (2c)'s capacity
monotonicity cap(A_z, S u D_2) >= cap(A_z, S) is purely variational and unchanged.

ROW (vii) — PE-DOORREACH SECTION 5 (PTW), HARNACK AT SCALE 1/beta. Needs
B_{2rho}(y) inter (D_2 u S) = empty for y in dA_z. From row (ii),
dist(y, D_2) >= c_0/G - rho >= (3/4) c_0 / G, and 3rho <= (3/4) c_0 / G for
beta >= 4G/c_0, so B_{2rho}(y) subset B_{3rho}(z) is disjoint from D_2. The
HARNACK INEQUALITY (NAMED, as landed: Gilbarg-Trudinger Thm 8.20; rows: (i)
u >= 0 weak H^1 solution on B_2 — MET, h_{D_2} is smooth and in [0,1] there;
(ii) uniform ellipticity ratio 1 — MET; (iii) |b'| <= G scale-invariant — MET by
rho = 1/beta) applies with the SAME beta-free constant C_H = C(n,G)
[proofs:8430-8433].

ROW (viii) — LEVEL OFFSET FROM z TO y in dA_z. Theta(y,S) <= Theta(z,S) + G/beta,
by prefixing any arc from z to S with the segment [y,z] of length <= rho on which
E_eps <= E_eps(z) + G rho <= Theta(z,S) + G/beta. The landed display carries the

========================================================
(ENTRY-ENV) For every z in R_0 in Regime A (Theta(z,S) <= theta_2 - c_0), every
y in dA_z, and every beta >= max( beta_2(N,delta,eps), beta_env ):

  h_2(y) = P_y( H_{TRAP_2^cl} < H_S )
        <= P_y( H_{D_2} < H_S )                                        [(ENV-MON), T4.3]

        <= C_3 * e^{2G} * beta^{2N+1} * e^{-beta c_0}                   [Regime A]

This is CHARACTER-FOR-CHARACTER the landed display at proofs:10133-10134, with

1. THE OBJECT, AND THE THREE LANDED LINES THAT ROUTE TO IT

=====================================================================
2. LEMMA TRAP-EXIST (the existence lemma, at exact strength)
=====================================================================
STATEMENT. Let M = T^{2N}, n := 2N, with its flat Riemannian metric and geodesic
distance dist [PX:8980 "M := T^{2N}, n := 2N, E_eps in C^inf(M)"]. Let
STRAT subset M be any NONEMPTY subset - NO regularity of STRAT is assumed - and
let rho > 0. Then there exists f_s in C^inf(M) and r in R with TRAP := {f_s <= r}
satisfying

  (S1)  STRAT subset {x : dist(x,STRAT) <= 2rho} subset TRAP;
  (S2)  TRAP subset {x : dist(x,STRAT) <= (25/8) rho} subset
                    {x : dist(x,STRAT) <= 4rho};
  (S3)  TRAP is a compact smooth n-manifold with boundary; its topological
        boundary is dTRAP = f_s^{-1}(r) exactly, a compact smoothly embedded
        two-sided hypersurface carrying the induced surface measure dS and the
        unit normal field n = -grad f_s / |grad f_s| pointing INTO TRAP;
  (S4)  dTRAP is NONEMPTY, provided TRAP is a proper nonempty subset of M.

Hence a set meeting the PX:8992 declaration EXISTS, and {f_s <= r} is one.

PROOF, BY ROWS.

ROW 1 (the distance function). d(x) := dist(x,STRAT) = inf{dist(x,y) : y in
STRAT}. HYPOTHESIS ROW: STRAT nonempty - MET (typed gap (a) below). Then d is
finite and |d(x) - d(x')| <= dist(x,x') by the triangle inequality applied under
the infimum, so d is 1-Lipschitz, in particular continuous. NO NAMED THEOREM IS
NEEDED and, LOAD-BEARING: NO REGULARITY OF STRAT IS USED. This is the structural
reason the route works at the main target: the mollified distance function
launders an arbitrary set, and STRAT's own regularity - which the lane nowhere
establishes for the union of label strata at PX:8990 - is never needed.

ROW 2 (smoothing). NAMED: WHITNEY APPROXIMATION THEOREM (Lee, Introduction to
Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed., Thm 6.21; equivalently Hirsch, Differential Topology,
Ch. 2). STATEMENT AS CONSUMED: if M is a smooth manifold, u : M -> R is
continuous, and eta : M -> R is continuous and strictly positive, there exists
f_s in C^inf(M) with |f_s(x) - u(x)| < eta(x) for every x in M.
HYPOTHESIS ROWS: (i) M a smooth manifold - MET (M = T^{2N}, PX:8980);
(ii) u continuous - MET (ROW 1, u := d);
(iii) eta continuous and strictly positive - MET (eta :== rho/8, a positive
constant, and rho = 1/beta > 0 by PX:8991 "rho := 1/beta (PE-DOORREACH's scale
choice)").
NOT CONSUMED: compactness of M; Lipschitz-ness of d beyond continuity. The
landed row "M compact smooth, d continuous - met" is therefore MET and slightly
over-strong; nothing is weakened by tightening it. OUTPUT: |f_s - d| <= rho/8
pointwise on M.

ROW 3 (Sard). NAMED: SARD'S THEOREM (Lee ISM 2nd ed., Thm 6.10; Milnor, Topology
from the Differentiable Viewpoint, Ch. 3).
HYPOTHESIS ROWS: (i) f_s : M^n -> R of class C^k with k >= n - MET (f_s in
C^inf by ROW 2); (ii) M a second-countable smooth n-manifold - MET (M compact).
OUTPUT: the set of critical values of f_s is Lebesgue-null in R. The interval
[2rho + rho/8, 3rho] = [17rho/8, 24rho/8] has length (7/8) rho > 0 for every
rho > 0, hence contains a regular value r. FIX one. NO THRESHOLD ON beta IS USED
AT THIS ROW.

ROW 4 (the sandwich, arithmetic displayed).
 (S1) If d(x) <= 2rho then f_s(x) <= d(x) + rho/8 <= 2rho + rho/8 <= r, so
      x in {f_s <= r} = TRAP. Consumes r >= 2rho + rho/8, the LEFT endpoint of
      the Sard interval, and the inclusion is with "<=" so the endpoint case is
      covered. And d = 0 on STRAT gives STRAT subset {d <= 2rho}.
 (S2) If x in TRAP then f_s(x) <= r <= 3rho, so d(x) <= f_s(x) + rho/8 <=
      3rho + rho/8 = (25/8) rho = 3.125 rho <= 4rho. Consumes r <= 3rho, the
      RIGHT endpoint. SLACK: (7/8) rho below the declared 4rho. This slack is
      used twice below (ROW 7 note, and Section 4's attainment micro-row) and is
      the concrete payoff of pinning the construction rather than leaving the
      declaration as a bare sandwich.
The declared sandwich therefore holds, with the upper inclusion strict by 7rho/8.

ROW 5 (smooth boundary). NAMED: REGULAR LEVEL SET THEOREM (Lee ISM 2nd ed.,
Cor 5.14: every regular level set of a smooth map is a properly embedded
submanifold of codimension equal to the dimension of the codomain), together
with the SUBMERSION LOCAL NORMAL FORM (Lee ISM 2nd ed., Thm 4.12) for the
manifold-with-boundary form of the sublevel set (the "regular sublevel set"
proposition; its edition numbering is not load-bearing here because the
one-line derivation is displayed).
HYPOTHESIS ROWS: (i) f_s smooth - MET (ROW 2); (ii) r a regular value of f_s -
MET (ROW 3); (iii) M smooth without boundary - MET.
OUTPUT: L := f_s^{-1}(r) is a properly embedded smooth hypersurface; L is closed
in M and M is compact, so L is COMPACT. At each x in L, grad f_s(x) != 0, so by
the submersion normal form f_s is a coordinate function near x and {f_s <= r} is
locally a closed half-space; hence TRAP is a compact smooth n-manifold with
boundary L. TWO-SIDEDNESS AND THE NORMAL: n(x) := -grad f_s(x)/|grad f_s(x)| is
defined and smooth on L and points INTO TRAP (f_s decreases in that direction),
so L is two-sided and carries the induced Riemannian surface measure dS. This is
exactly the object PX:9028 names ("Let n denote at dTRAP the normal pointing INTO
TRAP") and PX:9041 names ("e_D := - w partial_n h_z dS on dTRAP with n into
TRAP").

ROW 6 (the boundary is the level set, and it is nonempty). NEW; not written in
the landed clause.
 (a) IDENTIFICATION, two inclusions. {f_s < r} is open and contained in TRAP,
     hence contained in int(TRAP), so d(TRAP) subset {f_s = r} = L. Conversely
     let x in L; grad f_s(x) != 0, so along the integral curve of grad f_s
     through x the value f_s strictly increases through r, and every
     neighbourhood of x meets both {f_s > r} = M \ TRAP and {f_s < r} subset
     int(TRAP); hence x in d(TRAP). Therefore d(TRAP) = L exactly.
 (b) NONEMPTINESS. TRAP != empty since STRAT subset TRAP by (S1) and STRAT is
     nonempty. TRAP != M: by (S2), TRAP subset {d <= 4rho}, and by the FIRST
     clause of the landed (G4) - "R_0 inter TRAP = empty" [PX:9010] - which is
     derived from (S2) together with (G1),(G2),(G3) and consumes NO boundary
     property of TRAP, no point of the nonempty set R_0 lies in TRAP. M = T^{2N}
     is CONNECTED, so a subset that is nonempty, proper and closed cannot also
     be open; by (a) its topological boundary L is therefore NONEMPTY.
 DEPENDENCY ORDER, EXPLICIT, TO SHOW THERE IS NO CIRCULARITY:
     (S2) -> (G4) first clause -> TRAP proper -> L nonempty -> (S3)/(S4).
     Nothing in this chain uses the boundary.
 WHY THIS ROW MATTERS: without it the declaration's "dTRAP a smooth compact
 hypersurface" would be satisfiable VACUOUSLY by dTRAP = empty, and then
 (EQ-OCC) at PX:9035 would read "0 = mu(TRAP)" against mu(TRAP) > 0. The row
 converts a clause that could have been vacuous into a statement with content.

ROW 7 (beta-dependence is QUALITATIVE ONLY). NEW; the row the landed clause does

generally dist(z, TRAP) > k rho for every integer k <= 20.

Let y satisfy dist(y, TRAP) <= k rho. By (S2), TRAP subset

length < inj(M), which meets Delta_phi at some p by (G2), E_eps(p) >= Gate by
(G1), and |grad E_eps| <= G - gives
  E_eps(y) >= Gate - (k+4) G/beta.

5. THE ENERGY-ENVELOPE DEVICE AT THE MAIN TARGET: NOT NEEDED, NOT SAFE
=====================================================================
DISPOSITION OF THE F1 CHECKER'S MEDIUM 1. The sentence in CURE-XE4-1's typed gap
(d) - "If it turns out to need repair, the identical envelope device applies with
Door' at the gate level" - must be STRUCK. CONCURRED. But the checker's proposed
replacement ("the envelope device requires the target to be a superlevel set of
E_eps and does not transfer to a collar target") is right in its conclusion and
wrong in its stated reason, and the correct replacement is stronger: NO DEVICE IS
NEEDED, because the license is landed at PX:8992.

The checker's stated reason is that TRAP "contains low-energy stratum floor
points, so no energy superlevel set contains it". That is refuted by the corpus's
own floor rows. (MU-TRAP) establishes E_eps >= m_k + m_1(lambda) - 4G/beta on ALL
of TRAP [PX:9080-9081, from R3-STRAT's floor "E_eps >= m_k + m_1(lambda)
pointwise" and TRAP subset {dist(.,STRAT) <= 4rho}], and (G3) establishes
E_eps >= Gate - 4G/beta on TRAP inter {w_phi = 0} [PX:9009]. Hence
  TRAP subset { E_eps >= min(m_k + m_1(lambda), Gate) - 4G/beta }.
CONTAINMENT IS NOT WHAT FAILS.

What fails is EXPONENT PRESERVATION. For an envelope D := {E_eps >= c} at a
Sard-regular c and z with E_eps(z) < c, the communication height is c EXACTLY:
any arc from z into D attains max >= c, and the connected component of the open
set {E_eps < c} containing z has its boundary inside {E_eps = c}, so
Theta(z, D) = c. This is the same mechanism the companion leg uses, TRAPOCC-2
PX:10125-10127 ("by the INTERMEDIATE VALUE THEOREM, Theta(z,TRAP_2) >= theta_2
for any z with E_eps(z) < theta_2"). An envelope at the main target would
therefore replace (ENTRY)'s exponent input (GATE-LOWER) - "Theta(z, TRAP) >=
Gate - 4G/beta = m_k + 2 lambda - 4G/beta" [PX:9064] - by c, while PX:9074's
positivity margin is stated AGAINST GATE: "the exponent is at least Gate - S_k -
c_H - eta - 6G/beta >= 3 c_H - eta - 6G/beta > 0 by (G1)'s chain Gate >= S_k +
4 c_H". The lane nowhere establishes m_k + m_1(lambda) >= Gate = m_k + 2 lambda,
and the assembly deliberately does not need it: PX:9091-9093 telescopes the two
factors through "Theta_gate <= max(Theta(z,S), Theta(z,TRAP)) = Theta(z,TRAP)",
not through floor >= gate. So the envelope would import a relation the lane does
not have. It is unnecessary AND exponent-risky here; the direct license is
cheaper and stronger.

STEP 1. THE PLATE LEVEL, DERIVED AT THE QUARTER RADIUS, NOT INHERITED FROM THE

  "E_eps(x) <= m_k + eps w_k + (L_eps/2) dist(x, G_k)^2   on U.  (UP-QUAD)"

on the plate directly. Fix x in closure(S). Since g* in G_k [PX:890, PX:995,
PX:8988] and ||x - g*||_max <= delta/4,
  dist_euc(x, G_k)^2 <= dist_euc(x, g*)^2 <= 2N ||x - g*||_max^2
                     <= 2N (delta/4)^2 = N delta^2 / 8,
whence (UP-QUAD)'s cost term (L_eps/2) dist^2 is at most
(L_eps/2)(N delta^2/8) = L_eps N delta^2/16, i.e.

  (P1)   sup_{closure(S)} E_eps  <=  m_k + eps w_k + L_eps N delta^2/16.

E_eps is continuous and the bound is non-strict, so it holds on the CLOSED ball
verbatim; the boundary dS is included with no extra step.

STEP 6. FROM THE GAP TO THE DISTANCE. G := sup_M |grad E_eps| < infinity, landed

beta-free" [PX:10121-10122]), applied to a PAIR of points instead of a point and
a set. Combining with (P6) and taking the infimum over both arguments:

  (PLATE-SEP)   dist( closure(S), TRAP_2^cl ) >= c_plate/(2G) > 0,
                for every beta >= beta_plate := 2/c_plate;
                c_plate, G, beta_plate all beta-free.

NEVER STATED WITHOUT ITS THRESHOLD. Every downstream use of this margin carries

(PLATE-REG) H_S = H_{closure(S)} P_x-a.s. FOR EVERY x in M
--------------------------------------------------------

ROUTE (R-b), GIRSANOV TRANSFER. The regularity fact is proved for the DRIFTLESS
process and moved to the standing diffusion by an equivalence of measures. No
Brownian theorem is applied to a drifted object.

OBJECTS AND SIGMA-FIELDS (all landed; nothing new).
  STANDING SDE, verbatim: "dX_t = -grad E_eps(X_t) dt + sqrt(2/beta) dW_t on
  M = T^{2N}, flagship k=1, N>=10, M2-PIN (lambda>kappa), eps in [0, eps_2)
  fixed" [MM:3001 as anchored corpus-wide, current bytes MM:3002; quoted at
  PX:489, PX:2270-2272, PX:2709-2710] (the kappa in that quotation is the
  STANDING COUPLING; see SYMBOL DISCIPLINE); generator "L u = (1/beta) Delta u -
  <grad E_eps, grad u>" [PX:10015]; "E_eps is smooth and Lambda-periodic"
  [MM:1345, quoted at PX:835].
  b := -grad E_eps, |b| <= G := sup_M |grad E_eps| < infinity [PX:8363, PX:8997].
  (F_t) := the usual augmentation of the raw filtration of X: right-continuous
  and P-complete, "so hitting times of closed sets are (F_t)-stopping times
  [lane-minmig:3035]" [PX:11865-11866]. X has continuous paths.
  H_F := inf{ s >= 0 : X_s in F }; H_S := inf{ s >= 0 : X_s in S } [PX:11873].
  sigma := H_{closure(S)}, an (F_t)-stopping time by the landed row above,
  closure(S) being closed.
  sigma_S := inf{ s > 0 : X_s in S }, the PENETRATION time, the exact object the
  regularity statement below is about. At a point y not in S, H_S = sigma_S
  pathwise, so no s = 0 convention is ever used.
  H_S IS AN (F_t)-STOPPING TIME: S is open and paths are continuous, so
  {H_S < t} = union over rationals q in [0,t) of {X_q in S} lies in F_t; the
  right-continuity of (F_t) upgrades this to the stopping-time property.
  F_sigma := { A in F : A inter {sigma <= t} in F_t for every t >= 0 }.
  SIGMA-FIELDS USED, EXHAUSTIVELY: F_sigma, F_{theta^+(t)} (at (v2c) only), and,
  on the canonical space of (c) below, G_1 and G_{0+}. NO INDEPENDENCE IS CLAIMED
  ANYWHERE IN THIS CURE.

(a) GEOMETRY: AN EXPLICIT INTERIOR CONE, IN COORDINATES, AT FACES, EDGES AND
CORNERS ALIKE.
In the standing chart, "max norm, centred at the fixed g*" [MM:3006 as anchored
corpus-wide, current bytes MM:3007],
  closure(S) = { x : ||x - g*||_max <= delta/4 }
             = product over i = 1..2N of [ g*_i - delta/4, g*_i + delta/4 ],
  S = { x : ||x - g*||_max < delta/4 },   dS = closure(S) \ S,
consistent with "S = B_{delta/4}(g*) is a MAX-NORM ball (a cube, Lebesgue volume
(delta/2)^{2N})" [PX:1297]. Put
  r := delta/8,   B_r := { z : |z - g*|_euc <= r },
and note |.|_max <= |.|_euc gives B_r subset B^max_r(g*) subset S. For y in dS
put
  K_y := { (1-t) y + t z  :  t in [0,1], z in B_r }.
(a1) COORDINATE VERIFICATION, NO CASE SPLIT. Let x = (1-t) y + t z with t in
     [0,1], z in B_r. For EACH coordinate i,
       | x_i - g*_i | = | (1-t)(y_i - g*_i) + t (z_i - g*_i) |
                     <= (1-t) |y_i - g*_i| + t |z_i - g*_i|
                     <= (1-t)(delta/4) + t (delta/8)
                      = delta/4 - t delta/8.
     Therefore ||x - g*||_max <= delta/4 - t delta/8, which is STRICTLY less than
     delta/4 for every t in (0,1]. Hence
       K_y \ {y} subset S,   with the quantitative slack
       dist_max( x, dS ) >= t delta/8 at parameter t.
     THE BOUND USES ONLY |y_i - g*_i| <= delta/4 FOR EVERY i, which holds for
     every y in closure(S). It never inspects the active set
     J(y) := { i : |y_i - g*_i| = delta/4 }, never differentiates dS, and never
     case-splits on |J(y)| = 1 (face), 2 <= |J(y)| <= 2N-1 (edge) or |J(y)| = 2N
     (corner). Faces, edges and corners are covered by the same two lines. (v1
     obtained the same conclusion by citing Rockafellar's line-segment principle;
     the computation above replaces the citation and is self-contained.)
(a2) CONE SHAPE AND UNIFORM APERTURE. K_y = conv({y} u B_r) is the closed
     truncated circular cone with vertex y, axis the segment [y, g*], height
     |y - g*|_euc, and half-angle
       alpha_y = arcsin( r / |y - g*|_euc )
               >= arcsin( (delta/8) / ( sqrt(2N) . delta/4 ) )
                = arcsin( 1 / (2 sqrt(2N)) ) > 0,
     using |y - g*|_euc <= sqrt(2N) ||y - g*||_max = sqrt(2N) delta/4 on dS. Its
     height satisfies |y - g*|_euc >= ||y - g*||_max = delta/4 > 0. Both bounds
     are uniform over y in dS and free of beta; the aperture is free of delta.
(a3) LOCAL TRUNCATION, used from (e) on. Fix r_0 := delta/8 and put
       K_y^loc := K_y inter { x : |x - y|_euc <= r_0 }.
     K_y^loc is again a closed truncated circular cone with vertex y, the same
     axis, half-angle >= arcsin(1/(2 sqrt(2N))) and height r_0 > 0, and
     K_y^loc \ {y} subset S by (a1). (The truncation really is the full cone of
     height r_0: with d := |y - g*|_euc >= delta/4 and r = delta/8 <= d/2, one
     has d^2 - r^2 >= (3/4) d^2, so for |x - y|_euc = s <= r_0 the smallest
     admissible parameter satisfies t <= (4/3)(s/d) <= 2/3 <= 1.)
NOTE ON SCOPE. This is precisely the certificate (G3-CORNER) could not supply for
TRAP_2^cl, and the CUBE supplies it for free. NOTHING is claimed here about
TRAP_2^cl or about any multi-bond corner.

(b) LIFT TO THE UNIVERSAL COVER (so that the Euclidean statements below are
literally about a Euclidean process).
M = T^{2N} = R^{2N}/Lambda with the flat metric ("the compact flat torus
M = T^{2N} = T^N_theta x T^N_phi (dim M = 2N)" [MM:1345, quoted at PX:835]); let
pi : R^{2N} -> M be the covering projection. E_eps is "smooth and
Lambda-periodic" [MM:1345], so b~ := -grad(E_eps o pi) is a smooth
Lambda-periodic vector field on R^{2N} with sup |b~| = G < infinity, and b~ is
globally Lipschitz (smooth + periodic). The lifted equation
  dX~_s = b~(X~_s) ds + sqrt(2/beta) dW_s,   X~_0 = x~_0,  pi(x~_0) = x_0,
has a unique strong solution, and pi(X~) is the standing diffusion started at
x_0. HYPOTHESIS ROW: pi^{-1}(S) is a disjoint union of translates of the open
cube of side delta/2, each mapped isometrically onto S by pi - HOLDS because the
corpus reads S as an honest cube of side delta/2 with "Lebesgue volume
(delta/2)^{2N}" [PX:1297], i.e. delta/2 is below the period in each coordinate.
Let S~ be the component of pi^{-1}(S) whose closure contains x~_0. Then for every
path, { X~_s in S~ } implies { pi(X~_s) in S }, hence
  sigma_S( pi(X~) ) <= sigma_{S~}( X~ ),
and it suffices to prove sigma_{S~} = 0 a.s. for the lift. All of (c)-(g) is
performed on R^{2N} for the lift; the cone of (a) is built inside S~ in the
standing coordinates. NOTHING is claimed about the torus beyond this projection
inequality.

(c) GIRSANOV: THE DRIFT IS REMOVED BY AN EQUIVALENCE OF MEASURES.
CANONICAL SPACE. Omega_0 := C([0,1]; R^{2N}) with coordinate process Z, raw
filtration (G_t^0), and G_t := its usual augmentation. Two laws on Omega_0,
both started at x~_0:
  P := law of the lifted drifted solution X~ on [0,1];
  Q := law of the DRIFTLESS process Y, dY_s = sqrt(2/beta) dW_s, Y_0 = x~_0.
NAMED CLASSICAL FACT: Girsanov's theorem (Cameron-Martin-Maruyama-Girsanov), with
Novikov's sufficient condition for the exponential local martingale to be a
martingale.
CITED: Karatzas-Shreve, Brownian Motion and Stochastic Calculus, Ch. 3 Sec. 5
(Thm 5.1, Girsanov; Cor. 5.13, Novikov's condition).
HYPOTHESIS ROWS:
 - Dispersion constant and invertible: sigma_disp = sqrt(2/beta) I, with beta
   finite and fixed at every consumption site - HOLDS, "dX_t = -grad E_eps(X_t)
   dt + sqrt(2/beta) dW_t" [MM:3001 as anchored, current bytes MM:3002].
 - Drift progressively measurable and bounded on the horizon: b~ is smooth,
   periodic, |b~| <= G < infinity - HOLDS, "G := sup_M |grad E_eps| < inf"
   [PX:8363].
 - NOVIKOV. With theta_s := sqrt(beta/2) b~(Z_s) (the Girsanov integrand), the
   bound |theta_s|^2 <= (beta/2) G^2 gives
     E[ exp( (1/2) int_0^1 |theta_s|^2 ds ) ] <= exp( beta G^2 / 4 ) < infinity
   - HOLDS, for every fixed beta. (No beta-uniformity is claimed or needed: the
   conclusion drawn is a null-set statement, and null sets do not carry
   constants.)
 - Finite horizon: T = 1 - HOLDS by choice; nothing below looks past time 1.
CONCLUSION CONSUMED: P and Q are MUTUALLY ABSOLUTELY CONTINUOUS on G_1, the
density being the exponential martingale of the transformation. Consequences used:
 (c1) P and Q have the SAME null sets in G_1, hence the same null sets in
      G_{0+} subset G_1; so an event of G_{0+} has P-probability 1 if and only if
      it has Q-probability 1.
 (c2) The usual augmentation of (G_t^0) is the same under P and under Q
      (equivalent measures have the same null sets), so G_{0+} is unambiguous and
      no augmentation ambiguity is hidden in (c1). The canonical space is
      C([0,1]), so G_infinity^0 = G_1^0 and there is no horizon beyond 1 at which
      the two augmentations could differ.
NOT CLAIMED: anything about the two laws beyond horizon 1; any statement uniform
in beta; any independence.

(d) SCALE / TIME CHANGE, ONE LINE. Under Q, Z_s = x~_0 + sqrt(2/beta) W_s, so
(Z_s)_{s >= 0} has the law of ( x~_0 + B_{2s/beta} )_{s >= 0} with B a standard
2N-dimensional Brownian motion. For every set F,
  inf{ s > 0 : Z_s in F } = (beta/2) . inf{ u > 0 : x~_0 + B_u in F },
so the two hitting times vanish together and regularity of a point for a set is
invariant under this deterministic time change. The covariance (2/beta) I is
therefore not an obstacle to citing standard Brownian results, and no constant is
introduced.

(e) CONE CRITERION, FOR BROWNIAN MOTION, WHERE THE CITATION IS LEGITIMATE.
NAMED CLASSICAL FACT: the Poincare cone condition (Zaremba's cone criterion) for
regularity of a boundary point for BROWNIAN MOTION: if a closed set K contains a
truncated circular cone with vertex x~_0, positive height and positive half-angle,
then x~_0 is regular for K, i.e.
  P^{BM}_{x~_0}( inf{ s > 0 : B_s in K } = 0 ) = 1.
CITED: Karatzas-Shreve, Brownian Motion and Stochastic Calculus, Ch. 4 Sec. 2
(the Dirichlet problem; regularity of boundary points under the cone condition);
Port-Stone, Brownian Motion and Classical Potential Theory, Ch. 4.
WHY THE BROWNIAN CITATION IS LEGITIMATE HERE, AND WAS NOT IN v1: steps (c) and
(d) have moved the computation to the driftless law and then to standard Brownian
motion. The drift has been REMOVED BY AN EQUIVALENCE OF MEASURES, not ignored,
and the conclusion will be moved back in (g) through an event that lies in
G_{0+}. No theorem is applied to a drifted object at any point.

(f) POINTS ARE POLAR, AND THE STARTING POINT IS NOT REVISITED.
NAMED CLASSICAL FACT: polarity of singletons for Brownian motion in dimension
n >= 2 ( P^{BM}_x( T_{y} < infinity ) = 0 for x != y ).
CITED: Karatzas-Shreve Ch. 3 Sec. 3 (polarity of points).
HYPOTHESIS ROW: n = 2N >= 2 - HOLDS.
THE FORM ACTUALLY USED is non-revisiting of the START, and it is derived in one
line from the cited fact by the (simple) Markov property at a fixed time: for
every t > 0,
  P^{BM}_{x~_0}( exists s >= t : B_s = x~_0 )
      = E^{BM}_{x~_0}[ P^{BM}_{B_t}( T_{x~_0} < infinity ) ] = 0,
since B_t != x~_0 a.s. and points are polar; taking t = 1/m and the union over
m in N,
  P^{BM}_{x~_0}( exists s > 0 : B_s = x~_0 ) = 0.
INDEPENDENT SECOND ROUTE, kept because it is intrinsic to the standing form: a
singleton has zero capacity for the regular Dirichlet form (D, H^1(M)) on an
n >= 2 manifold with the standing w, and sets of zero capacity are polar. NAMED:
Fukushima-Oshima-Takeda Ch. 4; the regularity row is verbatim the one already met
at (WFF-1) [PX:11567-11571]. Either route suffices; the Brownian one is used
below because it lives on the same side of the Girsanov transfer as (e).

(g) EVERY y in dS IS REGULAR FOR THE OPEN S, UNDER THE STANDING DIFFUSION.
Fix y in dS and run (b)-(f) at x_0 := y. Under Q - equivalently, by (d), under
standard Brownian motion - (e) gives times s_m > 0 with s_m -> 0 and
Z_{s_m} in K^loc_y; (f) gives, a.s., Z_{s_m} != y for every m; hence
Z_{s_m} in K^loc_y \ {y} subset S~ by (a1) + (a3). Therefore
  Q( sigma_{S~} = 0 ) = 1,    sigma_{S~} := inf{ s > 0 : Z_s in S~ }.
MEASURABILITY OF THE EVENT, INSTANTIATED HERE AND NOT MERELY ASSERTED (v2 showed
this only for H_S on the torus). S~ is OPEN and Z has continuous paths, so for
every t in (0,1]
  { sigma_{S~} < t } = union over rationals q in (0,t) of { Z_q in S~ }:
the inclusion "superset" is immediate; for "subset", if sigma_{S~} < t there is
s in (0,t) with Z_s in S~, and by continuity of Z and openness of S~ the whole
set { u : Z_u in S~ } contains a neighbourhood of s inside (0,t), hence a
rational q. The right-hand side lies in the RAW G_t^0. Therefore
  { sigma_{S~} = 0 } = intersection over m of { sigma_{S~} < 1/m }
lies in intersection over m of G_{1/m}^0 subset G_{0+} subset G_1.
By (c1) the same event has P-probability 1. Projecting by (b), sigma_S = 0
P_y-a.s. for the standing diffusion started at y; and since y is not in S,
H_S = sigma_S pathwise, so
  P_y( H_S = 0 ) = 1     for every y in dS.
QED (g)

(h) TRANSFER FROM EVERY START. Fix x in M.
 (h1) closure(S) contains S, so sigma := H_{closure(S)} <= H_S pathwise.
 (h2) On { sigma = infinity }: H_S = infinity by (h1); equality holds.
 (h3) On { sigma < infinity }: X_sigma in closure(S), because paths are
      continuous and closure(S) is closed (take s_n decreasing to sigma with
      X_{s_n} in closure(S); the limit stays in the closed set).
      CASE X_sigma in S: then H_S <= sigma, and with (h1), H_S = sigma.
      CASE X_sigma in dS: H_S >= sigma by (h1), and X_s not in closure(S) for
      s < sigma, so the shift identity H_S = sigma + H_S o theta_sigma holds
      pathwise on that event. Apply:

      NAMED CLASSICAL FACT (v3; v2 deferred to an unresolved corpus pointer).
      STRONG MARKOV PROPERTY OF THE UNIQUE STRONG SOLUTION OF A TIME-HOMOGENEOUS
      SDE WITH BOUNDED LIPSCHITZ DRIFT AND CONSTANT NON-DEGENERATE DISPERSION:
      the family (P_x)_{x in M} of laws of the standing diffusion is a strong
      Markov family, i.e. for every (F_t)-stopping time tau, every bounded
      F-measurable Phi on path space and every x,
        E_x[ Phi o theta_tau | F_tau ] = E_{X_tau}[ Phi ]   P_x-a.s. on
        { tau < infinity }.
      CITED: Karatzas-Shreve, Brownian Motion and Stochastic Calculus, Ch. 5
      Sec. 4 (strong Markov property of solutions of stochastic differential
      equations); Rogers-Williams, Diffusions, Markov Processes and Martingales,
      Vol. 2, Ch. V.
      HYPOTHESIS ROWS, all discharged INSIDE this cure:

             which is the row that declares the augmentation.
       (sm4) tau := sigma = H_{closure(S)} is an (F_t)-stopping time - HOLDS by

       (sm5) Phi := 1{ H_S = 0 } is bounded and F-measurable - HOLDS: H_S is an
             (F_t)-stopping time by the row displayed in OBJECTS above, and
             theta_tau is measurable on path space.
       (sm6) NO MEASURABLE-SELECTION OR VERSION ISSUE: (g) delivers
             P_y(H_S = 0) = 1 for EVERY y in dS, and trivially for every y in S,

      CONSUMED: P_x( H_S o theta_sigma = 0 | F_sigma ) = P_{X_sigma}( H_S = 0 )

      NOT INHERITED: the landed deferral "by the STRONG MARKOV PROPERTY for the

 (h4) closure(S) = S u dS, so (h2)-(h3) exhaust the cases:

(v4) A_z AND THE PLATE. Landed: "A_z := closed B_rho(z) and B_{2rho}(z) are
disjoint from TRAP_2, and from S in the same way PE-TRAPOCC Section 7's near-S
case handles" [PX:10124-10125]. Three lines:
 (v4a) dist(z, closure(S)) = dist(z, S) for EVERY z, an infimum over a set being
   the infimum over its closure. So the landed near-plate separation
   dist(z,S) > 2rho delivers A_z u B_{2rho}(z) disjoint from closure(S) verbatim:
   NO new threshold, NO new case.
 (v4b) The only z the enlargement could bite are z in dS. There H_S = 0 P_z-a.s.
   by (PLATE-REG)(g), hence v_2(z) = 0 and E_z[int_0^{H_S ^ T} 1_{TRAP_2} ds] = 0:
   every consumed display holds at such z with no flux machinery invoked at all.
   The same holds at z in S. So the flux route is only ever run at
   z in M \ closure(S), where (v4a) applies.
 (v4c) In the CONSUMED instance the start is z in S^+ or z in dS^+
   [PX:12024-12026, PX:12030-12044]. On dS^+,
   dist_max(dS^+, closure(S)) = delta/2 - delta/4 = delta/4; since
   dist_euc >= dist_max, dist(z, closure(S)) >= delta/4 in either norm
   convention. With the landed scale "rho := 1/beta (PE-DOORREACH's scale
   choice)." [PX:8991, restated PX:10025, PX:11888], the condition
   2rho <= delta/4 reads beta >= 8/delta, and it SUFFICES with the open ball:
   any w in B_{2rho}(z) has |w - z| < 2rho <= delta/4 <= dist(z, closure(S)), so
   w is not in the plate; and A_z = closed B_rho(z) satisfies
   |w - z| <= rho < 2rho, likewise. Hence A_z u B_{2rho}(z) is disjoint from the
   plate for every beta >= 8/delta, a beta-free threshold of exactly the type
   already fixed at "for beta >= 2G/c_0" [PX:10124].

(PLATE-COR) A LANDED CLAUSE THAT IS FALSE AND IS SCOPED OUT, NOT RESTORED
--------------------------------------------------------

THE FACT. (SANDWICHw) step (3) reads "(3) Let H be the L-harmonic function on V
with H = u q.e. on dV = dA_z u dS (variational solution; dA_z, dS are smooth
spheres, so this is the landed regular case), and" [PX:11628-11629]. dS is the
boundary of a MAX-NORM ball - "S = B_{delta/4}(g*) is a MAX-NORM ball (a cube,
Lebesgue volume (delta/2)^{2N})" [PX:1297] - hence it carries 2N pairs of faces,
lower-dimensional edges and 2^{2N} corners, and is NOT a smooth sphere. The
clause is FALSE as landed.

THE REPAIR IS TO SCOPE, NOT TO RESTORE. The step consumes only q.e. boundary
values and H^1_0 membership. Landed, verbatim: "(3) ... and p := H - u. Then
p in H^1_0(V), p is L-harmonic on V \ Y, p = H q.e. on Y, and p >= 0."
[PX:11628-11631]; "Hence T_p >= 0 on V by the form-semigroup relation. Since
T_H = 0 on V, T_u|_V = -T_p <= 0." [PX:11633-11634]; and the proof advertises
exactly that discipline: "(Elementary weak minimum principle; it replaces the
C^0(closure) framing of GT Thm 8.1 at this one step and imports nothing.)"
[PX:11626-11627] and "it consumes NO boundary regularity of Y." [PX:11636].
Nothing in the step reads a pointwise boundary value. REPLACEMENT TEXT for the
parenthesis:
  "(variational solution with q.e. boundary values; no boundary regularity of dV
   is consumed at this step)".
v1 proposed instead to RESTORE "the landed regular case" via the cone row. That
was an over-claim: regularity of boundary points delivers continuous attainment
only for CONTINUOUS boundary data, and the continuity of u on dV was never
displayed. The clause is deleted, not replaced by another unearned hypothesis.

THE SAME SUBSTITUTION AT THE OTHER OCCURRENCE. "every boundary point regular -
met, dS and dDoor' are smooth hypersurfaces" [PX:9022-9024, quoted at
PX:11574-11575] is false for the same reason, and is already superseded:
machinery row 2 records "UPGRADED (row replaced) by (WFF-1)" [PX:11709]. Delete
the smoothness clause there too; NOTHING replaces it, because (WFF-1) is a
statement about compacts and consumes no boundary regularity of either member.
NOTE, NEW IN v3: the SAME row PX:11709 also carries defect (D2), the second
landed assertion "Y and S disjoint compacts". The row therefore needs BOTH edits:
delete the smoothness clause, and re-point the compactness parenthesis to
closure(S).

WHAT IS AVAILABLE IF A FUTURE CONSUMER WANTS POINTWISE ATTAINMENT, AND AT WHAT
STRENGTH - NOT CONSUMED HERE. For the TWO SPECIFIC potentials h_pl = h_{Y,
closure(S)} and h_z = h_{A_z, closure(S) u Y}, and ONLY at points of dS:
 - the boundary datum of each is locally constant on dV = dA_z u dS (value 0 on
   the plate piece, 1 on the other), and the two pieces are at positive distance
   by (PLATE-SEP) and (v4), so the datum is continuous - ROW HOLDS;
 - every y in dS is regular for S by (PLATE-REG)(g), a fortiori for closure(S) -
   ROW HOLDS;
 - the regular-point theorem then gives lim_{ V ni x -> y } h_pl(x) = 0 = h_pl(y).
   NAMED: continuity of the Dirichlet solution at a regular boundary point. The
   statement is needed FOR THE DIFFUSION, so it requires the same Girsanov
   transfer displayed at (PLATE-REG)(c), which is available; a reader who wants
   this must run that transfer, it is not free.
CLAIMED STRENGTH: continuity at regular boundary points, of these two specific
solutions, at plate boundary points. NOT CLAIMED: continuity of an arbitrary
solution; attainment at an arbitrary point of dV; attainment for discontinuous
data; anything at all about dA_z beyond its landed smoothness. NOT CONSUMED: no
display in this cure or in Section 4 uses any of it.

SCOPED NON-RE-PROOF. The SMOOTH route (a) instance at PX:10043-10047 ("Fix any
closed A_z disjoint from S u TRAP_2", defining e_S on dS by a normal derivative)
silently assumes dS smooth. It is superseded by the weak route and is NOT
consumed by the chain repaired here; it is NOT re-proved. Any future consumer of
it inherits this correction and would need either the cone row or a genuinely
smooth plate.

----------------------------------------------------------------
(1) LEMMA PE3p.3b (COMPONENT MEMBERSHIP AT THE POST-REACH START)
----------------------------------------------------------------

OBJECTS, ALL LANDED.
 (F_s)_{s>=0}  the augmented natural filtration of the standing SDE
               [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3035]; paths continuous on the compact
               M = T^{2N} [standing setting, :3002].
 Sec_k      := {w_theta = k}, OPEN [la3-reader-packet-v1.md:55-56].
 L          := inf{ s > 0 : X_s not in Sec_k }   (the literal terminus, (0)).
 D(0)       the delayed S-return [lane-minmig-proofs-v1.md:3015-3016].
 T'         ANY random time with T' <= L; in particular T = min(D(0), L)
            [terminus row], H_S wedge T, and H_S wedge L - the three termini
            E2-ASSEMBLY v2 rides.
 tau_lev    := inf{ s >= 0 : E_eps(X_s) >= S_k + c_H }   [PX:7453].
 R_0        := {w_theta = k, w_phi = 0, E_eps <= S_k + c_H}
               [lane-lp-product-saddle-v1.md:216-218].
 O_eta      := {w_theta = k, w_phi = 0, E_eps < S_k + c_H + eta}, eta > 0.
 R_0^*      := the connected component of O_eta containing g*  [PX:9180].
 Door       := {E_eps = S_k + c_H, w_theta = k, w_phi = 0} [PX:6614, PX:7680].

O_eta IS OPEN: {w_theta = k} and {w_phi = 0} are unions of connected components
of the complements of the closed sets Delta_theta, Delta_phi (the labels are
"well defined and locally constant off Delta" [la3:55-56]), hence open;
{E_eps < S_k + c_H + eta} is open by continuity of E_eps.

STOPPING OBJECTS, NAMED. tau_lev is the hitting time of the CLOSED set
{E_eps >= S_k + c_H}; L is the exit time from the OPEN set Sec_k. For a
continuous adapted process both are (F_s)-stopping times by the elementary
closed-set / open-set argument ({tau_lev <= t} = {min_{s in [0,t]}
dist(X_s, {E_eps >= S_k + c_H}) = 0}, the minimum attained over a compact
interval by continuity) - NO debut theorem and NO augmentation are used. T' <= L
is a random time only; the lemma is PATHWISE on an event and needs nothing more.
X_{tau_lev} is F_{tau_lev}-measurable, which is the only measurability the
schedule's strong-Markov step at PX:7679-7684 (and its E2 analogue) requires.
NO INDEPENDENCE IS USED OR CLAIMED ANYWHERE IN THIS LEMMA.

STATEMENT. Fix eta > 0. For every start z in closure(S^+) and every random time
T' <= L,

     P_z-a.s. on { tau_lev < T' } :   X_{tau_lev} in Door inter R_0^*.

NO INJECTIVITY CONDITION AND NO CONDITION ON THE STANDING delta IS USED; see
STEP 0. In particular (TRAPOCC-UNIF)'s supremum over R_0^* may be evaluated at
the post-reach start X_{tau_lev}, and (T2) H-CONN is DISCHARGED at the instance
the schedule consumes.

PROOF.

STEP 0 (SEED: closure(S^+) subset R_0^*). AM-R5-21, verbatim: "CLOSURE ROW.
closure(S^+) = the CLOSED max-norm ball of radius / delta/2 about g* satisfies
closure(S^+) subset R_0; in particular / dS^+ subset R_0." [PX:10569-10571],
with the LABELS clause "hence the labels at x are / (k, 0)" [AM-R5-21(ii),
PX:10579-10587, the quoted phrase at PX:10586; the corpus cites this step as
":10559-10562" at PX:12574 and the row header as "(PX:10542-10569)" at PX:12459,
both ANCHOR DRIFT at HEAD - quoted TEXT verbatim, non-load-bearing,
resolve-at-HEAD]. The closed max-norm ball of radius delta/2 about g* in
T^{2N} is exactly the image, under the covering projection pi : R^{2N} ->
T^{2N}, of the closed max-norm box of radius delta/2 about any lift of g*
(this is the definition of the quotient max-norm metric: dist_max(pi(x), pi(y))
= min_{v in Z^{2N}} |x - y + v|_max). The box is convex, hence connected; pi is
continuous; so closure(S^+) is CONNECTED. CLASSICAL FACT NAMED: the continuous
image of a connected set is connected. HYPOTHESES CHECKED: the box is connected;
pi is continuous. NO INJECTIVITY IS USED - the projection need not be injective
on the box for its image to be connected. closure(S^+) contains its centre g*.
Since eta > 0 gives R_0 subset O_eta, closure(S^+) is a connected subset of
O_eta containing g*, so it lies in the g*-component:
     closure(S^+) subset R_0^* .                                        (SEED)
In particular z in R_0^* with labels (k, 0). (SEED) UPGRADES AM-R5-21's CLOSURE
ROW from R_0-membership to R_0^*-membership, at NO cost in hypotheses.

STEP 1 (THE OPEN SECTOR, ON THE CLOSED INTERVAL). Work on {tau_lev < T'}. Then
[0, tau_lev] subset [0, T'), and T' <= L, so for EVERY s in [0, tau_lev] - the
right endpoint INCLUDED - we have s < L, hence X_s in Sec_k, hence w_theta(X_s)
is defined and equal to k, hence X_s is not on Delta_theta. This is the ONLY use
made of the label semantics in this lemma, and it is used AT THE CLOSED
ENDPOINT, which is exactly where the touch-and-return reading fails.

BOUNDARY CASE, STATED EXPLICITLY (a path that touches Delta_theta exactly AT
tau_lev). If X_{tau_lev} in Delta_theta then X_{tau_lev} not in Sec_k, so
L <= tau_lev, so T' <= L <= tau_lev and the event {tau_lev < T'} DOES NOT OCCUR.
The boundary case is excluded BY THE EVENT, not by an added hypothesis, and
nothing is evaluated there: on {tau_lev >= T'} Lemma PE3p.3 already gives zero
outside-R_0 occupation for the round. Under the touch-and-return reading this
case is NOT excluded, and X_{tau_lev} would then lie in NO component of O_eta at
all, w_theta being undefined on Delta_theta - that is precisely the defect XE-4
finding 3 names.

STEP 2 (LEVEL CEILING, AND THE VALUE AT tau_lev). If tau_lev = 0 the conclusion
is (SEED) plus E_eps(X_0) = S_k + c_H (forced by the definition of tau_lev at
0), so assume tau_lev > 0. By definition of the infimum, E_eps(X_s) <
S_k + c_H for every 0 <= s < tau_lev. E_eps is smooth and s -> X_s continuous,
so E_eps(X_{tau_lev}) >= S_k + c_H (the hit set is closed) and <= S_k + c_H (left
approach); this is verbatim the landed step "continuity of E_eps o X gives
E_eps(X_{tau_lev}) = S_k + c_H" [PX:7542; also PX:6358]. Hence

     E_eps(X_s) <= S_k + c_H   for every s in [0, tau_lev].            (CEIL)

STEP 3 (w_phi IS CONSTANT = 0 ON [0, tau_lev]). Every point of Delta_phi carries
E_eps >= m_k + 2 lambda: "LEMMA B.1 (barrier).  `J_mu >= 2 mu` on `Delta`."
[la3-reader-packet-v1.md:355-356] gives J_lambda >= 2 lambda; "[STD]   sector
minimum: J >= m_k on the winding-k sector" [gate-v17-la2f-brief-lt-v1.md:54-55]
gives J_kappa >= m_k; and "`E_eps = E_0 + eps W*`, `W* >= 0`" [lane-lp:85-86] has
the correct sign - PE3p.3 case (c) verbatim [PX:7469-7477]. The concordant
crossing form is THE GATE ROW: "The w_phi = 0 stratum is DYNAMICALLY CLOSED at
band levels: crossing Delta_phi needs E_eps >= m_k + 2 lambda > m_k + 2 kappa >=
S_k + 4 c_H (c_H ledger, M2-PIN strict), above the band top."
[lane-lp-product-saddle-v1.md:651-653, quoted at PX:9156]. The chain, each
inequality with its direction and strictness displayed:

  E_eps(X_s) <= S_k + c_H      (CEIL)
             <  S_k + 4 c_H    STRICT, and this is the ONLY step needing c_H > 0:
                               the ACTIVE ledger branch c_H =
                               (m_k + 2 kappa - S_k)/4 [lane-lp:153-156; active
                               on all N >= 10, lane-prodexc-design-v1.md:297-300
                               per AM-R4-6, as at PX:7475-7477]
             =  m_k + 2 kappa  EQUALITY, the same ledger identity rearranged
             <  m_k + 2 lambda STRICT, by M2-PIN (lambda > kappa).

The chain is BETA-FREE and the margin at the ceiling is 3 c_H > 0: no 1/beta
term and no err(delta) term enters a pointwise level comparison. So no point of
Delta_phi is visited on [0, tau_lev]. Since w_phi is "well defined and locally
constant off Delta" [la3:55-56], s -> w_phi(X_s) is a locally constant function
on the CONNECTED interval [0, tau_lev], hence constant, hence equal to
w_phi(z) = 0 by (SEED). CLASSICAL FACT NAMED: a locally constant function on a
connected set is constant. HYPOTHESES CHECKED: the domain [0, tau_lev] is
connected; the composite is locally constant because the path avoids Delta_phi
there and w_phi is locally constant off Delta.

STEP 4 (CONNECTEDNESS, AND THE COMPONENT). Put K := { X_s : 0 <= s <= tau_lev }.
By STEPS 1-3,
     K subset {w_theta = k} inter {w_phi = 0} inter {E_eps <= S_k + c_H}
       =  R_0  subset  O_eta .
K is the image of the connected compact interval [0, tau_lev] under the
continuous map s -> X_s, hence CONNECTED (CLASSICAL FACT NAMED: continuous
images of connected sets are connected; HYPOTHESES: continuity of paths on M,
connectedness of [0, tau_lev]). K meets R_0^*, since z = X_0 in K by (SEED).
CLASSICAL FACT NAMED: if O is open, C is a connected component of O, K subset O
is connected and K inter C is nonempty, then K subset C - because K union C is
then connected in O and C is maximal connected in O. HYPOTHESES CHECKED: O_eta
open (above); K connected (just shown); K subset O_eta (just shown); K inter
R_0^* nonempty (SEED). Therefore

     K subset R_0^* ,  and in particular  X_{tau_lev} in R_0^* .

With STEP 2 (E_eps(X_{tau_lev}) = S_k + c_H) and STEPS 1, 3 (labels (k, 0)),
X_{tau_lev} in Door inter R_0^*.  QED.

REMARK (SCOPE). The proof uses only T' <= L and z in closure(S^+). Hence it
covers, without change: the dS^+ starts of the reach display; the closure(S)
starts of the assembled row (closure(S) subset closure(S^+), the max-norm balls

except for the single start property w_phi = w_theta - k = 0, which AM-R5-21(ii)
delivers on all of closure(S^+).
SCOPE IN THE LEVEL VARIABLE (pre-covering a re-routing). Let theta <= S_k + c_H
be any level and tau_theta := inf{ s >= 0 : E_eps(X_s) >= theta }. The identical
proof gives, on {tau_theta < T'}, X_{tau_theta} in {E_eps = theta} inter R_0^*:
STEP 1 applies verbatim to [0, tau_theta]; (CEIL) reads E_eps <= theta <=
S_k + c_H, which is ALL that STEP 3's chain consumes; STEPS 0 and 4 are
unchanged. In particular the theta_2 start of the superseded route is covered -
"TRAP_2 := { E_eps >= theta_2, w_phi = 0 }, theta_2 a Sard-regular value in
[S_k + c_H - 1/beta, S_k + c_H]" [PX:8993], so theta_2 <= S_k + c_H and
tau_2 <= tau_lev. Recorded so that a future re-anchoring of the consumed
instance to theta_2 needs no new lemma.

TYPED AFTER THIS CURE — exact strength, where it binds, and what it costs.

importing file's own definition already reads the way this cure reads it, so

1. RESIDUAL-XE4-3-SECTORENTRY (CONSUMER-SIDE; binds NO display in either lane).
   EXACT REQUIRED STRENGTH, for a consumer that needs the time of ENTRY into an
     open theta-sector different from Sec_k rather than the time of EXIT from
     Sec_k: either (a) for every z in Delta_theta reachable as X_L,
     P_z( inf{ t > 0 : X_t in an open theta-sector different from Sec_k } = 0 )
     = 1 — the process enters a different open sector immediately on hitting
     Delta_theta; or (b) an err-class bound on the expected touch-to-entry lag.
     (a) implies (b) with lag 0. L is the exit time from the OPEN set Sec_k,
     hence an (F_s)-stopping time for the continuous adapted X, the filtration
     being the completed right-continuous one of MM:3035; that is all the
     measurability a strong-Markov step at L would need.
   WHERE IT BINDS: NOWHERE IN THE TWO LANES. MM's register is closed and
     classified (33 occurrences of "tau_change" on 31 lines at HEAD): every one
     is a use of the object DEFINED at MM:2191 as the first EXIT, so no display
     in MM needs the entry property; and the PROD-EXCURSION DAG never needs it
     (its occupation bounds and floors are stated up to termini T' <= L, and the
     accounting interval only shrinks). It binds only a reader who wants to
     re-read MM's deliverable as an entry time.
   PRIOR ART, IN MM ITSELF, AND ITS SCOPE: MM:3726-3740 records that this exact
     event was already demanded of the corpus ("This is exactly the / \"event
     that the process ENTERS A DIFFERENT OPEN SECTOR after the touch\" the /
     obligation demands (verdict; COORDINATION [23]:408-415 post-gate
     transmission)") and discharges it there by construction — endpoint interior
     to the different sector by margin 5 delta/4, and "the codim-2 corner
     {u_1 = u_2 = 0} is POLAR for the nondegenerate diffusion (N >= 2)".
     SCOPE, TYPED HONESTLY: that is asserted for that constructed event and that
     corner set, in the relocate leg. It is NOT a general statement that
     Delta_theta is crossed immediately from every reachable touch point, and
     this cure does not read it as one. NOT READ BY THIS CURE: COORDINATION [23]
     and lane-ls:140-141 (the source MM:3391 cites for the first-exit definition
     of tau_change). The reading adopted rests on MM's OWN three sites (:2191,
     :3390-3391, :3744), not on either unread source.
   DEGRADATION IF (a) AND (b) BOTH FAIL: nothing in either lane moves. A reader
     wanting the entry time learns only that MM's bound controls the exit time,
     which is smaller.
   REGISTERED IN: MM at :3053 (BLOCK G-3, with the withdrawal) and :1243-1245
     (BLOCK G-5); PX in AM-R5-26(0) (BLOCK A) and at :8313-8317, :12307-12313,
     :12410, :12422, :12424, :12559 (BLOCKS B, C, J, D-1, D-2, M).

   clause — every doorway level theta <= S_k + c_H, including the theta_2

5. WITHDRAWN IN v2 AND STILL WITHDRAWN: "(H-BALL) delta < 2 inj(T^{2N})". NOT
   NEEDED. closure(S^+) is the image, under the covering projection, of a convex
   max-norm box (this is the definition of the quotient max-norm metric), and the
   continuous image of a connected set is connected whether or not the projection
   is injective there. LEMMA PE3p.3b and AM-R5-21's upgrade use NO injectivity
   condition and NO condition on the standing delta.

TYPED row, not a discharged one, and its conclusion is correspondingly
