STEP 0 (the branch the lead offered first, EXAMINED AND DECLINED).
MM:3321 asserts "from q in the sub-cap basin the first pass incurs no
off-R_0 term". If the first-pass positive-invariance argument genuinely
delivered zero off-R_0 time, the i = 0 first-pass window would need no
absorption at all and could be displayed outright. It does not deliver
it, for a reason visible in the file's own citation. MM:4244 verbatim
names the rows: "The sub-cap composed pass reaches S in one Phase-R
window at floor p_sub (M2-ATTR(k,eps) THEOREM on [0,eps_0) superset
[0,eps_2): Crit(E_eps) intersect closure(D_k(eps)) = G_k, positive
invariance, strict descent off G_k,
lane-m2-attractor-pinning-small-coupling-v1.md:157,220; then M2P.5 RELAX
into U_ch; then the M5 chain to B_{h/2}(g*)=S ...)". Three observations,
each checkable on that line alone.
  (a) The three M2-ATTR rows named - critical-set identification,
      positive invariance, strict descent off G_k - are statements about
      E_eps and its descent flow on closure(D_k(eps)). They are
      DETERMINISTIC-flow rows.
  (b) MM:4244 consumes them to floor a PROBABILITY: the composed pass
      reaches S "at floor p_sub". It does not consume them for an
      almost-sure confinement of the path to R_0. The transfer from flow
      to path is SH.2 max-norm tracking at a floor, with an err(delta)
      charge - a probability statement, not an a.s. one.
  (c) The superseding piece does not make the zero-term claim. R6b's live
      display MM:4246 KEEPS the summand T_row exp(-beta(c_H/2 -
      err(delta))). If R6b believed the first pass contributed no off-R_0
      time it would not have carried the summand forward.
  CONCLUSION: the "no off-R_0 term on the first pass" clause at MM:3321
  is NOT delivered by the M2-ATTR rows for the diffusion, and this cure
  does not display it. It is recorded as a superseded over-reading in N1.
  The typed re-pointing branch is taken instead. This is the honest
  disposition the lead's option (4) contemplates as the alternative.

CLAIM (DOM-0). Work at i = 0, on the sigma_0 scaffold of R6b S5, which is
MM:4244's own object: "Run the S3 scaffold from kappa_0 := 0, X_0 = q,
with success the first delayed S-return D(0) (route (r)) or a crossing
(route (x)); Phase A of subcycle 0 is empty." Exact stopping objects,
named:
   kappa_0 := 0, X_0 = q in D_k(eps);
   for m >= 1, kappa_m := the S3 subcycle epochs of that scaffold;
   alpha_m := inf{ s >= kappa_m : X_s in R_0 or w_theta(X_s) != k }
              (MM:4183's Phase-A endpoint, the S3 definition the
              scaffold is run with);
   L_0 := the route-(x) time of this scaffold, i.e. the first
          theta-label change after time 0 (the i = 0 instance of
          MM:4183's L_i; if MM's L_i carries a further clause, this
          object inherits it verbatim);
   D(0) = sigma_0 (MM:4244: "R5a S2 defines sigma_0 := D(0)");
   Y_0 := integral_0^{min(D(0), L_0)} 1_{M \ R_0}(X_s) ds, taken in
          [0, infinity].
Conditioning field: F_0 = F_{kappa_0}, the initial field of the augmented
right-continuous completed filtration (MM:3036 for the filtration; the
same construction at time 0).
Then, granting ONLY ROW SIGMA0-EXC (Part 3) at F_0 - and nothing else:
   (i)  E[ sum_{m >= 1} (alpha_m - kappa_m) | F_0 ] <= the SIGMA0-EXC
        bound, a.s.; i.e. the per-subcycle Phase-A windows of the sigma_0
        scaffold are ABSORBED into SIGMA0-EXC's single aggregate and
        require NO per-window instantiation of any row;
   (ii) Y_0 < infinity a.s. GIVEN SIGMA0-EXC - a conclusion this cure
        does NOT need and does NOT use; see the caveat below.
No conditioning on H_m = F_{alpha_m} or on F_{kappa_m} is used.

PROOF. Step 1' is Step 1 of (DOM) with the round window replaced by
[0, min(D(0), L_0)): each segment [kappa_m, alpha_m) lies entirely off
R_0 by the DEFINITION of alpha_m as a first entrance into
R_0 union {w_theta != k}; Phase A of subcycle 0 is empty (MM:4244); the
segments are pairwise disjoint and disjoint from Phases E and R and their
union is contained in the scaffold window; hence PATHWISE
   sum_{m >= 1} (alpha_m - kappa_m)  <=  Y_0.
Hypothesis rows, checked: the scaffold run at i = 0 is the S3 scaffold
(MM:4244 says so in those words), so its stopping-time row transfers with
its own anchor - MM:4199 verbatim: "Each alpha_m, beta_m, kappa_m, rho_i
is an F_t-stopping time"; 1_{M \ R_0} is Borel and X has continuous
paths, so Y_0 is a well-defined [0, infinity]-valued random variable;
Lebesgue additivity over a disjoint union of intervals is elementary. NO
independence is used and none is claimed.
Step 2' is NOT (DOM)'s Step 2 and does not cite the row. It cites ROW
SIGMA0-EXC at conditioning field F_0, start domain D_k(eps), index i = 0:
E[ Y_0 | F_0 ] <= the SIGMA0-EXC bound, a.s. That row is TYPED, NOT
discharged. Monotonicity of conditional expectation then gives (i).
Step 3' would be (DOM)'s CLASSICAL FACT applied to (Y_0, F_0), giving
(ii). IT IS DELIBERATELY NOT USED, see the caveat.

CAVEAT, stated so the two lemmas cannot be conflated. (DOM) derives an
UNCONDITIONAL a.s. finiteness at i >= 1, because its Step 2 cites a row
E2-ASSEMBLY discharges. (DOM-0) cannot: its Step 2' cites a typed row, so
any a.s. finiteness read off Step 3' would be CONDITIONAL on SIGMA0-EXC.
This cure does not read it off, and does not need to: the a.s. finiteness
of sigma_0 from arbitrary q is proved unconditionally and by a different
route at R5a S2, MM:3031 (Part 5 item 2, note N17). (DOM-0) is used for
GRANULARITY ONLY - to say that the per-window invocations at MM:3321 are
consequences of the single aggregate and instantiate nothing extra.

WHAT (DOM-0) DOES AND DOES NOT LICENSE.
  LICENSES: reading MM:3321's "any off-R_0 recovery ... and subsequent
  recoveries are bounded by the same aggregate" as an abbreviation for
  the pathwise domination above against SIGMA0-EXC's aggregate, with no
  per-window instantiation and no H_m or F_{kappa_m} conditioning.
  DOES NOT LICENSE: (a) any H_m-conditional or F_{kappa_m}-conditional
  off-R_0 bound at i = 0; (b) the zero-first-pass claim (Step 0); (c) any
  unconditional a.s. finiteness (that is MM:3031's, not this lemma's).

  [CURE-XE4-4 RATIONALE, WITH TWO POINTS THE v2 DRAFT GOT WRONG OR LEFT
  UNANCHORED. (a) THE PROVISO IS PART OF THE FACT. MM:3031's sentence
  carries "(given the process has not yet crossed)" and it is reproduced
  here verbatim rather than paraphrased away. It costs nothing at this
  site - a crossing terminates the scaffold by route (x), which is
  exactly the other branch of min(D(0), L_0) - but the house rule is
  verbatim citation, and a proviso silently dropped is how a fact gets
  strengthened by accident. (b) THE DOMAIN. MM:3031 proves a.s.
  finiteness "from anywhere in U"; R5a's own register restates it as
  "sigma_0 is A.S. finite from arbitrary q in U" (lane-minmig:3163). This
  site starts from q in D_k(eps). The file treats D_k(eps) as a certified
  basin lying INSIDE U, in two places, verbatim: lane-minmig:3371, "the
  out-of-basin residual (q in U outside the certified basin D_k(eps)) is
  honestly typed as not-claimed"; and lane-minmig:4253, "for q in U
  outside the certified basin the sub-cap RELAX leg is not licensed and
  E_q[sigma_0] is not claimed". Both sentences contrast q in D_k(eps)
  with q in U OUTSIDE it, which is well-formed only if D_k(eps) is a
  subset of U. THE INFERENCE IS NAMED, NOT ASSUMED: it is a reading of
  those two sentences, not a definitional containment, because this cure
  did not read the definitions of U and D_k(eps). IF A REVIEWER REFUSES
  THE READING, the fallback is exact and cheap: the containment becomes a
  one-line hypothesis row GAP-DK-U ("D_k(eps) subset U"), on which this
  re-pointing - and nothing else in this cure - depends; the re-typing of
  the second summand is untouched by it either way.]

  [0, infinity], where D(0) = sigma_0 and L_0 is this scaffold's route-(x)
  time. (1) Phase A of subcycle 0 is empty (this paragraph); for m >= 1,

     x -> d(z,x) is continuous, so its infimum over B equals its infimum over closure(B).
     Hence dist(z,P) = dist(z,S) >= 4/beta = 4 rho. QED
     WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CONSUME, STATED BECAUSE v1 GOT IT WRONG: it does not consume
     (v4c)'s dS^+ computation [PX:14495-14499]; it does not consume ANY norm convention
     (both dist(z,S) at [PX:9041] and the balls A_z, B_{2rho}(z) are stated in the same
     ambient metric of M); and it asserts NOTHING delta-universal. It is rho-class and it
     is TIGHT - PX:13644 records the landed reading of exactly this budget: "the
     'dist(z,S) >= 4/beta' clause gives dist(y,S) >= 2rho for y in B_{2rho}(z), which is
     exactly enough for the OPEN ball to miss S - tight, not slack."

(R3) P inter D_2 = empty. LANDED, TRAPOCC-4 row (ii) closing clause [PX:12803-12809]:
     "E_eps <= A_tube on the collar by (UP-QUAD) with A_tube < theta_2 - 1/beta for
     beta >= beta_*", and "Since D_2 = {E_eps >= theta_2} and A_tube < theta_2,
     S inter D_2 = empty. NOTHING ABOUT THE PLATE CHANGES." RE-READ AT closure(S): the
     (UP-QUAD) collar bound is stated on the max-norm collar S^+ = B^max_{delta/2}(g*)
     [PX:9777, PX:9911], which STRICTLY CONTAINS the closed max-norm ball closure(S) of
     radius delta/4. So E_eps <= A_tube < theta_2 on closure(S) and P inter D_2 = empty.
     HOLDS. (Only this row of Section 2 needed re-reading; it re-reads by enlarging
     nothing.)

(R4) Y inter P = empty with margin dist(Y,P) >= c_plate/(2G), for beta >= beta_plate :=
     2/c_plate. LANDED, (PLATE-SEP) [PX:13856-13858, PX:13867-13868]. HOLDS.

(R5) Y subset D_2. LANDED, (T4.3) containment [PX:12751-12755]: "TRAP_2^cl :=
     {E_eps >= theta_2} inter closure({w_phi = 0})" [PX:11456], so Y subset
     {E_eps >= theta_2} = D_2. THE TARGET'S LEVEL CLAUSE AND NOTHING ELSE; no property of
     the label factor and no regularity of Y is used. HOLDS.

(R6) THE WORKING ROW. For every y in the OPEN ball B_{2rho}(z) and every beta >= beta_W:
       B_{2rho}(y) subset B_{4rho}(z) subset W := M \ (D_2 u P).
     PROOF. If |x - y| < 2rho and |y - z| < 2rho then |x - z| < 4rho, which is the first
     containment. For the second: (i) P side - by (R2), every point of P is at distance
     >= 4rho from z, so no point of the OPEN ball B_{4rho}(z) lies in P; (ii) D_2 side -
     by (R1), dist(z,D_2) >= c_0/G, and 4rho = 4/beta <= c_0/G for beta >= 4G/c_0, so no
     point of B_{4rho}(z) lies in D_2. QED
     CONSEQUENCE: for every y in B_{2rho}(z), A_y = closed B_rho(y) subset B_{2rho}(y)
     subset W, so A_y, P, D_2 are PAIRWISE DISJOINT COMPACTS, and so are A_y, P, Y
     (Y subset D_2 by (R5)).
     BUDGET NOTE, DISPLAYED BECAUSE IT DECIDES SECTION 4: the P-side margin here is
     EXACTLY the landed 4rho and NOT ONE rho MORE. Section 4 therefore may NOT ask for
     B_{6rho}(y) subset W (which would need dist(z,P) >= 7rho); this is why the Harnack
     row is chained rather than enlarged.

THE COLLECTED beta-FREE THRESHOLD OF THE MAIN BRANCH:
  beta_W := max( beta_2(N,delta,eps), beta_env, beta_plate, 6G/c_0, 2/c_0 ),
with beta_env := max(4G/c_0, 2/c_0) [PX:12783] and beta_plate := 2/c_plate [PX:13798].
The entries 6G/c_0 and 2/c_0 are what Section 5A's admissibility line spends at A_y for
y in B_{2rho}(z); 4G/c_0 inside beta_env is what (R6) spends. NO delta-CLASS ENTRY APPEARS
IN THE MAIN BRANCH - v1's 12/delta is WITHDRAWN together with the (R2) it came from.
Every entry is beta-free.

--------------------------------------------------------
2B. THE NEAR-S BRANCH (CASE 2). The landed reduction, re-run in the weak frame.
--------------------------------------------------------
THE LANDED REDUCTION, VERBATIM:
  "NEAR-S CASE (removing dist(z,S) >= 4/beta). If z in S then H_S = 0 and the left side
   is 0. If 0 < dist(z,S) < 4/beta, replace S by S' := B_{delta/8}(g*) subset S:
   H_S <= H_{S'} so the occupation before H_S is dominated by the occupation before
   H_{S'}, and dist(z,S') >= delta/8 - 4/beta > 2/beta for beta >= beta_*. Every step
   above runs with S', and (CAP-LOW*) is unchanged in the exponent because sup_{S} E_eps
   and sup_{S'} E_eps differ by O(delta^2) inside the same err class. No exponent moves."
  [PX:9128]

(N1) THE SEPARATION, RE-DERIVED AT THE CLOSED SET. Let 0 < dist(z,S), so z is not in S,
     hence |z - g*|_max >= delta/4. S' is the max-norm ball of radius delta/8 about g*,
     so dist_max(z, S') >= delta/4 - delta/8 = delta/8, and dist(z,P') = dist(z,S') >=
     dist_max(z,S') >= delta/8 by the landed convention row "dist_euc >= dist_max"
     [(v4c), PX:14495-14499] together with dist(z, closure(B)) = dist(z,B).
     THIS IS THE ONE PLACE THIS PIECE CONSUMES A NORM CONVENTION, and it consumes it in
     the SAFE direction (a max-norm lower bound implies an ambient lower bound). It also
     inherits the landed injectivity clause under which lifted max-norm computations on
     T^{2N} are legitimate at delta scale [(G3), PX:9009]. TYPED at Section 10 (I4).
(N2) (R6) RE-RUNS at P': B_{4rho}(z) inter P' = empty as soon as 4rho <= delta/8, i.e.
     beta >= 32/delta. (R1),(R3),(R4),(R5) are unaffected or improve: P' subset P, so
     P' inter D_2 = empty and dist(Y,P') >= dist(Y,P).
     beta_W' := max( beta_W , 32/delta ). Beta-free.
(N3) THE CONSUMER DIRECTION IS CONSERVATIVE, IN BOTH READINGS.
     PROBABILISTIC: S' subset S gives H_{S'} >= H_S, so P_y(H_Y < H_S) <= P_y(H_Y < H_{S'}).
     VARIATIONAL: by (GRD-MON) of Section 6A, h_{Y,P} <= h_{Y,P'} q.e.
     So a bound of 1/2 proved for the S' object yields the bound for the S object.
(N4) THE EXPONENT ABSORBS AN ERR-CLASS TERM, AND v1's "NO CONSTANT INCREASES" IS
     RETRACTED HERE. The denominator object becomes cap(A_y, P') and the height becomes
     Theta(y,S'). The landed row asserts Theta-invariance inside err class - "(CAP-LOW*)
     is unchanged in the exponent because sup_{S} E_eps and sup_{S'} E_eps differ by
     O(delta^2) inside the same err class" [PX:9128] - which this piece CONSUMES AS A
     TYPED ROW (NEARS-ERR): Theta(y,S') <= Theta(y,S) + err_S, err_S beta-free of err
     class. It is asserted at PX:9128 as a sup-comparison, not proved as a communication-
     height inequality. Section 7's margin row then reads c_0 > eta + err_S in this branch.

========================================================
3. (RATIO-W) - THE WEAK THREE-SET RATIO   [UNCHANGED FROM v1]
========================================================

This section proves, for ARBITRARY pairwise disjoint compacts A, P, F in M, the weak
analogue of PE-DOORREACH Section 2's (RATIO) [PX:8394-8395]. It is the (SANDWICHw)
pattern: every surface term of the landed proof becomes a Riesz measure of (WFF-2), and
every normal-derivative comparison becomes a test of T against an admissible H^1 function.
IT IS STATED FOR ABSTRACT (A, P, F) SO THAT THE NEAR-S BRANCH RE-RUNS IT VERBATIM WITH
P' IN PLACE OF P.

STANDING INSTANCES. All four pairs below are pairs of DISJOINT COMPACTS, so (WFF-1) and
(WFF-2) apply verbatim with their landed hypothesis rows [PX:11559-11597]:
  (P1) (F, P):        H     := h_{F,P},     T_H     = e - e',
                      e >= 0 on F, e' >= 0 on P.
  (P2) (A, P u F):    h_A   := h_{A, P u F}, T_{h_A} = e_A - e_P - e_F,
                      e_A >= 0 on A, e_P >= 0 on P, e_F >= 0 on F.
  (P3) (A, F):        g     := h_{A,F},     T_g     = e_A^0 - e_F^0,
                      e_A^0 >= 0 on A, e_F^0 >= 0 on F.
  (P4) (F, A u P):    k     := h_{F, A u P}, T_k     = f_F - f_A - f_P,
                      f_F >= 0 on F, f_A >= 0 on A, f_P >= 0 on P.
THE POSITIVITY OF THESE MEASURES IS A PROBABILISTICALLY PROVED INPUT, NOT A VARIATIONAL
ONE - see Section 9A; it is landed at [PX:11576-11592] for arbitrary disjoint compacts.
THE THREE-SET SPLITS at (P2) and (P4) are the LANDED operation, not a new one: "For
h_z := h_{A_z, S u Y}: T_{h_z} = e_z - e_D - e_S with e_z >= 0 on A_z, e_D >= 0 on Y,
e_S >= 0 on S" [PX:11596-11597], licensed because the two components of the grounding set
are disjoint compacts - the checker's row "the three-set Riesz decomposition e_z - e_D -
e_S is legitimate since Y and S are disjoint compacts" [PX:11791], re-read at closure(S)
by CURE-XE4-2 v3 defect (D3) [PX:14603-14607].

TESTING ROW, NAMED ONCE. For each pair, T(f) = D(potential, f) = int f~ d(positive part)
- int f~ d(negative part) for EVERY f in H^1(M), f~ its quasi-continuous version.
HYPOTHESIS ROWS: the Riesz measures have finite energy integral and charge no set of zero
capacity, so they integrate quasi-continuous functions unambiguously - MET, (WFF-2)
closing clause [PX:11590-11592]; NAMED: Fukushima-Oshima-Takeda, Dirichlet Forms and
Symmetric Markov Processes, Ch. 2 (measures of finite energy integral). This is exactly
the operation the landed Section 4 already performs, e.g. "Take f = v_2 in (WFF-2) for h:
D(h, v_2) = int v_2 de - int v_2 de_S" [PX:11609-11610].

--------------------------------------------------------
(W0) NORMALISATION.
--------------------------------------------------------
Testing f = h_A in (P2): h_A = 1 q.e. on A, 0 q.e. on P u F, so
  D(h_A, h_A) = e_A(A),  i.e.  e_A(A) = cap(A, P u F)  by (WFF-1).
Testing f = 1 in (P2) (1 in H^1(M) since M is compact; grad 1 = 0):
  0 = D(h_A, 1) = e_A(A) - e_P(P) - e_F(F).                                 (W0-CONS)
[(W0-CONS) is (FLUX-CONSw) at this pair, the f = 1 case of (WFF-2) [PX:11615-11618].]
POSITIVITY OF THE NORMALISER: h_A = 1 q.e. on A and 0 q.e. on P, both of positive
mu-measure (mu has a smooth strictly positive density and both sets have positive Lebesgue
measure; a set of zero capacity is mu-null, FOT Ch. 2), so h_A is nonconstant and
cap(A, P u F) = D(h_A) > 0. Hence
  nu := e_A / e_A(A)
is a PROBABILITY measure, CARRIED BY THE COMPACT A (not by dA). The carrier is part of the
statement: this is the CARRIER-CHANGED label adopted at AM-R5-24(e) [PX:11836-11839].

--------------------------------------------------------
(W-FLUX) THE WEAK FLUX IDENTITY.   int_A H de_A = e_F(F).
--------------------------------------------------------
PROOF. Two tests and one symmetry, exactly the (EQ-OCC-2w)/(FLUX-ID'w) pattern.
 (a) Test f := H in (P2). H = 0 q.e. on P (the (WFF-1) constraint at (P1)) and H = 1
     q.e. on F (same). Hence
       D(h_A, H) = int H de_A - int H de_P - int H de_F = int_A H de_A - 0 - e_F(F).
 (b) Test f := h_A in (P1). h_A = 0 q.e. on P u F, so BOTH terms die:
       D(H, h_A) = int h_A de - int h_A de' = 0.
 (c) D is symmetric. Therefore int_A H de_A = e_F(F). QED
THIS IS the landed (FLUX-ID) "int_{dA} h de = Fl" [PX:8390] with its Green second identity
[PX:8388] deleted and its surface measures replaced by the Riesz measures of (WFF-2). NO
SURFACE INTEGRAL, NO NORMAL DERIVATIVE, NO SMOOTH BOUNDARY ON ANY OF A, P, F.

--------------------------------------------------------
(W-NUM) THE ABSORBED FLUX IS AT MOST THE TWO-SET CAPACITY.   e_F(F) <= cap(A,F).
--------------------------------------------------------
This is the weak replacement for the landed step (2b) [PX:8392], whose ONLY proof was
"the inward normal derivative of phi at dDoor' is >= 0".

(i) e_F^0(F) = cap(A,F). Test f = g in (P3): g = 1 q.e. on A, 0 q.e. on F, so
    D(g,g) = e_A^0(A), i.e. e_A^0(A) = cap(A,F) by (WFF-1). Test f = 1 in (P3):
    0 = e_A^0(A) - e_F^0(F). Hence e_F^0(F) = cap(A,F).
(ii) psi := g - h_A satisfies psi = 0 q.e. on A u F.
    g = 1 q.e. on A and h_A = 1 q.e. on A; g = 0 q.e. on F and h_A = 0 q.e. on F.
(iii) FOR EVERY f in H^1(M) WITH f = 0 q.e. ON A u F:   D(psi, f) = int f de_P, which is
    >= 0 if f >= 0. PROOF. T_psi = T_g - T_{h_A} = (e_A^0 - e_F^0) - (e_A - e_P - e_F).
    Every term other than e_P is carried by A or by F; the measures charge no set of zero
    capacity and f = 0 q.e. there, so those terms contribute 0. QED
(iv) psi >= 0 q.e. on M.  PROOF (weak minimum principle, the SAME one (SANDWICHw) step (2)
    uses [PX:11625-11627] and the internal checker certifies [PX:11793]). Write
    psi = psi^+ - psi^-. By the STAMPACCHIA TRUNCATION (NAMED: Gilbarg-Trudinger Lemma 7.6,
    weak derivative of the positive part; hypothesis rows: psi in W^{1,2} - MET) one has
    grad psi^+ = 1_{psi>0} grad psi and grad psi^- = -1_{psi<0} grad psi a.e., so
    <grad psi^+, grad psi^-> = 0 a.e. and D(psi^+, psi^-) = 0; hence
    D(psi, psi^-) = -D(psi^-, psi^-). Since psi = 0 q.e. on A u F, so is psi^-, and psi^-
    >= 0, so (iii) gives D(psi, psi^-) = int psi^- de_P >= 0. Therefore
    D(psi^-, psi^-) <= 0, hence = 0. Since w > 0 everywhere, grad psi^- = 0 a.e., so psi^-
    is a.e. constant on the CONNECTED manifold M, and its quasi-continuous version equals
    that constant q.e. That constant is 0 because psi^- = 0 q.e. on A and cap(A) > 0
    (A has nonempty interior, hence mu(A) > 0, and zero-capacity sets are mu-null).
    Hence psi^- = 0 q.e. and psi >= 0 q.e. QED
(v) D(psi, k) <= 0.  PROOF. Test f := psi in (P4): psi = 0 q.e. on F and on A, so the f_F
    and f_A terms vanish, leaving D(k, psi) = - int psi df_P <= 0, because psi >= 0 q.e.
    by (iv), f_P >= 0, and f_P charges no zero-capacity set. Symmetry of D gives
    D(psi, k) <= 0. QED
(vi) CONCLUSION. Test f := k in (P2) and in (P3). k = 0 q.e. on A u P and k = 1 q.e. on F,
    so D(h_A, k) = 0 - 0 - e_F(F) = -e_F(F) and D(g, k) = 0 - e_F^0(F) = -e_F^0(F).
    Subtracting, D(psi, k) = e_F(F) - e_F^0(F), and (v) gives
      e_F(F) <= e_F^0(F) = cap(A, F)     by (i).                              (W-NUM)
    QED

--------------------------------------------------------
(W-MON) THE DENOMINATOR MONOTONICITY.   cap(A, P u F) >= cap(A, P).
--------------------------------------------------------
LANDED ROW, RE-READ, NOT A NEW LEMMA. Machinery row 3 verbatim: "Purely variational;
enlarging the grounding set shrinks the admissible class, so the infimum can only rise.
No boundary smoothness enters the definition or the monotonicity." [PX:11711]; the same
instance is (M-ii) of CURE-XE4-2 v3 [PX:14662-14666]. HOLDS. THIS STEP IS GENUINELY
VARIATIONAL (Section 9A).

--------------------------------------------------------
(RATIO-W) THE WEAK THREE-SET RATIO.
--------------------------------------------------------
For pairwise disjoint compacts A, P, F in M, with H := h_{F,P} the (WFF-1) equilibrium
potential and nu := e_A/e_A(A) the (WFF-2) equilibrium probability measure of A against
P u F, carried by the COMPACT A:

  E_nu[H]  =  (int_A H de_A) / cap(A, P u F)          [(W0), (W-FLUX)]
           =  e_F(F) / cap(A, P u F)
          <=  cap(A, F) / cap(A, P u F)               [(W-NUM)]
          <=  cap(A, F) / cap(A, P).                  [(W-MON)]           (RATIO-W)

CONSUMED: (WFF-1) at four pairs of disjoint compacts; (WFF-2) at the same four pairs,
including its probabilistically proved positivity and the landed three-set split; the
finite-energy-measure testing row; symmetry of D; GT Lemma 7.6; connectivity of M;
positivity of cap(A). NOT CONSUMED: Green's first or second identity, any surface measure,
any normal or directional derivative, any exterior sphere or cone condition, any
C^0(closure) framing, any regularity of dA, dP or dF, any independence.

DIRECTION CHECK. Both inequalities point the conservative way: (W-NUM) raises the numerator
to a capacity that the ramp bounds above, and (W-MON) lowers the denominator to a capacity
that the tube bounds below. (RATIO-W) is therefore an UPPER bound on E_nu[H], which is what
the consumer needs.

RELATION TO THE LANDED DISPLAY. (RATIO-W) is PE-DOORREACH (2c)'s "(RATIO) E_nu[h] =
Fl / cap(A, S u Door') <= cap(A, Door') / cap(A, S)" [PX:8394-8395] with (a) the smooth-
boundary hypothesis row [PX:8385] DELETED, not weakened; (b) Fl := - int_{dDoor'} w
partial_n h_A dS replaced by the Riesz mass e_F(F); (c) nu carried by A instead of dA.
NO VALUE, NO CONSTANT AND NO EXPONENT DIFFERS IN THIS SECTION.

========================================================
4. (PTW-W) - HARNACK AT THE COMPACT CARRIER, AT THE LICENSED RADIUS
========================================================

INTERIOR SMOOTHNESS OF H ON THE BALL. On W = M \ (D_2 u P), T_H = 0 by (WFF-2)'s first
line, so H in H^1(M) is a weak solution of div(w grad H) = 0 there. By INTERIOR ELLIPTIC
REGULARITY (NAMED: Gilbarg-Trudinger Thm 8.10 with Cor 8.11; hypothesis rows: (i) uniform
ellipticity on compact subsets of W - MET, w smooth and bounded away from 0 on compact M;
(ii) C^inf coefficients - MET; (iii) H in W^{1,2}(W) - MET) H has a C^inf version on W,
and the quasi-continuous version agrees with it q.e. on W (two quasi-continuous functions
equal a.e. on an open set are equal q.e. there). By (R6), B_{2rho}(y) subset W for every
y in B_{2rho}(z) and beta >= beta_W. This is TRAPOCC-3 machinery row 13's pattern
[PX:11731] and the landed line "h is smooth in Omega by interior elliptic regularity"
[PX:8380].

--------------------------------------------------------
4A. WHY THE LANDED INSTANTIATION MUST BE CORRECTED, AND WHY IT CANNOT BE CORRECTED BY
    ENLARGING THE BALL.
--------------------------------------------------------
GT Thm 8.20 (Harnack) reads: for a nonnegative weak solution on a domain Omega and any
ball with B_{4R}(p) subset Omega, sup_{B_R(p)} u <= C inf_{B_R(p)} u with C = C(n,
Lambda/lambda, nu R). The landed rows [PX:9053, PX:12864-12867, and TRAPOCC-2's "(PTW*)
(GT Thm 8.20 Harnack on B_{3/2}, rows verbatim as in PE-TRAPOCC (4d))" PX:10126] apply it
at R = 3/2 with only B_2 available. That is over-radius: R = 3/2 requires B_6.
THE OBVIOUS REPAIR IS UNAVAILABLE. Requiring B_{6rho}(y) subset W for every y in
B_{2rho}(z) would force dist(z,P) >= 8rho, and requiring it only for y in A_z would force
dist(z,P) >= 7rho. THE LANDED STANDING SEPARATION IS EXACTLY 4rho [PX:9041] and the corpus
itself records that budget as "tight, not slack" [PX:13644]. So the radius cannot be bought;
it must be chained.

--------------------------------------------------------
4B. (PTW-W), CHAINED.
--------------------------------------------------------
(PTW-W) For every y in B_{2rho}(z) and every beta >= beta_W:   H(y) <= C_H'' inf_{A_y} H,
with C_H'' := C(n, e^{4G})^8, BETA-FREE.

PROOF. Rescale u(x) := H(y + rho x) for |x| < 2, rho = 1/beta. Then u is a nonnegative
weak solution on B_2 = B_2(0) of the DIVERGENCE-FORM equation div_x( w~ grad_x u ) = 0
with w~(x) := w(y + rho x), because B_{2rho}(y) subset W by (R6) and T_H = 0 there.
HYPOTHESIS ROWS OF GT Thm 8.20, CHECKED IN PLACE:
 (i) u >= 0 - MET: 0 <= H <= 1 q.e. by (WFF-1), and the C^inf version inherits it.
 (ii) UNIFORM ELLIPTICITY WITH BETA-FREE RATIO - MET: w = (1/beta) e^{-beta E_eps}, so on
      B_2 the oscillation of E_eps is at most G . (4 rho) = 4G/beta, whence
      Lambda/lambda = sup w~ / inf w~ <= exp( beta . 4G/beta ) = e^{4G}. BETA-FREE. The
      1/beta prefactor cancels in the ratio; this is the same cancellation the landed row
      records as "beta-free exactly because the equation is multiplied by beta".
 (iii) LOWER-ORDER COEFFICIENTS - MET trivially: in this form b = c = d = 0, so nu = 0 and
      C = C(n, e^{4G}). (The landed non-divergence reading - Delta u = <grad E_eps,
      grad u> with scale-invariant drift |b'| <= G, giving nu = G and nu R = G/4 - is also
      admissible inside GT Ch. 8's operator class; either reading yields a beta-free
      constant, and nothing below depends on which is taken.)
 (iv) THE RADIUS ROW - MET AT R = 1/4 AND ONLY THERE: for any p with |p| <= 1, every
      x in B_1(p) has |x| < |p| + 1 <= 2, so B_{4R}(p) = B_1(p) subset B_2. HENCE
        sup_{B_{1/4}(p)} u <= C inf_{B_{1/4}(p)} u,  C := C(n, e^{4G}),  for all |p| <= 1.
THE CHAIN. Fix x with |x| <= 1. Put p_i := (i/m) x, i = 0,...,m, with m := 8; then
|p_i| <= |x| <= 1 for every i, and |p_{i+1} - p_i| = |x|/8 <= 1/8 < 1/4, so p_i and
p_{i+1} both lie in B_{1/4}(p_i). Therefore u(p_i) <= sup_{B_{1/4}(p_i)} u <=
C inf_{B_{1/4}(p_i)} u <= C u(p_{i+1}) for each i, and composing the 8 links,
  u(0) <= C^8 u(x)   for every x with |x| <= 1.
Undoing the rescaling, H(y) <= C_H'' H(x) for every x in A_y = closed B_rho(y), i.e.
H(y) <= C_H'' inf_{A_y} H. Since nu_y - the (W0) probability measure of the triple
(A_y, P, D_2) - is a PROBABILITY measure carried by A_y,
  H(y) <= C_H'' inf_{A_y} H <= C_H'' int H dnu_y = C_H'' E_{nu_y}[H].  QED

WHAT MOVED AND WHAT DID NOT. The carrier change is already certified by the corpus's own
checker: "I checked (PTW*) still closes, since rescaled A_z = closed B_1 subset B_{3/2}
and GT 8.20 gives u(0) <= C_H' inf_{B_{3/2}} u <= C_H' u(y) for every y in B_1"
[PX:11773] - that certification is retained in its CONCLUSION and corrected in its
RADIUS. NO EXPONENT MOVES AND NO POWER OF beta MOVES. THE BETA-FREE CONSTANT INCREASES,
from C_H' to C_H'' = C(n,e^{4G})^8; this is displayed, not hidden, and it propagates only
into the beta-free threshold beta_2 at which Section 7's last line becomes <= 1/2. That is

========================================================
6. THE LATTICE MONOTONICITY LEMMA AND ITS TWO INSTANCES
========================================================

--------------------------------------------------------
6A. (LAT-MON) - ONE LEMMA, TWO INSTANCES, GENUINELY VARIATIONAL.
--------------------------------------------------------
(LAT-MON) Let Y1 subset Y2 be compacts and Q1 superset Q2 be compacts, with Y2 inter Q1 =
empty. Then h_{Y1,Q1} <= h_{Y2,Q2} q.e. on M.
PROOF. Put u := h_{Y1,Q1}, v := h_{Y2,Q2}, both given by (WFF-1) at pairs of disjoint
compacts, both satisfying 0 <= . <= 1 q.e.
 (a) u ^ v := min(u,v) is admissible for the pair (Y1,Q1): it lies in H^1(M); it equals 1
     q.e. on Y1 because u = 1 q.e. on Y1 and v = 1 q.e. on Y2 superset Y1; it equals 0
     q.e. on Q1 because u does and v >= 0.
 (b) u v v := max(u,v) is admissible for the pair (Y2,Q2): it equals 1 q.e. on Y2 because
     v does and u <= 1; it equals 0 q.e. on Q2 because v = 0 q.e. on Q2 and u = 0 q.e. on
     Q1 superset Q2.
 (c) By the STAMPACCHIA TRUNCATION (NAMED: Gilbarg-Trudinger Lemma 7.6; rows: u, v in
     W^{1,2} - MET), grad(u ^ v) = 1_{u<v} grad u + 1_{u>=v} grad v and grad(u v v) =
     1_{u>=v} grad u + 1_{u<v} grad v a.e., so pointwise a.e.
       |grad(u ^ v)|^2 + |grad(u v v)|^2 = |grad u|^2 + |grad v|^2,
     hence D(u ^ v) + D(u v v) = D(u) + D(v) = cap(Y1,Q1) + cap(Y2,Q2).
 (d) By (a),(b) and (WFF-1), D(u ^ v) >= cap(Y1,Q1) and D(u v v) >= cap(Y2,Q2). With (c)
     both are EQUALITIES, so u ^ v and u v v are minimisers of their respective problems.
 (e) UNIQUENESS OF THE (WFF-1) MINIMISER, checked in place rather than assumed: if f1, f2
     both minimise over the same admissible class, the parallelogram law gives
     D(f1 - f2) = 2D(f1) + 2D(f2) - 4D((f1+f2)/2) <= 0, so grad(f1 - f2) = 0 a.e.; M is
     connected and w > 0, so f1 - f2 is a.e. constant, and the constant is 0 because both
     equal 1 q.e. on a set of positive capacity. Hence u ^ v = u and u v v = v q.e., i.e.
     u <= v q.e. QED

INSTANCE (ENV-VAR), TARGET SIDE: Y1 = TRAP_2^cl subset D_2 = Y2 by (R5), Q1 = Q2 =
closure(S). Therefore
  h_pl := h_{TRAP_2^cl, closure(S)}  <=  H_2 := h_{D_2, closure(S)}   q.e. on M.  (ENV-VAR)
INSTANCE (GRD-MON), GROUND SIDE, USED ONLY IN THE NEAR-S BRANCH: Y1 = Y2 = TRAP_2^cl,
Q1 = closure(S) superset closure(S') = Q2. Therefore
  h_{TRAP_2^cl, closure(S)}  <=  h_{TRAP_2^cl, closure(S')}   q.e. on M.        (GRD-MON)
CONSUMES: (R5)'s level clause and nothing else about Y; no regularity of Y, D_2, S or S';
no probabilistic input. THIS LEMMA IS GENUINELY VARIATIONAL (Section 9A).

STEPS THAT ARE GENUINELY VARIATIONAL (no probabilistic input beyond the existence and

2. STEP A — THE STANDING FORM IS A REGULAR DIRICHLET FORM ON L^2(M, mu)
(UNCHANGED FROM v1; ATTACKED AND HELD)
========================================================

Landed inside (WFF-1) and quoted, not re-derived, verbatim: "HYPOTHESIS ROWS:
(D, H^1(M)) is a regular Dirichlet form on L^2(M, mu) - HOLDS (M compact
smooth; w = (1/beta) e^{-beta E_eps} smooth, bounded above and below away from
0; mu = e^{-beta E_eps} dx smooth strictly positive); the associated Hunt
process is the standing diffusion - HOLDS by ROW SR-PE1.2 reversibility
div(w grad u) = mu L u [proofs:1881-1885]" [PX:11566-11571]. DISPLAYED:

 (A1) CLOSED. w_min := (1/beta) e^{-beta max_M E_eps} > 0 and
   w_max := (1/beta) e^{-beta min_M E_eps} < infinity; the same two-sided bound
   holds for the density of mu, by compactness of M and smoothness of E_eps.
   Hence D_1(f,f) := D(f,f) + ||f||^2_{L^2(mu)} is equivalent to the standard
   H^1(M) norm, and (H^1(M), D_1) is complete. ROW: M compact, E_eps smooth -
   HOLDS.

 (A2) MARKOVIAN. For the normal contraction f -> (0 v f) ^ 1, |grad f#| <=
   |grad f| a.e. and f# in H^1(M), so D(f#) <= D(f). ROW: chain rule for Sobolev
   functions under Lipschitz maps, the map 1-Lipschitz and fixing 0 - HOLDS.

 (A3) REGULAR. Core C := C^inf(M), D_1-dense in H^1(M) (mollification on a
   compact smooth manifold) and uniformly dense in C(M) (Stone-Weierstrass);
   M compact so C_c(M) = C(M). ROWS: M compact smooth without boundary - HOLDS;
   w and the mu-density smooth and two-sidedly bounded - HOLDS by (A1).

 (A4) ASSOCIATED HUNT PROCESS = THE STANDING DIFFUSION. For u, f in C^inf(M),
   D(u,f) = -int_M (div(w grad u)) f dx = -int_M (L u) f dmu by ROW SR-PE1.2,
   so the L^2(mu)-generator of the form extends L on C^inf(M). The SDE has
   smooth coefficients on the compact M, hence a unique conservative strong
   solution from every start, defining a Feller diffusion with generator L
   (NAMED: Karatzas-Shreve Ch. 5 Thm 2.5, strong uniqueness; ROWS: Lipschitz
   coefficients - HOLDS, smooth on compact/periodic; the landed row at
   PX:17303-17309). Uniqueness of the mu-symmetric Hunt process properly
   associated with a regular Dirichlet form (NAMED: Fukushima-Oshima-Takeda,
   Dirichlet Forms and Symmetric Markov Processes, Ch. 4, Thm 4.2.8-class;
   ROWS: the form is regular - (A3); both processes are Hunt with the same
   generator on a core - HOLDS) gives the identification.

CONCLUSION (A). (D, H^1(M)) is a regular Dirichlet form on L^2(M, mu), and X is
its properly associated Hunt process.

3. STEP B — THE PART FORM ON G IS A REGULAR DIRICHLET FORM ON L^2(G, mu)
(UNCHANGED FROM v1 EXCEPT (B3), WHERE "LITERALLY" IS RETIRED)
========================================================

DEFINE F_G := { u in H^1(M) : u~ = 0 q.e. on M \ G } = { u in H^1(M) : u~ = 0
q.e. on closure(S) }, u~ the quasi-continuous version (which every element of
the form domain possesses, unique up to q.e.; NAMED: FOT Ch. 2 Thm 2.1.3-class;
ROWS: (D, H^1(M)) regular - (A3)). DEFINE E^G := D restricted to F_G x F_G.

 (B1) F_G IS D_1-CLOSED. If u_k -> u in D_1 with u_k in F_G, a subsequence of
   the quasi-continuous versions converges q.e. (NAMED: FOT Ch. 2 Thm
   2.1.4-class; ROWS: regular Dirichlet form - (A3)); the q.e. limit is 0 q.e.
   on closure(S). So u in F_G, and (F_G, D_1) is a Hilbert space.

 (B2) (E^G, F_G) IS THE PART OF (D, H^1(M)) ON THE OPEN SET G, AND IT IS A
   REGULAR DIRICHLET FORM ON L^2(G, mu|_G).
   NAMED: FOT Ch. 4 (part of a Dirichlet form on an open set; Thm 4.4.3-class:
   the part of a regular Dirichlet form on an open set is regular).
   HYPOTHESIS ROWS: (D, H^1(M)) regular Dirichlet form on L^2(M, mu) - HOLDS by
   (A); G an OPEN subset of M - HOLDS by construction, closure(S) closed.
   NO regularity of the boundary of G is required, and none is available: dG is
   the boundary of a max-norm cube, with faces, edges and corners. This is why
   the part-form route is the right one - it is the route that consumes no
   boundary regularity, in the same spirit as (WFF-2)'s "NO SURFACE INTEGRAL,
   NO NORMAL DERIVATIVE, NO SMOOTH dY" [PX:11592-11593] and (WFF-1)'s "NO
   boundary regularity of Y enters" [PX:11572].

 (B3) THE PART PROCESS IS THE KILLED PROCESS, AND THE DEBUT CONVENTION IS
   PINNED (LOW finding, repaired - v1's word "LITERALLY" is withdrawn).
   The part process X^G is X killed at tau_G := inf{ t >= 0 : X_t not in G }.
   Since M \ G = closure(S) = P,
     tau_G = inf{ t >= 0 : X_t in P } = H_P
   under the debut convention inf{t >= 0}, which is the convention this piece
   fixes and uses throughout. UNDER THE ALTERNATIVE CONVENTION inf{t > 0}
   (the one FOT standardly writes for the part-process exit time) the two
   quantities agree P_x-a.s. for every x, by (PLATE-REG)(g) - "every y in dS
   regular for S" [PX:14479] - and, for x in G, they agree PATHWISE for every

   H_P is an (F_t)-stopping time by the landed row [PX:11864-11866], P closed.
   NAMED: FOT Ch. 4 Thm 4.4.2-class (the Dirichlet form of the part process on
   an open set is the part form). HYPOTHESIS ROWS: (D, H^1(M)) regular with
   properly associated Hunt process X - (A); G open - HOLDS.

 (B4) THE HORIZON IS THE LANDED ONE. (PLATE-REG)(h4), landed verbatim:

 (C1) UNIFORM BOUND ON THE KILLING TIME. C_0 := sup_{x in M} E_x[H_S] <

5. STEP D — THE KILLED-RESOLVENT REPRESENTATION, AND THE q.e. IDENTITY
(UNCHANGED FROM v1; ATTACKED AND HELD)
========================================================

FORM SIDE (Riesz representation on the Hilbert space (F_G, D_1); no FOT needed).
For alpha > 0 and f in L^2(G, mu), (u,g) -> E^G(u,g) + alpha <u,g>_{L^2(mu)} is
a bounded coercive inner product on F_G, so there is a unique u = R_alpha^G f in
F_G with
  (RES-alpha)   E^G(u, g) + alpha <u, g>_mu = <f, g>_mu   for every g in F_G.
ROWS: (F_G, D_1) Hilbert - (B1); alpha > 0 gives coercivity - HOLDS.

PROBABILISTIC SIDE. NAMED: Fukushima-Oshima-Takeda Ch. 4 (Thm 4.4.2-class with
Thm 4.2.3-class): the resolvent of the part process,
  R_alpha^G f (x) = E_x[ int_0^{tau_G} e^{-alpha t} f(X_t) dt ],
is a QUASI-CONTINUOUS version of the L^2(G, mu)-resolvent of the part form; more
generally every alpha-excessive function of the properly associated Hunt process
lying in the form domain is quasi-continuous.
HYPOTHESIS ROWS: (E^G, F_G) regular Dirichlet form on L^2(G, mu|_G) - (B2); its
properly associated Hunt process is the part process X^G - (B3); X^G is X killed
at tau_G = H_P - (B3); f in L^2 inter L^infinity, f >= 0 - (C2) with f = 1_Y.
NO boundary regularity of G, NO smoothness of dS, NO connectivity of G, NO
independence claim.

 (D1) UNIFORM ENERGY BOUND. u_alpha := R_alpha^G 1_Y. Pathwise 0 <= u_alpha(x)
   <= u_0(x) <= C_0 by (C3). Taking g = u_alpha in (RES-alpha),
     E^G(u_alpha, u_alpha) + alpha ||u_alpha||^2_{L^2(mu)} = <1_Y, u_alpha>_mu
       <= C_0 mu(Y) < infinity,
   uniformly in alpha > 0; and ||u_alpha||^2_{L^2(mu)} <= C_0^2 mu(M) <
   infinity. So { u_alpha : 0 < alpha <= 1 } is bounded in (F_G, D_1).

 (D2) POINTWISE MONOTONE LIMIT. For each x, u_alpha(x) increases as alpha
   decreases and u_alpha(x) -> u_0(x) as alpha -> 0 by MONOTONE CONVERGENCE on
   int_0^{tau_G} e^{-alpha t} 1_Y dt (ROW: integrand nonnegative, increasing
   pointwise to 1_Y - HOLDS; integral finite by (C3)). Since 0 <= u_alpha <= C_0
   and mu(M) < infinity, DOMINATED CONVERGENCE gives u_alpha -> u_0 in L^2(M,mu).

 (D3) u_0 IS IN F_G AND SOLVES THE NEW-PAIR EQUATION. Take alpha_k -> 0. By (D1)
   the sequence (u_{alpha_k}) is bounded in (F_G, D_1); by BANACH-SAKS (ROW:
   bounded sequence in a Hilbert space - HOLDS) a subsequence has Cesaro means
   m_j converging STRONGLY in D_1 to some m in F_G. Each m_j is a finite convex
   combination of the u_{alpha_k}, hence converges pointwise everywhere to u_0
   by (D2). Therefore m = u_0 in L^2(M, mu), so u_0 in F_G.
   Fix g in F_G. By (RES-alpha), E^G(u_{alpha_k}, g) = <1_Y, g>_mu
   - alpha_k <u_{alpha_k}, g>_mu with |alpha_k <u_{alpha_k}, g>_mu| <=
   alpha_k C_0 ||g||_{L^1(mu)} -> 0, so E^G(u_{alpha_k}, g) -> <1_Y, g>_mu, and
   so do the Cesaro means; by D_1-strong convergence E^G(m_j, g) -> E^G(u_0, g).
   Hence
     E^G(u_0, g) = int_M g 1_Y dmu   for every g in F_G,   u_0~ = 0 q.e. on P.
   That is EXACTLY the re-pointed (WFF-3).

 (D4) UNIQUENESS AT THE NEW PAIR, DISPLAYED. If u, u' in F_G both satisfy (D3),
   then D(u - u', g) = 0 for every g in F_G; take g = u - u': D(u - u') = 0, so
   grad(u - u') = 0 a.e., and M = T^{2N} is CONNECTED, so u - u' = c a.e. for a
   constant c. Constants are continuous hence quasi-continuous, so the
   quasi-continuous version of u - u' equals c q.e.; it is 0 q.e. on closure(S),
   and Cap(closure(S)) > 0 because closure(S) contains the nonempty open S
   (Lemma POLAR-OPEN, (E0)). Hence c = 0. QED

 (D5) THE q.e. IDENTITY. By (D3)+(D4), u_0 IS the (WFF-3)-at-the-new-pair
   solution: v_2^new = u_0 as elements of F_G. That the POINTWISE-DEFINED u_0 is
   itself a quasi-continuous version: each u_{alpha_k} is quasi-continuous (the
   FOT row above), hence so is each Cesaro mean m_j; by FOT Ch. 2 Thm
   2.1.4-class, D_1-convergence m_j -> u_0 gives a subsequence converging q.e.
   to a quasi-continuous version of u_0, and the m_j converge POINTWISE
   EVERYWHERE to u_0 by (D2). Hence u_0 is quasi-continuous and
     v_2^new~ = u_0   q.e. on M.
   (ALTERNATIVE ROUTE, recorded, not executed: u_0 is 0-excessive for X^G and
   finite, and a finite excessive function in the form domain is
   quasi-continuous, FOT Ch. 4 Thm 4.2.3-class.)

 (D6) CONCLUSION OF STEP D:
     v_2^new(x) = E_x[ int_0^{H_{closure(S)}} 1_Y(X_t) dt ]   for q.e. x in M.
   This is verbatim the display XE-5 named as missing.

--------------------------------------------------------
(E0) POLAR SETS ARE LEBESGUE-NULL — DISPLAYED
--------------------------------------------------------
LEMMA (POLAR-OPEN). If N subset M has Cap(N) = 0 then mu(N) = 0 and Leb(N) = 0.
Consequently no set of zero capacity contains a nonempty open set, and
Cap(U) > 0 for every nonempty open U subset M.
PROOF. Let Cap(N) = 0. Choose open O_j superset N with Cap(O_j) -> 0 and let e_j
be the equilibrium potentials of the O_j (NAMED: FOT Ch. 2 Thm 2.1.1-class -
existence and uniqueness of the equilibrium potential of an open set, with
e_j in H^1(M), e_j >= 1 a.e. on O_j and Cap(O_j) = D_1(e_j, e_j); ROWS: regular
Dirichlet form - (A3). This is the row v1 used without naming; named now).
Then
  mu(O_j) <= int_{O_j} e_j^2 dmu <= ||e_j||^2_{L^2(mu)} <= D_1(e_j, e_j)
          =  Cap(O_j) -> 0,
so mu(N) = 0. THE ONE-LINE IMPLICATION TO LEBESGUE, DISPLAYED: mu =
e^{-beta E_eps} dx with e^{-beta E_eps} >= e^{-beta max_M E_eps} > 0 continuous
on the compact M, so
  Leb(N) <= e^{beta max_M E_eps} * mu(N) = 0.
Conversely mu(U) > 0 for every nonempty open U (continuous strictly positive
density), whence Cap(U) > 0. QED
NOTE ON STRENGTH: this is the standard "polar sets have empty interior" fact,
proved here in EVERY dimension for this form because mu is equivalent to
Lebesgue measure on M; no dimension hypothesis is imported. THIS IS THE HONEST
ROUTE CHOSEN: the implication runs through the form's own capacity-vs-measure
inequality, NOT through an asserted Cap >= c Leb bound on compacts.

COROLLARY (A.E. EQUALITY OF THE TWO OBJECTS).
  u_0 = v_2^new~   q.e. on M   by (D5),
hence, the exceptional set being polar and therefore Lebesgue-null by
POLAR-OPEN,
  u_0 = v_2^new~   LEBESGUE-a.e. on M.                                 (AE-EQ)
(AE-EQ) IS THE ONLY OUTPUT OF STEPS A-D THAT SECTION 6 CONSUMES.

--------------------------------------------------------
(E1) THE VARIATIONAL SIDE IS CONTINUOUS ON G — INTERIOR De Giorgi-Nash-Moser
--------------------------------------------------------
(This repairs the MODERATE finding: v1 named GT Thm 9.15, which is a GLOBAL
Dirichlet-problem theorem for STRONG solutions on a C^{1,1} domain, has no
interior form, and presupposes W^{2,p} regularity that a merely-H^1 weak
solution does not have. It is NOT the right row and is NOT used.)

THE WEAK FORMULATION, DISPLAYED. For f in C_c^infinity(G) we have f in H^1(M)
and f = 0 on a neighbourhood of closure(S), hence f = 0 q.e. on closure(S),
hence f in F_G. So (D3) gives
  int_G w <grad v_2^new, grad f> dx = int_G f 1_Y e^{-beta E_eps} dx
for every f in C_c^infinity(G), i.e. v_2^new restricted to G is a W^{1,2}(G)
WEAK SOLUTION of the DIVERGENCE-FORM equation
  D_i ( a^{ij} D_j v ) = g   in G,   a^{ij} := w delta^{ij},
                                     g := - 1_Y e^{-beta E_eps}.

NAMED: Gilbarg-Trudinger Thm 8.22 (Ch. 8, local Holder continuity of weak
solutions; De Giorgi-Nash-Moser).
HYPOTHESIS ROWS, CHECKED IN PLACE:
 (i)   Operator in DIVERGENCE FORM with bounded measurable coefficients:
       a^{ij} = w delta^{ij}, and b = c = d = 0 - MET (w is in fact smooth on
       the compact M).
 (ii)  UNIFORM ELLIPTICITY: w_min |xi|^2 <= w |xi|^2 <= w_max |xi|^2 with
       0 < w_min <= w_max < infinity - MET by (A1). (Bookkeeping disclosure:
       the corpus records the constant diffusion matrix as "(2/beta) I"
       [PX:4944] in one place and "(1/beta) Id" [PX:12851] in another; these are
       normalisation conventions of the same nondegenerate constant matrix, and
       ONLY uniform ellipticity is consumed here, so nothing in this row turns
       on which convention is adopted.)
 (iii) u in W^{1,2}(G) - MET: v_2^new in H^1(M), restricted to G.
 (iv)  RIGHT-HAND SIDE in the required integrability class: g in L^infinity(M)
       since 0 <= 1_Y <= 1 and e^{-beta E_eps} is bounded on the compact M -
       MET by (C2) and (A1); the L^{q/2}, q > n condition of GT Thm 8.22 is met
       a fortiori on the finite-measure M; and f^i = 0.
 (v)   INTERIOR STATEMENT ONLY: the conclusion is local Holder continuity in G.
       NO boundary datum, NO domain regularity, NO exterior sphere or cone
       condition, NO C^{1,1} domain, NO strong-solution hypothesis. So NOTHING
       is asked of dG (the max-norm cube, with faces, edges and corners) and
       nothing of dY.
CONCLUSION (E1). v_2^new has a version v~ in C^{0,alpha}_loc(G); in particular
v~ is CONTINUOUS at every point of G and BOUNDED on every compact subset of G.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT CLAIMED. No W^{2,p}_loc and no C^{1,alpha}_loc
statement is made or needed. In particular the landed sentence "interior
W^{2,p}_loc regularity for L v_2 = -1_{TRAP_2^cl} with L^infinity source holds
across the target boundary on all of M\S, and route (b) uses no boundary trace
of v_2" [PX:11760] is NOT consumed: this piece consumes strictly less.

(E2) THE PROBABILISTIC SIDE IS THE LANDED v_2 — HORIZON AND SOURCE ONLY
--------------------------------------------------------
NO CONTINUITY OF THE PROBABILISTIC SIDE IS ASSERTED HERE. Two identifications
only, both landed:
 (i) HORIZON. By (PLATE-REG)(h4) [PX:14264-14265], H_P = H_S P_x-a.s. for EVERY
   x, so u_0(x) = E_x[ int_0^{H_S} 1_Y(X_t) dt ] for every x in M.
 (ii) SOURCE. (T3-ID) is landed, verbatim "By (T3-ID) the source
   1_{TRAP_2^cl} = 1_{TRAP_2} Lebesgue-a.e." [PX:11731], i.e. the symmetric
   difference N := Y triangle TRAP_2 is Lebesgue-null. The occupation time of a

   by Tonelli E_x[ int_0^T 1_{Delta_phi}(X_s) ds ] = int_0^T P_x(X_s in
   Delta_phi) ds = 0 for every x, T" [PX:4945-4948], with the NAMED IMPORT
   "existence of a Lebesgue transition density for a uniformly elliptic
   diffusion with smooth bounded coefficients on a compact manifold (Friedman,
   Stochastic Differential Equations and Applications, Ch. 6; hypothesis rows:
   M compact and smooth - HOLDS [lane-minmig:1345]; diffusion coefficient
   constant and nondegenerate, = (2/beta) I - HOLDS [same line]; drift smooth,

   corpus's own row register as SR-DENS [PX:7230-7234]. Applying it with N in
   place of Delta_phi and letting T increase (monotone convergence; H_S <
   infinity P_x-a.s. by (C1)) gives E_x[int_0^{H_S} 1_N(X_s) ds] = 0. THEREFORE
     u_0(x) = E_x[ int_0^{H_S} 1_{TRAP_2}(X_t) dt ] = v_2^prob(x)
   for EVERY x in M. (This upgrades the landed a.e.-level sentence at PX:11731,
   stated for the PDE source, to the pathwise occupation functional - the object
   the probabilistic side actually integrates.)
COMBINING (E2) WITH (AE-EQ):
  v_2^prob = v~   LEBESGUE-a.e. on G.                                  (AE-G)

--------------------------------------------------------
(E3) THE SMALL-TIME MEAN-VALUE IDENTITY
--------------------------------------------------------
CLAIM. For every z in M and every t > 0,
  v_2^prob(z) = E_z[ int_0^{t ^ H_P} 1_Y(X_s) ds ] + E_z[ 1_{t < H_P}
                v_2^prob(X_t) ].                                       (MV-t)

PROOF. Work with u_0 = v_2^prob (equal everywhere by (E2)).
 (a) PATH DECOMPOSITION. int_0^{H_P} 1_Y(X_s) ds = int_0^{t ^ H_P} 1_Y(X_s) ds
   + 1_{t < H_P} int_t^{H_P} 1_Y(X_s) ds.
 (b) SHIFT IDENTITY, DISPLAYED. On { H_P > t }: H_P(X) > t means X_s not in P
   for all s in [0,t]; hence inf{ s >= 0 : X_{t+s} in P } = inf{ u >= t :
   X_u in P } - t = H_P - t, i.e. H_P = t + H_P o theta_t on { H_P > t }.
   Consequently 1_{t<H_P} int_t^{H_P} 1_Y(X_s) ds = 1_{t<H_P} ( F o theta_t ),
   where F(X) := int_0^{H_P(X)} 1_Y(X_s) ds.
 (c) MARKOV PROPERTY AT A DETERMINISTIC TIME. NAMED: the simple Markov property
   of X at the deterministic time t with sigma-field F_t:
     E_z[ F o theta_t | F_t ] = E_{X_t}[ F ]   P_z-a.s.
   HYPOTHESIS ROWS: X is the Hunt/Feller diffusion properly associated with the
   form, with the usual-augmented filtration (F_t) - MET by (A4) and the landed
   row "(F_t) the usual augmentation (right-continuous, P-complete)"
   [PX:11864-11865]; F is a NONNEGATIVE measurable functional on path space -
   MET (H_P is the debut of a closed set for a continuous path, hence a
   measurable path functional; the statement extends from bounded to nonnegative
   F by monotone convergence); { t < H_P } is in F_t - MET, H_P being an
   (F_t)-stopping time by [PX:11865-11866]. NO STRONG MARKOV PROPERTY IS USED.
   NO INDEPENDENCE IS CLAIMED. No conditioning at a random time occurs.
 (d) Taking E_z of (a), using (b) and (c) on the second term, and E_{X_t}[F] =
   u_0(X_t) with 0 <= u_0 <= C_0 by (C3), gives (MV-t). QED

REMARK. (MV-t) is the elementary dynamic-programming identity for the killed
occupation functional. It introduces no new object and no new threshold.

--------------------------------------------------------
(E4) THE LIMIT t -> 0 AT A START OFF THE PLATE
--------------------------------------------------------
FIX z in G. THE CONSUMED START SETS ARE OFF THE PLATE - stated here and
established exhaustively at (E6): every start at which a consumed display
evaluates a VARIATIONAL object pointwise lies in G, and the corpus's own
sentence "the flux route is only ever run at z in M \ closure(S)"
[PX:14493-14494] is the exhaustiveness clause.

CHOOSE r > 0 with the CLOSED ball B_r(z) contained in G (possible, G open).
Let K := sup_{B_r(z)} |v~| < infinity by (E1) (continuity on a compact set).
Let tau_r := inf{ t >= 0 : X_t not in the open ball B_r(z) }, the hitting time
of the CLOSED set M \ B_r(z), an (F_t)-stopping time by [PX:11865-11866].
PATHWISE FACTS, from continuity of paths and X_0 = z:
  tau_r > 0 for every path (z is interior to the ball);
  H_P > 0 for every path (P is closed and z is not in P).
Hence H_P ^ tau_r > 0 PATHWISE, so 1_{ t < H_P ^ tau_r } -> 1 as t decreases to
0, for every path. In particular P_z(t < H_P) -> 1.

NOW TAKE t -> 0 IN (MV-t), TERM BY TERM.

 TERM 1. 0 <= E_z[ int_0^{t ^ H_P} 1_Y(X_s) ds ] <= t -> 0.

 TERM 2, SPLIT AT tau_r.
   E_z[1_{t<H_P} u_0(X_t)] = E_z[1_{t < H_P ^ tau_r} u_0(X_t)]
                            + E_z[1_{t<H_P, t >= tau_r} u_0(X_t)].
  (2b) THE REMAINDER VANISHES: | E_z[1_{t<H_P, t>=tau_r} u_0(X_t)] | <=
    C_0 P_z(tau_r <= t) -> 0 as t decreases to 0, since the events
    { tau_r <= t } decrease to { tau_r = 0 }, which is empty pathwise.
  (2a) THE MAIN TERM: REPLACE u_0 BY v~ AT ZERO COST. On { t < tau_r } one has
    X_t in B_r(z) contained in G, so v~(X_t) is defined. The replacement error is
      | E_z[ 1_{t<H_P^tau_r} ( u_0 - v~ )(X_t) ] |
        <= E_z[ 1_{X_t in B_r(z)} | u_0 - v~ |(X_t) ]
        =  int_{B_r(z)} | u_0 - v~ |(y) p_t(z, y) dy
        =  0,
    where the middle equality is the LANDED transition-density row SR-DENS
    [PX:7230-7234] - "existence of a transition density p_t(x, .) w.r.t.
    Lebesgue for t > 0 for the nondegenerate diffusion" - applied at the fixed
    t > 0, and the last equality holds because u_0 = v~ Lebesgue-a.e. on G by
    (AE-G) while |u_0 - v~| <= C_0 + K is bounded on B_r(z) and p_t(z, .) is a
    probability density. THIS IS THE WHOLE MECHANISM OF THE UPGRADE: the law of
    X_t is absolutely continuous, so the value of the integrand may be changed
    on any Lebesgue-null set - in particular u_0 may be replaced by ITS
    CONTINUOUS VARIATIONAL REPRESENTATIVE. Nothing about the PDE satisfied by
    u_0 is used, and nothing about continuity of u_0 is used.
    THEN, BOUNDED CONVERGENCE: 1_{t<H_P^tau_r} v~(X_t) is bounded in absolute
    value by K (on { t < tau_r }, X_t lies in B_r(z)); it converges P_z-a.s. to
    v~(z), because X_t -> X_0 = z by path continuity, v~ is continuous at z by
    (E1), and 1_{t<H_P^tau_r} -> 1 pathwise. Hence
      E_z[ 1_{t<H_P^tau_r} v~(X_t) ] -> v~(z).
    ROWS FOR BOUNDED CONVERGENCE: dominating constant K - MET; a.s. pointwise
    convergence - MET as displayed.

CONCLUSION (E4). The left side of (MV-t) does not depend on t. Letting t
decrease to 0:
    v_2^prob(z) = 0 + v~(z),   i.e.   v_2^prob(z) = v~(z).

(V2ID) IDENTIFICATION OF THE NEW-PAIR OCCUPATION POTENTIAL
--------------------------------------------------------
Let G := M \ closure(S), P := closure(S), Y = TRAP_2^cl, and let v_2^new be the
unique solution of (WFF-3) at the new pair, i.e. the unique v in H^1(M) with
v = 0 q.e. on closure(S) and D(v, f) = int_M f 1_Y dmu for every f in H^1(M)
with f = 0 q.e. on closure(S). Assume the landed standing threshold
beta >= beta_S4 := max(2/c_plate, 8/delta) [PX:13984-13986]. Then:

  (a)  v_2^new(x) = E_x[ int_0^{H_{closure(S)}} 1_Y(X_t) dt ]
                  = E_x[ int_0^{H_S} 1_{TRAP_2}(X_t) dt ]
                  = v_2^prob(x)                                for q.e. x in M;

  (b)  the SAME identity holds at EVERY point x of the open set G, with
       v_2^new read as its C^{0,alpha}_loc(G) version v~;

  (c)  for x in closure(S): v_2^prob(x) = 0 pointwise by (PLATE-REG)(g), and
       v_2^new~ = 0 q.e. on closure(S) by membership in F_G. NO pointwise
       identity on closure(S) is claimed, and by (E6)(iii) none is consumed.

PROOF. Step A -> Step B -> Step C -> Step D gives (a). (E0) converts (a) to
Lebesgue-a.e. equality; (E1) gives the continuous variational representative on
G by interior De Giorgi-Nash-Moser; (E2) identifies the probabilistic side
pointwise everywhere with the landed v_2; (E3) is the small-time mean-value
identity from the Markov property at a deterministic time; (E4) takes t -> 0
using SR-DENS to replace the integrand by v~ at zero cost, and bounded
convergence. That gives (b). (c) is (v4b) plus F_G-membership. QED

STRENGTH DELIVERED vs STRENGTH DEMANDED.
  XE-5 demanded: "equality of quasi-continuous representatives via the q.e.
  killed-resolvent representation, plus the pointwise/continuity upgrade on
  consumed start sets." DELIVERED: (a) is the first; (b) + (E6) the second.

  [PX:17290-17292] is CORRECTED: a.e. equality is insufficient for the

f with f = 1 on A_z, f = 0 on S, (int <J, grad f>)^2 = 1 <= En(J) D(f) with
En(J) := int |J|^2/w, so cap(A_z,S) >= 1/En(J)." [PX:9067]

PRINCIPLE FOR COMPACTS. For disjoint compacts Y, Y' the class K(Y,Y') := {f in
H^1(M): f = 1 q.e. on Y, f = 0 q.e. on Y'} is nonempty, convex and closed in
H^1(M); D is coercive on it; the unique minimizer h_{Y,Y'} satisfies
0 <= h <= 1 (truncation lowers D) and cap(Y,Y') = D(h_{Y,Y'}) - which is the
corpus's OWN definition "cap(Y,Y') = inf{D(f): f=1 on Y, f=0 on Y'}"
[proofs:10008], so no object is redefined." [PX:11559-11564]; and
"cap_pl( A ; F ) := cap( A, closure(S) u F ),   cap_pl(A) := cap_pl( A ; empty )
= cap( A, closure(S) ), the (WFF-1) variational capacity at the new grounding
set" [PX:14315-14317].

THE DIRECTION FAILURE, STATED ONCE. Write
  Lip(A,B) := { g : M -> R Lipschitz, g = 1 pointwise on A, g = 0 pointwise on B },
  K(A,B)   := { f in H^1(M) : f~ = 1 q.e. on A, f~ = 0 q.e. on B }.
Lip(A,B) subset K(A,B) (a continuous function is its own quasi-continuous
version; pointwise equality on a set is a fortiori q.e. equality on it). The
landed display proves
  D(g) >= 1/En(J)   for every g in Lip(A_z, S),
i.e. inf over the SMALLER class is >= 1/En(J). The consumer needs
  inf over K(A_z, closure(S)) >= 1/En(J),
an infimum over a LARGER class, which is <= the infimum over the smaller class.
A lower bound proved on a subclass does NOT propagate to a superclass. This is
the whole defect and it is not repaired by either landed route:
  ROUTE A [PX:14431-14440] asserted that every f admissible at the new pair "is
  admissible at the old pair"; that inclusion is between the two q.e. classes,

  "ROUTE A's class inclusion is WITHDRAWN; ROUTE B (typed comparison) is the
  operative route, per the checker" [PX:17293-17294].
  ROUTE B [PX:14442-14443], "by (M-i), cap_pl(A_z) >= cap(A_z, S) >= LB(beta)
  via (DIR-1)": the first inequality is a correct monotonicity step (shrinking

  landed Lipschitz-class bound read against the SAME H^1/q.e. infimum. ROUTE B
  relocates the defect; it does not remove it.
THIS PIECE DOES NOT RESURRECT ROUTE A. It proves a DENSITY statement, which is a
different and correct assertion: every K-competitor is approximated in energy
from WITHIN Lip, with the constraints preserved.

ROW-CAP (DEFINITION, NOT AN IMPORT). Cap denotes the 1-capacity of the form
ROW-REG names:
  for O open,   Cap(O) := inf{ E_1(u,u) : u in H^1(M), u >= 1 a.e. on O },
  for E subset M, Cap(E) := inf{ Cap(O) : O open, E subset O }.
"q.e." means outside a set of Cap zero; "quasi-continuous" means: for every
b > 0 there is an OPEN O with Cap(O) < b such that the restriction to M \ O is
continuous. This is the SAME capacity the corpus's own (WFF-1) row means by
"q.e." at [PX:11559-11564], and it is the capacity of the chapter already
imported at [PX:11565-11567]. Outer regularity of Cap is DEFINITIONAL in the
second line, not an imported theorem.

    (N8-iv) and is proved inline. THE GENERAL FACT IS TRUE AND STANDARD; IT IS
    STILL NOT IMPORTED, BECAUSE IT IS NOT NEEDED.

(N1) EXISTENCE AND q.e.-UNIQUENESS OF QUASI-CONTINUOUS VERSIONS. [IMP-1]
Every u in H^1(M) admits a quasi-continuous version u~ (in particular u~ = u
a.e.), and any two quasi-continuous versions of the same element of H^1(M)
agree q.e.
NAMED: Fukushima-Oshima-Takeda, Dirichlet Forms and Symmetric Markov Processes,
Ch. 2, §2.1 (quasi-continuity for regular Dirichlet forms; Theorem 2.1.3-class
existence statement and the accompanying q.e.-uniqueness statement).
HYPOTHESIS ROWS: (D, H^1(M)) regular Dirichlet form on L^2(M,mu) — MET by
ROW-REG; u in the form domain — MET by hypothesis; the capacity with respect to
which "q.e." is read is the form's 1-capacity — MET by ROW-CAP, which is the
same object the corpus's (WFF-1) row already reads "q.e." against
[PX:11559-11564].
THE UNIQUENESS CLAUSE IS LOAD-BEARING IN v2: every clause of (N8) is proved by
exhibiting a quasi-continuous candidate that is a.e.-equal to the target and
then invoking this clause. It is declared here, once.
EXACT EDITION/THEOREM NUMBERING IS NOT CERTIFIED HERE; the lane convention
already in force is chapter-level naming with the mathematical hypotheses
checked against the landed objects ([PX:11565-11567]; XE-5 "WHAT WAS NOT
CHECKED", verdicts/XE-5-2026-07-27.md:101).

(N2) EQUILIBRIUM POTENTIAL OF AN OPEN SET. [IMP-2]
For O open with Cap(O) < infinity there is e_O in H^1(M) with e_O >= 1 a.e. on
O and E_1(e_O, e_O) = Cap(O); it satisfies 0 <= e_O <= 1 a.e. and e_O~ = 1
q.e. on O.
NAMED: FOT Ch. 2, §2.1 (existence, uniqueness and the 0 <= e <= 1 /
q.e.-attainment properties of the 1-equilibrium potential) — the same chapter
already imported at [PX:11565-11567] for the compact-set equilibrium potential.
HYPOTHESIS ROWS: form regular — MET (ROW-REG); O open — MET by construction;
Cap(O) < infinity — MET, since Cap(O) <= Cap(M) <= E_1(1,1) = mu(M) < infinity
by (REG-b).
CONSEQUENCES USED: D(e_O) <= E_1(e_O) = Cap(O); ||e_O||^2_{L^2(mu)} <=
E_1(e_O) = Cap(O); and, via (N8-iv), 0 <= e_O~ <= 1 q.e.
NOTE ON THE BOUND'S MODE: FOT delivers 0 <= e_O <= 1 as an a.e. statement about
the form-domain element. v1 used it against q.e. statements without saying so.
v2 upgrades it explicitly and inline by (N8-iv).

(N3) SUBADDITIVITY OF Cap ON OPEN SETS — PROVED INLINE, NO IMPORT. For O_1, O_2
open, Cap(O_1 u O_2) <= Cap(O_1) + Cap(O_2).
PROOF. Let u_i >= 1 a.e. on O_i, u_i in H^1(M). Then u_1 v u_2 >= 1 a.e. on
O_1 u O_2 and, for the concrete form,
  D(u_1 v u_2) + D(u_1 ^ u_2) = D(u_1) + D(u_2),
because grad(u_1 v u_2) = grad u_1 a.e. on {u_1 > u_2}, = grad u_2 a.e. on
{u_2 > u_1}, and grad u_1 = grad u_2 a.e. on {u_1 = u_2}; the same partition
gives the identity for the L^2(mu) parts. Hence
E_1(u_1 v u_2) <= E_1(u_1) + E_1(u_2). Take infima. QED
(By ROW-CAP's second line, subadditivity passes to arbitrary sets; only the open
case is used below. USED TWICE: at step (3) of the Lemma, and inside (N8-0).)

(N4) Cap-NULL IMPLIES LEBESGUE-NULL — PROVED INLINE, NO IMPORT. If Cap(E) = 0
then Leb(E) = 0; hence "q.e." implies "a.e.".
PROOF. For O open and u >= 1 a.e. on O, E_1(u,u) >= ||u||^2_{L^2(mu)} >= mu(O),
so Cap(O) >= mu(O). By ROW-CAP, Cap(E) = inf over open O containing E of
Cap(O) >= inf mu(O) >= mu(E). So mu(E) = 0, and mu has the smooth strictly
positive density e^{-beta E_eps} (ROW-REG), so Leb(E) = 0. QED

(N5) LIPSCHITZ COMPOSITION LOWERS D. [LND-1] For T : R -> R 1-Lipschitz and
u in H^1(M), T(u) in H^1(M) and D(T(u)) <= D(u). (On the COMPACT M constants
lie in H^1(M) by (REG-b), so T(0) need not vanish.)
LANDED IN THE CORPUS as "0 <= h <= 1 (truncation lowers D)" [PX:11562]; the
general 1-Lipschitz case is the same chain rule (|grad T(u)| <= |grad u| a.e.).
No new external import.

(N6) SMOOTH URYSOHN FUNCTIONS ON M. [IMP-3] For compacts P subset Q^o with Q
closed there is chi in C^infinity(M) with 0 <= chi <= 1, chi = 1 on a
neighbourhood of P, supp chi subset Q^o.
NAMED: standard smooth partition-of-unity / Urysohn construction on a smooth
manifold. HYPOTHESIS ROWS: M smooth — MET (ROW-REG); P compact, P subset Q^o
open — MET by construction below. DECLARED AS AN IMPORT IN v2; v1's ledger
omitted it.

(N7) CHART MOLLIFICATION ON A COMPACT MANIFOLD, WITH POINTWISE PRESERVATION.
Fix a finite atlas {(psi_i, V_i)} of M and a smooth partition of unity {chi_i}
subordinate to it, and let L_atlas < infinity be a common bi-Lipschitz constant
for the finitely many charts. For F in H^1(M) and r_mol > 0 define
  F_{r_mol} := sum_i chi_i . ( ( J_{r_mol} ( F o psi_i^{-1} ) ) o psi_i ),
J_{r_mol} = convolution with a NONNEGATIVE Euclidean mollifier of total mass 1
and support radius r_mol. Then (i) F_{r_mol} in C^infinity(M); (ii)
F_{r_mol} -> F in H^1(M) as r_mol -> 0; (iii) if F >= 1 a.e. on an open U and
r_mol < dist(P, M \ U)/L_atlas for a compact P subset U, then F_{r_mol} >= 1
pointwise on an open neighbourhood of P; and symmetrically with "<= 0 a.e." and
"<= 0 pointwise".
CLAUSE (ii) IS THE IMPORT [IMP-4]. NAMED: the standard Meyers-Serrin /
chart-mollification density theorem (C^infinity(M) dense in H^1(M) for compact
M). HYPOTHESIS ROWS: M compact smooth without boundary — MET (ROW-REG; the
corpus's own identification M = R^{2N}/Lambda, [PX:17299-17307]); F in H^1(M) —
MET; finite atlas — MET by compactness. CLAUSES (i) AND (iii) ARE PROVED INLINE.
PROOF OF (iii), the only nonstandard clause: for x with the r_mol-ball around
psi_i(x) contained in psi_i(U), the value (J_{r_mol}(F o psi_i^{-1}))(psi_i(x))
is an average of F over a subset of U against a nonnegative kernel of mass 1,
hence >= 1; summing against sum_i chi_i(x) = 1 gives F_{r_mol}(x) >= 1. The
uniform radius condition r_mol < dist(P, M\U)/L_atlas makes this hold at every
x in the open set {x : dist(x,P) < dist(P, M\U)/2} for r_mol small. QED
REMARK (NOT CONSUMED): under the landed flat identification M = R^{2N}/Lambda a
single global convolution replaces the atlas and (iii) is immediate; the chart
version above is used so that no flatness of the metric is assumed.

(N8) THE QUASI-CONTINUOUS CALCULUS — PROVED INLINE FROM (N1) AND (N3),
     NO IMPORT. [THIS ROW IS NEW IN v2 AND IS THE HIGH-2 REPAIR.]
Throughout, u~ is THE quasi-continuous version of u in H^1(M) supplied by (N1);
it satisfies u~ = u a.e. and is unique q.e. Call a function v : M -> R
quasi-continuous in the sense of ROW-CAP.
 (N8-0) GLUING OF EXCEPTIONAL SETS. If v_1, v_2 are quasi-continuous then for
   every b > 0 there is ONE open O with Cap(O) < b off which BOTH restrict
   continuously: take O_i with Cap(O_i) < b/2 and put O := O_1 u O_2, open, with
   Cap(O) < b by (N3). CONSEQUENCE: any CONTINUOUS function of finitely many
   quasi-continuous functions is quasi-continuous. QED
 (N8-i) LINEARITY. For u, v in H^1(M) and reals a, b: (a u + b v)~ = a u~ + b v~
   q.e. PROOF. a u~ + b v~ is quasi-continuous by (N8-0), and equals a u + b v
   a.e. because u~ = u and v~ = v a.e. So it IS a quasi-continuous version of the
   element a u + b v of H^1(M); by (N1)'s q.e.-uniqueness clause it agrees q.e.
   with (a u + b v)~. QED
   (Constants: a constant function is continuous, hence its own quasi-continuous
   version, so (u + c)~ = u~ + c q.e.)
 (N8-ii) CONTINUOUS MULTIPLIER. For chi in C(M) and u in H^1(M) with chi u in
   H^1(M): (chi u)~ = chi . u~ q.e. PROOF. chi . u~ is quasi-continuous by
   (N8-0) and equals chi u a.e.; same uniqueness step. QED
 (N8-iii) LIPSCHITZ COMPOSITION. For T : R -> R Lipschitz and u in H^1(M):
   T(u) in H^1(M) by (N5), and T(u)~ = T(u~) q.e. PROOF. T(u~) is
   quasi-continuous by (N8-0) and equals T(u) a.e.; same uniqueness step. QED
 (N8-iv) CONSTANT BOUNDS UPGRADE FROM a.e. TO q.e. If a <= u <= b a.e. for REAL
   CONSTANTS a <= b, then a <= u~ <= b q.e. PROOF. Put T(t) := min(b, max(a,t)),
   1-Lipschitz. Then T(u) = u a.e., so T(u) and u are THE SAME ELEMENT of
   H^1(M) (elements are a.e.-classes) and therefore have the same
   quasi-continuous version q.e. By (N8-iii), u~ = T(u)~ = T(u~) q.e., and T
   takes its values in [a,b] AT EVERY POINT. QED
   SCOPE FENCE, STATED BECAUSE IT IS THE EXACT FAULT LINE XE-5 FINDINGS 2 AND 3
   NAMED: (N8-iv) upgrades bounds by CONSTANTS only. NO a.e. inequality between
   two non-constant functions is upgraded anywhere in this piece.
 (N8-v) SMOOTH MULTIPLIER STAYS IN H^1. For chi in C^infinity(M) and u in
   H^1(M) on compact M, chi u in H^1(M) with grad(chi u) = chi grad u +
   u grad chi a.e. PROOF. True for u in C^infinity(M) by the classical Leibniz
   rule; chi, grad chi are bounded on compact M, so both sides are continuous in
   the H^1 topology, and C^infinity(M) is dense by (N7)(ii). QED

---------------------------------------------------------------------
3. LEMMA (CORE-DENSITY): THE CONDENSER CAPACITY IS ATTAINED FROM THE CORE
---------------------------------------------------------------------
[CARRIED FROM v1. The mathematical content is unchanged — my checker attacked
the neighbourhood-to-compact limit (attack 1), the eps-argument (attack 2) and
the tube-flux extension (attack 5) and broke none of them. The ONLY v2 edits are
that every q.e./a.e. passage now cites the (N8) row that licenses it.]

LEMMA (CORE-DENSITY). Let A, B be DISJOINT COMPACT subsets of M. Put
  K(A,B)    := { f in H^1(M) : f~ = 1 q.e. on A, f~ = 0 q.e. on B },
  Core(A,B) := { g : M -> [0,1] Lipschitz : g = 1 on an OPEN neighbourhood of A,
                                            g = 0 on an OPEN neighbourhood of B }.
Then Core(A,B) subset Lip(A,B) subset K(A,B), both classes are nonempty, and
  inf_{Core(A,B)} D  =  inf_{K(A,B)} D  =  cap(A,B).                  (CORE-EQ)

PROOF.
(0) INCLUSIONS AND NONEMPTINESS. A Lipschitz function on compact M lies in
H^1(M) and, being continuous, is its own quasi-continuous version (take the
empty exceptional open set in ROW-CAP); pointwise equality on A is a fortiori
q.e. equality on A. So Core(A,B) subset Lip(A,B) subset K(A,B). Core(A,B) is
nonempty by (N6) applied to the disjoint compacts A, B. Hence
  inf_{Core} D >= inf_{Lip} D >= inf_{K} D = cap(A,B),               (CORE-GE)
the last equality being the landed definition [PX:11563].

(1) NORMALISATION. Fix f_0 in K(A,B) and put T_0(t) := min(1, max(0,t)),
1-Lipschitz, and f := T_0(f_0). Then D(f) <= D(f_0) by (N5), and by (N8-iii)
f~ = T_0(f_0~) q.e., so f~ = T_0(1) = 1 q.e. on A and f~ = T_0(0) = 0 q.e. on
B: f is again in K(A,B). Moreover, since T_0 has range [0,1] AT EVERY POINT,
  0 <= f~ <= 1   q.e. on M.                                          (SQ-0)
[(SQ-0) IS A q.e. STATEMENT OBTAINED WITHOUT ANY a.e.-TO-q.e. UPGRADE OF A
NON-CONSTANT INEQUALITY. v1 asserted "0 <= f <= 1" a.e. and then read it against
q.e. objects in step (6); that gap is what (N8-iii) now closes at its source.]
Fix a_sq in (0, 1/4] and b_cap in (0,1).

(2) SEPARATING COLLARS. Put d_sep := dist(A,B) > 0 and
  W_A' := { x : dist(x,A) < d_sep/4 },  W_A := { x : dist(x,A) < d_sep/2 },
  W_B' := { x : dist(x,B) < d_sep/4 },  W_B := { x : dist(x,B) < d_sep/2 }.
All four are open; closure(W_A') subset W_A, closure(W_B') subset W_B, and
W_A inter W_B = empty (a common point would force dist(A,B) < d_sep). By (N6)
pick chi_A, chi_B in C^infinity(M) with 0 <= chi <= 1, chi_A = 1 on W_A',
supp chi_A subset W_A, chi_B = 1 on W_B', supp chi_B subset W_B.

(3) THE SMALL OPEN SET. Let N_A subset A and N_B subset B be the Cap-null sets
off which f~ = 1 on A resp. f~ = 0 on B. By ROW-CAP's quasi-continuity of f~
(supplied by (N1)) choose O_1 open with Cap(O_1) < b_cap/2 and f~|_{M \ O_1}
continuous. By ROW-CAP (outer regularity, definitional) choose O_2 open with
N_A u N_B subset O_2 and Cap(O_2) < b_cap/2. Put O := O_1 u O_2, OPEN, with
Cap(O) < b_cap by (N3). Put
  O_A := O inter W_A',   O_B := O inter W_B'    (open, Cap <= Cap(O) < b_cap).

(4) OPEN NEIGHBOURHOODS OF A AND OF B. For x in A \ O we have x not in N_A,
so f~(x) = 1 > 1 - a_sq/2. Since f~|_{M \ O} is continuous, the set
{ x in M \ O : f~(x) > 1 - a_sq/2 } is relatively open in M \ O, hence equals
Q_A inter (M \ O) for some OPEN Q_A subset M. Symmetrically
{ x in M \ O : f~(x) < a_sq/2 } = Q_B inter (M \ O) with Q_B open. Define
  U_A := ( Q_A inter W_A' ) u O_A,     U_B := ( Q_B inter W_B' ) u O_B.
Both are OPEN. A subset U_A: indeed A \ O subset Q_A and A subset W_A', so
A \ O subset Q_A inter W_A'; and A inter O subset O inter W_A' = O_A. Likewise
B subset U_B. Finally U_A subset W_A' and U_B subset W_B', so
U_A inter U_B = empty, U_A inter supp chi_B = empty and
U_B inter supp chi_A = empty.

(5) THE PATCHES. Let e_{O_A}, e_{O_B} be the equilibrium potentials of (N2) and
set pA := chi_A . e_{O_A}, pB := chi_B . e_{O_B}. By (N8-v), pA, pB in H^1(M).
By (N2) and (N8-iv), 0 <= e_{O_A}~ <= 1 q.e., hence by (N8-ii)
  pA~ = chi_A . e_{O_A}~ q.e.,  so  0 <= pA~ <= 1 q.e.,
and since chi_A = 1 POINTWISE on W_A' superset O_A while e_{O_A}~ = 1 q.e. on
O_A by (N2),
  pA~ = 1 q.e. on O_A;   likewise  pB~ = 1 q.e. on O_B.
Also supp pA subset W_A and supp pB subset W_B, so pB = 0 POINTWISE on U_A and,
by (N8-ii), pB~ = 0 q.e. on U_A; symmetrically pA~ = 0 q.e. on U_B.
ENERGY OF THE PATCHES. With (REG-a), (N8-v) and (N2),
  D(pA) = int_M w |grad(chi_A e_{O_A})|^2 dx
        <= 2 int_M w chi_A^2 |grad e_{O_A}|^2 dx
           + 2 ||grad chi_A||_infinity^2 int_M w e_{O_A}^2 dx
        <= 2 D(e_{O_A}) + 2 ||grad chi_A||_infinity^2 (1/beta)
             ||e_{O_A}||^2_{L^2(mu)}
        <= ( 2 + 2 ||grad chi_A||_infinity^2 / beta ) b_cap
        =: C_patch . b_cap,
and the same bound for pB after enlarging C_patch. C_patch depends on A, B and
beta ONLY (through the fixed cutoffs); it is held FIXED while b_cap -> 0. See
Section 5 (BETA ACCOUNTING).

(6) THE PATCHED COMPETITOR. Put f' := ( f - a_sq/2 ) / ( 1 - a_sq ) in H^1(M),
so D(f') = (1 - a_sq)^{-2} D(f). By (N8-i) (affine map, constant function
included),
  f'~ = ( f~ - a_sq/2 ) / ( 1 - a_sq )   q.e.,
so (SQ-0) gives, for a_sq <= 1/4, the q.e. bounds
  f'~ >= -a_sq/(2(1-a_sq)) >= -a_sq   and   f'~ <= (1-a_sq/2)/(1-a_sq) <= 2,
and, at q.e. x, EXACTLY the two implications
  f~(x) > 1 - a_sq/2  ==>  f'~(x) > 1 ;    f~(x) < a_sq/2  ==>  f'~(x) < 0.
Define
  F := f' + 2 pA - 2 pB   in H^1(M),   so   F~ = f'~ + 2 pA~ - 2 pB~ q.e.
                                             by (N8-i).
CONSTRAINT CHECK ON U_A. Let x in U_A, outside the union of the finitely many
Cap-null sets named above (a Cap-null set by (N3)). Either x in O_A, where
pA~(x) = 1 and pB~(x) = 0 (U_A inter supp chi_B = empty), so
F~(x) >= -a_sq + 2 >= 1; or x in (Q_A inter W_A') \ O_A, and since x in W_A' the
condition x not in O_A means x not in O, hence x in Q_A inter (M\O), hence
f~(x) > 1 - a_sq/2, hence f'~(x) > 1, and pA~(x) >= 0, pB~(x) = 0, so
F~(x) > 1. Therefore F~ >= 1 q.e. on U_A.
CONSTRAINT CHECK ON U_B. Symmetrically: on O_B, pB~ = 1 q.e., pA~ = 0 q.e., and
f'~ <= 2 q.e., so F~ <= 2 - 2 = 0 q.e.; on (Q_B inter W_B') \ O_B, f'~ < 0,
pA~ = 0, pB~ >= 0, so F~ < 0. Therefore F~ <= 0 q.e. on U_B.
By (N4), q.e. implies a.e., and F~ = F a.e.:
  F >= 1 a.e. on the OPEN set U_A superset A,
  F <= 0 a.e. on the OPEN set U_B superset B.                        (NBHD)
ENERGY. By the triangle inequality for the seminorm D^{1/2},
  D(F)^{1/2} <= (1 - a_sq)^{-1} D(f)^{1/2} + 2 D(pA)^{1/2} + 2 D(pB)^{1/2}
             <= (1 - a_sq)^{-1} D(f)^{1/2} + 4 ( C_patch b_cap )^{1/2}.  (ENER)

(7) MOLLIFY AND TRUNCATE. [VERBATIM FROM v1 — SUSTAINED UNDER ATTACKS 2 AND 5.]
A is compact and U_A open, B is compact and U_B open;
pick r_mol > 0 smaller than min( dist(A, M\U_A), dist(B, M\U_B) ) / L_atlas and
form F_{r_mol} of (N7). By (N7)(iii) and (NBHD), F_{r_mol} >= 1 pointwise on an
open neighbourhood of A and F_{r_mol} <= 0 pointwise on an open neighbourhood of
B. Put
  g := min( 1, max( 0, F_{r_mol} ) ).
Then g is Lipschitz (smooth composed with a 1-Lipschitz map on compact M), takes
values in [0,1], equals 1 on an open neighbourhood of A, equals 0 on an open
neighbourhood of B — i.e. g in Core(A,B) — and D(g) <= D(F_{r_mol}) by (N5).
NOTE, RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS WHAT MAKES THE TUBE-FLUX EXTENSION EXACT: every g
produced here is an EXACT competitor, equal to 1 and to 0 POINTWISE on open
neighbourhoods, not merely close to them. The approximation is pushed entirely
onto the ENERGY, never onto the constraint.

(8) LIMITS. By (N7)(ii), D(F_{r_mol}) -> D(F) as r_mol -> 0. Hence by (ENER)
  inf_{Core(A,B)} D  <=  D(F)
                     <=  ( (1-a_sq)^{-1} D(f)^{1/2}
                           + 4 ( C_patch b_cap )^{1/2} )^2.
Send b_cap -> 0 with a_sq fixed, then a_sq -> 0 (C_patch is fixed at each stage;
it depends on a_sq through nothing, and on b_cap through nothing):
  inf_{Core(A,B)} D  <=  D(f)  <=  D(f_0).
This holds for every f_0 in K(A,B), so inf_{Core} D <= inf_{K} D = cap(A,B).
With (CORE-GE), all three infima coincide. QED (CORE-EQ)

---------------------------------------------------------------------
4. (CLASS-BRIDGE) AND THE DELIVERED DISPLAY (CAP-LOW*-H1)
---------------------------------------------------------------------
[CARRIED FROM v1 VERBATIM, INCLUDING THE eps-FORM AND THE TUBE-FLUX EXTENSION.
Only scope-fence item (a) is sharpened, and Section 6 now discharges the
consequence v1's propagation item 2 got wrong.]

COROLLARY (CLASS-BRIDGE). Let A, B be disjoint compacts in M and let L be a
constant such that
  D(g) >= L   for EVERY Lipschitz g with g = 1 pointwise on A and g = 0
  pointwise on B                                                     (LIP-BOUND)
Then
  cap(A,B) := inf{ D(f) : f in H^1(M), f~ = 1 q.e. on A, f~ = 0 q.e. on B }
           >= L.                                                     (CLASS-BRIDGE)
PROOF, WITH THE DIRECTION TRACKED EXPLICITLY. Every g in Core(A,B) satisfies the
hypothesis of (LIP-BOUND) (it equals 1 on a neighbourhood of A, hence pointwise
on A; and 0 on a neighbourhood of B, hence pointwise on B), so D(g) >= L for
every g in Core(A,B), i.e. inf_{Core} D >= L. By (CORE-EQ),
cap(A,B) = inf_{Core} D >= L. QED
EQUIVALENT eps-FORM, DISPLAYED AS THE VERDICT ASKS. Let f in K(A,B) and c > 0.
By step (8) of the Lemma there is g_c in Core(A,B) with D(g_c) <= D(f) + c.
By (LIP-BOUND), D(g_c) >= L. Hence D(f) >= L - c for every c > 0, so D(f) >= L
for every f in K(A,B), so cap(A,B) >= L.
MINIMISING-SEQUENCE FORM. Take g_m in Core(A,B) with D(g_m) -> inf_{Core} D =
cap(A,B) (possible by (CORE-EQ)). Each g_m satisfies D(g_m) >= L by (LIP-BOUND).
Passing to the limit, cap(A,B) = lim_m D(g_m) >= L. The two forms are the same
argument written in the two directions; the load-bearing content in both is
(CORE-EQ), i.e. that the infimum over the SMALL class is not strictly larger
than the infimum over the LARGE class.

DELIVERED DISPLAY.
(CAP-LOW*-H1). Let z in R_0 with dist(z,S) >= 4/beta, rho = 1/beta,
A_z := closed B_rho(z), and let gamma, Tub, Ell, J, Ar, En(J) be the landed tube
objects of [PX:9067] with beta >= beta_*. Then, for the (WFF-1) variational
capacity at the plate,
  cap_pl(A_z) = cap(A_z, closure(S))
              = inf{ D(f) : f in H^1(M), f~ = 1 q.e. on A_z,
                                          f~ = 0 q.e. on closure(S) }
              >= 1 / En(J)
              >= ( Ar / ( beta Ell ) ) exp( -beta ( Theta(z,S) + eta + G/beta ) )
              =  c(N,delta) beta^{-2N} exp( -beta ( Theta(z,S) + eta ) )
              =: LB(beta),      c(N,delta) beta-free.          (CAP-LOW*-H1)
PROOF. Apply (CLASS-BRIDGE) with A := A_z, B := closure(S), L := 1/En(J).
HYPOTHESIS ROWS.
  (i) A, B disjoint compacts — MET by ROW-PLATE-SEP, margin d_sep >= 3rho.
  (ii) (LIP-BOUND) at these A, B — MET by the LANDED display, verbatim: "for
