5. DIRECTION LEDGER AND BETA ACCOUNTING — NO CONSTANT MOVES
---------------------------------------------------------------------
D1. Core(A,B) subset Lip(A,B) subset K(A,B): infima are ordered
    inf_Core >= inf_Lip >= inf_K. The lemma proves the reverse inequality
    inf_Core <= inf_K, hence EQUALITY throughout. The bridge consumes only
    "inf_Core <= inf_K"; the trivial direction is recorded for completeness.
D2. The landed (LIP-BOUND) is a LOWER bound on a SMALLER class; the consumer
    needs a LOWER bound on a LARGER class. The bridge is exactly (CORE-EQ);
    without it the implication is FALSE in general and this piece does not
    claim it.
D3. BETA ACCOUNTING. Three beta-dependent quantities appear inside the proof of
    (CORE-EQ) and NONE survives into (CAP-LOW*-H1):
      - the factor 1/beta in (REG-a), used only inside the patch-energy bound;
      - ||grad chi_A||_infinity, which is of order 1/d_sep = O(beta) since
        d_sep >= 3rho = 3/beta, so C_patch = O(beta);
      - Cap(M) <= mu(M), used only for finiteness in (N2).
    All three enter only through the term 4 (C_patch b_cap)^{1/2} in (ENER),
    and b_cap is sent to 0 at FIXED beta. The conclusion (CAP-LOW*-H1) is a
    statement for each fixed beta >= beta_*; the approximation is purely
    qualitative. THEREFORE: no constant, no power of beta and no exponent in
    (CAP-LOW*) changes. c(N,delta) is the landed beta-free constant, the power
    is beta^{-2N}, the exponent is -beta(Theta(z,S) + eta). This matches the
    landed bookkeeping claim, verbatim: "which is the landed final bound with
    the SAME constant c(N,delta), the SAME power beta^{-2N} and the SAME
    exponent -beta(Theta(z,S) + eta)" [PX:14675-14676] — now with the claim
    supported rather than typed.
D4. NO ROUTE-A RESURRECTION. This piece never asserts that an H^1/q.e.
    competitor is Lipschitz or is admissible in the landed pointwise class. The
    withdrawn assertion of [PX:14431-14440] stays withdrawn per AM-R5-26(c)(ii)
    [PX:17293-17294]. What is proved instead is a one-sided ENERGY
    APPROXIMATION of each H^1/q.e. competitor from within the Lipschitz class.
D5. NO INDEPENDENCE, NO STOPPING OBJECT, NO SIGMA-FIELD, NO PHYSICS VOCABULARY,
    NO TIME-DEPENDENCE is introduced. The only probabilistic word appearing is
    in the CITATION of ROW-REG, which is consumed as a hypothesis row, not
    re-derived.
D6. NO SET IS REDEFINED. A_z, S, closure(S), Y, TRAP, TRAP_2^cl, Tub, D_0,
    D_end, J, En(J), Ar, Ell, Theta(z,S), eta, c(N,delta), LB(beta) are all
    consumed with their landed definitions.
D7. THE a.e./q.e. LEDGER (NEW IN v2). Every mode change in this piece is one of
    exactly three licensed moves, each named at its use site: q.e. -> a.e. by
    (N4); a.e. -> q.e. FOR CONSTANT BOUNDS ONLY by (N8-iv); and transport of a
    q.c. version through an affine map, a continuous multiplier or a Lipschitz
    composition by (N8-i)/(N8-ii)/(N8-iii). NO OTHER MODE CHANGE OCCURS. In
    particular the general q.e.-order property is neither imported nor used.

landed conditionality at MM:3163 that was never validly superseded)

0. WHY v1 IS ABANDONED RATHER THAN PATCHED
===================================================================

v1 attempted to CURE Finding 4 by retyping the operative initial-delay
object to D(0) ^ L_0 across the whole Wald/LP.5 propagation (eleven residual
sites R1-R11, plus amendments A6/A7 and two lane-file registers). Its five
BLOCKINGs were not five separable slips; each was a consequence of the
approach:

  - to make the retype produce a live estimate, v1 had to re-read MM:4246's
    FIRST summand as an IN-R_0 occupation bound, an object MM never states
    (the mirror image of the defect being cured);
  - to make the retype complete, v1 had to close an inventory it did not
    close, and it inherited PX:17097-17099's "and nothing else" byte-count
    claim instead;
  - to make the retype land, v1 had to disposition MM:3348-3356 and
    MM:3169-3177 without reading them, and both refute the stated
    expectation;
  - the retype's object is incompatible with GAP-LP-RECUR's NAMED object at
    MM:3163, which v1 never edited and mis-stated;
  - and A6 is a ratified amendment naming an object, a rationale and a site,
    so it cannot take a "mechanical" retype.

A DE-CLAIM has none of these costs. It estimates nothing, sweeps nothing,
retypes no object, and amends no amendment. It deletes one overclaimed
display and lets the corpus fall back to a conditionality it already carried
in its own bytes. That is the whole of v2.

  local-Holder statement for W^{1,2} weak solutions of divergence-form

EDIT 2 — ROW (N9) [IMP-6] AND THE CITATION INSIDE (N3)

(a) INSERT the following row between (N4) [PX:19740-19746] and (N5)
[PX:19747]:

(N9) SOBOLEV LATTICE / STAMPACCHIA GRADIENT IDENTITY. [IMP-6]
For v in H^1(M):
 (a) v^+ := max(v,0) lies in H^1(M) and grad v^+ = 1_{{v > 0}} grad v
     a.e.;
 (b) for every real constant c, grad v = 0 a.e. on the level set
     {v = c};
 (c) consequently, for u_1, u_2 in H^1(M), writing
       u_1 v u_2 = u_2 + (u_1 - u_2)^+,   u_1 ^ u_2 = u_1 - (u_1 - u_2)^+,
     both lie in H^1(M) and
       grad(u_1 v u_2) = grad u_1  a.e. on {u_1 > u_2},
                       = grad u_2  a.e. on {u_2 > u_1},
                       = grad u_1 = grad u_2  a.e. on {u_1 = u_2},
     with the two roles exchanged for u_1 ^ u_2. Hence at a.e. point the
     unordered pair ( grad(u_1 v u_2), grad(u_1 ^ u_2) ) equals
     ( grad u_1, grad u_2 ), which is EXACTLY the a.e. partition (N3)
     displays.
NAMED: Gilbarg-Trudinger, Elliptic Partial Differential Equations of
Second Order, Lemma 7.6 (weak derivative of the positive part), with its
standard corollary (b). THIS IS THE LANE'S OWN NAME FOR THIS FACT: the
sibling C1 material already cites it in the same words at [PX:17686] and
[PX:17917] and books it in its import list at [PX:18150]
("Gilbarg-Trudinger Lemma 7.6 (Stampacchia truncation)"). v2 dropped the
naming while keeping the use.

INSERTION:

(N10) THE EUCLIDEAN MOLLIFIER PACKAGE. [IMP-7]
Let d := dim M and let J_r denote convolution on R^d with the kernel of
(N7): j_r(y) = r^{-d} j(y/r), j in C_c^infinity(B_1), j >= 0,
integral j = 1. Then, for the two displayed bounds:
  (MOL-1)  || J_r h ||_{L^2(R^d)}  <=  || h ||_{L^2(R^d)}
           for every h in L^2(R^d);
  (MOL-2)  || J_r h - h ||_{L^2(R^d)}  ->  0   as r -> 0,
           for every h in L^2(R^d);
and the commutation clause
  (MOL-3)  grad ( J_r h ) = J_r ( grad h )  a.e., for every
           h in W^{1,2}(R^d).
NAMED: the standard mollifier package — Evans, Partial Differential
Equations, Appendix C (properties of mollifiers), equivalently Brezis,
Functional Analysis, Sobolev Spaces and Partial Differential Equations,
Ch. 4 (regularisation by convolution); (MOL-1) is Young's / Minkowski's
integral inequality for a nonnegative kernel of total mass 1, (MOL-2) is
continuity of translation in L^2, (MOL-3) is differentiation under the
convolution integral against the definition of the weak derivative.
HYPOTHESIS ROWS: kernel nonnegative, C_c^infinity, total mass 1, support
in B_r — MET by (N7)'s own construction, which already needs C^infinity
for clause (i) and nonnegativity plus mass 1 for clause (iii); h in L^2
resp. W^{1,2}(R^d) — MET at the single use below, where h has compact
support in a chart image.
 (c) CHART TRANSFER, RECORDED IN THE SAME ROW BECAUSE IT IS USED ONLY
 HERE: if psi is a smooth diffeomorphism of an open V subset M onto an
 open Omega subset R^d, and |D psi|, |D psi^{-1}| <= L_atlas on the
 relevant compact, then G |-> G o psi maps W^{1,2}(Omega) to H^1(V) with
   || G o psi ||_{H^1(V)}  <=  C(L_atlas, d) || G ||_{W^{1,2}(Omega)},
 and symmetrically. This is the classical chain rule and change of
 variables, which extends from smooth G to W^{1,2} by (ii-a). C(L_atlas,d)
 depends on the FIXED atlas only and is never displayed downstream.

PROOF OF (ii-b), THE DISPLAYED FAMILY. Recall the display [PX:19766]:
  F_{r_mol} = sum_i chi_i . ( ( J_{r_mol} ( F o psi_i^{-1} ) ) o psi_i ),
over the finite atlas {(psi_i, V_i)} with partition of unity {chi_i},
supp chi_i compact in V_i, sum_i chi_i = 1 pointwise on M.
STEP A (WELL-DEFINEDNESS AND LOCALISATION). By (N6) pick, for each i,
theta_i in C^infinity(M) with theta_i = 1 on an open neighbourhood
Theta_i of supp chi_i and supp theta_i subset V_i. Put
  K_i := psi_i( supp chi_i ),   r_1 := min_i dist( K_i, R^d \ psi_i(Theta_i) ),
a minimum over finitely many i of distances from a compact set to the
complement of an open set containing it, hence r_1 > 0. For
r_mol < r_1 and x in supp chi_i, the ball of radius r_mol about psi_i(x)
lies in psi_i(Theta_i), so the value
( J_{r_mol}( F o psi_i^{-1} ) )( psi_i(x) ) depends only on the values of
F on Theta_i; off supp chi_i the i-th summand vanishes by its factor
chi_i. Therefore, for r_mol < r_1, the DISPLAYED family is unchanged if
F o psi_i^{-1} is replaced by
  h_i := ( ( theta_i F ) o psi_i^{-1} ), extended by 0 to all of R^d,
and theta_i F in H^1(M) by (N8-v), so h_i in W^{1,2}(R^d) with compact
support by (N10)(c). No claim is made for r_mol >= r_1; the Lemma's step
(7) already fixes r_mol below an explicit threshold [PX:19939], and
r_1 is folded into that threshold.
STEP B (CONVERGENCE IN THE CHART). By (MOL-2) applied to h_i and, using
(MOL-3), to each weak partial derivative partial_k h_i (k = 1..d):
  || J_{r_mol} h_i - h_i ||_{W^{1,2}(R^d)}  ->  0   as r_mol -> 0.
(MOL-1) is what makes the family bounded uniformly in r_mol, so no
subsequence or diagonal argument is needed.
STEP C (ASSEMBLY ON M). Since sum_i chi_i = 1 and F = h_i o psi_i on
Theta_i superset supp chi_i, for r_mol < r_1
  F_{r_mol} - F = sum_i chi_i . ( ( J_{r_mol} h_i ) o psi_i - F ),
each summand supported in supp chi_i. By (N8-v) (Leibniz, with
chi_i and grad chi_i bounded on compact M) and (N10)(c),
  || F_{r_mol} - F ||_{H^1(M)}
     <=  sum_i ( 1 + || grad chi_i ||_infinity ) C(L_atlas, d)
             || J_{r_mol} h_i - h_i ||_{W^{1,2}(R^d)},
a sum of FINITELY many terms each tending to 0 by STEP B. Hence
F_{r_mol} -> F in H^1(M). QED (ii-b)
NORM ROW, STATED SO THAT NO CONSTANT IS SMUGGLED: the H^1(M) norm here is
the form norm E_1^{1/2} = ( D + || . ||^2_{L^2(mu)} )^{1/2}. By (REG-a)
and ROW-REG the weight w and the density of mu are smooth and bounded
above and below away from 0 on the compact M, so E_1^{1/2} is equivalent
to the Riemannian W^{1,2}(M) norm with FIXED constants. (ii-b) is
consumed only as a LIMIT, at step (8); the equivalence constants and
C(L_atlas,d) therefore enter no display, and no power of beta moves. The
consumed consequence is the one step (8) reads, obtained from the
seminorm triangle inequality
  | D(F_{r_mol})^{1/2} - D(F)^{1/2} |  <=  D(F_{r_mol} - F)^{1/2}  ->  0.
REMARK, THE SECOND ROUTE, NOT CONSUMED: under the landed identification
M = R^{2N}/Lambda [PX:17299-17307] a single global convolution on the
quotient replaces the atlas; STEP A and (N10)(c) become vacuous and
STEPS B-C reduce to (MOL-1)-(MOL-3) applied once, with C(L_atlas,d) = 1.
The chart route above is the one printed, so that no flatness of the
metric is assumed anywhere.

the eps-window in force. ... to be checked at the landing, not waved through").
